instances.label: Supervising a scheduled undergraduate teaching-lab session (soils, agronomy, horticulture, food or animal science): instructor circulates among 20-30 students at benches, demonstrates a technique hands-on (titration, soil texturing, microscope work, aseptic transfer), corrects grip/technique, enforces PPE and hazard rules, intervenes on spills or unsafe acts, and signs off on results at the end of the period.

Supervising student field work on university-controlled land: research farm plots, orchard, greenhouse, teaching dairy or feedlot. Instructor leads the group to the site, demonstrates soil coring, plot staking, plant/tissue sampling or livestock handling, monitors safety around machinery and animals, and keeps the class on schedule in weather-variable outdoor conditions.

Supervising off-campus field work in unstructured settings: rangeland transects, streams and lakes for fisheries classes, commercial farms, woodlots or wetlands. Instructor scouts hazards, demonstrates sampling in situ, supervises wading/ATV/electrofishing safety, adapts the exercise to found conditions, and accounts for all students.

Physical preparation and processing of standardized material for a teaching or research lab: weighing and aliquoting soil subsamples, making up reagents and standards, staging identical kits at each bench station, loading and running analytical instruments (pH, spectrophotometer, sieve stack) and verifying calibration before the session.

Coordinating overall laboratory operations: scheduling room and instrument use across sections, ordering and inventorying chemicals and consumables, keeping maintenance/calibration records, arranging repairs, managing hazardous-waste streams and chemical hygiene/IACUC compliance, and directing lab technicians and TAs.

Overseeing graduate and undergraduate researchers' bench, greenhouse and animal-facility work: reviewing protocols before they run, watching a student perform a new procedure, troubleshooting a failing instrument with them, checking data quality and animal/biosafety compliance during the run.

sources.title: Royal Marsden doubles genomic testing capacity through automation
sources.claim: Automata's LINQ robotic platform automates end-to-end lab workflows with a robot arm and labware transport layer, and is deployed in a clinical genomics laboratory at The Royal Marsden for robotic sample processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine laboratory sample handling and instrument feeding. It transfers to the professor's lab-prep/processing instance because the objects (tubes, plates, reagents), the pipetting/weighing precision, and the enclosed purpose-built workcell presentation are the same.

sources.system: Automated/robotic soil laboratory testing lines in Fugro geotechnical laboratories
sources.title: Transforming Soil Laboratory Testing with AI Technology
sources.claim: Modern soil-testing laboratories use automated systems that perform sample preparation (sieving, moisture conditioning, specimen loading) and automatic instrument calibration, with robotic pick-and-place handling high sample volumes with minimal manual intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial soil sample preparation and analysis. Same materials (soil, sieves, pH/organic matter tests) and same precision as an agronomy teaching lab's sample prep, performed in a purpose-built automated line.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (Nature 2020, 583, 237) and successor multi-robot SYNTHESIS-BOT workflow
sources.title: AI-driven mobile robots team up to tackle chemical synthesis - News - University of Liverpool
sources.claim: A mobile robotic chemist autonomously navigated a chemistry laboratory, operated benchtop instruments and chose its own experiments, running almost 700 catalysis experiments over eight days without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of laboratory instruments and materials handling in a research lab. Supports the physical execution part of coordinating laboratory operations (running and servicing instrument workflows), not supervision of students.

sources.system: Laboratory Safety Assistant (LSA) socially assistive robot framework
sources.title: Socially Assistive Robot as Laboratory Safety Assistant for Science Students
sources.claim: Robotic supervision of students in a teaching laboratory exists only as a research prototype framework that detects unsafe student behaviours; it does not run sessions, teach technique, or accept student output.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to supervising laboratory sessions; cited to show only prototype behaviour-detection exists, so it cannot support a positive judgment on the supervision instances.

instances.label: Multi-technique wet-lab molecular/cell biology project in the professor's university research lab: cloning, cell culture and transfection, PCR/qPCR, protein blots, fluorescence microscopy, with iterative troubleshooting of failed experiments, then figure assembly, manuscript writing, submission and revision through peer review.

Automatable microplate assay campaign in a university lab or core facility: compound or genetic library screening, or media/reaction optimization run on plate readers and liquid handlers, hits re-tested, results analyzed and written up for a journal or preprint server.

Organismal work in an institutional vivarium, aquatics facility or greenhouse: mouse colony husbandry, injections or survival surgery, behavioral assays, dissection and histology, or plant growth and phenotyping trials, followed by analysis and publication.

Field research at forest, wetland, coastal or agricultural sites: laying transects, trapping/netting/tagging animals, collecting plant, soil or water samples across seasons in weather and terrain taken as found, then lab processing, analysis and publication.

Computational or data-driven research done at a desk in a campus office: bioinformatic analysis of existing sequence or imaging datasets, modeling, literature synthesis/review, plus manuscript writing, submission and response to reviewers.

sources.system: Ginkgo Autonomous Lab / Cloud Lab (RACs + Catalyst) driven by GPT-5
sources.title: Ginkgo Bioworks' Autonomous Laboratory Driven by OpenAI's GPT-5 Achieves 40% Improvement Over State-of-the-Art Scientific Benchmark
sources.claim: Ginkgo Bioworks' cloud laboratory, built from reconfigurable automation carts and driven by an OpenAI reasoning model, ran a closed-loop biological research campaign (36,000 experimental conditions over six cycles and six months) that designed, executed and analyzed experiments with minimal human involvement and beat the published state of the art for cell-free protein synthesis cost; findings were released as a preprint.

sources.developer: Aberystwyth University / University of Cambridge (Ross King et al.)
sources.title: The automation of science - PubMed
sources.claim: Robot Scientist 'Adam', a purpose-built laboratory-automation system, autonomously generated functional-genomics hypotheses about yeast and tested them experimentally with microplate growth assays; the work was published in Science, with humans confirming conclusions manually and writing the paper.

sources.title: AI-driven mobile robots team up to tackle chemical synthesis - University of Liverpool News
sources.claim: A mobile robot chemist worked autonomously in a human-scale university chemistry laboratory, choosing its own next experiments and running about 700 catalysis experiments over eight days; a 2024 follow-on extended this to teams of mobile robots doing exploratory synthesis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous experimental campaigns at a standard laboratory bench. It shows a robot can navigate and operate human-scale lab instruments unattended, but the assays are chemistry with a human-specified search space, and humans framed the question and wrote the paper, so it does not carry a biology project to publication.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University with Emerald Cloud Lab
sources.title: Autonomous Chemistry and Materials Innovation Driven by Scientific Agents | JACS Au
sources.claim: Coscientist, an LLM-driven agent coupled to liquid-handling robots and a cloud lab, autonomously designed, planned and executed chemistry experiments such as palladium-catalysed cross-couplings, reported in Nature.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: agent-directed execution of bench protocols on automated liquid handlers, the same hardware class used for microplate biology assays; supports the E1 judgment that plate-based campaigns can run without a human at the bench.

sources.developer: The Ohio State University (Kline et al.)
sources.title: WildWing: An open-source, autonomous and affordable UAS for animal behaviour video monitoring - Methods in Ecology and Evolution
sources.claim: WildWing is an open-source unmanned aerial system that autonomously collects behavioural video data of group-living ... in the field (demonstrated on Grevy's zebras), i.e., autonomous field data collection only, not study design, sampling, analysis or write-up.

sources.title: Introducing Kosmos: 'AI Scientist' That Makes Discoveries Overnight | ALZFORUM
sources.claim: Kosmos is an autonomous 'AI scientist' that iterates literature search, data analysis and hypothesis generation to produce reported discoveries from existing datasets; it has no physical embodiment and its outputs are reports that human scientists validate and write up.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as context for the desk-based research instance: it is a software-only system with no physical embodiment, so under the rules it cannot support a positive tier judgment.

instances.label: Natural-area field trip for an ecology/organismal biology course: instructor drives or accompanies 10-30 students to a woodland, stream, wetland, prairie or shoreline; carries and sets out gear; demonstrates and supervises hands-on technique (quadrats and transects, dip nets and kick seines, Secchi disk and water-chemistry kits, mist nets or sweep nets, plant/insect keys), handles live organisms, answers on-the-spot identification questions, and manages safety on uneven ground in variable weather.

Class visit to an institution-controlled interpretive site (natural history museum, zoo, aquarium, botanical garden, herbarium): instructor arranges access, leads the cohort through selected exhibits/collections, delivers course-tied commentary linking specimens to lecture material, fields substantive student questions, and administers an accompanying worksheet or observation assignment.

Escorted tour of a working technical facility (campus research lab or imaging/sequencing core, greenhouse, animal facility, hospital clinical lab, wastewater plant, biotech or agricultural company): instructor coordinates the host, gives the safety/PPE briefing, keeps the group together in occupied working space, prompts and interprets equipment demonstrations, and connects what students see to course content.

Short on-campus outdoor exercise during a lab period: instructor takes students to the campus arboretum, lawn, pond or restoration plot to run quadrat sampling, tree/lichen identification, soil or insect collection, or a pollinator observation; distributes and demonstrates equipment, circulates among small groups checking technique and data sheets, then walks the class back.

Multi-day or residential field experience (field station, marine lab, barrier island, mountain research site): instructor manages travel, lodging and gear logistics, runs boat- or dawn/dusk-based sampling, supervises student-led projects in remote terrain, troubleshoots equipment in the field, and handles risk management away from campus support.

sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (CONTACT and SOFTBOTS units)
sources.title: Next-Gen Museum Guides: Autonomous Navigation and Visitor Interaction with an Agentic Robot
sources.claim: Alter-Ego, an autonomous dual-arm mobile robot, gave LLM-driven guided tours in a real maritime museum, navigating autonomously between exhibit areas and answering visitor questions; in the 34-participant trial it answered only about half of the questions asked (mean 3.71 answered of 7.29 asked), with comprehension failures, latency complaints, and network/battery failures.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: leading people through an out-of-classroom site and explaining what they see. It transfers only partially: the setting is an indoor, institution-controlled exhibit hall with a fixed knowledge base, the robot serves one or two visitors rather than a class, it answers roughly half of questions, and it performs no equipment handling, specimen collection, safety supervision or assessment, so it does not complete a course-related biology experience at instructor quality.

sources.title: Lindsey the Tour Guide Robot - Usage Patterns in a Museum Long-Term Deployment
sources.claim: Lindsey is an autonomous tour-guide robot deployed long-term at The Collection museum in Lincoln, UK, giving daily guided tours and information to walk-in visitors of an archaeology exhibition, with roboticists intervening only occasionally.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guiding visitors through an institution-controlled exhibit space with scripted interpretive content. Shows sustained autonomous navigation and narration indoors, but the content is fixed docent material for casual visitors, not a curriculum-linked biology experience with technique demonstration, substantive Q&A, group supervision and graded output, so it does not carry over to completing this task.

sources.developer: SUSTech / Shenzhen University / Honda Research Institute Europe
sources.title: ProjecTA: A Semi-Humanoid Robotic Teaching Assistant with In-Situ Projection for Guided Tours
sources.claim: ProjecTA is a semi-humanoid robotic teaching assistant that leads walk-and-talk guided tours in a university makerspace, projecting explanatory overlays near objects; its explanatory gesture sequences were teleoperated and recorded in advance for playback, and it was evaluated in a 24-participant lab study rather than deployed as an instructor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an out-of-classroom guided learning tour of a campus facility. It is the closest educational analogue found, but gestures were pre-recorded by teleoperation and the system was tested in ... controlled 24-participant study, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

instances.label: After a majors' cell-biology or microbiology section, the instructor services shared benchtop gear in a campus teaching lab: cleans compound-microscope optics/stages and checks illuminators, drains and wipes water baths, cleans hot plates and vortexers, wipes incubator spills, checks gel boxes and leads, levels and zeroes balances, and returns items to the prep room. Benches are cluttered with student leftovers.

An instrument fails mid-semester: a benchtop centrifuge won't reach speed, a thermocycler throws a lid error, an autoclave leaks at the door gasket, a vacuum pump needs an oil change/rebuild, or a microscope stage jams. The professor consults manuals, opens housings, tests fuses/belts/seals, replaces a part or improvises a fix, reassembles and test-runs, or packs the unit for vendor service.

Gravimetric calibration and verification of volume-dispensing devices before a quantitative lab or assay run: dispense set volumes onto an analytical balance, compute accuracy and precision, adjust the device or flag it out of spec, and document results.

Maintenance and calibration of electrochemical probes used in ecology/physiology teaching and research (pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity): clean and rehydrate electrodes, run multi-point buffer calibration, check slope, replace membranes or fill solution, and log results.

Servicing optical instrumentation in a research lab: realign a fluorescence microscope illumination path or laser line, replace and align a lamp, clean and realign optics on a bench setup, and verify beam alignment and image quality after disturbance.

Upkeep of cold-storage and culture-support equipment in a shared departmental facility: defrost and clean -80 freezer gaskets and filters, service CO2 incubators (water pan, decon cycle, swap CO2 cylinder), refill LN2 dewars, clean autoclave chamber and drain screen, maintain aquaria/growth-chamber pumps, filters and lights.

sources.title: Automatic cleaning and calibration of pH sensors | Endress+Hauser — Liquiline Control CDC90
sources.claim: Commercial system that automatically cleans, calibrates and adjusts pH/ORP sensors installed in retractable armatures, with dosing of buffer and cleaning media, deployed at industrial plants (Dow Stade, AVR Rotterdam, mining sites).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cleaning/calibration/adjustment of a pH electrode at a process measuring point. It is the same physical maintenance operation an instructor performs on a lab pH/ORP probe (rinse, buffer calibration, slope adjustment, documentation), on the same class of sensor, in a purpose-built installation.

sources.system: Closed-loop robotic optics framework (UFACTORY xArm7 + hierarchical vision)
sources.title: A Framework for Closed-Loop Robotic Assembly, Alignment and Self-Recovery of Precision Optical Systems
sources.claim: A 7-DoF robotic arm autonomously builds, aligns and maintains a tabletop laser cavity from ... placed optical components on a fiducial-structured optical table, including recovery from induced misalignment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous alignment and self-recovery of a precision optical system. Optical realignment after disturbance is the same maintenance operation as realigning a microscope or bench light path, with comparable (sub-mm/sub-mrad) precision, performed on lab optical hardware.

sources.system: TECAN Freedom EVO automated gravimetric calibration procedure
sources.title: Automated Gravimetric Calibration to Optimize the Accuracy and Precision of TECAN Freedom EVO Liquid Handler - PMC
sources.claim: Published, fully automated gravimetric calibration procedure in which a liquid-handling robot dispenses set volumes onto an integrated balance, evaluates accuracy and precision, adjusts pipetting parameters and generates reports without operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: gravimetric volume calibration and adjustment of a pipetting device. It is the same measurement, acceptance and adjustment workflow the instructor runs on pipettes, executed on a purpose-built robot deck where the dispensing device and balance are fixtured.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulators in a real chemistry laboratory operate human instruments — opening instrument doors and loading dispensing cartridges — while running experiments over eight days.
sources.transferJustification: Closest lab-robot capability to equipment servicing: the robot manipulates instrument doors and consumable cartridges in a human lab. It shows current lab mobile manipulators execute pre-programmed experiment steps on instrumented equipment, not diagnosis, disassembly or repair.

sources.system: WARA Robotics Mobile Manipulation Challenge entries (four academic mobile manipulator systems)
sources.developer: WASP / ABB Corporate Research with AstraZeneca
sources.title: The First WARA Robotics Mobile Manipulation Challenge -- Lessons Learned (arXiv:2505.06919)
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulation for laboratory glassware transport and cleaning (including loading industrial dishwashers) was still posed as an unsolved academic challenge, with lessons-learned and design improvements needed for a second iteration.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine physical lab upkeep (cleaning and handling labware) in a working laboratory. It bounds the state of the art for robot upkeep work in labs — still a research challenge in 2024-2025, well short of servicing benchtop instruments.

sources.title: AI-powered robots can now autonomously repair other bots (New Atlas)
sources.claim: Bimanual manipulator demonstration in a fixed workcell autonomously replacing a gripper/finger on another robot — a single trained part-swap, not diagnosis or general repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical part replacement by a robot. It is the nearest 'repair' demonstration, but covers one known modular swap in a fixtured workcell with a task-specific learned policy, with no fault diagnosis, housing disassembly or post-repair verification.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Undergraduate teaching-lab section in geology/oceanography/meteorology: 20-30 students at benches with rock, mineral and fossil samples, microscopes, maps, streamtables and dilute acid; the instructor circulates for 2-3 hours, checks each group's work, physically demonstrates techniques (hand-lens use, strike/dip on a sample, scope alignment), corrects procedural errors, enforces PPE and hazard rules, handles spills or misused equipment, and signs off on completed exercises.

Supervising undergraduate/graduate researchers in a research laboratory (sediment core lab, geochem wet lab, clean lab, mass spectrometer or thin-section prep room): training new students on instruments hands-on, intermittently checking protocol adherence and sample handling, troubleshooting failed runs at the bench, enforcing chemical/laser/cryogen safety, and reviewing intermediate data quality.

Leading and supervising a day-long or multi-day field trip in open terrain: driving/accompanying students to roadcuts, quarries, stream reaches or soil pits; demonstrating hammering, sampling, compass-clinometer and GPS use at the outcrop; monitoring a dispersed group for traffic, cliff, heat, weather and wildlife hazards; doing headcounts and first aid; checking field notebooks and sample labels on site.

Supervising marine/coastal field work from an institutional small research vessel: overseeing student deployment and recovery of CTD, plankton nets, grabs or gravity cores over the side; managing deck safety (winch, wire, lifejackets, footing in swell), instructing on sample splitting and logging, and adapting the plan to weather and vessel schedule.

Supervising a computer/instrument lab session: students at workstations doing synoptic map analysis, GIS/remote-sensing exercises or model runs, plus a short outdoor component such as launching a radiosonde or reading a campus weather station; instructor circulates, checks screens and outputs, fixes instrument and software problems, and answers questions.

sources.system: Spot (with Spot Arm and Orbit software)
sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs autonomous Autowalk inspection missions in industrial facilities (thermal monitoring, gauge reading, acoustic leak detection), with over 1,000 units deployed in 35+ countries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility patrol and equipment inspection. Transfer to supervising students fails: Spot reads gauges and flags asset anomalies on fixed routes; it does not evaluate a person's technique, demonstrate a manual procedure, intervene in a human safety incident, or accept responsibility for a class.

sources.system: 6-axis-arm-equipped quadruped robot with multi-modal/Vision Foundation Model monitoring
sources.title: Autonomous Monitoring of Pharmaceutical R&D Laboratories with 6 Axis Arm Equipped Quadruped Robot and Generative AI: A Preliminary Study
sources.claim: A quadruped robot with a 6-axis arm plus generative-AI vision was used in a proof-of-concept for autonomous monitoring of a pharmaceutical R&D laboratory, detecting anomalies and generating reports; the authors describe it as preliminary with acknowledged limitations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous laboratory monitoring for compliance/housekeeping anomalies. It is the closest analogue to lab supervision, but it monitors the room, not people's experimental technique, and is an explicitly preliminary proof of concept, so it cannot substitute for an instructor supervising a student lab section.

sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom
sources.claim: The social robot Pepper linked to an LLM was trialled in a high-school classroom to deliver new learning content to student groups and answer questions; the study reports technical testing and student acceptance rather than autonomous responsibility for a class.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot teaching assistant delivering instruction. Transfer fails for supervising lab/field work: Pepper is stationary-to-slow indoors, cannot manipulate lab apparatus, cannot inspect a student's sample or bench, and the trial involved researcher setup and oversight rather than unsupervised class responsibility.

sources.title: The Museum Tour-Guide Robot RHINO
sources.claim: The autonomous mobile robot RHINO guided hundreds of visitors through a museum exhibition over a six-day deployment, showing autonomous navigation and group guiding inside an institution-controlled building.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously leading groups of people through a building. It shows navigation and narration among people, but supervising field or lab work additionally requires hazard judgment, hands-on demonstration, correction of student technique, and legal duty of care, none of which RHINO or its successors perform.

instances.label: Procurement cycle for a research purchase in a university department: specifying an instrument or supplies, comparing vendors and getting quotes, entering a requisition in the campus purchasing system against a grant account, tracking the order, then receiving the delivery in the lab/office, opening cartons, checking contents against the packing list and invoice, and shelving or logging the item in the departmental inventory.

Routine upkeep and calibration of bench instruments in a campus research lab (e.g., mass spectrometer, ICP-OES, gas chromatograph, water-quality sonde, analytical balance): cleaning cells/probes, replacing consumables (columns, filters, membranes, electrolyte, gas cylinders, pump oil), running standards and blanks, adjusting and verifying calibration, and logging results in the maintenance record.

Diagnosing and fixing a malfunctioning research instrument: interpreting error behavior, opening panels, testing subassemblies, sourcing and swapping a failed part (pump, lamp, valve, cable, board), reassembling, re-aligning and verifying performance against standards - or deciding to escalate to a vendor service engineer and supervising the repair.

Full service visit to a field-deployed monitoring installation (weather station, stream gauge, seismic vault, flux tower, soil/snow sensor array) reached by truck, boat or on foot: inspecting the mast and enclosure, clearing vegetation/ice/dust, cleaning radiation shields and solar panels, testing and replacing a degraded sensor, re-leveling and re-orienting, checking wiring and telemetry, and verifying good data before leaving.

Standardized consumable service of a docked or easily presented field unit: swapping the battery pack, exchanging a data card or payload/sensor module, and reseating the unit so monitoring resumes - a repeatable exchange on an identical, purpose-designed instrument.

Preparing and maintaining marine/field research gear on a research vessel deck, dock or gear locker: rinsing CTD rosettes, Niskin bottles and corers with freshwater, replacing O-rings, anodes and shackles, charging and testing battery packs, pressure-testing housings, spooling and greasing winch wire, and bench-testing sensors before a cruise or deployment.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A KUKA mobile manipulator autonomously operated existing analytical instruments in a largely unmodified university chemistry lab for eight days (688 experiments); it ran instruments, while humans built, stocked and serviced the stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of laboratory instruments in a university research lab. It shows what mobile lab robots can do (load samples, open instrument doors, trigger measurements) but not instrument upkeep - cleaning, consumable replacement, calibration adjustment or repair, which remained human work.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry
sources.title: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry | Nature
sources.claim: Two cooperating KUKA mobile robots autonomously navigated a working chemistry laboratory and used instruments (UPLC-MS, photoreactor, NMR) for exploratory synthesis campaigns.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrument operation and sample transport in a human-scale research lab. Demonstrates navigation and instrument actuation, but the reported work is running experiments, not servicing, calibrating or repairing the instruments themselves.

sources.title: ANYbotics ANYmal robot is addressing key challenges in Industrial Robotics | RoboticsTomorrow
sources.claim: Legged inspection robots are commercially deployed and run autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, but the vendor states that manipulation for maintenance and repair is a future goal rather than current deployed capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous equipment inspection in structured industrial plants, an E2 setting comparable to a campus facility. It bounds the state of the art: deployed robots inspect equipment, while hands-on maintenance manipulation is still aspirational.

sources.system: Optimus automated drone system with robotic airbase
sources.title: Airobotics Unveils Completely Automated Drone Platform - sUAS News
sources.claim: An automated drone base station uses a robotic arm to exchange the aircraft's batteries and payload modules without human intervention, keeping a field-deployed sensing platform in service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended consumable/module service of a field sensing instrument. The exchanged items (battery packs, payload/sensor modules on a standardized docked unit) and the required precision match the routine swap service on a purpose-designed monitoring instrument presented in a purpose-built fixture.

sources.title: Miner South32 to trial autonomous drones | CIO
sources.claim: The robotic base station swaps drone batteries and payloads without human intervention at a mining company's site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended battery/module exchange on a field instrument at an industrial site, corroborating that the swap runs autonomously in a real deployment rather than only in a demonstration.

sources.system: Emerald Cloud Lab / CMU Cloud Lab
sources.developer: Emerald Cloud Lab, Carnegie Mellon University
sources.title: Carnegie Mellon to Open First-Ever Academic Cloud Lab | Tradeline
sources.claim: In the most automated research laboratories (cloud labs), robots execute experiments across roughly 200 instrument models, but the instruments themselves are kept running by trained human technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic operation of an entire research instrument park. It is the closest analogue to a professor's lab run by machines, and shows that equipment upkeep, calibration and repair remain with human technicians.

sources.developer: academic research group, Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing | ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A vision-guided UR10e robot cell autonomously unscrews fasteners during electronic device disassembly in a laboratory setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening a fixtured device by removing screws, a sub-step of instrument repair. It covers only unscrewing of presented devices in a purpose-built cell, not fault diagnosis, part replacement, reassembly or performance verification.

tasks.label: Establish, teach, and monitor students' compliance with safety rules for handling chemicals, equipment, and other hazardous materials.

instances.label: First-week/pre-lab safety instruction for a large general chemistry course: presenting the lab safety rules, PPE requirements, emergency procedures (eyewash, shower, fire extinguisher locations), and administering a safety quiz or signed safety contract before students may enter the teaching lab.

General chemistry teaching laboratory session (20-24 students at benches): circulating during the period, watching for goggle/glove violations, improper reagent transfer, unlabeled containers, food/drink, and issuing verbal corrections or written infractions; recording compliance and sanctioning repeat offenders.

Organic/analytical teaching lab with higher-hazard work: briefing on flammable solvents, corrosives, and waste segregation, showing correct fume-hood sash and glassware handling at the front of the ..., then monitoring students' technique and enforcing hood use and waste rules during the period.

Research-group setting: establishing written SOPs and hazard assessments for a new reagent or procedure, training incoming undergraduate/graduate researchers one-on-one, documenting training records, and spot-checking group members' compliance during unsupervised bench work.

Departmental/institutional level: drafting or revising the chemical hygiene plan and course safety policies, coordinating with EHS on inspections and citations, and following up with students and TAs on identified deficiencies.

Analytical/instrumental or physical chemistry lab: small student groups operate shared instruments (UV-Vis, GC-MS, FTIR, NMR, calorimeters); instructor supervises scheduling and correct instrument use, verifies calibration, interprets anomalous readings with students, and enforces instrument-room protocols.

Oversight at a distance within the course: briefing and monitoring graduate teaching assistants who run parallel lab sections, reviewing lab notebooks and reports, handling safety incident documentation, and adjusting protocols between sections.

instances.label: Bench synthetic chemistry project at a research university: the professor frames a novel target/hypothesis, then runs or directly supervises multistep synthesis at the bench (glassware, inert atmosphere, workup, column chromatography), characterizes products by NMR/MS/XRD, troubleshoots failures, interprets results, and writes and revises a journal manuscript through peer review.

Analytical/measurement-driven project: real or field-collected samples (environmental, biological, materials) prepared and run on departmental core-facility instruments (LC-MS, GC-MS, ICP-MS, NMR), with method development and validation, statistical analysis, and write-up for a professional journal.

Physical/materials chemistry project requiring the professor to build, align and debug custom apparatus (laser/spectroscopy tables, vacuum and gas-handling lines, electrochemical or photoelectrochemical cells), collect data over months, and publish.
Computational/theoretical chemistry project: DFT, MD or ML modeling on a workstation/cluster, code writing, literature analysis, figure preparation, manuscript drafting and revision; no wet-lab work.

Closed-loop optimization or screening study in a well-defined parameter space (reaction-condition optimization, photocatalyst/formulation/materials screening) run on an automated synthesis-and-analysis platform in the group's lab, with the resulting optimized conditions and data written up as findings.

Research at a primarily undergraduate institution or chemistry-education research: modest bench projects with undergraduates using standard teaching-lab equipment and shared instruments, or classroom/survey data collection, analyzed and published in venues such as J. Chem. Educ.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / UC Berkeley (Ceder group) with Google DeepMind
sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials | Nature
sources.claim: A-Lab is an autonomous robotic solid-state synthesis laboratory at LBNL that planned, executed and interpreted syntheses of inorganic powders over 17 days of continuous robotic operation inside a purpose-built enclosed cell (powder dispensing station, robotic arms, furnaces, automated XRD).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inorganic materials synthesis campaigns. It transfers to a chemistry professor's experimental campaign because the objects (powders, crucibles, diffraction data), the closed-loop decision-making and the laboratory setting are the same class of work; target selection and manuscript writing remained human.

sources.developer: R. Palgrave (UCL) and L. Schoop (Princeton), reported by Chemistry World
sources.title: New analysis raises doubts over autonomous lab's materials discoveries | Chemistry World
sources.claim: Independent reanalysis found A-Lab's claimed new materials were not novel and that its automated XRD/Rietveld analysis contained systematic errors; Nature corrected the paper in 2026 and critics say concerns remain, indicating autonomous campaign output has not reached publication-grade reliability without human chemists.

sources.title: Autonomous chemical research with large language models - PubMed (Nature 624, 570)
sources.claim: Coscientist, a GPT-4-driven agent controlling a benchtop liquid handler and cloud-lab hardware, autonomously designed, planned and executed palladium-catalysed cross-coupling optimization experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous reaction optimization. Comparable reagents, microplate-scale liquid handling and analytical feedback to a professor's condition-screening study, so performance carries over to the closed-loop screening instance.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa based)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist (Nature 583, 237) - University of Liverpool Repository
sources.claim: A mobile robot chemist at the University of Liverpool autonomously ran a multi-day photocatalyst discovery campaign in a working university chemistry laboratory, performing hundreds of experiments in a ten-variable space and finding much more active photocatalyst mixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous closed-loop photocatalyst optimization in a university lab, using the same vials, solvents and instruments a chemistry professor's screening study uses, so it substantiates the screening instance in a human-work lab setting.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry
sources.title: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry | Nature
sources.claim: A follow-on Liverpool system used free-roaming mobile robots to operate a ... synthesis platform, a UPLC-MS and a benchtop NMR for exploratory synthetic chemistry, sharing standard laboratory equipment with human researchers rather than requiring a redesigned robotic cell.

sources.system: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry
sources.title: Autonomous mobile robots for exploratory synthetic chemistry | Nature
sources.claim: The same Liverpool study reports that an unexpected product was misassigned by the automated workflow, which the authors present as showing the limits of autonomous decision-making on edge cases; human chemists interpreted and corrected the result.

sources.title: Autonomous synthesis robot uses AI to speed up chemical discovery - HIMS, University of Amsterdam
sources.claim: RoboChem is a benchtop autonomous flow-photochemistry platform with a robotic needle sampler and inline benchtop NMR that self-optimizes and scales up photocatalytic reactions continuously; the developers note that every molecule reported in the resulting Science paper was isolated and checked manually by human chemists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous optimization of photochemical transformations. Same reagent handling, reaction scale and NMR analysis as a professor's methodology-optimization study, supporting the closed-loop screening instance.

sources.title: Verification and execution of the scientific literature via chemputation augmented by large language models | Communications Chemistry
sources.claim: An LLM-augmented chemputation workflow translates published synthetic procedures into robot code and executes them on Chemputer robotic synthesis platforms to verify literature syntheses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic execution of literature synthesis procedures. It shows purpose-built platforms can run already-specified multistep syntheses, but not novel exploratory bench work with unanticipated intermediates.

sources.title: GitHub - SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-v2
sources.claim: The AI Scientist-v2 is a software-only agent (no physical embodiment) whose autonomously written manuscript was accepted at an ICLR 2025 workshop; it demonstrates autonomous authoring in machine learning, not laboratory chemistry, and is not a robotic system.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as context for the non-physical write-up half of the task; being software-only it cannot substantiate any physical instance.

tasks.label: Select, order, and maintain materials and supplies for teaching and research, such as textbooks, chemicals, and laboratory equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Desk-based selection and ordering: reviewing textbook editions/publisher options and adopting a text for a course; building chemical and consumable orders from vendor catalogs (Sigma-Aldrich, Fisher), checking SDS/hazard restrictions and prices, entering requisitions in the university e-procurement system, tracking grant/departmental budgets and chasing back-ordered items. Performed in a faculty office at a computer.

Receiving and putting away deliveries in the teaching-lab stockroom: opening cartons of reagent bottles, solvents, glassware and consumables, checking contents against packing slips, wiping/labeling and barcoding containers, shelving them in the correct cabinet by hazard class (flammables cabinet, acid cabinet, ventilated storage), and entering them into the chemical inventory database. Cluttered institution-controlled stockroom with mixed glass containers.

Periodic chemical inventory and stock maintenance: walking cabinets, shelves and fume hoods with a scanner or list, reading and reconciling bottle labels, checking quantities remaining, checking expiry and peroxide-former dates, flagging low stock for reorder, relabeling degraded labels, segregating incompatibles, and pulling expired or unwanted containers for EHS waste pickup.

Preparing and restocking materials for undergraduate teaching labs: weighing out solids and making up bulk reagent/titrant solutions from stock chemicals, filling and labeling bench dispensing bottles, standardizing solutions, assembling per-bench kits of glassware and small equipment, replacing broken or missing items, and washing/putting away glassware after the session. Occurs in a departmental prep room and teaching lab.

Maintaining teaching and research instruments and equipment: calibrating balances and pH meters, cleaning and servicing rotovaps, vacuum pumps and hot plates, changing GC septa/liners and HPLC columns/solvent reservoirs, swapping gas cylinders and regulator fittings, diagnosing simple faults, and arranging vendor service for what cannot be fixed in-house. Occurs in a research or instrument lab.

sources.system: BD Rowa Vmax / BD Rowa EasyLoad automated pharmacy stockroom
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page, in commercial deployment for years)
sources.title: BD Rowa - store & pick medications automatically
sources.claim: BD Rowa Vmax automated stockroom systems store and pick medication packs in pharmacies, with the EasyLoad option performing fully automatic input including expiry-date detection and overnight stock inputting, maintaining the stock record.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving, putting away and inventory-maintaining small boxed/bottled consumables in a controlled stockroom. Objects (palm-sized packs/bottles), the precision required to shelve them in defined locations, and the requirement to keep an accurate, expiry-aware stock database match the chemistry stockroom put-away and inventory instances, in a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: BD Rowa EasyLoad — Fully automatic input
sources.claim: The EasyLoad input unit separates, measures, scans and inputs incoming packs into the automated store without an operator handling each item.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: automated intake, identification and shelving of incoming inventory is the machine analogue of unpacking a delivery, verifying it and stocking it while updating records.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan Stow robot, using force sensing, autonomously stows individual items of varied shape into cluttered fabric pod bins in operating fulfillment centers in Spokane and Hamburg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: put-away of individual heterogeneous items into designated storage locations with contact-rich handling, the manipulation core of stocking a stockroom shelf, performed in a purpose-built robotic storage aisle.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking arm handles items of many shapes, sizes and packaging and is live in multiple Staples fulfillment centers, and is being deployed for online pharmacy Apotea's logistics center.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking assorted small articles from presented bins into order/kit containers — the same operation as assembling per-bench kits of small lab items when the parts are presented to a fenced picking cell.

sources.system: Chemspeed SWING RP (gravimetric solid/liquid dispensing platform)
sources.title: Automated Gravimetric Solid & Liquid Reaction Preparation
sources.claim: Chemspeed's SWING RP platform automatically dispenses powders, solids and liquids gravimetrically into vials, plates or reactors under program control, a commercial laboratory workstation for reaction and solution preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: weighing out solids and dispensing liquids to make up reagent solutions — identical chemistry, comparable or tighter mass/volume precision than teaching-lab reagent prep, inside an enclosed purpose-built workstation.

sources.title: BioProcess™ inline conditioning system | Cytiva
sources.claim: Cytiva's BioProcess inline conditioning system automatically produces buffers on demand at process volume by diluting concentrated stock solutions of salt, ... with water, under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making up litre-scale aqueous reagent solutions to specification from concentrates, with automated verification (conductivity/pH), matching the bulk solution-making part of teaching-lab prep in a purpose-built skid.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A KUKA-based mobile robotic chemist operated autonomously for eight days in a wet chemistry laboratory, running 688 experiments and operating analytical instruments and a solid-dispensing station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of vials, solids and solvents and movement between fixed lab stations, showing chemical-container manipulation is feasible when station positions and holders are engineered for the robot.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously scans store shelves and reports product availability, pricing and placement, and is deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: walking a facility to audit stock on shelves. It shows autonomous inventory data capture in a human-built facility, but Tally has no manipulator, so it cannot open cabinets, handle bottles, or remove expired chemicals.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in more than 25 ... and has completed over one million intra-facility deliveries, including 300,000 pharmacy deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport of supplies inside a structured human facility. It substantiates fetch-and-deliver logistics at E2 but not unpacking, shelving by hazard class, or reagent preparation.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid has moved more than 100,000 ... a GXO Logistics facility, picking totes on and off mobile robots and loading conveyors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk container handling in a human-standard facility. Shows E2-level tote logistics only; the objects are uniform totes, not fragile labelled reagent bottles needing hazard-class placement.

tasks.label: Clean laboratory facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-session reset of a teaching lab (gen chem/organic): clearing leftover beakers, flasks, burettes, spatulas and reagent bottles from student benches to the sink/rack, wiping benchtops with water/ethanol, removing residues and spills, resetting each station for the next section.

Washing labware: scrubbing/rinsing glassware at the sink or loading a lab glassware washer, acetone/DI rinses, checking for film or residue, drying in a rack or oven and returning items to shelves and drawers.

Cleaning shared equipment and fixtures: wiping out fume hood interiors and sashes, sinks, balance pans, rotovap/hotplate surfaces, polishing electrodes, cleaning cuvettes/NMR tubes and instrument parts between users in a research or instrument room.
Routine floor housekeeping in the lab, prep room and adjoining corridor: sweeping/vacuuming debris and mopping or scrubbing hard floors after classes, keeping traffic aisles clear.

Hazardous-materials housekeeping: consolidating, capping and labeling solvent/aqueous waste carboys and moving them to the satellite accumulation area, emptying sharps and broken-glass boxes and trash, decontaminating small chemical spills and contaminated surfaces per the chemical hygiene plan.

sources.title: Avidbots: Neo 2W - Material Handling 24/7
sources.claim: Neo 2 autonomous floor-scrubbing robot is commercially deployed for hard-floor cleaning in institutional facilities including universities, airports and hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cleaning facility floors) in an institution-controlled building; lab and corridor hard floors match the surfaces Neo scrubs.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots' autonomous scrubbers operate in schools, hospitals and other people-occupied facilities worldwide.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot cleans fixtures and floors and picks up trash in commercial buildings during normal operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine surface/fixture cleaning inside an institution-controlled building, showing autonomous wet cleaning of standardized fixtures; restroom fixtures are far simpler than lab benches holding glassware and chemical residue.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business
sources.claim: The Somatic restroom robot runs autonomously day to day after a human-assisted mapping/VR setup phase.

sources.title: ORGANA: A robotic assistant for automated chemistry experimentation and characterization (Matter)
sources.claim: ORGANA, a benchtop robotic chemistry assistant, autonomously performs a physical cleaning/preparation operation (mechanical polishing of electrodes) as part of chemistry experiments in a purpose-built bench cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning/polishing laboratory equipment surfaces (electrodes) to an acceptable analytical standard — the same class of residue-removal work as cleaning instrument parts in a chemistry lab.

sources.title: Robot automates dishwashing in commercial kitchens
sources.claim: Dishcraft's robotic dishwashing machine picks, scrubs, vision-inspects and racks dishes that humans pre-load into carts, achieving an inspected cleanliness standard inside an enclosed purpose-built machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing rigid vessels to an inspected cleanliness standard with automated scrub-and-recheck; transfers to washing racked labware when dirty items are presented to the machine as a purpose-built setting would present them.

sources.system: Chemspeed FLEX robotic platform tool library (active cleaning station)
sources.title: Extensive Robotic Tool Library | Chemspeed Automation
sources.claim: Chemspeed's commercial robotic lab platforms include an automated active cleaning station for cleaning instrument parts with aqueous and solvent-based media inside the robotic deck.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated solvent/aqueous cleaning of laboratory hardware between runs, the same residue-removal output as cleaning instrument components, with parts presented to the station by the platform's gantry.

sources.system: XtalPi Intelligent Automation workstations with ABB GoFa cobots
sources.title: ABB Robotics partners with XtalPi to build intelligent automated laboratories
sources.claim: XtalPi built automated laboratory workstations around 100+ ABB GoFa cobots that handle labware for preparation, dilution, filtration, reaction and UPLC steps in an enclosed automated lab facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of flasks, vials and labware inside a purpose-built lab cell — the clearing/racking half of bench cleanup, when labware is presented in fixtured racks.

sources.title: Alphabet's X has 'Everyday Robots' test fleet that autonomously performs office maintenance tasks
sources.claim: A fleet of over 100 ... prototypes autonomously wiped tables and sorted trash in Google's office buildings; the program was discontinued in 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous wiping of horizontal work surfaces in an institution-controlled building; shows squeegee wiping of clear cafeteria tables, not clearing chemical glassware or removing chemical residue.

sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 mobile manipulator autonomously tidies and wipes in previously unseen homes, but the developers state it frequently makes mistakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general tidying/wiping of cluttered surfaces; cited to show that current open-world cleanup manipulation remains a research demo below worker reliability.

sources.title: Self-driving labs are changing how chemists work
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 self-driving chemistry systems remain bench-fixed; a mobile robot that walks around a lab picking up glassware and cleaning up is described as a future goal.
sources.transferJustification: Negative/limiting evidence on in-situ lab cleanup by mobile robots.

tasks.label: Supervise students' laboratory and field work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly undergraduate teaching-lab section (intro environmental science/ecology/soils): ~20-24 students at benches running water-chemistry titrations, spectrophotometry, soil texture/pH, microscopy. Instructor circulates for 2-3 hours, watches each group's technique, corrects mis-set glassware and mis-calibrated probes, answers questions, enforces goggles/gloves/fume-hood use, troubleshoots balky instruments, and signs off on data before students leave.

Day field lab at a local stream, wetland, forest plot or campus natural area: instructor leads students over uneven, muddy or brushy terrain in variable weather, oversees water sampling, quadrat/transect surveys, use of sondes, GPS, corers and nets; corrects sampling technique on the spot, keeps track of scattered small groups, judges hazards (deep water, ticks, weather, traffic) and intervenes for safety.

Supervising individual or small-group undergraduate research/capstone work in a departmental research lab: training students on GC/ICP-MS/spectrophotometer or digestion and filtration protocols, intermittent check-ins over weeks, watching a step performed, spotting contamination or protocol drift, verifying QA/QC and data quality, authorizing chemical and waste handling.

Overseeing graduate students' or field-crew independent research campaigns: site visits to remote or multi-day field locations, checking deployment of loggers, sondes, plots or traps, reviewing methods in situ, correcting installation errors, ensuring permits and field-safety protocols are followed while the students do the physical work.

Lab safety and compliance oversight around a teaching session: pre-lab briefing and hazard walkthrough, checking PPE and hood sashes, supervising chemical dispensing and hazardous-waste segregation, and responding hands-on to incidents (spill, broken glass, burner or chemical exposure, equipment shutdown) during student work.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa-based autonomous lab robot)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: The closest robotic systems to a laboratory supervisor are autonomous laboratory robots that perform the experimental work themselves; the Liverpool mobile robotic chemist ran experiments autonomously for eight days in a chemistry lab, but it executes protocols rather than observing, correcting or assessing human students' technique.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the nearest related capability (autonomous work inside a chemistry lab). It does not transfer: the robot performs its own experiments in a lab configured for it, and there is no evidence it monitors human students, judges their technique, enforces PPE, or intervenes in student errors, which is what supervision requires.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid 'Sally' with Optio AI teaching assistant
sources.title: Salamanca City Central School District in New York to deploy humanoid robot teacher this fall
sources.claim: The most advanced classroom robot deployments are conversational humanoid teaching assistants that talk with students; a Realbotix humanoid ('Sally') is being piloted with an AI teaching-assistant program in a New York school ..., with no reported ability to oversee hands-on laboratory or field procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the nearest related capability (an embodied system in an instructional role). It does not transfer: the system is a conversational, essentially stationary avatar for K-12 tutoring support; nothing indicates it monitors students' physical laboratory technique, manipulates lab equipment, or intervenes in safety incidents.

sources.system: YOLOv5-based real-time smart lab-safety monitoring system
sources.title: Development of YOLOv5-Based Real-Time Smart Monitoring System for Increasing Lab Safety Awareness in Educational Institutions
sources.claim: Laboratory PPE-compliance and unsafe-behavior monitoring in educational institutions has been demonstrated only as fixed-camera computer-vision software (e.g., YOLO-based smart lab monitoring), not as an embodied robotic supervisor that can intervene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is one narrow slice of supervision (PPE checking). It cannot substantiate the instance: it is software on fixed cameras, not a physically embodied system, and it covers none of the technique correction, equipment troubleshooting, hands-on intervention, or sign-off that supervision requires.

instances.label: Theoretical/computational physics research: a faculty member formulates a research question, derives analytic results or writes and runs simulations on a departmental or national HPC cluster, analyzes output, and drafts, submits and revises a journal manuscript. Work occurs at a desk/office in a university building; the only physical acts are keyboard/terminal work.

Benchtop experimental research in the professor's own university lab (AMO/optics, condensed matter, biophysics): designing and building apparatus, mounting and aligning optics on a table, wiring and debugging electronics, cryostat or vacuum work, mounting samples, running measurement campaigns over weeks with frequent troubleshooting of unexpected faults, then analyzing data and writing the paper.

Research at a primarily-undergraduate or comprehensive institution: modest-budget projects run with student assistants using teaching-lab-grade apparatus (spectrometers, small telescopes, electronics benches, 3D-printed rigs) or physics-education-research data collection in classrooms; assembling and repairing the setup, collecting data, and publishing in AJP/PRPER or a regional journal.

Work at a shared user facility or in a large collaboration: writing a beam-time/observing proposal, preparing and mounting samples or detector hardware at a synchrotron, accelerator, cleanroom or observatory, taking operations shifts, reducing data, and producing a collaboration paper with internal review.

Scholarly production and dissemination: literature review, statistical/data analysis of existing datasets, figure preparation, writing review articles, book chapters or textbook sections, arXiv posting, responding to referees, and preparing electronic-media versions of findings; done at a desk.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A mobile robot (KUKA-based mobile robotic chemist, Liverpool) autonomously operated benchtop instruments in a human chemistry lab for 8 days, running 688 experiments in a human-defined 10-variable photocatalyst space; humans set the problem, interpreted the result and wrote the Nature paper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous experimental physical-science research campaign in a wet lab. It is the closest robotic analogue to running an experimental physics campaign (manipulating samples/instruments in a lab built for people), so it bounds what robots can do toward this task; it nonetheless covers only the execution sub-step of a human-defined optimization, not question formulation, apparatus development or publication.

sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of novel materials (Journal Article) | OSTI.GOV
sources.claim: The A-Lab is a purpose-built autonomous solid-state synthesis platform with robotic arms, furnaces and XRD that ran 17 days and produced 41 of 58 computationally predicted target compounds with ML-driven planning; the research targets, oversight and publication came from human scientists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous closed-loop materials synthesis and characterization, the sub-step of materials-physics research that most resembles a lab measurement campaign. It shows purpose-built (E1-style) robotic cells can execute synthesis/characterization loops, but not that they can carry a research project through to an accepted publication.

sources.developer: University College London (Palgrave et al.) / Chemistry World reporting
sources.title: New analysis raises doubts over autonomous lab's materials discoveries | Chemistry World
sources.claim: Independent analysis of A-Lab's outputs concluded the automated lab's claimed novel materials and its automated phase identification did not hold up, and the Nature paper was later corrected — evidence that current autonomous-lab output does not reach publication quality without expert human interpretation.
sources.transferJustification: Bears on the AT WORKER QUALITY criterion for any autonomous-lab-based judgment: the flagship autonomous discovery campaign's published findings were contested and corrected, so the robotic pipeline did not deliver output an employer would accept in place of a faculty researcher's.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University / Emerald Cloud Lab
sources.title: Autonomous Chemistry and Materials Innovation Driven by Scientific Agents | JACS Au
sources.claim: Coscientist, an LLM agent coupled to a liquid-handling robot and cloud lab, autonomously planned and executed known chemical reactions from high-level goals, demonstrating machine control of standard lab hardware but within tasks specified by human researchers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: agent-directed robotic execution of laboratory procedures. It shows an AI agent can drive standard lab automation, the nearest analogue to a physicist operating instruments, but the demonstrated scope is executing known procedures in an automation-ready cell, not conducting and publishing original research.

sources.title: The automation of science - Research Explorer The University of Manchester
sources.claim: Robot Scientist Adam, a purpose-built automated laboratory, autonomously generated and experimentally tested functional-genomics hypotheses, but its conclusions were verified by human manual experiments and reported by human authors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hypothesis generation plus robotic experimentation, the fullest existing robotic approximation of the research cycle. Even here the machine's findings required human confirmation and human authorship, and the domain (microbiology assays in a bespoke automated rig) does not transfer to building and running physics apparatus.

sources.system: Sample-efficient ML auto-alignment for experimental optics
sources.title: Automating Experimental Optics with Sample Efficient Machine Learning Methods (arXiv:2503.14260)
sources.claim: Machine-learning controllers can autonomously perform a physics-lab sub-step — mode-matching/alignment of a free-space optical resonator via motorized mounts — with minimal human supervision, but this is one step of apparatus setup, not a research project.
sources.transferJustification: Directly in the physics-lab domain: it substantiates automation of optical alignment, a component of experimental physics research, showing that only narrow sub-steps of apparatus preparation are automated, with humans still building, debugging and interpreting the experiment.

sources.title: [2504.08066] The AI Scientist-v2: Workshop-Level Automated Scientific Discovery via Agentic Tree Search
sources.claim: The AI Scientist-v2 is a software-only agentic system that generated a workshop paper accepted through peer review; it has no physical embodiment and therefore does not count as a robotic system, and the venue was a workshop rather than a professional journal.
sources.transferJustification: Included to document the state of automated research writing: it is software-only (machine-learning experiments run in code), so under the stated rules it cannot support a positive judgment for any instance, including the desk-based ones.

tasks.label: Maintain and repair laboratory equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between lab sections in an undergraduate teaching lab: professor walks ~20 heterogeneous student stations (carts and tracks, photogates, power supplies, meters, spectroscopes, ripple tanks), tests each setup, finds and fixes the faults — dead batteries, blown fuses/bulbs, broken banana leads to re-solder, loose clamps and mounts, a dead supply to swap out — then cleans and stows the gear. Mixed-vintage apparatus, cluttered benches, no two faults alike.

A bench instrument in a teaching or research lab quits (function generator, oscilloscope, lock-in amplifier, HV supply, pulse counter). Professor opens the case with hand tools, reads the schematic, probes with a multimeter/scope to localize the fault, desolders and replaces a fuse, capacitor, connector or IC, reassembles, and verifies against a known signal before returning it to service.

Optical bench / laser setup upkeep in a research or advanced lab: an interferometer, spectrometer, or beam path has drifted or been disturbed; professor cleans and repositions mirrors, lenses and beamsplitters on the table, swaps a failed optic or detector, and walks the beam back into alignment until fringe visibility or signal level meets spec.

Vacuum and cryogenic system maintenance: change roughing-pump oil, replace worn O-rings and flange seals on a chamber, helium leak-check and re-torque fittings, service or replace a turbo pump, refill an LN2 dewar or service a cryocooler cold head, then pump down and verify base pressure/temperature.

Detector, sensor and data-acquisition troubleshooting: a computer-interfaced probe or DAQ chain reads wrong or not at all; professor reseats and continuity-tests cables, replaces a broken connector or sensor head, checks grounding/shielding, re-runs the interface calibration against a reference standard, and confirms readings before class.

Departmental machine/electronics shop: fabricate or repair a mechanical part needed to restore an apparatus — measure the broken bracket, mount or fixture, cut/drill/tap/mill a replacement from stock, deburr, then fit and adjust it on the apparatus so the experiment works again.

sources.system: AI-Driven Robotics for Optics platform (MIT, Soljacic group)
sources.title: AI-Driven Robotics for Optics (arXiv:2505.17985)
sources.claim: An AI-driven robotic platform (7-DoF xArm7 with stereo cameras and LiDAR) autonomously assembles free-space optical setups from off-the-shelf optics and performs micrometer-scale fine alignment, including interferometers, in a standard optics laboratory equipped with custom 3D-printed magnetic bases and ArUco-marked component housings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous assembly and fine alignment of optical setups rather than 'maintenance'. Transfer holds for the optics-upkeep instance because the objects (mirrors, lenses, beamsplitters, detectors on an optical table), the micrometer precision, and the lab setting are the same as when a professor repositions and realigns disturbed optics; the platform's own workspace, however, requires robot-specific magnetic bases and fiducial-marked housings.

sources.developer: Russian Quantum Center / Oxford (Sorokin, Ulanov, Sazhina, Lvovsky)
sources.title: Interferobot: aligning an optical interferometer by a reinforcement learning agent (arXiv:2006.02252)
sources.claim: A reinforcement-learning agent (Interferobot) trained in simulation transferred to a real Mach-Zehnder interferometer with motorized mirror mounts and aligned it autonomously from camera images of the fringe pattern, matching human-expert performance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: initial alignment of an interferometer rather than repair. It transfers to the optics-maintenance instance because restoring a drifted or disturbed interferometer to spec is the same physical act on the same hardware, judged by the same acceptance criterion (fringe visibility).

sources.title: The slow rise of robots in the data center - DCD
sources.claim: Alibaba Cloud's second-generation Tianxun data-centre robot autonomously locates and replaces failed hard disks in server racks without human intervention, in operating data halls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: swapping a failed, standardized hot-swap module whose fault is reported by software telemetry, in racks engineered for machine access. It does not transfer to diagnosing and repairing heterogeneous bench instruments or apparatus, which requires case disassembly, schematic-based probing and component-level rework; cited to bound, not support, that instance.

sources.developer: University of Coimbra (Pedro Neto et al.)
sources.title: An in-Contact Robotic System for the Process of Desoldering PCB Components (arXiv:2403.05309)
sources.claim: A robotic system with a purpose-built force-controlled tool desolders and extracts components from printed circuit boards for e-waste recycling, achieving near-100% removal success on larger components; the work covers removal only, not fault diagnosis or replacement soldering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic component removal in recycling. It covers only one sub-step of instrument repair (extraction of a known component from a fixtured board) and provides no fault localisation, replacement soldering or functional verification, so it cannot substantiate completion of the repair instance.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa based)
sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A free-roaming autonomous mobile robot operated in a working human chemistry laboratory for eight days, navigating between fixed instrument stations and performing thousands of pre-defined sample manipulations; its repertoire is experiment execution, not servicing or repairing the instruments it uses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation inside an ordinary (E2) academic laboratory. It shows navigation and instrument operation at stations pre-registered by touch, but no diagnosis, disassembly, tool use on faulty hardware, or repair, so it does not transfer to maintaining or repairing lab equipment.
