tasks.label: Conduct research in a particular field of knowledge and present findings in professional journals, books, electronic media, or at professional conferences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Archaeological field research project: the professor directs survey and excavation at an outdoor site (varying terrain, weather, unknown stratigraphy, fragile in-situ finds), records contexts and samples, then analyzes the material and publishes results in a peer-reviewed journal.

Laboratory/collections-based research: analysis of lithics, ceramics, faunal or human skeletal remains, or preparation of isotope/aDNA samples in a university lab or museum collections room, followed by interpretation, drafting and submission of an article.

Ethnographic or linguistic field research: months of participant observation, interviewing and note-taking in a community, town or workplace setting the researcher does not control, followed by writing a monograph or journal article.

Desk and computational research in a campus office: reanalysis of existing datasets, GIS/remote-sensing data, archival documents and published literature; statistical or comparative analysis; drafting, revising and submitting a peer-reviewed article or book chapter.

Dissemination of completed findings: preparing and delivering a conference paper at a professional meeting, a public lecture, or electronic media (podcast, blog, data repository release), including responding to questions and reviewer/audience critique.

sources.developer: Kyriakoulia et al., University of Peloponnese / ICCS (survey of many systems)
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology (Sensors 2025)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed survey documents that robotics in archaeology consists of UAV/AUV/ROV sensing and 3D-documentation platforms used as instruments by archaeologists, not systems that independently conduct and report research.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic data capture at archaeological sites. It does not transfer to the whole task: the platforms are sensing/documentation tools operated by archaeologists, and the survey describes mixed 'autonomous and semi-autonomous' operation with human interpretation and authorship of findings.

sources.developer: Stanford Robotics Lab (Oussama Khatib) with KAUST and DRASSM
sources.title: Stanford Robotics Lab — Ocean One
sources.claim: The most capable humanoid robot used on an archaeological excavation recovered an artifact from a shipwreck under human piloting with haptic feedback, i.e. teleoperation rather than autonomous research.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = physical recovery of an archaeological artifact in the field. It cannot support a positive judgment because operation is by a human pilot, and the robot performed only a manipulation sub-step, not project design, analysis or publication.

sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials (Nature)
sources.claim: Autonomous closed-loop laboratory robots exist for materials chemistry in purpose-built labs, but they operate on standardized powder synthesis in a fixtured cell, and their human authors framed, interpreted and published the results (which were later contested).
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous experimental research in a purpose-built lab. Transfer fails: objects are standardized reagent powders rather than unique fragile artifacts or skeletal remains, the domain reasoning is computational materials screening, and human researchers authored and defended the findings.

sources.title: Automating Science: Philosophical and Social Dimensions (Cambridge repository)
sources.claim: The Robot Scientist Adam autonomously generated and experimentally tested hypotheses in yeast functional genomics inside a dedicated automated laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous hypothesis generation and experimentation. Transfer fails: it operates in a narrow, formally modelled biological domain inside a purpose-built microplate-handling cell; it does not conduct anthropological or archaeological inquiry, nor author and present scholarly findings.

tasks.label: Supervise students' laboratory or field work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Undergraduate teaching-lab session on campus (osteology, lithics, ceramics, or artifact identification): the professor circulates among benches while students work through a lab exercise, checks their identifications and measurements, answers questions, corrects reasoning, enforces specimen-handling protocols, and signs off on completed lab sheets. Purpose is served by observing and giving verbal/written guidance and evaluation.

Archaeological field school at an excavation site: the professor oversees several student-staffed units, inspects stratigraphy and unit walls, critiques trowel/screening technique, reviews level forms, feature drawings, and photo logs, decides when to change contexts, and monitors safety. Physical acts (scraping a profile, holding an artifact) are illustrative; the deliverable is direction, correction, and approval of student work.

Supervising individual undergraduate honors or graduate students doing independent lab research (sample preparation, cataloging, curation, data recording): periodic one-on-one check-ins, protocol review, reviewing bench notebooks and datasets, and approving next steps.

Supervising off-campus ethnographic or survey fieldwork (interviews, participant observation, pedestrian survey, mapping): scheduled site visits and remote check-ins, review of field notes and IRB/permit compliance, troubleshooting access and methods problems, and evaluating collected data.

Overseeing student work in a specialized instrument lab (stable isotope, ancient DNA, geoarchaeology, microscopy): verifying training and safety compliance, watching students run a procedure, catching protocol deviations, and authorizing use of instruments and reagents.

tasks.label: Conduct ethnographic field research.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Extended participant observation at a community field site (rural village, Indigenous community, or small town, often abroad): the professor lives in or near the community for weeks to months, joins daily activities (meals, farming, fishing, household work), builds rapport in the local language, and writes analytic field notes and a fieldwork journal each day. Conditions vary daily; no institution controls the setting.

Urban/domestic ethnography in a US city or region: repeated visits to neighborhoods, homes, shops, clinics waiting rooms, churches, or street corners; hanging out with interlocutors, informal conversation, walking-along observation, jotting notes discreetly and expanding them later; negotiating consent and access with strangers in uncontrolled public and private space.

Institutional ethnography: sustained observation inside an organization that controls its premises (hospital ward, school, laboratory, factory, museum, courthouse, corporate office) under a negotiated access agreement; shadowing staff, observing meetings and routines, taking notes, occasionally recording, working around institutional rules and privacy constraints.

Semi-structured, life-history and key-informant interviews conducted in interlocutors' homes, cafes, or offices: obtaining informed consent, setting up an audio recorder, adapting questions in real time to what the interlocutor says, reading emotional cues, taking contextual notes on the domestic setting, and later transcribing.

Event-based fieldwork: attending and documenting rituals, festivals, markets, political rallies, protests or migration crossings; moving with crowds, photographing and video-recording where permitted, capturing overheard talk and spatial arrangements, and writing dense descriptive notes immediately after.

sources.system: EMAH (Empathic Mechanized Anthropomorphic Humanoid) on Ameca Gen 1
sources.developer: University research group (Engineered Arts Ameca hardware)
sources.title: Exploring LLM-powered multi-session human-robot interactions with university students
sources.claim: An LLM-driven social humanoid robot (EMAH, on an Engineered Arts Ameca platform) autonomously held open-domain, multi-turn conversations with 13 university students across four weekly sessions in a university lab setting; it is a stationary conversational torso, not a mobile fieldworker, and produced no ethnographic analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-conducted conversational interviewing. It is the nearest analogue to the interview component of ethnographic fieldwork, but transfer fails: the robot is fixed in a lab, conducts open-domain chat rather than consented research interviews in interlocutors' own settings, and does not observe, take field notes, or produce analytic output.

sources.developer: University of Plymouth / QUT research team (SoftBank Robotics NAO hardware)
sources.title: Experiences of a Motivational Interview Delivered by a Robot: Qualitative Study (JMIR)
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid robot delivered a fully scripted motivational interview to participants in a controlled study setting; the interview was pre-programmed rather than adaptively conducted, illustrating that robot 'interviewing' to date is script-bound.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: structured interviewing by a robot. Shows the state of the art is a fixed script in a controlled room, which cannot transfer to ethnographic interviewing where questions must follow emergent themes, rapport, and cultural context.

sources.system: Telepresence robots in higher education (e.g., Double/Beam-class platforms)
sources.title: Telepresence Robots for Remote Participation in Higher Education
sources.claim: Telepresence robots used for remote participation in academic teaching and research are driven by a remote human operator, so any 'remote fieldwork' they enable is continuous teleoperation rather than autonomous robotic performance of the task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote presence at a research or teaching site. It is the only deployed way a robot body appears in field-like settings for researchers, but it is continuously human-driven, which the rating rules exclude from supporting positive judgments.

instances.label: Nursing/allied-health clinical skills lab: faculty member supervises 15-25 students practicing injections, IV starts, catheterization, wound care and vitals on manikins and each other; sets up and resets stations and supplies, circulates to watch technique, physically corrects hand placement and sterile field breaks, intervenes on sharps/contamination hazards, and signs off competency check-offs during a 2-3 hour session.

Clinical laboratory science / microbiology / pharmacy compounding wet lab: faculty supervises students at benches and in laminar-flow hoods handling reagents, cultures, blood specimens and analyzers; distributes and checks materials, enforces PPE and biosafety practice, verifies aseptic technique and instrument use hands-on, manages spills or equipment faults, and validates student results before dismissal.

Gross anatomy / histology lab in a medical, PA, or health-sciences program: faculty supervises dissection or microscopy, handles cadaveric specimens and prosections, repositions tissue to point out structures, checks student cuts and slide work, enforces formalin/PPE and specimen-handling rules across a room of tables.

Dental or dental hygiene preclinical simulation lab: faculty supervises students at mannequin-head units preparing typodont teeth or scaling; takes the handpiece/instrument to demonstrate on a student's typodont, inspects preparations with mirror and explorer, adjusts patient-chair and student ergonomics, and grades work chairside.

Physical therapy, occupational therapy, respiratory or veterinary technology skills lab: faculty supervises students practicing manual techniques, transfers, mobilization, ventilator setup, or restraint and handling on peers, standardized patients, or live animals; physically guides students' hands, positions the subject/animal, and steps in to prevent injury.

sources.system: Mobile telepresence robot (TPR) in undergraduate nursing simulation
sources.developer: University nursing programs (ACM eLearn Magazine report)
sources.title: elearn Magazine: Utilizing Telepresence Robots in Undergraduate Nursing Simulations
sources.claim: Telepresence robots are used in nursing simulation labs and clinical education to let a remote instructor observe and interact with students, but the robot is a remote-presence conduit driven by a human, performing no autonomous supervision or physical intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system for lab supervision, but it does not transfer: a human instructor performs all observation, judgment and instruction through the robot, and the robot cannot handle specimens, correct a student's hands, or intervene physically.

sources.system: Mobile sentry robot for laboratory safety inspection
sources.developer: Zhang et al. (Security and Communication Networks, Wiley)
sources.title: Mobile Sentry Robot for Laboratory Safety Inspection Based on Machine Vision and Infrared Thermal Imaging Detection
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile sentry robot patrols university chemistry laboratories using machine vision and infrared thermal imaging to detect hazards such as fires and raise alarms; it monitors the room but does not instruct, assess, or physically assist students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is laboratory hazard patrol, one narrow slice of lab supervision; it does not transfer because it involves no student instruction, technique correction, competency assessment, or handling of the students' specimens and equipment.

sources.developer: University of Liverpool / RSC Digital Discovery authors
sources.title: Chemist Eye: a visual language model-powered system for safety monitoring and robot decision-making in self-driving laboratories
sources.claim: Chemist Eye provides vision-language-model safety monitoring and robot decision-making inside self-driving (robot-only) laboratories, watching equipment and mobile robots rather than supervising human students performing procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is safety oversight of an automated lab; it does not transfer because the supervised agents are robots in a purpose-built self-driving lab, not students performing health-science procedures needing hands-on correction and sign-off.

sources.developer: DenTeach / PrepScanner developers (reviewed in Oral Health Group)
sources.title: Transforming continuing education for dentists: A technological review of DenTeach and PrepScanner powered by AI and robotics
sources.claim: A robotic/laser grading device measures completed dental tooth preparations to give objective scores, automating one assessment sub-step of a preclinical dental lab rather than running or supervising the session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated grading of a finished workpiece; it does not transfer to supervising the session, which requires live oversight of many students, demonstration, hands-on correction, and safety intervention across a room.

sources.developer: US robotics firm (reported by eWeek / Interesting Engineering)
sources.title: US firm to deploy humanoid robot teaching assistant in New York schools
sources.claim: A humanoid teaching-assistant robot pilot is being placed in New York classrooms to support teachers and engage students in STEM lessons; it assists a human teacher and is not reported to supervise hands-on health-science laboratory work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is classroom instructional support; it does not transfer because the robot supplements a present human teacher, with no evidence of manipulating specimens or instruments, correcting technique physically, or enforcing biosafety.

tasks.label: Evaluate and grade students' class work, laboratory and clinic work, assignments, and papers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Supervise students' laboratory and clinical work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Clinical rotation on a hospital medical-surgical unit: the instructor is on the unit with 8-10 pre-licensure students assigned to real patients, rounding among rooms, directly observing and physically assisting first-time procedures (IV starts, Foley care, wound dressings), double-checking drawn medications and dose calculations at the bedside/Pyxis, co-signing, intervening physically to stop unsafe acts or take over care, and coordinating with staff RNs and charge nurse.

Skills/task-trainer laboratory session on campus: instructor supervises 10-16 students rotating through stations (injections, sterile dressing change, NG tube, catheterization, vital signs) on manikins and partial-task trainers; sets up and restocks supplies, circulates to correct hand position and sterile technique, enforces sharps and infection-control safety, and performs graded competency check-offs on each student.

High-fidelity simulation scenario: instructor operates the patient simulator from a control room or at bedside, adjusts physiologic parameters in response to student actions, may enter as an embedded participant, monitors safety and equipment (defibrillator, IV pump, oxygen), pauses or redirects the scenario, then leads a structured debrief with video review.

Specialty high-acuity clinical (labor & delivery, pediatrics, ICU, perioperative): one or two students at a time under close direct supervision, sterile fields, tight unit rules, instructor frequently hands-on with the student and the patient, and must be able to assume care immediately if the student falters.

Community/itinerant placements (home health visits, school nursing, clinics, long-term care): instructor travels between sites, supervises students intermittently in settings the school does not control, adapting to whatever layout, equipment, family members and patient conditions are found on arrival.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0, Advancing The Largest Fleet of Deployed AI-Powered Mobile Manipulation Robots
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous mobile-manipulation robot deployed in US hospitals performs materials logistics (delivering medications, lab samples, supplies) on inpatient units; it does not observe, coach, evaluate, or physically intervene in student-delivered patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to delimit the frontier of hospital robot autonomy (related task: intra-hospital transport). It shows autonomous navigation of an E2 hospital corridor is solved, but transport of carts and supplies involves no observation of a student's technique, no bedside procedural assistance, and no competency judgment, so it does not transfer to supervising students' clinical work.

sources.system: Telepresence robots in clinical/simulation education (e.g., Double/Ohmni-class platforms)
sources.developer: Various (study reported in J Educ Technol Health Sci)
sources.title: Telepresence robotics in clinical education: Enhancing student engagement and learning outcomes
sources.claim: Robots used in nursing clinical education are either simulated patients or teleoperated telepresence platforms driven by a remote human; the telepresence robot streams the remote instructor/student into the room rather than autonomously supervising anyone.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the closest robotic system used in the supervision setting itself. Because a human operator drives it and it has no manipulator, it cannot autonomously judge technique or physically intervene, so under the teleoperation rule it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.system: Video-language model pipeline for AI-assisted nursing skills assessment
sources.title: Automated Procedural Analysis via Video-Language Models for AI-assisted Nursing Skills Assessment
sources.claim: Automated assessment of nursing skills remains an open research problem addressed by software video-language models, which are assistive and not physically embodied; researchers state current manual and automated methods do not capture the full complexity of nursing ....
sources.transferJustification: Cited to show that even the evaluative, non-physical portion of supervision is unsolved and is being pursued with software only (not a robotic system by the definition used here), so it cannot substantiate robotic completion of the task in any environment.

tasks.label: Demonstrate patient care in clinical units of hospitals.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On a medical-surgical unit, the clinical instructor demonstrates fundamental hygiene, comfort and mobility care on an assigned inpatient with 2-8 students crowded at the bedside: partial bed bath or peri-care, oral care, repositioning/turning with pillows, occupied bed change, safe transfer bed-to-chair with a gait belt or ceiling lift, and assisted ambulation with IV pole and drains, while narrating rationale, maintaining privacy/dignity and adapting to the patient's pain, tubing and confusion.

The instructor demonstrates patient assessment on a real inpatient: hand hygiene and two-identifier check, manual blood pressure and radial pulse, respiratory count, pulse oximeter and thermometer placement, then a focused head-to-toe exam — auscultating lung and heart sounds and bowel sounds, palpating pedal pulses and edema, capillary refill, skin/wound inspection, neuro and pain assessment — showing students landmarks and interpreting findings against the monitor and chart.

The instructor demonstrates safe medication administration in the clinical unit: pulling meds from the automated dispensing cabinet, three checks and five rights, barcode scanning at the bedside, crushing/administering oral meds to a patient with swallowing difficulty, drawing up and giving a subcutaneous or IM injection, an IV push, programming a smart infusion pump, sharps disposal and documentation in the EHR, explaining each step to students.

The instructor demonstrates a sterile or invasive nursing procedure at the bedside: setting up a sterile field, donning sterile gloves, a wet-to-dry or complex wound dressing change, indwelling urinary catheter insertion, peripheral IV start/venipuncture on a real patient's arm, NG tube insertion and placement check, or tracheostomy/oropharyngeal suctioning — with PPE, patient coaching, aseptic technique visible to the students, and specimen/waste handling.

In a specialty unit (ICU, telemetry, ED, peds, L&D, oncology, OR/PACU), the instructor demonstrates higher-acuity care: care of a ventilated patient with lines and drains, central line dressing/flush, chest tube and drain assessment, newborn bath and cord care or infant feeding, fetal monitor application, chemotherapy handling precautions, or post-op assessment — in a crowded, alarm-filled room with the primary nurse present and students observing.

sources.title: Physical artificial intelligence in nursing: Robotics - Nursing Outlook
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed review in Nursing Outlook assessing physical AI/robotics in nursing concludes that bedside robotics remains largely human-operated or preprogrammed with limited autonomy and has not been transferred to direct patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Directly characterizes hands-on bedside patient care by robots, which is the physical content the instructor demonstrates to students.

sources.system: Collaborative robots (cobots) in acute care nursing pilot
sources.developer: US hospital/academic pilot reported in nursing informatics literature
sources.title: When Collaborative Robots Meet the Bedside: Nurses Informing Emerging Artificial Intelligence Technology
sources.claim: A multi-year US acute-care hospital pilot of collaborative robots at the bedside found value only in non-urgent delivery workflows; the cobots could not meaningfully take on nurses' patient care workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Same environment (US acute-care inpatient units) and same work content (nurse patient-care workflows) as the instructor's bedside demonstrations.

sources.title: Moxi | Montage Health / Diligent Robotics Unveils Moxi 2.0
sources.claim: Moxi, the largest deployed fleet of hospital mobile manipulation robots (100 units, 25+ hospital systems, 1.3M+ tasks), performs supply, medication and lab-sample transport, explicitly non-patient-facing tasks, not hands-on care.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the ceiling of what autonomous robots actually do inside real hospital units: logistics rather than bedside patient care.

sources.developer: Foxconn with NVIDIA and Kawasaki Heavy Industries
sources.title: Kawasaki Develops Nurse Assistant Robot with Foxconn
sources.claim: Nurabot, an autonomous nurse-assistant robot in field trials at Taichung Veterans General Hospital since April 2025, handles medicine and specimen transport, ward patrols, delivery of wound-care kits to bedsides, and visitor guidance — no hands-on patient care.
sources.transferJustification: The most advanced humanoid nursing robot trialed in a real hospital ward; its task list bounds what such systems can do in the instance setting.

sources.title: Medtech company Vitestro pulls US$70M together for autonomous blood draw tech
sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous blood-drawing device received CE marking in August 2024 and has been deployed at Dutch hospitals (OLVG, Amsterdam UMC), performing venipuncture autonomously on a patient's arm placed in the device in a blood-collection room.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed system to one sub-step of the invasive-procedure instance (venipuncture); cited to test, and bound, the invasive-procedure judgment.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: RABBIT, a research robot-assisted bed bathing system, autonomously performed washing, rinsing and drying of limbs, but was evaluated in a laboratory case study with a single participant with multiple sclerosis.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system to the hygiene/ADL instance; cited to test whether a bed-bath demonstration could be completed, and it is a single-subject lab prototype, not a hospital-unit capability.

sources.developer: Teaching and Learning in Nursing review authors
sources.title: Preparing nurses for the technological future: Robotic integration in nursing education
sources.claim: A December 2025 review of robotic integration in nursing education found only a handful of studies, all of which used robots in simulated settings rather than in clinical units.
sources.transferJustification: Directly addresses robots in the instructional half of this task and confirms no robot performs instructor-led clinical demonstrations in hospital units.

instances.label: Nursing faculty member holds a nurse-practitioner faculty-practice session (typically a half-day per week) in an outpatient clinic (family/primary care, student health, specialty clinic): rooms patients, takes history, performs hands-on physical exam (auscultation, palpation, otoscopy, skin/joint exam), runs point-of-care tests, gives injections or minor procedures, prescribes, and documents in the EHR.

Faculty member works per-diem or part-time staff RN shifts on a hospital med-surg, ICU, or ED unit: head-to-toe assessments, medication and IV administration, IV starts and blood draws, wound care and dressing changes, catheter/NG care, repositioning and ambulating patients, responding to alarms and rapid changes in condition, shift handoff documentation.

Faculty carries a small patient assignment on a clinical unit while precepting students: personally performs bedside care (meds, assessments, dressing changes, ostomy or tube care) and demonstrates technique to students at the bedside.

Specialty procedural practice to maintain licensure/certification: CRNA administering anesthesia in an OR, nurse-midwife managing labor and delivery, dialysis or infusion nurse cannulating access and running treatments, or perioperative nurse in sterile-field roles.

Community-based practice: home health or hospice visits in patients' houses and apartments, mobile/free-clinic or shelter clinics, school or parish nursing, correctional or public-health field work - assessment, wound care, medication management and teaching in settings taken as found.

Episodic low-acuity clinical practice: staffing vaccination/flu-shot clinics, community health-fair screenings (blood pressure, glucose fingerstick, blood draws), campus wellness events - screening for contraindications, consenting, giving the injection or collecting the specimen, observing for reactions, documenting.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, the most widely deployed hospital mobile manipulator in the US, works autonomously inside hospitals but its work is supply and specimen transport, not patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-hospital logistics in the same E2 setting (corridors, supply rooms, elevators). It does not transfer to maintaining a clinical practice - Moxi performs no patient assessment, no hands-on care, and no clinical decision-making.

sources.system: Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (Vitestro Aletta), ADOPT trial NCT05878483
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic phlebotomy device drew blood from outpatients in Dutch hospital phlebotomy departments with a 94.5% first-stick success rate, showing one narrow fixtured nursing sub-step can be automated in a structured facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: venipuncture, a sub-step of nursing practice, on a patient whose arm is positioned in the device. Covers only that step - the device could not always identify a suitable vein, and it performs no assessment, medication administration, or care planning.

sources.title: NVIDIA, Foxconn and Taiwan Medical Centers Bring Agentic and Physical AI to 'Healthy Taiwan'
sources.claim: Nurabot nursing robots moved from pilots into clinical operations in Taiwanese hospitals, but the work they take over is transport and logistics so that nurses can do the direct patient care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ward-level material transport in a hospital (E2). It explicitly does not transfer - the deployment reserves direct patient care for human nurses.

sources.system: SRT-H (Surgical Robot Transformer - Hierarchy) on a da Vinci Research Kit
sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - PubMed
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous clinical procedure execution is a surgical robot completing a multi-step gallbladder dissection fully autonomously on ex vivo animal tissue in a laboratory rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous execution of a clinical procedure. Performed on excised tissue fixtured in a lab rig for one pre-defined procedure, so it does not transfer to a live clinical caseload requiring assessment, judgment, and patient interaction.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid teleoperated surgical feasibility study
sources.title: In vivo feasibility study of humanoid robots in surgery (arXiv)
sources.claim: A 2026 humanoid-in-surgery feasibility study characterizes hospital robots in service today as logistics and administrative systems rather than systems performing clinical procedures.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as a survey of the state of clinical robotics, not as a positive capability claim; the humanoid work itself is teleoperated and therefore cannot support a positive judgment.

roles.title: Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.description: Teach courses in drama, music, and the arts including fine and applied art, such as painting and sculpture, or design and crafts. Includes both teachers primarily engaged in teaching and those who do a combination of teaching and research.

tasks.label: Explain and demonstrate artistic techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Applied music lesson or studio class in a campus practice room/recital hall: the professor demonstrates a technique on the instrument or with the voice (bowing, articulation, pedaling, embouchure, breath support), plays the passage at tempo and again slowly, deliberately reproduces the student's error, and narrates why the motion works, adapting the demo to what the student just played.

Two-dimensional studio course (drawing, painting, printmaking) in a campus art studio: the instructor demos at an easel or table before 15-25 students - loading and dragging a loaded brush, wet-on-wet blending, gesture drawing, inking and pulling a print - narrating throughout, then circulates and repeats short demos directly on individual students' work.

Three-dimensional studio/shop course (ceramics, sculpture, jewelry, woodworking) in a campus studio or fabrication shop: the instructor centers and opens clay on the wheel, carves or models, or sets up and runs a torch/welder/kiln, explaining hand pressure, tool angle, material state and safety while students watch closely and then try it with the instructor guiding.

Acting, voice, or movement class in a campus rehearsal studio or black box theater: the instructor physically demonstrates vocal projection and resonance, breath work, stage combat moves, physical characterization, or blocking, then repeats the demonstration modified for a particular student's body and scene.

Design/digital media course (graphic design, animation, digital audio, photography lighting) in a computer lab or media studio: the instructor demonstrates a software workflow at a projected workstation or sets up lights, camera, and microphone on a subject, narrating the parameter choices and repeating steps on request.

sources.developer: Visual Computing Group, University of Konstanz (Oliver Deussen)
sources.title: e-David, a painting robot | Goldsmiths, University of London
sources.claim: e-David is a robotic arm that paints on canvas with real brushes and paint, using visual feedback of the drying canvas to plan successive strokes; it operates in a university lab cell that requires markers on the painting surface for feedback.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous easel painting. It shows a robot can execute brush strokes with real media in a fixtured cell, the physical core of a painting demo, but the cited work is picture production, not delivering and narrating a specified technique to students or re-demonstrating on a student's canvas.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (Gil Weinberg)
sources.title: Performance Showcase — CHI 2010
sources.claim: Shimon is an autonomous marimba-playing ... that listens to human players and improvises with them; it has performed in dozens of concerts and ... on ordinary stages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live musical performance alongside humans. It shows autonomous, real-time instrument playing at performance quality on one percussion instrument, but no evidence of selecting, narrating, and re-demonstrating a specific technique for a student.

sources.title: instruMentor: An Interactive Robot for Musical Instrument Tutoring
sources.claim: instruMentor is a research tutor robot with robotic hands that plays a recorder and shows novice learners how to hold and finger the instrument in real time; evaluation was a small user study with beginners in a lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered instrument tutoring. Closest published system to this task, but it targets absolute beginners on a simple recorder in a lab, autonomy of the interaction is not established, and it is far below the expressive, diagnostic demonstration a postsecondary applied-music instructor gives.

sources.system: USC Viterbi robotic hand (perception-in-action music learning)
sources.developer: USC Viterbi School of Engineering (Brain-Body Dynamics Lab)
sources.title: USC robot learns music by ear, opening new possibilities in medicine and therapy | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: A USC Viterbi robotic hand can hear a short melody and reproduce it on a keyboard after about two minutes of self-directed practice, without sheet music or pre-programmed scores; it is a laboratory prototype playing simple melodies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous keyboard playing by ear. Shows current frontier of robot instrumental skill acquisition on real hardware; the output is a simple melody, not an expressive technique demonstration with explanation.

sources.title: Dexterous Robotic Piano Playing at Scale (arXiv:2511.02504)
sources.claim: OmniPianist learns to play nearly a thousand piano pieces through large-scale reinforcement and imitation learning, but the reported results are agent/simulation experiments rather than a real piano played at performance quality before an audience.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bimanual robotic piano playing. Relevant to the music instance, but the evidence is learning-agent experiments without a demonstrated physical instructor-quality performance, so it cannot substantiate completion of a teaching demonstration.

sources.title: RoPotter: Toward Robotic Pottery and Deformable Object Manipulation with Structural Priors
sources.claim: RoPotter introduces the robotics research task of continuously deforming clay ...; it is an early-stage lab system using structural priors for simple wheel-throwing deformations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic wheel-throwing of clay. Shows the physical act of shaping clay on a wheel is still an open research problem, well short of an instructor centering and opening clay while narrating the technique.

sources.title: Italy Invents Robot That Carves Sculptures Out of Marble Like Michelangelo
sources.claim: Robotor's robots carve marble sculptures from 3D models in a Carrara stone yard, a purpose-built machining cell, producing finished works for artists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stone sculpture fabrication in an E1 cell. It substantiates automated art object production from a digital model, not the teaching act of demonstrating and explaining hand-carving technique to students.

tasks.label: Display students' work in schools, galleries, and exhibitions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hanging a student show of 2D work (framed/matted paintings, drawings, prints, photos) on the walls of a campus or school art gallery: laying out spacing, measuring center-lines, installing hooks/nails/cleats, leveling each piece, adding wall labels.

Mounting student work on hallway bulletin/tack boards and filling lobby display cases in a school building: pinning or taping unframed sheets, arranging small pieces and cards, closing and securing the case.

Installing 3D student work — ceramics, small sculpture, design models — on pedestals and inside vitrines in a campus gallery or foyer: moving fragile one-off pieces, positioning and securing them, adding plinth labels.

Installing a student exhibition in an off-campus, found venue (community gallery, café, library, pop-up storefront, art-fair booth): transporting and unpacking crated/wrapped work, deciding a layout for an unfamiliar room, hanging, ladder work, aiming track lights, signage.

Music/drama/design variants: setting up display tables, poster/foamcore boards, costume and set-model displays, program boards, and screens or monitors showing student media work at a recital hall, theater lobby, or conference venue.

sources.developer: AIST (Japan National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology)
sources.title: Development of a humanoid robot prototype, HRP-5P, capable of heavy labor
sources.claim: AIST's HRP-5P humanoid autonomously performed gypsum-board installation — mapping its surroundings, separating a board from a stack, carrying and positioning it against a wall frame, and screwing it in place — at a simulated (purpose-built) residential construction site.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixing a large flat panel to a wall. It shares the core physical acts of hanging 2D student work — separating one flat sheet from a stack, transporting it, registering it at a specified position on a wall, and fastening it — and was done autonomously in an environment built as a mock-up for the robot, i.e. E1.

sources.system: MWES vision-guided picture frame assembly line (FANUC robots)
sources.title: Flexibility & Production Speed with Robotic Vision | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: A commercial four-robot FANUC cell assembles picture frames of seven styles, using machine vision to align and place glass, paper mats and back ... into frames at high rate with recipe-driven changeover.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling framed pictures. It handles exactly the materials of matted/framed student artwork — sheet glass, paper mats, backing boards, frames of varying size — with vision-guided, damage-free precision placement, but only inside a fenced, fixtured production cell (E1).

sources.system: MWES Robotic Paint Line Tending Cell (FANUC R-2000iB/185L)
sources.title: Robotic Paint Line Tending Cell | Midwest Engineered Systems
sources.claim: Six fully automated FANUC robot cells load 4–12 ft steel beams onto the hanging carriers of an existing paint line and unload and stack painted beams, at a 15-second cycle with only minimal operator intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading long, awkward workpieces onto overhead hanging carriers. This is the physical act of registering an object onto hanging hardware at a known position, the mechanical core of hanging framed work, demonstrated reliably but only in a purpose-built fenced cell (E1).

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Introduces the RightPick 4 System – The Next-Generation Autonomous Robotic Piece-Picking System for Warehouse Order Fulfillment
sources.claim: RightPick 4 is a commercially deployed autonomous piece-picking system that grasps a wide range of differently shaped and sized items and places them at designated destinations in order-fulfillment operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking varied, previously unseen objects and placing them at a specified destination. It supports grasping and positioning heterogeneous 3D objects such as ceramics and small sculpture, but the demonstrated work occurs in an engineered pick cell with presented totes (E1).

sources.title: Telexistence Deploys AI and Remote-Controlled Robots in 300 Convenience Stores, Utilizing Azure
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is installed in the backrooms ... roughly 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, where it autonomously detects empty beverage shelf positions and restocks bottles and cans, with staff able to intervene remotely when AI stocking fails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing objects onto shelves inside a human-run facility (E2). It marks the frontier of autonomous placement in a structured human facility, but is a fixed-rail machine handling uniform bottles on standardized cooler shelving, so it does not carry over to arranging unique, fragile student work in a display case or on a gallery wall.

tasks.label: Participate in campus and community events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Attends a campus event as a departmental presence — a student recital, senior thesis exhibition opening, guest-artist lecture, convocation or commencement — sitting in the audience, applauding, then mingling at the reception with students, parents, alumni and donors in the campus concert hall or gallery.

Performs or exhibits at a campus or community event: plays a program in a faculty chamber recital or community orchestra concert, acts in or directs a departmental production, or shows and discusses their own artwork in a community exhibition, including instrument/stage setup, tuning, warm-up and post-performance greeting of the audience.

Serves as adjudicator, panelist or speaker at an event — judging a high-school art competition or district music festival, giving a gallery talk about an exhibition, or joining a post-show Q&A panel — requiring evaluation of live work and unscripted discussion with attendees.

Community outreach with a hands-on component: staffing the department's table at a public arts festival, county fair or college fair (hauling and setting up the table, banner and handouts) and running a demonstration or short workshop — throwing pots, sketching portraits, teaching a drumming circle — at a local school, library or festival tent, often outdoors and weather-exposed.

Behind-the-scenes support for a campus or community event: helping hang and light a student exhibition, moving risers, chairs, music stands and instruments, running the reception table, ushering and handing out programs, then striking the setup afterward.

sources.developer: Georgia Tech Center for Music Technology (Gil Weinberg)
sources.title: Shimon | Center for Music Technology - Georgia Tech
sources.claim: Shimon, an improvising robotic marimba player from Georgia Tech, autonomously listens to and analyzes music and improvises with human players on stage, and has appeared in dozens of concerts and ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: live musical performance at a public event, the closest analog to a music faculty member performing at a campus or community concert. It falls short of the instance because Shimon plays only improvised marimba lines alongside human musicians, is transported and set up by its research team, and does not deliver a prepared faculty recital program or the surrounding audience engagement.

sources.title: Sotheby's Will Auction First Artwork Made by Humanoid Robot Ai-Da Using AI Algorithms
sources.claim: Ai-Da, a humanoid robot artist, produced a painting of Alan Turing using AI algorithms and a robotic drawing/painting arm; the work was exhibited and auctioned at Sotheby's, and the robot has appeared at public events such as the UN AI for Good Summit accompanied by its human team.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an artist exhibiting work and appearing at art-world events, analogous to an art professor exhibiting at a community show. It does not substantiate the instance: the exhibition installation, transport and public presentation are handled by a human team, and the robot's spoken event participation is scripted/curated rather than autonomous professional engagement.

sources.system: RobotLAB social humanoid greeter / Unitree R1 EDU lobby greeter
sources.title: University & Research Robots · RobotLAB
sources.claim: Commercially deployed social humanoid greeter robots in higher-education settings welcome visitors, answer routine questions and guide people through a space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: staffing a fixed point in a campus building and interacting with visitors, the nearest deployed analog to attending an event or staffing a departmental booth. Capability does not transfer: these units handle narrow scripted FAQ exchanges from a fixed spot and cannot set up a booth, judge student work, or hold substantive professional conversations with prospective students and donors.

tasks.label: Maintain or repair studio facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine floor care in a university art building: after ceramics/painting sessions, sweeping and wet-mopping clay and plaster dust, paint drips and plaster chips from studio floors and the adjoining corridors so the space is safe and usable for the next class.

Servicing and repairing studio production equipment in place: diagnosing and replacing burned-out kiln elements, thermocouples and relays; rebuilding a slipping potter's wheel or pug mill; changing blades and belts and clearing the dust collector on the scene-shop table saw; re-felting the etching press bed; swapping spray-booth filters.

Repairing the physical fabric of the studio/shop: fixing broken easels, worktables, stools, flats and storage racks; re-hanging a sagging door; replacing burnt lamps in track lighting and stage instruments; mounting shelving and pegboard; clearing a clogged clay-trap sink.
Refinishing wall surfaces: between exhibitions and terms, patching nail holes and dings in studio and student-gallery walls, then sanding and repainting the emptied room to a clean, even finish.

Music/media facility upkeep: tuning and lightly regulating studio and practice-room pianos, restringing instruments, repairing music stands and stools, testing and re-soldering audio cables, cleaning and re-lamping projectors and calibrating recording-studio gear.

Studio reset and non-floor housekeeping: wiping down wedging tables, wheels and glaze buckets, scrubbing sinks and brushes, emptying scrap clay and trash to the dumpster, refilling solvent and stock stations, and rearranging tables, easels and dividers for the next course's layout.

sources.system: R3 Vacuum, R3 Scrubber, R12 Rex Scrubber (SSC/FES autonomous custodial fleet)
sources.developer: SSC Services for Education / Texas A&M Facilities & Energy Services (robot OEM fleet)
sources.title: Facilities & Energy Services Deploys Autonomous Technology at Texas A&M University
sources.claim: Texas A&M University has autonomous vacuums and floor scrubbers (R3 Vacuum, R3 Scrubber, R12 Rex Scrubber) in routine operation inside campus buildings since August 2025, performing everyday floor cleaning in a university facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional custodial floor cleaning. Studio floor upkeep after art classes is the same act (sweeping/wet scrubbing hard floors) on the same class of surfaces inside the same kind of university building.

sources.system: Autonomous robot floor cleaner (SFU Facilities Services)
sources.developer: Simon Fraser University Facilities Services (commercial cleaning-robot vendor)
sources.title: New robot cleaner rolls onto campus - Facilities Services - Simon Fraser University
sources.claim: A large autonomous floor-cleaning robot has been added to the custodial team across Simon Fraser University's Burnaby campus, with staff setting routes and monitoring progress via an app.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: campus custodial floor cleaning; corroborates that autonomous scrubbers do the floor-care portion of facility upkeep in university buildings to an accepted standard.

sources.system: Okibo EG7 / EG7+ painting and drywall-finishing robot
sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7/EG7+ mobile manipulators autonomously plaster (drywall finish) and paint interior walls, scanning and modeling the room themselves with no site prep or external markers, and are in commercial use on US and European construction sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior wall skim-coating and painting. Repainting an emptied studio/gallery is the same operation on the same substrate (gypsum board walls) at the same finish quality; the robot needs no fixtures or markers and fits through standard doorways.

sources.title: Okibo launches autonomous, AI-guided painting and drywall finishing EG7+ robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Okibo nationally launched the EG7+ and its platform was used by a contractor (PCI) on a real commercial interior project, indicating the autonomous finishing robot is a fielded product rather than a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (interior wall finishing/painting); establishes commercial maturity of the cited system.

An arts-education faculty member runs an empirical study: designing the protocol, obtaining IRB approval, collecting survey/observation data from students or performers, analyzing results statistically or qualitatively, and writing up findings for a professional journal.

A studio art, design, or performance faculty member pursues practice-based research and publishes an account of it — an exhibition catalog essay, a documented process article, or a digital/electronic-media publication including images, audio, or video documentation of the work.

Publication-cycle work: submitting to journals or presses, responding to peer reviewers, revising, correcting proofs, securing image permissions, and disseminating the finished piece through institutional repositories, professional websites, or other electronic media.

instances.label: Manufacturing/welding lab at a community or technical college: instructor oversees 15-24 students running lathes, mills, CNC machines, grinders and welding booths simultaneously — verifying workholding and setups before a cut, checking PPE and hot-work practice, correcting grip/feed technique, physically stopping or e-stopping a machine when a student does something dangerous, and stepping in to secure a workpiece or clear a jam.

Automotive/diesel technology shop: instructor circulates among bays while students use lifts, hoists, torque wrenches, impact guns, presses, welders and scan tools on live vehicles — checking lift points and jack stands before students go under a car, watching fuel/battery handling, taking a tool from a student to demonstrate the correct move, and halting work when a setup is unsafe.

Cosmetology/barbering clinic floor with paying clients: instructor monitors students using shears, razors, clippers, thermal irons and chemical services — observing hand position and sectioning, physically guiding a student's hand or repositioning the client's head, checking processing timers and product mixing, and stopping a service before a chemical burn or bad cut occurs.

Culinary arts kitchen or allied-health/lab-based CTE course: instructor supervises students using knives, slicers, mixers, fryers and ranges, or autoclaves, centrifuges and clinical simulation equipment — enforcing safe handling, correcting technique mid-task, taking over a hazardous step, and checking equipment condition and shutdown at the end of the period.

Construction/HVAC/electrical trades instruction at an outdoor build site, a gutted training house, or a rotating job-site lab: students on ladders and scaffolds with nail guns, circular saws, torches and live circuits; layout, weather and hazards differ site to site and the instructor must move around the site, spot unsafe positions, and physically intervene (lock out a panel, steady a ladder, take a tool away).

CDL truck-driving or heavy-equipment program: instructor supervises students operating trucks, excavators or forklifts on a training range and on public roads — riding in the cab with dual controls or spotting from the ground, calling corrections, and taking the wheel/controls or triggering a stop when the student errs.

sources.system: Laboratory Safety Assistant (LSA) framework on Misty II Plus
sources.developer: Hosei University / Jagiellonian University / South Valley University (Hasnine et al.)
sources.title: Social Robot Assistive Intervention for Science Students to Prevent Laboratory Accidents
sources.claim: The Laboratory Safety Assistant framework uses a Misty II Plus social robot that drives around a (simulated) science laboratory on a patrol cycle, captures video, and runs a YOLOv8 detector to flag whether students are wearing goggles, gloves, aprons and lab shoes or are using a phone; the actual corrective intervention is left to the human teacher via a dashboard. It is a research prototype tested in a simulated lab, not a deployed supervisor.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robotic monitoring of students' safety compliance in an instructional lab. It covers only PPE-presence checking in a simulated lab and explicitly hands intervention to the teacher, so it does not transfer to judging tool technique or physically intervening at a machine.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously patrols enterprise facilities such as FedEx sites, streaming AI analysis to remote human specialists who handle interactions; it detects anomalies and reports them but does not assess how people operate tools or intervene physically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor patrol and anomaly detection inside a controlled facility. It shares only the mobile-observation element; it cannot evaluate a student's cutting or welding technique, cannot correct it, and has no manipulator or authority to stop a machine, so it does not transfer to supervising students' tool use.

Individualized coaching at a student's station during shop/lab practice time: the instructor observes the student's technique (weld bead, brake job, wiring a circuit), diagnoses the error, explains and demonstrates the correction, and has the student repeat until the work meets standard.

Scheduled remedial instruction in foundational academic skills that gate trade coursework — shop math, measurement and fractions, reading technical manuals and blueprints, test-taking for licensure exams — delivered to one student or a pair in a classroom or learning center.

Individualized instruction delivered asynchronously or by accommodation plan: designing a make-up/accelerated learning path, giving written or recorded feedback on submitted work through the LMS, holding a video office-hour session, and documenting progress for a student with a disability accommodation or a re-entering adult learner.

One-on-one instruction on a clinic or live-work floor (cosmetology salon clinic, dental assisting clinic, campus auto customer bay) with a paying client or customer vehicle present: the instructor talks the student through the service step by step, intervening or taking over when the client's outcome or safety is at risk.

instances.label: Hands-on trade shop/lab session on campus (welding, automotive, HVAC, machining, construction, electrical): 12-20 students at live stations with torches, lifts, saws or energized panels; instructor circulates for 2-4 hours, enforces PPE and lockout, answers questions, corrects grip/technique hands-on, adjusts machine settings, inspects work in progress, intervenes on hazards, and signs off competencies.

Services/clinical teaching lab with live clients or simulators (cosmetology clinic floor, dental assisting, culinary kitchen, nursing/allied-health skills lab): students perform chemical services, food production or patient-care skills; instructor checks each step, enforces sanitation and infection control, and must correct or take over work in progress on a real client/patient.

Computer- or classroom-based group and independent project work (IT/networking racks, CAD/drafting, medical coding, business capstones): instructor circulates among tables and workstations, reviews on-screen and bench work, troubleshoots student configurations, keeps groups on task and on schedule, and evaluates deliverables.

Off-site field placement/internship visit at an employer or institutional facility (hospital or nursing-home clinical rotation, dealership service bay, salon, restaurant): instructor travels to the site, observes the student performing on real patients/customers, evaluates competencies, intervenes if the student errs, and confers with the site preceptor.

Off-site placement in an uncontrolled field setting (residential construction/remodel job site, roadside heavy-equipment or utility work, mobile service calls): instructor visits a site laid out differently each time, watches the student work amid changing hazards and other trades, and judges safety and workmanship in situ.

Open-lab, after-hours or independent capstone supervision: two to six students working on their own projects in the shop or lab; instructor monitors intermittently, provides one-on-one troubleshooting, authorizes use of restricted equipment, verifies safe shutdown and cleanup, and signs off progress.

sources.system: Laboratory Safety Assistant (LSA) framework on Misty II Plus
sources.title: A Participatory Design Approach to Designing Educational Interventions for Science Students Using Socially Assistive Robots
sources.claim: A socially assistive robot (Misty II Plus) was proposed as a 'Laboratory Safety Assistant' to monitor student behavior against safety rules in a science lab; the work is a participatory-design study with 20 students, not a deployed supervisor, and covers only safety reminders rather than instruction, hands-on correction or competency sign-off.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic monitoring of students in a teaching laboratory. It is the closest system to lab supervision, but it is a design-study prototype limited to detecting unsafe behaviors and issuing reminders; it does not answer technical questions, correct technique physically, or evaluate work, so it does not transfer to whole-task supervision.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Spot performs autonomous, repeatable inspection rounds inside industrial facilities, navigating routes and collecting gauge, thermal and acoustic data; this is autonomous mobile monitoring of equipment, not oversight of people performing skilled work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol and monitoring rounds in an institution-controlled facility (an E2 setting comparable to a college shop). It substantiates autonomous navigation and observation only; the machine reads assets, not learners' technique, and cannot instruct, correct, or grade, so it does not carry over to supervising students.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics releases Spot and Orbit 5.1 with new Spot Cam
sources.claim: In autonomous patrol missions Spot's response to detecting a person is to pause, light up, capture imagery and raise an alert to a remote human; it does not engage, instruct or intervene with the person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous person detection during facility patrol. It shows the state of the art for robots encountering humans on autonomous rounds is alerting a remote human, which falls far short of supervising, coaching and physically correcting students.

sources.title: Telepresence robotics in clinical education: Enhancing student engagement and learning outcomes
sources.claim: Telepresence robots used for faculty supervision of students in clinical education are driven by the human instructor, who observes and speaks through the robot; the supervision is performed by the remote person, not by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote faculty supervision of student practice sessions. Because a human instructor continuously teleoperates the robot and supplies all judgment and feedback, it cannot support a positive autonomy judgment for this task.

tasks.label: Select and assemble books, materials, supplies, and equipment for training, courses, or projects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Annual/term selection of instructional materials: reviewing publisher samples, online catalogs and industry-certification requirements, choosing textbooks, workbooks, software licenses and consumable supply lines, then compiling requisitions for purchasing; later receiving delivered cartons and distributing books/manuals to students. Office and campus receiving area.

Weekly/daily prep for a shop or lab session (automotive, welding, HVAC, machining, electrical): per the lesson plan, pulling consumables (rods, tips, fasteners, filters, fluids, stock), hand tools, meters and PPE from a cluttered stockroom/tool crib and staging matched sets at 10-16 student stations; heterogeneous items, some heavy or sharp.

Culinary, cosmetology or health-science lab prep: pulling bulk ingredients or product from coolers/dry storage, portioning into per-station trays or kits (mise en place; mannequin heads, chemicals, implements; practice supplies) and staging them at each student bench before class.

Project-based course prep (carpentry, welding fabrication, electrical, manufacturing): selecting stock material, cutting/preparing it to project size, and bundling the hardware, fasteners and components into a materials package for each student team's build, in the school shop.

Setting up and verifying equipment in the classroom/lab before instruction: rolling out engine or HVAC trainers, connecting welders to power and shielding gas, powering up CNC/diagnostic machines, loading software, testing that each station functions and swapping out failed units; also placing handouts and texts at seats.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick system autonomously picks a wide range of small, varied items and is deployed commercially for automated kitting workflows (building assorted item sets per order) in fulfillment, pharmacy and grocery operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic order kitting. Assembling a per-station supply kit from a lesson-plan list is the same operation as filling a kit from a pick list - heterogeneous small items, bin-to-tote placement, no fine assembly - and the cited cells are purpose-built, with goods presented in totes, matching the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-driven arms autonomously pick, portion and place multiple different ingredients into trays at production speed, deployed at food manufacturers including Amy's ... with tens of millions of servings produced.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioned meal assembly. Preparing per-student mise en place or product kits is the same act of dispensing measured portions of many different materials into individual trays presented on a line, at comparable precision.

sources.title: US: BMW deploys Figure 03 humanoid at smart factory for logistics
sources.claim: Figure's Figure 03 humanoid was deployed in June 2026 in BMW's Spartanburg logistics hall to pick unsorted components out of containers and sequence them into trolleys for delivery to assembly stations, running on the Helix vision-language-action policy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parts sequencing/kitting. Sorting mixed parts from containers into per-station trolleys is the industrial analogue of assembling per-workstation material sets, and the robot works at a designated station where containers are presented to it.

sources.system: Library automated storage and retrieval system ('The Robot')
sources.developer: Library AS/RS vendor installation at UMKC Libraries
sources.title: The Robot - UMKC Libraries
sources.claim: Academic libraries run automated storage and retrieval systems in which robotic cranes autonomously retrieve requested books and materials from bins and deliver them to a staff/patron station; UMKC's Miller Nichols Library has operated such a system since 2010.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated book retrieval. Pulling the specific titles/copies needed for a course is the physical half of 'assemble books', done reliably by these purpose-built systems, though the adoption decision itself is not automated.

sources.title: AutomaTech Robotik advances woodworking process - Wood & Panel USA
sources.claim: Standard robotic cells for CNC nesting/cut-to-size lines load and unload panel stock and sort cut parts automatically, and have been integrated many times in woodworking plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cut-to-size and cut-part handling. Cutting project stock to size and separating the pieces for each student team is the same fixtured cutting-plus-part-handling operation performed in these cells.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi autonomous mobile manipulator is deployed in more than 25 ... with over a million deliveries, but its work is transporting closed payloads (supply bins, lab samples, pharmacy items) through corridors rather than selecting individual items off storeroom shelves.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E2 case: the most mature mobile manipulator in a structured human facility performs point-to-point transport of loaded containers, not lesson-plan item selection from shop shelves or bench-side staging.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots autonomously restock refrigerated shelves with bottled and ... in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores - a single-SKU, fixed-geometry replenishment task in a human retail facility.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound the E2 case: item handling inside a human facility is demonstrated only for uniform beverage containers on a fixed shelf installation, not for the assorted tools, consumables and equipment a shop-class kit requires.

tasks.label: Conduct on-the-job training classes or training sessions to teach and demonstrate principles, techniques, procedures, or methods of designated subjects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Welding / metal fabrication lab session at a community college: instructor sets up a coupon at a demo booth, physically lays a bead (SMAW/GMAW/GTAW) narrating rod angle, travel speed and puddle control, then circulates among 15-20 students in booths, adjusts their machine settings and body position, inspects and destructively tests their welds, and enforces hot-work/PPE safety.

Automotive/diesel technology shop session: instructor demonstrates a service or diagnostic procedure (brake job, valve adjustment, scan-tool driveability diagnosis) on a vehicle at a lift in the college shop bay with students gathered around, then supervises students repeating it on other vehicles, answers questions, and verifies torque and completion.

Cosmetology/barbering clinic-floor session: instructor demonstrates a haircut, color application, perm wrap or shave on a mannequin head or live client while students watch, then coaches students hand-over-hand on their own clients, correcting shears/comb angle and chemical timing, and signs off practical competencies.

Health-science/allied-health skills lab (CNA, EMT, phlebotomy, dental assisting): instructor demonstrates a clinical procedure on a manikin or peer (venipuncture, CPR, transfer, suctioning), then runs students through repeated practice, corrects technique, and performs competency check-offs.

Construction/HVAC/electrical training conducted at an off-campus live job site or a partially built lab house: instructor demonstrates framing, conduit bending and pulling, brazing or rough-in on the actual structure amid varying weather, clutter and site conditions, then supervises student crews performing the work.

Customized on-the-job training session delivered at an employer's plant for incumbent workers: instructor demonstrates setup, changeover, or a maintenance procedure on the company's own production equipment on the shop floor and coaches operators through repetitions.

sources.title: India's first sari-donning AI humanoid robot teacher starts teaching
sources.claim: Humanoid/AI 'teacher robots' deployed in schools function as conversational, multilingual content-delivery and Q&A avatars; there is no evidence they physically demonstrate manual trade techniques or supervise hands-on shop practice, and their autonomy versus scripting/operator control is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = classroom instruction delivery. Cited to show the closest existing 'robot teacher' handles speech/Q&A only; it does not transfer to demonstrating welding, haircutting or vehicle repair, which require tool manipulation and workpiece judgment.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid with Optio AI assistant
sources.title: US firm to deploy humanoid robot teaching assistant in New York schools
sources.claim: The most recent US school humanoid deployment is an AI teaching assistant/tutor built around digital avatars and conversational interaction, used as subject matter for AI/robotics coursework rather than as an instructor performing manual demonstrations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = tutoring/classroom assistance. Shows state of the art in robot-embodied instruction is verbal tutoring, with no manipulation of tools or workpieces, so it cannot substantiate demonstrating trade techniques.

sources.developer: Academic prototypes surveyed in MDPI Robotics
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: No commercial haircutting robot has been deployed as of 2025, so no cited system can perform the cosmetology demonstration that a barbering/cosmetology instructor executes in front of students.

sources.system: Robotic welding and plasma-cutting cells in the SDCCE welding facility
sources.developer: San Diego College of Continuing Education (industrial robot vendors)
sources.title: Robotic welding coming to College of Continuing Education
sources.claim: Where robots do appear in CTE trade labs, they are fixtured industrial welding/plasma-cutting cells that are the subject matter of the course; the human program chair and instructors conduct the training around them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic arc welding on fixtured parts. Even granting an E1 fixtured cell can lay a bead, that capability covers only one demonstration motion and not conducting the session, coaching students, or inspecting their work.

tasks.label: Acquire, maintain, and repair laboratory equipment and tools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly/between-class upkeep of a college shop's mixed equipment (auto bay lifts and diagnostic scanners, welders, table saws/planers, lathes and mills, HVAC trainers, cosmetology stations): blow out chips and dust, check fluids and air lines, swap worn belts/blades/filters, lubricate ways and fittings, verify guards and interlocks, and reset the stations for the next class.

Welding lab consumable service: ream/clean spatter from MIG gun gas nozzles, apply anti-spatter, cut back wire, and replace worn contact tips and diffusers on the program's torches so students get stable arcs the next session.

Troubleshooting and repairing a machine that fails mid-term (two-post lift that won't raise, CNC mill throwing a spindle/axis alarm, salon dryer or clipper, bench grinder, engine trainer): diagnose the fault, source or scavenge the part, disassemble, replace, reassemble, test under load, and document the fix.

Acquiring a new machine: writing specifications, comparing vendor quotes, submitting the requisition through the college's purchasing system, then receiving the crated delivery at the dock, uncrating it, moving and positioning it in the lab, leveling/anchoring, hooking up power and compressed air, calibrating and safety-checking before student use.

Reconditioning cutting tools for a machining/manufacturing program's tool room: resharpening dull drill bits, end mills, and lathe tooling to spec (geometry, relief, point angle) and returning the batch to service.

Tool crib and consumable stock management: issuing and collecting hand tools each lab period, tracking who has what, end-of-term inventory count, pulling damaged or worn tools out of service, and reordering and restocking consumables (abrasives, gloves, wire, shampoo, filters) onto shelves and carts.

Arranging and overseeing outside service and compliance: scheduling vendor/warranty technicians and mandated inspections (lift certification, autoclave/boiler, fume extraction), lockout-tagging unsafe equipment, escorting the technician in the lab, and keeping maintenance and equipment records.

sources.system: ANCA AR300 robot tool loader with FX5/CPX Linear CNC tool grinders
sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product line commercial for years)
