sources.claim: ANCA's AR300 robotic loader integrated into CNC tool-grinding machines loads mixed batches of tools from a pallet for unattended automatic resharpening in a purpose-built machine enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial cutting-tool regrinding. Same objects (drills, end mills, lathe tooling) and same accepted output (tool restored to correct geometry and returned to service) as an instructor resharpening the program's cutting tools; the robot loader handles presentation and the grinder holds tolerances tighter than a hand-ground tool.

sources.system: ABICOR BINZEL Torch Cleaning Station TCS Compact / TCS-6 reamers
sources.title: Cleaning Stations & Reamers | ABICOR BINZEL
sources.claim: Automatic torch cleaning/reaming stations perform welding-torch consumable maintenance — reaming the gas nozzle of spatter, cutting the wire and spraying anti-spatter — as an automated step inside a robotic welding cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preventive maintenance of MIG welding consumables in an automated weld cell. It is the same physical operation (clearing spatter from the nozzle, protecting the tip, trimming wire stick-out) on the same hardware a welding instructor services, performed automatically with the torch presented to the station.

sources.title: Quadruped robot boosts safety and maintenance at aging cement plant
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged robot autonomously walks inspection routes in a working industrial plant, reading equipment condition (heat, vibration, leaks), but performs condition monitoring rather than physical maintenance or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine equipment condition checks in an industrial facility. It is the closest deployed system to the inspection portion of shop upkeep, but it only senses and reports; it does not clean, lubricate, change consumables, or repair, so it cannot carry the maintenance instances.

sources.title: How BMW is Using Figure AI Humanoid Robots in Production | Manufacturing Digital
sources.claim: Figure's humanoid runs autonomous logistics shifts at BMW's Spartanburg plant, handling packages and carts with a vision-language-action policy; the deployed work is parcel sequencing, not machine servicing, uncrating, or installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose manipulation inside a structured factory. It marks the frontier of deployed autonomous manipulation, but the demonstrated repertoire (grasp, orient, place packages/parts) does not include diagnosing faults, disassembling machines, or hooking up and calibrating new equipment.

sources.title: RoboCrib VX1000 | Industrial Vending Machine | Snap-on AutoCrib
sources.claim: Automated industrial tool cribs mechanically dispense and accept return of tools and consumables with perpetual inventory tracking, but the machines are stocked and their contents inspected by people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tool crib issue/return and inventory control. It covers the check-out/check-in and counting portion of tool management, but not restocking shelves and carts or pulling damaged tools out of service, so it does not complete the instance.

sources.title: Spot Arm | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot Arm manipulates valves, levers and doors only semi-autonomously or by telemanipulation, i.e. under operator initiation rather than end-to-end autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile manipulation of plant hardware. Even the most capable fielded mobile manipulator is limited to constrained, operator-initiated actions, which cannot support autonomous diagnosis and repair of shop machinery.

tasks.label: Teach basic skills, such as color, shape, number and letter recognition, personal hygiene, and social skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-group circle time in a preschool/pre-K classroom: teacher leads 12-20 three- to five-year-olds through calendar, color/shape/number/letter songs, flashcards and pointing at charts, calling on individual children, correcting answers, and continuously redirecting wandering or disruptive children.

Small-group / learning-center hands-on activity: teacher sits with 4-6 children at a table or on the rug, sets out manipulatives (color sorting bears, shape puzzles, counting cubes, letter tiles), demonstrates, hands materials to individual children, scaffolds each child's attempts, and adapts as children spill, grab, or lose interest.

One-on-one targeted practice with an individual child at a table: 5-15 minutes drilling and reinforcing a specific basic skill (recognizing the letters in the child's name, counting objects to ten, naming colors/shapes), with prompting, praise and error correction.

Handwashing routine instruction at the classroom sink: teacher demonstrates and coaches the steps (sleeves, soap, scrub, rinse, dry) for children arriving one at a time before snack or after toileting, checking technique and prompting the child until done correctly.

Other personal-care/hygiene instruction: teaching nose blowing with a tissue, coughing into the elbow, toileting hygiene, and self-help dressing steps, taught in the moment with demonstration and hands-on guidance for a 3-4 year old.

In-the-moment social-skills teaching during free play or on the fenced preschool playground: mediating a conflict over a toy, coaching turn-taking and sharing, labeling emotions, guiding a child to apologize or join a group, amid noise and several other children.

sources.developer: Vogt et al. / L2TOR consortium (Tilburg, Utrecht, Plymouth, Bielefeld, Koc)
sources.title: Second Language Tutoring using Social Robots: A Large-Scale Study (PDF)
sources.claim: In the L2TOR project a NAO robot delivered a series of seven one-on-one English vocabulary lessons (including counting/number words) to 5-6 year old preschool children in Dutch schools, running as a nearly autonomous tutor with a tablet interface.
sources.transferJustification: Teaching L2 vocabulary and number words to 5-year-olds is the same instructional act as teaching number/letter/color recognition: same age group, same school setting, same naming-prompt-feedback format, and no object manipulation beyond pointing and a tablet.

sources.title: Second Language Tutoring using Social Robots. A Large-Scale Study - Tilburg University Research Portal
sources.claim: The 194-child preregistered study found children acquired and retained the taught words from the robot tutor about as well as from a tablet application, i.e. measurable but modest learning gains from robot-delivered lessons.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: it measures learning outcomes of robot-delivered basic-vocabulary instruction to preschool-aged children, the closest measured analogue to teaching letter/number recognition.

sources.developer: MIT Media Lab (Personal Robots Group) with Affectiva
sources.title: Tega - Affectiva
sources.claim: MIT Media Lab's Tega, described as an autonomous social robot tutor for early-literacy and vocabulary activities, ran personalized one-on-one tutoring games with 34 children over two months in a local preschool.
sources.transferJustification: Early-literacy vocabulary and storytelling games with preschoolers exercise the same one-on-one basic-skill instruction (word/letter learning, prompting, feedback) in the same preschool setting as this task's individual practice instance.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens
sources.claim: The Keeko robot, described as autonomous, was adopted in several hundred Chinese kindergartens where it tells stories and poses logic problems to children, but operates as a teacher's aide whose content teachers prepare and upload, with the teacher still leading the class.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to group basic-skills instruction in an early-childhood classroom; it shows what deployed classroom robots actually do (story/quiz delivery alongside a teacher) rather than running the lesson.

sources.system: social robots in education (NAO, Pepper and similar; review)
sources.developer: Belpaeme et al., University of Plymouth / Ghent University
sources.title: Robots will never replace teachers but can boost children's education - University of Plymouth
sources.claim: A Science Robotics review of social robots in education concludes that technical limits, especially child speech recognition and social interaction, confine classroom robots to teaching-assistant or tutor roles rather than replacing teachers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly reviews robots doing the instructional task in question with children; used as negative evidence about whole-lesson, group-level teaching.

sources.developer: Amol Deshmukh, Mary Ellen Foster, Emily S. Cross (University of Glasgow)
sources.title: WallBo: A Social Robot for Fostering Hand Hygiene For Children (CHI EA '26)
sources.claim: WallBo is a low-cost social robot built to teach WHO handwashing technique to children at school sinks; its current iteration is reported to run fully autonomously, after earlier field studies that used teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Teaching WHO handwashing steps to children is exactly the personal-hygiene instruction named in this task, delivered at a school sink to children arriving one at a time.

sources.title: WallBo - The handwashing robot buddy - AI for Good, ITU
sources.claim: WallBo is described as an embodied tutor that uses privacy-preserving computer vision ... judge how well a child washes ..., assesses motor proficiency against WHO guidelines, and gives real-time adaptive scaffolding and verbal encouragement.
sources.transferJustification: Perceiving and correcting a child's handwashing technique is the substance of teaching the hygiene routine in a preschool washroom.

sources.title: Assessing Children's First Impressions of "WallBo" - A Robotic Handwashing Buddy (IDC '21)
sources.claim: Earlier WallBo school trials (one week, Scottish school, 16 pupils aged 6-7) raised handwashing compliance to about 86% and improved hygiene knowledge, but that generation of studies was teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Same hygiene-teaching task and school setting; recorded as teleoperated so it provides outcome context only and is not decisive for any positive judgment.

sources.developer: academic study reported in Early Childhood Research Quarterly
sources.title: Preschool children's engagement with a social robot compared to a human instructor
sources.claim: A study of 35 preschool children comparing a social robot instructor with a human instructor on early literacy/language tasks found children were behaviourally and emotionally more engaged with the human instructor.
sources.transferJustification: Direct comparison on the task in question (instructing preschoolers in early literacy) showing robot-delivered instruction falls short of a human teacher on engagement, the driver of preschool learning.

tasks.label: Establish and enforce rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Adapt teaching methods and instructional materials to meet students' varying needs and interests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide a variety of materials and resources for children to explore, manipulate, and use, both in learning activities and in imaginative play.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Before children arrive or between sessions, the teacher stocks and arranges the classroom's learning centers and activity tables: puzzles, unit blocks, manipulatives, books, dramatic-play props, pre-cut paper and markers set out at each seat, arranged as an inviting 'invitation to play' matched to the week's theme. Classroom layout is the teacher's own, shelves are low and crowded, objects are diverse in size, shape and material.

During a structured group activity, the teacher hands out and replenishes materials to 12-20 seated 3-5 year-olds: paper, glue sticks, safety scissors, paint cups, counting bears, instruments. She adjusts what each child gets, replaces dropped or used-up items, mops up spills, and keeps unsafe items away from the youngest children, all while children are moving and reaching.

Preparing messy/sensory exploration materials: filling a water or sand table, scooping rice/beans/pasta into bins, mixing and portioning playdough, laying out scoops, funnels, tweezers, magnifiers and natural loose parts on trays for a science or sensory station.

In-the-moment provisioning during free play: a child asks for a doctor kit or more tape, the teacher notices play stalling and fetches a new prop (fabric, cardboard tubes, animal figures) to extend imaginative play, swaps out a broken or unsafe toy, and retrieves items from high storage — all in an active room with children underfoot.

Providing materials outdoors on the playground, in a yard, or on a walk/field trip: carrying out bins of balls, chalk, sand toys, gardening tools and loose parts, distributing them, and collecting them again in variable weather and terrain, with the public or other groups sometimes present.

Periodic curation of the material collection: rotating toy and manipulative sets in and out of storage, inspecting for broken or unsafe pieces, washing and sanitizing toys, sorting mixed pieces back into labeled sets, and restocking consumables from a supply closet.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics™ | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick system autonomously picks a wide range of small, diverse items from mixed totes and places them into destination containers/cubbies for kitting and order fulfillment, at up to ~1,200 items/hour, and is commercially deployed (e.g., Staples fulfillment centers). This is the closest commercial analog to assembling and setting out sets of small preschool materials when the work is presented to the machine in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse piece-picking/kitting. Transfer: comparable objects (small, diverse, rigid or semi-rigid items of varied shape) and comparable precision (grasp from a bin, place into a specified compartment/tray), which is the manipulation core of stocking trays and bins of preschool materials — but demonstrated only inside an enclosed, purpose-built workcell with items presented in totes on conveyors.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm detects, selects and handles individual products of many shapes and sizes, moving them from one container into specific totes, and has been rolled out beyond pilot into fulfillment operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating and consolidating individual consumer goods. Transfer: the objects (varied everyday items) and the action (identify, grasp, place into a designated container) match the material-set assembly core of this task; environment is a fenced fulfillment-center workcell built around the machine.

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI meal-assembly robots autonomously portion and dispense loose and granular ingredients into trays moving on production conveyors, using vision to track trays; deployed in production at named food manufacturers, having assembled tens of millions of meals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic portioning of variable bulk food into trays. Transfer: filling a container with a measured quantity of loose granular material (rice, beans, pasta-like media) is the same manipulation problem as filling a sensory bin or portioning playdough; demonstrated on a purpose-built food production line.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi, the largest deployed fleet of mobile manipulators in human work facilities, autonomously navigates hospital corridors and delivers supplies and pharmacy items across 25+ US hospitals (1M+ deliveries). Its deployed competence is point-to-point fetch-and-deliver of contained items, not arranging many diverse loose objects on shelves or handing items to children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous supply delivery with a mobile manipulator inside a structured human facility (E2). It marks the ceiling of deployed E2 mobile manipulation: items are transported in totes and drawers, so it does not substantiate stocking learning centers with diverse loose materials or distributing supplies to children.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv:2504.16054)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 controls a mobile manipulator to tidy and clean kitchens and bedrooms in homes never seen in training, performing 10-15 minute multi-stage manipulation of everyday clutter. It is a research result with partial success rates, not a deployed or commercial system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up and putting away diverse household objects in unstructured rooms — the nearest analog to setting out and putting away toys in a classroom. It is demo-grade (partial success, slow, no deployment, no children present), so it cannot support worker-quality completion at E2 or E3.

sources.title: These tidying robots clean up toys, put Roomba to shame
sources.claim: Preferred Networks demonstrated fully autonomous room-tidying robots that recognize scattered toys, socks and stationery and use an arm to pick them up and put them away; reporting describes the demonstration as effective but very slow, and no commercial deployment followed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pick-and-place of toys in a furnished room. Objects match preschool materials, but throughput and reliability are far below a teacher's, and the demo was staged at an exhibition rather than deployed in a childcare facility.

tasks.label: Serve meals and snacks in accordance with nutritional guidelines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Family-style lunch in a center-based preschool classroom: teacher carries serving bowls, a milk pitcher and child-size plates to two low tables, sits with 8-10 three- to five-year-olds, passes each bowl, prompts each child to take at least one spoonful of each required component (grain, protein, fruit/vegetable), pours or supervises pouring of milk, offers seconds, converses through the meal, then has children scrape plates.

Mid-morning or afternoon snack for 15-18 children in the classroom: teacher retrieves the snack (crackers, cheese sticks, sliced fruit, water/milk) from the classroom cart or kitchenette, portions the CACFP-required components onto plates or napkins, fills small cups, distributes them around two or three tables, handles requests for seconds, wipes up spills and clears.

Center with a central kitchen: bulk hot pans, milk crate and fruit arrive on an insulated cart; the teacher/aide checks the posted menu against the meal-component/portion-size requirements and portions each child's serving (e.g., 1/4 cup vegetable, 1/2 oz grain) from the bulk pans onto individual plates or divided trays, loading the completed plates back onto the cart ready for service.

Allergy and special-diet service: teacher cross-checks the classroom allergy/diet roster and medical substitution forms, prepares and labels the substitute item (soy milk, nut-free spread, gluten-free grain), serves that child a separate plate away from cross-contact, monitors the table for food sharing during the meal, and records intake on the required form.

Hands-on assistance during the meal for younger or less skilled eaters: opening yogurt and milk cartons, cutting grapes and sandwiches, steadying cups, refilling water, scooping a serving for a child who cannot manage the serving spoon, wiping faces, hands and spilled food, and encouraging reluctant eaters to try each component.

Snack served outside the classroom: on the playground after outdoor play or at a park/field-trip picnic table, teacher carries a cooler and bag, portions fruit and crackers onto napkins on a bench or blanket, hands them out to children seated on grass or benches, manages wind, insects, dropped food and trash cleanup.

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-controlled robotic arms autonomously dispense accurate, weight-verified portions of cooked food into trays moving on a production line, deployed at multiple US/Canadian food manufacturers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portion-controlled meal assembly in food manufacturing. It covers the portioning-to-specified-serving-size element of serving meals per nutritional guidelines, with comparable foods (rice, pasta, vegetables, proteins) and finer portion precision than a preschool plate requires, but only on a fixtured conveyor line, not at a children's table.

sources.title: Chef Robotics launches its most advanced assembly robot yet - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The Chef+ meal-assembly robot uses a three-camera vision system to track conveyor speed and trays ... and is running in production at customer food-manufacturing sites.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (portion-controlled tray assembly); confirms current commercial deployment and that the work is presented to the machine on a conveyor with staff-loaded ingredient pans, i.e. a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Servi Q: The Compact Service Robot That Goes Where Others Can't — Bear Robotics
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots autonomously navigate dining rooms to run food and bus dishes in restaurants, hotels, senior living and hospitals; staff load the trays and diners take their own plates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting plated food to tables in a structured hospitality facility. It transfers only to the transport step of meal service; the robot has no manipulator, does not portion food, does not place plates in front of diners, and relies on diners self-serving from its trays, which preschoolers cannot do.

sources.system: School cafeteria cooking robots (Seoul/Gyeonggi education offices)
sources.developer: Korea Institute for Robot Industry Advancement / suppliers
sources.title: School hires robots as cafeteria chefs - The Korea Herald
sources.claim: Cooking robots are installed in South Korean school canteen kitchens to stir-fry, make soup and fry bulk school lunches, while human cafeteria staff continue to portion and serve the trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk food preparation inside an institutional school food facility. It shows automation reaching the kitchen side of school meals only; autonomy is not established and no cited step covers portioning to individual children or serving them at tables.

sources.title: VoicePilot: Harnessing LLMs as Speech Interfaces for Physically Assistive Robots
sources.claim: Commercial assistive feeding devices exist for individual diners, but the diner or caregiver commands each scoop and delivery via switches; the device serves one seated person from pre-loaded bowls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted eating. It is the closest commercial system to helping a child eat, but it is user-commanded (treated as teleoperated), pre-loaded by a caregiver, and serves one stationary diner, so it cannot support a positive judgment for classroom meal assistance.

tasks.label: Attend to children's basic needs by feeding them, dressing them, and changing their diapers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Diapering routine in a toddler/two-year-old classroom: lift a squirming child onto the changing table, unfasten and remove a soiled diaper, wipe and clean the child, apply cream, fasten a fresh diaper, re-dress the child, wash the child's hands, sanitize the table and log the change; repeated 5-10 times a shift on a licensed center's schedule.

Toileting support for children in potty training or after an accident: walk the child to a small bathroom, help pull pants and underwear down and up, wipe, help on and off the toilet, remove wet or soiled clothing, clean the child, dress them in spare clothes and bag the soiled items.

Snack and mealtime service and feeding assistance for a group of 8-16 children at low tables: serving portions family-style, opening cartons and packages, pouring, cutting food, spoon-feeding or bottle-feeding the youngest who cannot self-feed, watching for choking and allergies, wiping faces, hands and spills.

Dressing for outdoor play or weather: putting coats, hats, mittens, boots or shoes on 3-5 year olds who wriggle and resist, zipping and buttoning, tying shoes, and changing children into dry clothes after water play or a spill, done at a cubby area with children coming and going.

Other basic care through the day: wiping noses, applying sunscreen or lotion, adjusting clothing and shoes, tucking in and covering a child at nap time, comforting and holding a distressed child, and re-dressing after nap.

sources.title: Obi Robotic Feeding Device | School Health
sources.claim: Obi is a commercially sold robotic feeding device used in homes, schools and care settings, but each bite is commanded by the diner using accessibility switches rather than delivered autonomously to a passive care recipient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assistive feeding of a seated person. It bounds the preschool feeding instance because the device requires a cooperative diner who can operate a switch and hold position, unlike a toddler being fed by a teacher.

sources.system: Assistive Dexterous Arm (ADA) robot-assisted feeding system
sources.developer: Cornell EmPRISE Lab / University of Washington
sources.title: Lessons Learned from Designing and Evaluating a Robot-assisted Feeding System for Out-of-lab Use (ACM/IEEE HRI 2025)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted feeding evaluated with care recipients outside the lab autonomously handled only about half of meals at the >=80% bite level, with teleoperation needed otherwise, and with cooperative adults directing the system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: feeding a person bites of a meal. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to spoon-feeding a child; the reliability shortfall and the need for a still, cooperative recipient show it does not transfer to worker-quality feeding of toddlers.

sources.system: Force-modulated visual dressing policy on a robot arm
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: The best current robot-assisted dressing results are laboratory human studies in which a robot pulls a sleeve partway up a cooperative adult's arm, not complete dressing of a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing of a human limb. It maps directly onto putting coats and clothes on children, and shows only partial single-arm sleeve dressing on still, consenting adults has been achieved.

sources.title: Getting dressed with help from robots | MIT News
sources.claim: Researchers working on robot-assisted dressing note that a squirming young child is a harder, unmodeled case than the frail adults their systems target, and their work remains laboratory research.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot dressing of a person. It bounds the dressing and toileting instances by stating that unpredictable child motion lies outside the modeled operating conditions of these systems.

sources.title: Comparison of the Physical Care Burden on Formal Caregivers between Manual Human Care Using a Paper Diaper and Robot-Aided Care in Excretion Care (IJERPH)
sources.claim: The only fielded 'excretion care' robots are worn bidet-suction devices for bedridden adults that clean the perineal area in place; they do not remove and refit a diaper or handle a mobile child.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: excretion and incontinence care. It is the nearest deployed analogue to diapering, but it requires an immobile bedridden adult already wearing the device, so it does not transfer to changing a squirming toddler on a changing table.

tasks.label: Meet with parents and guardians to discuss their children's progress and needs, determine their priorities for their children, and suggest ways that they can promote learning and development.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Organize and lead activities designed to promote physical, mental, and social development, such as games, arts and crafts, music, storytelling, and field trips.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-group circle time in the preschool classroom: teacher gathers 15-20 three-to-five-year-olds on the rug, reads a picture book aloud while showing pictures, asks open-ended questions, leads songs, finger plays and movement rhymes, redirects children who wander or disrupt, and transitions the group to the next activity.

Arts-and-crafts activity at classroom tables: teacher gathers and sets out paint, glue, scissors, paper and smocks, demonstrates the process, moves between 4-8 children giving hands-on help (steadying scissors, opening glue, taping, writing names), manages spills and safety, then leads cleanup and displays the work.

Learning centers / table games and manipulatives: teacher sets up blocks, puzzles, sorting and matching games and dramatic-play props, rotates among small groups, scaffolds play with questions and prompts, mediates disputes over materials, and prompts cleanup at the end of the period.

Gross-motor / movement games on the fenced playground or in an indoor gross-motor room: teacher organizes running games, parachute, obstacle courses and dances; sets out equipment; supervises safety, watches for falls and rough play, comforts and checks injured children, and counts the group in and out.

Small-group teacher-directed exploration (science/sensory table, cooking or planting activity) with 4-6 children: teacher prepares materials, guides each step, gives hand-over-hand assistance, monitors mouthing/allergy hazards, and narrates to build vocabulary.

Off-site field trip (farm, zoo, library, fire station or neighborhood walk): teacher organizes supplies and permissions, loads children onto a bus or walks them on public sidewalks, holds hands at crossings, does repeated head counts in crowds, manages toileting and snacks, and leads the on-site activity.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens
sources.claim: Keeko, a small wheeled autonomous robot, has been sold into Chinese kindergartens where it tells stories and poses logic problems to young children; it is armless, works alongside teachers, and covers only a narrated/quiz segment rather than running a class period.

sources.title: 'It looks adorable and children love it': Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens
sources.claim: Scale of the Keeko kindergarten deployment: more than 600 kindergartens, used as an adjunct inside teacher-run classrooms rather than as a substitute leader of activities.

sources.developer: Jouen, Matsunaka & Hiraki (academic study, Int. J. Social Robotics)
sources.title: Once Upon a Time… Acquisition of Second Language Vocabulary Through Robotic Storytelling in Classroom Settings
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid told a story autonomously from a pre-scripted scenario to children in real classrooms, showing a robot can deliver a fixed narration segment but not select, adapt or manage the surrounding group activity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led storytelling to children in a classroom, the closest published analogue to leading circle-time storytelling. It covers only the narration sub-step, with teachers and researchers present and in charge of the group.

sources.developer: Oregon State University (Fitter, Logan et al.)
sources.title: Toddlers show increased physical activity with a robot playmate moving around the room
sources.claim: GoBot, a toddler-sized custom mobile robot, ran a simple autonomous keep-away routine that raised 2-3 year olds' physical activity in one-on-one playroom sessions with researchers present; it does not organize or supervise a group game.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-promoted gross-motor play with toddlers, the closest analogue to leading physical games. It shows only stimulation of one child's movement, not organizing, equipping or safety-supervising a group activity.

sources.date: 2021-08 product coverage; long-term in-school field study published 2025-12
sources.title: Robot tutors bring machine learning to the classroom
sources.claim: ABii is a commercially sold, desktop-sized autonomous robot tutor used in K-5 schools, delivering one-to-one adaptive math and reading lessons at a desk; it has no manipulator or mobility for leading classroom activities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered instruction to young children inside a school. It substantiates only seated one-to-one tutoring, not organizing and leading group games, crafts, music or field trips.

sources.system: socially assistive robot in an inclusive daycare (KIT ethnographic study)
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Rixen, Gerling, Bruno)
sources.title: Long-Term Integration of a Robot in an Inclusive Daycare: An Ethnographic Study Focused on Children and Caregivers
sources.claim: A four-month deployment of a socially assistive robot in ... found caregivers still had to integrate the robot into their own structures, and the authors note long-term practical integration in such settings remains largely unknown.

tasks.label: Assimilate arriving children to the school environment by greeting them, helping them remove outerwear, and selecting activities of interest to them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard morning drop-off in a preschool classroom or cubby hallway: teacher greets each arriving 3-5 year old and the parent by name at the door, takes/receives the backpack, helps the child pull off a light jacket and hang it plus the bag in the correct cubby, checks the folder/lunch, then walks the child to a table activity (playdough, puzzles, drawing) chosen to suit that child's current interest and settles them into it.

Winter arrival: child comes in wearing a heavy coat, hat, mittens, scarf, snow pants and boots; teacher kneels down, unzips and peels off the coat, removes wet boots and swaps them for indoor shoes, stows wet items to dry, manages a child who is off-balance, squirming or partly resisting, then steers the child to an activity.

Difficult separation: child arrives crying, clinging to the parent, or refusing to enter; teacher physically receives/holds or crouches with the child, offers comfort and reassurance, negotiates with the parent, removes the coat later once the child calms, and redirects the child to a favorite, calming activity while monitoring emotional state.

Warm-weather or staggered/late arrival: little or no outerwear; teacher greets the child mid-session, does a quick health/mood check, puts away the bag, and inserts the child into an activity already in progress or opens a new one matched to the child's interest, while continuing to supervise the rest of the group.

Curbside / car-line or lobby handoff on school grounds: teacher greets the family at the vehicle or entrance, unbuckles or receives the child, carries the bag, escorts the child indoors through the corridor to the classroom, then helps with outerwear and an opening activity.

sources.system: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing (CMU, CoRL 2025)
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Hao, Wang, Ravie, Hegde, Held, Erickson)
sources.title: Force-Modulated Visual Policy for Robot-Assisted Dressing with Arm Motions
sources.claim: Frontier robot-assisted dressing: a CMU system autonomously puts a long-sleeve garment onto the arm of a seated adult participant in a lab, adapting to arm motion; it is one-arm dressing of a cooperative adult, not undressing a young child.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing. It is the closest published capability to 'helping children remove outerwear'. Transfer fails: the demonstration is a lab rig with 12 consenting adults holding a seated pose, dressing (not removing) a single sleeve, whereas the task requires removing coats, boots and mittens from unpredictable, sometimes resisting 3-5 year olds in a classroom.

sources.system: Compliant gripper for robot-assisted trouser dressing-undressing
sources.title: Development of a Compliant Gripper for Safe Robot-Assisted Trouser Dressing-Undressing
sources.claim: Undressing assistance is still at the component-prototype stage: a specialized compliant gripper for trouser dressing/undressing of hemiplegic adults, evaluated in the lab, with no demonstration of whole-garment removal from a moving person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted undressing, the physical core of 'helping them remove outerwear'. It shows the state of the art is a gripper prototype for cooperative adults; autonomy is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment for removing a child's coat, mittens or boots.

sources.system: socially assistive robot deployed in an inclusive daycare (4-month deployment)
sources.title: Long-Term Integration of a Robot in an Inclusive Daycare: An Ethnographic Study Focused on Children and Caregivers (ACM/IEEE HRI 2026)
sources.claim: Robots that are actually placed in daycare and preschool rooms are socially assistive/tabletop platforms that talk, play and teach; they perform no physical handling of children or their clothing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot presence in a childcare facility. It bounds what is deployed in this exact environment - social interaction only - and provides no manipulation capability for outerwear or for physically escorting and settling an arriving child.

sources.system: NAO social robot in preschool classrooms
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics platform, used by education researchers (e.g., Crompton et al.)
sources.title: Preschool children's engagement with a social robot during early literacy and language activities
sources.claim: Social robots used with 3-5 year olds in preschool classrooms are stationary conversational/tutoring agents used in short lesson blocks alongside a teacher; greeting is verbal only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot greeting/interacting with preschoolers. It covers only the verbal greeting fragment; the robot cannot remove outerwear, hang belongings, escort a child, or judge and set up an activity, so it cannot complete any instance of this task.

tasks.label: Observe and evaluate children's performance, behavior, social development, and physical health.

tasks.label: Prepare materials and classrooms for class activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Before children arrive, the teacher sets out the learning centers in a licensed center or school classroom: blocks and figures on the block rug, puzzles and manipulatives in trays on low shelves, books faced out in the reading corner, dramatic-play props arranged, materials for the day's theme placed at each table. Dozens of varied small objects, some retrieved from closed storage closets, placed in child-accessible positions.

Preparing craft and art materials: cutting construction paper into shapes, precutting strips for a project, counting out and portioning crayons, glue sticks and scissors into per-child sets or table caddies, writing children's names on papers, laminating and trimming picture cards. Done at a work table or staff workroom, often the evening before.

Arranging the physical space: moving child-sized tables and chairs into activity groupings, clearing the floor for the circle-time rug, pushing furniture aside for gross-motor play, setting out and later stacking nap cots or mats. Heavier, low-precision work in a room with fixed built-ins and stored equipment.

Resetting and sanitizing the room between activities: clearing art supplies and dishes off tables, wiping and sanitizing tabletops before snack and after messy play, sweeping or vacuuming crumbs and scraps, spraying and washing mouthed toys. Done quickly, often while children are in the room or just out of it.

Preparing sensory and messy-play materials: mixing or warming playdough, pouring tempera paint into cups and loading easels, filling the water table, filling sensory bins with rice, sand or beans, mixing paste, portioning shaving cream or goop into trays. Bulk, wet and granular media measured into containers.

Preparing wall displays and visual aids: backing and bordering bulletin boards, stapling up letters, charts and calendars, mounting and hanging children's artwork, posting picture schedules and labels at child eye level around the classroom. Work on vertical surfaces spread around the room, often standing on a stool.

sources.developer: Princeton/Stanford/Columbia (Wu et al.), Autonomous Robots journal
sources.title: TidyBot: personalized robot assistance with large language models | Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: TidyBot, an autonomous mobile manipulator, picks up diverse household objects in real rooms and puts them in designated places, but succeeds on only 85% of objects — research-grade, not worker-quality reliability for arranging a room.
sources.transferJustification: Tidying is the inverse of setting out learning-center materials: both require picking many varied small objects and placing each at a designated spot in a room. The cited 85% success in controlled test rooms bounds what is achievable in an as-found classroom.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking cells are deployed across Staples' North American fulfillment centers, picking diverse office and school supply items from presented bins into totes at fixtured stations.
sources.transferJustification: Order-picking of pens, glue sticks, paper and similar school/office items into totes is the same physical operation as counting out and kitting classroom supplies or filling activity trays: varied small objects presented in bins, placed into designated containers.

sources.system: Zünd S3 cutter with robotic arm
sources.title: Fachpack 21 - Zünd demonstrates digital cutting at an industrial level
sources.claim: A Zünd digital cutting system paired with a robot arm cuts sheet and board material, and the robot automatically removes the cut parts and deposits them at predefined ..., as a commercial production configuration.
sources.transferJustification: Cutting paper and card shapes for craft activities and laying the pieces out in defined positions is the same operation as digital cutting of cardboard/paper sheets plus robotic off-load to predefined positions.

sources.title: Zünd Sheet Feeder | Fully automatic material feed
sources.claim: Zünd's automatic sheet feeder loads paper, film and dense cardboard sheets onto the cutting table with suction cups and collects cut parts and waste on an off-load table, converting the cutter into an unattended production machine.
sources.transferJustification: Separating and handling single paper sheets from a stack is the material-handling step of preparing cut craft materials; suction-cup sheet feeding is the purpose-built equivalent of a teacher pulling sheets from a ream.

sources.system: Chef Robotics meal assembly robot / Chef+
sources.title: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly | AgFunderNews
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' meal-assembly robots are deployed at food manufacturers (Amy's Kitchen, Sunbasket, Chef Bombay, Cafe Spice), autonomously scooping and depositing many different ingredients in varying portion sizes into trays on a line; over 40 million meals served.
sources.transferJustification: Portioning wet, sticky and granular food into trays on a fixtured line is the same manipulation problem as portioning paint into cups, scooping playdough, or filling sensory bins with rice: bulk deformable media dispensed by measure into presented containers.

sources.title: Trusted, Integrated Commercial Robotic Solutions for Schools | SoftBank Robotics America
sources.claim: SoftBank Robotics' Whiz autonomous vacuums are deployed in US school districts — two units at an elementary school and ... since 2022 — cleaning school floors autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous vacuuming in schools covers only the floor-cleaning fragment of resetting a classroom; it does not clear or wipe tables or wash toys, so it cannot carry the whole reset instance.

sources.title: UVD Robots Deploys Nation's Largest Fleet of Autonomous Disinfection Robots to a School District | Business Wire
sources.claim: UVD Robots' mobile, fully autonomous UV-C disinfection robots were deployed as a 37-robot fleet across a New Mexico school district to disinfect classrooms.
sources.transferJustification: Room disinfection substitutes for part of sanitizing a classroom, but the robot performs no manipulation: it neither clears nor physically wipes tables and toys, covering only a fraction of the reset instance.

sources.title: Table Cleaning Robot Tried at Hawker Centers - Weston Robot
sources.claim: Weston Robot's table-cleaning robot — a LiDAR-navigating AMR base with a 6-DOF arm holding cloths — autonomously drives to tables, checks for items on them, and mops the surfaces; trialled in a Singapore hawker centre with the national environment agency.
sources.transferJustification: Wiping tables before snack or after art is the same operation as hawker-centre table mopping — a flat, known-height surface wiped with cloths — but the trial status and inability to clear objects restrict it to cleared, uniform tables.

sources.developer: HKUST (Guangzhou) — Bi, Zhang, Chen, Zhao, Li, Ma
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator
sources.claim: ALORE demonstrates a legged manipulator autonomously rearranging large objects such as chairs, ... specified target positions and orientations in indoor test scenes.
sources.transferJustification: Rearranging classroom tables and chairs for an activity is exactly the demonstrated task class (chairs, tables and bins moved to target poses); the demonstration is in controlled indoor test scenes with targets specified in advance.

sources.title: RoboMill – Assembler Edition » Industrial Robotics
sources.claim: A commercial robotic cell automates the assembly and stapling of wooden furniture frame parts, replacing the manual assemble-and-staple operation in production.
sources.transferJustification: Positioning flat parts on a fixtured backing and stapling them is the mechanical core of assembling a bordered bulletin-board display; the cell performs placement plus stapling autonomously on presented workpieces.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid | The Robot Report
sources.claim: General-purpose home humanoids marketed for chores still depend on remote human operators, and no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end to end autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Setting up and resetting rooms full of varied objects is the chore class these humanoids target; continued teleoperation dependence is direct evidence that as-found room preparation is not autonomous at E2 or E3.

sources.title: Building Services Contractor Bee Clean Deploys BrainOS-Powered Tennant Robotic Scrubbers at Canadian Polytechnical Institute | Brain Corp
sources.claim: BrainOS-powered Tennant T7AMR robotic scrubbers are deployed by a building-services contractor to clean floors at a Canadian polytechnic institute, issuing proof-of-clean reports after each shift.
sources.transferJustification: Autonomous scrubbing in an educational facility covers the floor portion of resetting a classroom; it requires clear open floor and addresses neither tables, toys, nor materials.

tasks.label: Arrange indoor and outdoor space to facilitate creative play, motor-skill activities, and safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily setup and reset of indoor activity centers in a preschool classroom: putting out art supplies, blocks, puzzles, books, manipulatives and dramatic-play props at the right tables and shelves, restocking bins, and re-sorting scattered materials between activity blocks so each center is ready for the next group of 3-5 year olds.

Periodic rearrangement of the classroom's physical layout: moving child-size tables, chairs, shelving units, easels, cots and area rugs to create or reconfigure learning centers, open floor space, and clear sightlines (start of year, thematic changes, or when a center isn't working).

Outdoor play-yard setup and takedown on a fenced center playground: hauling out and positioning tricycles, balls, sand and water toys, cones, tunnels and portable climbers; distributing them across the yard for varied motor play; collecting and storing them afterward, in whatever weather the day brings.

Setting up indoor gross-motor/motor-skill activities: clearing an open area in the classroom or multipurpose room and laying out floor mats, pop-up tunnels, balance beams, bean-bag targets, hoops and tape lines to form an obstacle course, then breaking it down.

Safety arrangement and hazard checks of indoor and outdoor space: scanning for and removing choking hazards, broken or splintered toys and debris; wiping spills; checking that shelves and heavy furniture are stable/anchored, exits and pathways clear, playground surfacing and equipment intact and not overheated; fixing or reporting what is found.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Digit, a humanoid robot, is in full-time commercial deployment at GXO's warehouse, autonomously picking totes on and off mobile robots, loading conveyors and stacking containers at floor locations — bulk object transport and placement in a structured, robot-oriented workcell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse tote handling. Transfers to placing bulky play-material containers and equipment at designated floor/shelf positions when items are presented in known poses, as an E1 setting would present them; it does not transfer to a cluttered occupied classroom.

sources.title: Amazon's tiny robot drives do the heavy lifting - Amazon Science
sources.claim: Amazon's Hercules drive units autonomously lift and transport heavy shelving pods to precise positions in fulfillment centers whose floors are laid out specifically for the robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving heavy inventory pods to specified floor locations. Comparable to repositioning shelving units and tables to marked positions when the room is laid out for the machine (fiducials, standardized furniture, no people present).

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick system autonomously picks and places a wide range of small, heterogeneous items into totes for kitting workflows in fixtured fulfillment cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking/kitting of diverse small goods. Transfers to distributing small play materials (blocks, puzzle pieces, markers) into fixed bins/stations when items and destinations are fixtured and presented, as at E1.

sources.title: Harvey - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: Harvest Automation's HV-100 autonomously locates, transports and organizes potted plants into spaced layouts both indoors and on outdoor nursery fields marked with reference tape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor spacing/organizing of uniform containers. Shows autonomous outdoor object distribution to a target layout when the ground area is prepared for the robot, comparable to distributing standardized play equipment across a prepared yard at E1.

sources.title: How BMW is Using Figure AI Humanoid Robots in Production
sources.claim: Figure 03 humanoids run Helix vision-language-action policies in BMW's Spartanburg logistics hall, manipulating parts and repositioning their bodies to pull heavy wheeled carts alongside human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: factory logistics part handling and cart moving. Supports moving wheeled furniture/carts and handling rigid objects in a standardized facility, but the demonstrated repertoire is fixed-station part flow, not arbitrary room re-layout.

sources.title: TidyBot: Personalized Robot Assistance with Large Language Models (arXiv:2305.05658)
sources.claim: TidyBot, an autonomous mobile manipulator using LLM-derived preferences, picks up scattered objects in real rooms and puts them away, succeeding with 85% of objects at roughly 15-20 seconds per object.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying / putting objects away. Nearest analog to resetting classroom materials; its 85% per-object success and slow cycle time fall well short of a teacher's reset of a room, so it supports capability only in fixtured settings, not a working classroom.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (π0.5)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 model let a mobile bimanual robot perform multi-step cleanup (putting items in drawers, dishes in the sink, wiping spills) in homes never seen in training, while still making frequent semantic and physical mistakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: open-world household tidying. Shows the current research frontier for arranging objects in human spaces taken as found; the developer's own caveat about frequent mistakes shows it is not at worker quality for a licensed childcare room.

sources.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor
sources.claim: Consumer home humanoids marketed for household chores in 2026 still depend on human teleoperators for complex tasks rather than autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household object handling in human-occupied rooms. Establishes that the leading in-home mobile manipulator is teleoperated, so it cannot support positive judgments for arranging occupied human spaces.

tasks.label: Teach proper eating habits and personal hygiene.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Handwashing routine coaching in a center-based preschool classroom/washroom: before snack and meals and after toileting or outdoor play, the teacher stages 15-20 three-to-five-year-olds at low sinks, rolls sleeves, adjusts water, scaffolds each step verbally and by demonstration, uses hand-over-hand guidance for the youngest or resistant children, dispenses soap/towels, checks results and reinforces the habit, all amid classroom traffic and noise.

Mealtime/snack instruction at family-style tables: teacher sits with the children, models and guides passing bowls and serving with tongs/spoons/small pitchers, corrects utensil grip and cup handling (often physically repositioning fingers), teaches chewing with mouth closed, napkin use, trying new foods and self-serve portions, prompts clean-up and face/hand wiping, and manages spills, refusals, allergy and choking safety.

Planned group lesson on nutrition and hygiene at circle time or in learning centers: reading a book about germs or food groups, singing a handwashing song, running a Glo-Germ/glitter demonstration, brushing a model mouth's teeth, sorting food-group cards, or a tasting/cooking activity, while keeping a group of 15-20 preschoolers engaged, seated and safe with materials.

Incidental hygiene coaching spread through the day: teaching and prompting nose blowing with tissues, covering coughs with the elbow, keeping hands out of mouths, toileting hygiene (wiping, flushing, redressing, with hands-on help for some children), toothbrushing after lunch, and tidying clothing, delivered one-on-one in close physical proximity as situations arise.

Individualized coaching and family partnership for a specific child (extreme picky eater, sensory food aversion, refusal to wash or brush): implementing a step-by-step desensitization plan hands-on at snack and at the sink over weeks, documenting progress, and demonstrating the routine for the family at a conference or Head Start home visit in the family's own home.

sources.title: WallBo - The handwashing robot buddy - AI for Good (ITU)
sources.claim: WallBo is a wall-mounted 'embodied tutor' (screen, camera, speaker, edge computer) that autonomously assesses a child's handwashing technique against WHO steps and gives adaptive on-screen and verbal coaching; piloted at school washrooms in the UK and India. It performs no physical action - it only displays motions on a screen - so under the rating rule it is not a robotic system, and it covers only the prompting part of the handwashing instance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is prompting/coaching hand hygiene at a school sink; cited as the closest system to instance 1, but it neither manipulates soap, water, towels nor guides children's hands, so it cannot complete the preschool routine.

sources.developer: University of Glasgow / Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham
sources.title: Pepe: A social robot that teaches hygiene skills - Embracing The World
sources.claim: Pepe, a low-cost social robot mounted above a handwashing tap in a Kerala primary school, increased handwashing with soap, but researchers drove its interactions by tele-operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is teaching children handwashing technique at a school tap; it is teleoperated and non-manipulating, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of the preschool handwashing instance.

sources.title: School District Deploys Classroom Robots - Industrial Equipment News
sources.claim: Movia Robotics' Kebbi, a small humanoid educational robot, was deployed as a 'teacher's aide' at Shawsheen Preschool in Andover, MA, running lesson content mainly one-to-one with autistic students alongside a human educator; it delivers speech, expressions and gestures but no object manipulation or physical assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robot-assisted instruction of preschoolers; relevant to the circle-time lesson instance, but it works with individual children on scripted lessons under a teacher and cannot run hands-on hygiene/nutrition activities or manage a group.

sources.title: Day care facilities test robots as high-tech solution to alleviate staffing shortages - The Japan Times
sources.claim: Childcare robots actually fielded in nurseries are monitoring devices: Global Bridge Holdings' bear-shaped Vevo greets and identifies children and records temperatures, with cot sensors tracking naps; it does not teach or physically assist with eating or hygiene routines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic support inside a childcare facility; it establishes that fielded nursery robots perform sensing/greeting only, not mealtime or hygiene instruction.

sources.title: FEAST: A Flexible Mealtime-Assistance System Towards In-the-Wild Personalization (arXiv 2506.14968)
sources.claim: FEAST is a state-of-the-art robot mealtime-assistance system that feeds, gives drinks and wipes the mouth of a seated adult care recipient in the home, with a fixed wheelchair/table-mounted arm and user-issued commands; it represents the frontier of robotic mealtime manipulation and does not instruct anyone or handle mobile children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is physical mealtime assistance; cited as the ceiling of robot capability at a table. It serves one stationary consenting adult and cannot model family-style serving or correct a preschooler's utensil grip, so capability does not transfer.

tasks.label: Demonstrate activities to children.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Circle-time / group-time demonstration of a movement or song activity in the classroom: teacher models a finger-play, action song, dance, stretching or imitation game ("do it like this") for 10-20 three-to-five-year-olds seated on the carpet, pacing and repeating the motions so children can copy them.

Art and craft demonstration at the art table with a small group: teacher shows how to hold and cut with child scissors, spread glue, load a brush and paint, roll/press play-dough, tear and paste collage paper, narrating each step and then handing materials to the children.

Table-top manipulative / pre-academic / sensory demonstration: modeling how a puzzle piece fits, how to build and balance a block tower, how to sort or count counters, how to trace and form a letter, or how to scoop and pour water, sand or rice at the sensory or science table.

Self-care and hygiene skill demonstration: teacher models handwashing at the child-height sink, zipping/buttoning a coat, using a fork or spoon, opening a lunch container, blowing a nose, often kneeling beside a child and repeating the motion slowly.

Classroom routine and clean-up demonstration: showing children how to put toys back in labelled bins, push in chairs, wipe the table with a sponge, and set out cups and napkins for snack, modeling the sequence before the children take over.

Outdoor playground or indoor gym gross-motor demonstration: teacher models throwing/catching a ball, tossing a beanbag into a hoop, hopping on one foot, running an obstacle course, climbing steps to a slide or pedaling a trike, on the school's fenced playground.

sources.system: NAO robot dance tutor (Ros, Baroni & Demiris)
sources.developer: Imperial College London / La Salle - Universitat Ramon Llull
sources.title: Adaptive human-robot interaction in sensorimotor task instruction: From human to robot dance tutors - Universitat Ramon Llull
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid was programmed to act as a dance tutor that autonomously instructs and demonstrates dance sequences to children, tested with 12 children over 18 sessions inside a hospital (an institution-controlled human facility).
sources.transferJustification: Near-identical task: the robot demonstrates a movement activity to a child and guides imitation, which is what a preschool teacher does when modeling an action song or dance at circle time.

sources.developer: MIT Media Lab Personal Robots Group
sources.title: Meet Tega, the New Robot in School | MIT Alumni Association
sources.claim: The Tega social robot ran autonomous story and learning-activity sessions with young children weekly for three months in 12 Massachusetts kindergarten classrooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously leading a structured learning activity with preschool/kindergarten children in their own school; establishes that autonomous social robots can run activity sessions with this age group inside real classrooms.

sources.developer: Peking University EPIC Lab et al.
sources.title: ScissorBot: Learning Generalizable Scissor Skill for Paper Cutting via Simulation, Imitation, and Sim2Real
sources.claim: ScissorBot is a learning-based robot system that autonomously cuts curves in paper with scissors mounted on a robot arm, with the paper hung and its top edge fixed in a purpose-built rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting paper along a line with scissors is the physical core of a preschool scissors demonstration; same objects (paper, child-scale scissors) and comparable precision, but only shown with the paper fixtured in a lab rig.

sources.title: Gemini Robotics: Google DeepMind's New AI Models for Robots - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Gemini Robotics driving the bimanual ALOHA 2 arms performed fine paper craft and other delicate tabletop manipulations, including folding a sheet of paper into an origami ..., in laboratory workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous paper folding and fine object handling on a fixed workcell table is the manipulation core of craft and manipulative demonstrations (folding, placing pieces, handling small materials).

sources.title: pi-0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: The pi-0.5 vision-language-action model let a mobile manipulator autonomously tidy kitchens and bedrooms — picking up and putting away objects — in real homes that were not in its training data.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting objects away and wiping surfaces in a lived-in room is the physical content of a preschool clean-up routine demonstration (toys into bins, wiping the table), with comparable objects and lower precision demands.

sources.title: FRIDA: A Collaborative Robot Painter (project page)
sources.claim: FRIDA is a robot arm with a paintbrush that plans and executes paintings on a canvas, optimizing its brush-stroke plan from visual feedback in a laboratory setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: brush painting on a mounted canvas is the physical core of a painting demonstration; the robot loads and applies a brush with comparable materials, but only at a fixed easel in a lab.

sources.developer: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham and University of Glasgow
sources.title: Handwashing robot helps schoolkids make a clean break with bad habits - University of Glasgow
sources.claim: The Pepe hygiene robot installed by school washrooms did not physically perform handwashing; it was teleoperated to speak to pupils and direct their attention to a poster of the handwashing steps.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system to a hygiene-skill demonstration for children; cited to show that even this system was teleoperated and screen/poster-based rather than physically modeling the skill, supporting a negative judgment.

tasks.label: Plan and conduct activities for a balanced program of instruction, demonstration, and work time that provides students with opportunities to observe, question, and investigate.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-group circle/meeting time in the classroom: teacher gathers 12-20 three- to five-year-olds on the rug, leads calendar, songs, a read-aloud and discussion, introduces the day's investigation question, fields spontaneous child questions, redirects wiggling/off-task children, and manages transitions to the next block.

Teacher-led small-group demonstration and hands-on investigation (e.g., sink-or-float water tub, planting seeds, mixing paint colors, simple cooking): teacher sets out real materials, demonstrates a technique with hands and tools (scissors, droppers, measuring cups), prompts children to predict and question, scaffolds each child's turn, keeps hazards controlled, and leads cleanup.

Free-choice work/center time: teacher circulates among block, dramatic-play, art, sensory and manipulative centers, joins play, asks extending questions, resolves conflicts over materials, redirects unsafe behavior, replenishes and rotates supplies, and records anecdotal observations of individual children.

Outdoor playground or large-motor room activity: teacher leads movement games, obstacle courses, or a nature/observation walk around the fenced yard, adapts the activity to weather and children's energy, and supervises safety across a spread-out, mobile group.

Planning and preparing the balanced weekly program before/after children arrive: writing developmentally appropriate lesson plans tied to state early learning standards, then gathering, cutting, labeling and arranging materials and learning centers in the classroom for the planned instruction, demonstration and work-time blocks.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens
sources.claim: Keeko, a small autonomous wheeled robot, is deployed in Chinese kindergarten classrooms where it tells stories and poses logic/puzzle challenges as a teaching assistant, with the human teacher running the class and handling the materials and children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering a story/puzzle segment to young children in a kindergarten. It bears on 'conduct activities' only for the verbal, screen-mediated portion; Keeko is armless, does not set out or demonstrate with physical materials, does not plan the program, and does not manage group behavior or safety, so it does not substantiate completion of a whole activity block.

sources.title: Robot education peers in a situated primary school study: Personalisation promotes child learning
sources.claim: Two autonomous NAO-type robots were embedded as learning companions in primary school classrooms for two weeks without experimenter supervision, delivering narrow personalized tutoring interactions while the classroom teacher remained responsible for the class.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot-led tutoring inside a real school classroom. It shows autonomy is achievable for a scripted one-to-one learning game, but the robot handles no physical materials, leads no group, and the teacher supervises, so it does not carry over to conducting a preschool instruction/demonstration/work-time block.

sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics (study by Australian university researchers)
sources.title: Preschool children's engagement with a social robot compared to a human instructor
sources.claim: In a preschool study, a NAO social robot instructed 4-year-olds one-to-one in Simon Says and iPad drawing tasks; children were measurably less engaged with the robot instructor than with a human instructor, indicating below-worker-quality delivery even for these narrow activities.

sources.title: US Firm's Humanoid Robot Teaching Assistant to Support 500 Students in 2026
sources.claim: The frontier US school deployment of an embodied AI teaching assistant is Realbotix's Optio plus an M-Series humanoid at a New York district, providing conversational tutoring and homework support to high school students, not conducting hands-on activity blocks with preschoolers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: embodied AI assisting instruction in a US school. It marks the current commercial ceiling — a stationary conversational avatar/humanoid for teenagers — and shows no system conducts materials-based early-childhood activity blocks.

sources.system: Humanoid intelligent robot in human-robot collaborative teaching system
sources.title: Effects of a human-robot collaborative teaching approach on preschoolers' social-emotional competence and learning behaviors
sources.claim: A 2025 preschool social-emotional learning study built the robot into a human-robot collaborative teaching system, with the humanoid robot and the human teacher jointly delivering the activities rather than the robot conducting them alone.
