tasks.label: Organize and label materials and display students' work in a manner appropriate for their ages and perceptual skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily/after-activity reset of the classroom: gathering blocks, puzzle pieces, manipulatives, books, dress-up clothes, crayons and art scraps left on floors and tables and returning each to its designated labeled bin, tub or low shelf so materials stay accessible at child height; done in 10-20 minutes in a room with children, furniture and spills present.

Making and affixing labels: printing or drawing picture-plus-word labels and photos of contents, cutting and laminating them, and taping or velcroing them onto bins, shelf edges, cubbies, hooks and center signs at child eye level so nonreaders can find and return materials.

Displaying children's work: selecting paintings, collages and writing samples, backing/trimming them, adding name and dictation captions, and mounting them with staples, tape, pins or clothespins on bulletin boards, walls, doors and hallway displays at children's eye level in a legible arrangement.

Pre-class preparation of learning centers: assembling trays and caddies of art supplies, paper, scissors, glue, playdough and sensory items, restocking shelves, and rotating themed toy sets in and out of storage bins so each center holds the right materials and quantities for the age group.

Periodic rotation of displays and materials: taking down mounted artwork without tearing it (pulling staples/pins, peeling tape), filing pieces into individual portfolios and cubby folders to send home, boxing seasonal materials into labeled storage, and installing the new display.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual diverse products, picking a single item from a tote of mixed items and placing it into a designated tray, inside a fenced robotic workcell in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating and sorting heterogeneous small goods into designated containers. Transfers to organizing classroom materials into labeled bins when, as at E1, items are presented in totes and bins are fixtured; object size, weight and grasp variety are comparable to blocks, puzzle pieces and manipulatives.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout
sources.claim: Sparrow has run in production at an Amazon facility, singulating items from mixed totes and placing them into trays, and was ready for wider rollout.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above, with sustained production use rather than a demo, establishing worker-rate reliability for presented-work sorting.

sources.system: FE Technologies Bookmatic Automated Materials Handling System
sources.date: product page accessed 2026; library AMH in service since the 2010s
sources.title: AUTOMATED MATERIALS HANDLING – FE Technologies
sources.claim: Automated materials handling systems installed in libraries identify returned items and sort them into large numbers of designated destination bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting labeled educational materials into destination bins by machine-read label. Transfers to sorting and putting away classroom materials when items are fed to a purpose-built sorter, which is the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: Figure Humanoid Robots Sort Packages Non-Stop in 24/7 Demo
sources.claim: Three Figure 02 humanoids running Helix 02 sorted tens of thousands of packages over a roughly 40-hour continuous livestreamed warehouse run, fully autonomously with no teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: long-duration autonomous handling and sorting of varied rigid and flexible items at a fixed station. Supports E1-style sorting of assorted materials presented to the machine, not in-situ classroom work.

sources.title: Figure's Humanoid Robot Picks Up Toys, Wipes Surfaces in New Demo
sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 was shown autonomously tidying a living room — collecting scattered toys and blocks into containers, wiping a surface, tossing a pillow — in a company demonstration rather than a deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest in-situ analogue to resetting a classroom; cited as the state of the art for picking up toys in a room, but it is a minutes-long staged demo in a company-controlled living room, not sustained worker-quality room resets.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: The pi0.5 vision-language-action model controls a mobile manipulator to clean ... homes not seen during training, performing multi-stage tidying behaviors, with partial success rates reported.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting household objects away in unfamiliar rooms. Relevant to in-situ classroom organizing, but reported performance is partial and slow, so it evidences the frontier rather than worker-quality completion.

sources.title: Self-adhesive label printer-applicator - Legi-Air 6000 - Weber Marking Systems
sources.claim: Industrial print-and-apply labelers autonomously print and apply pressure-sensitive labels ... passing cartons on a production line at high rates and with accurate placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: generating a label and adhering it to a specified spot on a container. Transfers to labeling classroom bins and tubs when, as at E1, the containers are conveyed to the labeling station; object type and placement precision are comparable.

sources.title: Robot Labeler | TOPPAN Infomedia Inc.
sources.claim: A robot arm automatically applies printed labels to taught surfaces and locations on packages, cardboard boxes and containers, with layouts varying per item, and verifies them with a reader mounted on the arm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic placement of per-item-variable labels at taught positions on containers. Transfers to affixing picture/word labels to bins and shelf parts presented to a robot cell.

sources.title: The Rise of Robotics: Automating Wide Format Print Production
sources.claim: Durst's P5 Robotics uses two KUKA arms and a registration station to pick single sheets from a stack — including thin stock such as foil paper — and place them in exactly the right position, running unmanned for a full production shift.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: single-sheet picking of thin, floppy paper and precise registered placement onto a board. Combined with adhesive label application, this covers the physical acts of mounting children's paper work in a planned layout on a fixtured display panel at E1.

tasks.label: Prepare reports on students and activities as required by administration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Collaborate with other teachers and administrators in the development, evaluation, and revision of preschool programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Plan and supervise class projects, field trips, visits by guests, or other experiential activities and guide students in learning from those activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classroom hands-on project: teacher plans an art/sensory/science/cooking activity, preps and sets out materials (paint, glue, scissors, dough, water table), distributes them to 15-18 three-to-five-year-olds at tables, circulates to assist small hands, prompts learning talk, mediates disputes, manages spills and safety, leads cleanup and a closing discussion.

Multi-day/project-based investigation on site (planting and tending a garden bed, block-building study, classroom pet or life-cycle observation): teacher sequences the work over days, gathers materials, supervises rotating small groups, documents with photos/dictation, and guides reflection at circle time.

Guest visit in the classroom or center gym (firefighter, dentist, parent, musician, community helper): teacher arranges the visit, preps children on expectations, seats and settles the group, keeps preschoolers attentive and safe around the guest and equipment, facilitates questions, and leads a follow-up activity linking the visit to learning goals.

Outdoor experiential activity on center grounds (playground nature hunt, weather walk, sand/water exploration, garden visit): teacher supervises a whole group outdoors within the fenced center property, tracks head counts, manages climbing/traffic and conflicts, and guides children's observations and vocabulary.

Off-site field trip (zoo, farm, library, fire station, neighborhood walking trip): teacher plans logistics and permission slips, loads children on a bus or walking rope, keeps continuous head counts among crowds and traffic, handles toileting, upsets and lost items, guides children's attention and learning at the destination, and returns everyone safely.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid ('Sally') with Optio AI teaching assistant
sources.title: Humanoid robot enters New York classroom | ETIH EdTech News
sources.claim: Realbotix has begun a pilot placing a conversational M-Series humanoid and its Optio AI teaching assistant in a New York school ...; the robot converses and tutors under teacher oversight, with no reported manipulation of materials or supervision of children.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed system to 'guiding students in learning activities' in a school; cited to show the frontier is conversational tutoring under teacher oversight, not planning/supervising projects, handling materials, or escorting children.

sources.title: Android teachers invade kindergartens in China, but can they replace human educators?
sources.claim: Keeko, a small armless wheeled autonomous robot used in Chinese kindergartens, tells stories and poses logic problems to young children; it has no arms and does not handle materials or supervise groups.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading a learning activity with preschoolers. Cited because it is an autonomous early-childhood classroom robot, yet it is armless and stationary-scale, so its performance does not transfer to setting up projects, assisting children with materials, or supervising outings.

sources.system: Avatar robots for classroom activities (Kawata et al. field trial)
sources.developer: Osaka University / Ishiguro lab and collaborators
sources.title: Encouraging classroom activities for children using avatar robots: a field trial (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: Avatar robots used to assist whole-classroom activities with children are operated by remote human operators in rotation, i.e., teleoperated rather than autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supporting/encouraging children's participation in classroom activities. It shows that even partial support of group activities currently requires continuous human teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: Social robots for education (NAO, IROBI and similar platforms)
sources.developer: Various (review by Belpaeme et al., Science Robotics)
sources.title: Social robots for education: A review | Science Robotics
sources.claim: A review of social robots in education characterizes their demonstrated role as tutors or peer learners in constrained learning interactions, not as supervisors of group projects or outings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led instruction of children. Establishes that the demonstrated capability envelope is one-on-one or small-group tutoring dialogue, with no evidence of material handling, behavior management, or child supervision.

tasks.label: Meet with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Select, store, order, issue, and inventory classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: A carton delivery of classroom supplies arrives at the child-care center or school; the teacher unpacks mixed items (construction paper, tempera paint, glue sticks, crayons, wipes, snack items, manipulative sets), sorts them and stores them on classroom shelves, in labeled bins, and in locked upper cabinets for hazardous items, rotating older stock forward, before or after class hours.

Issuing materials for the day's activities in a classroom in session: portioning paint into cups, dividing playdough, laying out paper, scissors, glue and snack cups at each activity table/center, and handing out replacement or extra items to 3-5 year-olds on request while children move about the room.

Daily/weekly restock and cleanup of classroom centers: replenishing paper towels, tissues, wipes and art paper; returning toys, blocks and manipulatives to their labeled shelves and bins at cleanup; pulling broken or unsafe items and sanitizing shared materials.

Periodic physical inventory of classroom cabinets and the center's supply closet: counting and checking stock (partially used paint bottles, remaining paper reams, sets with missing pieces), noting condition/expiration, and recording counts on a paper form or app for the director.

Selecting and ordering: reviewing curriculum plans and inventory results, choosing age-appropriate, safe, developmentally suitable items from vendor catalogs within a budget, preparing a requisition for director approval, and checking arriving deliveries against packing slips.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan arm autonomously picks and stows a wide variety of individual items into compartments of inventory pods in production fulfillment centers, escalating to a human when it cannot handle an item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stow. Storing preschool supplies is the same act of placing heterogeneous small goods (bottles, boxes, paper, packaged items) into designated storage compartments; Vulcan handles comparable object diversity and precision, but only in a fixtured pod cell.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: Independent assessment: robotic pick-and-place of items of varying fragility and weight is in production deployment, but the deployed system works in a humanless, purpose-built zone with fixtured pods and minimal mobility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse picking/stowing. Establishes both that heterogeneous item handling is production-grade and that it is confined to environments engineered around the machine (E1).

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon Sparrow autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products of many types before packaging, in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating and transferring individual goods into totes/containers. This is the kitting equivalent of assembling and issuing a set of classroom materials when the items are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage shelves in about 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, with remote operators taking over only to recover from errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking inside a human-run facility (E2). It marks the frontier: only uniform bottles/cans on a purpose-built rail-mounted cooler shelf, not mixed classroom supplies on arbitrary shelving.

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe’s Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously navigates grocery stores and captures shelf-level inventory data (availability, pricing, placement), now deployed across 17 Harmons stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking inventory of shelved goods in a human facility. Transfer is limited: Tally counts barcoded, planogrammed retail facings, not partially used, unlabeled classroom supplies in opaque bins.

sources.title: Autonomous warehouse drones streamline inventory control | TechTarget
sources.claim: Verity's fully autonomous indoor drones perform inventory counting audits in operating warehouses, replacing manual counts of thousands of storage locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical stock counting and discrepancy reporting. Carries over to inventorying supplies only when stock sits in labeled, machine-readable locations and people are absent — the E1 arrangement.

sources.title: The SmartStore Vending Program: Industrial Vending for the Masses
sources.claim: Fastenal's industrial vending/SmartStore cabinets mechanically dispense supplies to authorized workers, track every transaction, and trigger automatic replenishment orders when stock runs low.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing supplies to workers and reordering. It shows machine issue-plus-reorder works only when items are loaded into the machine's own fixtured slots — a purpose-built (E1) arrangement.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators autonomously transport supplies and pharmacy items between departments in more than 25 US ..., over a million deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving supplies through an institutional building (E2). It substantiates autonomous transport of supply bins among people, but not unpacking, shelving, portioning or counting them, which Moxi does not do.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: Independent assessment of room tidying (placing loose items and toys into their proper locations): the most complete system, Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5, is judged only 'validated in lab' with imperfect first-try reliability and no commercial deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting toys and loose objects back where they belong. Directly comparable to classroom cleanup/restocking; the assessment shows it is not yet at deployable worker quality in as-found rooms.

tasks.label: Provide students with disabilities with assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restroom/toileting assistance for a 3-5 year-old with a disability in the preschool bathroom: escorting or wheeling the child in, transferring them onto the toilet or changing table, managing clothing and diapers/pull-ups, wiping and hygiene, hand washing, and returning them to the activity - with the child sometimes resistant, crying, or physically dependent.

Setting up and handing over assistive technology in the classroom: retrieving the child's AAC tablet or speech device, mounting it on a wheelchair tray or table stand, powering it up and opening the right vocabulary page, placing switches/adapted utensils/pencil grips within reach, re-presenting the device after the child drops or throws it during circle time or centers.

Positioning the child in adaptive equipment: lifting or guiding the child into an adaptive chair, stander, prone wedge, corner seat or gait trainer, fastening trunk/hip straps and footplates, checking alignment and comfort, and repositioning several times across the day per the physical therapist's plan.

Assisting access to facilities and mobility around the building: guiding a child using a walker, crutches, or wheelchair through classroom doorways, hallways, ramps, the cafeteria, and out to the fenced playground; holding doors, clearing toys and other children out of the path, steadying the child on steps and playground equipment.

Sensory and health-support devices: putting on and adjusting a weighted vest, noise-cancelling headphones, glasses, orthotic braces or an FM/hearing-aid transmitter; checking devices are on and fitted, and removing them when the child becomes distressed.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulator, performs fetch-and-deliver of supplies inside hospitals at commercial scale, showing autonomous item transport in a structured human facility but not personal care or fitting devices to a person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous retrieval and delivery of small items inside an institution. It bounds what deployed mobile manipulators do - transporting objects between fixed points - and shows no capability for mounting a device on a child's tray, fitting it, or handling a child's body.

sources.title: WHILL - Winnipeg Airports Authority
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs carry mobility-impaired travellers along fixed routes through airport terminals and return themselves; passengers board and alight by themselves and staff handle transfers and screening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a person with limited mobility through a facility. Transfer is limited: the rider is a self-boarding, self-directing adult on a mapped route, whereas the preschool instance requires lifting/steadying a small child, clearing a toy-strewn classroom, and continuous supervision.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: General-purpose home/care humanoids remain far from autonomous whole-task performance; the NEO humanoid intended for household assistance relies on teleoperation for real tasks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household/personal assistance around people. It establishes that the most capable humanoids doing person-centred chores are teleoperated, so they cannot support positive judgments for hands-on child care.

sources.developer: University of York Institute for Safe Autonomy / Honda Research Institute / TU Delft
sources.title: New dressing robot can 'mimic' the actions of care workers - TechXplore
sources.claim: A bimanual robotic dressing-assistance scheme was demonstrated in a laboratory, with one arm supporting the person's hand while the other puts a garment on the arm; it remains a research prototype tested on cooperative adult participants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing, the closest published capability to clothing management during toileting and to putting on vests or braces. It is a lab sub-step with a still, cooperative adult, far from managing a wriggling preschooler's clothing at worker quality.

sources.title: Yueban Xiaoban is a self-driving robot toilet for people with limited mobility
sources.claim: A self-driving robot toilet that drives to a mobility-impaired user and locks in place was unveiled at a 2026 assistive-devices expo; it relocates the fixture but does not transfer, undress, wipe or dress the user.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: toileting support. Even this most-targeted product only repositions a fixture for a self-transferring adult; it performs none of the caregiver acts (lifting, clothing management, cleaning) the preschool instance requires.

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as hall and cafeteria monitoring and bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hallway and transition duty: a preschool teacher supervises a line of 12-18 three-to-five-year-olds moving between classroom, restroom, gym and playground — physically redirecting wanderers, holding hands, zipping coats and fixing shoes, separating pushing children, keeping the group clear of doors and stairs, and reporting a child who is missing or hurt.

Cafeteria / lunchroom duty: monitoring preschoolers eating in a cafeteria or multipurpose room — opening milk cartons and containers, cutting or repositioning food, watching for choking and allergen exposure, wiping spills and faces, prompting and helping with tray/table cleanup, and calming disputes.

Bus and car-line loading/unloading at arrival and dismissal: escorting small children across a school driveway or loading zone, helping them up bus steps, fastening harnesses or car-seat buckles, verifying the adult picking up is authorized and signing the child out, in weather, traffic noise and parent crowding.

Arrival greeting and outdoor/playground supervision duty: receiving children at the door, taking backpacks and coats, doing quick health/wellness checks, then scanning a play yard for climbing, falls and conflicts and intervening physically (lifting a child down, first aid for a scrape).

Miscellaneous coverage duties: monitoring the nap room, restroom or an adjacent classroom during staff breaks, escorting an individual child to the office or nurse, and covering a colleague's group for short periods.

sources.title: Florida School Deploys Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot is deployed on a school campus, where it patrols autonomously as a sensor platform that detects and reports; it does not supervise, handle or physically assist children.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to 'hall monitoring' found in search: autonomous patrol/monitoring of an institutional campus. Capability does not transfer — the robot observes and escalates and has no manipulators, so it cannot redirect, dress, buckle or physically protect preschoolers.

sources.title: Cobalt intelligent indoor security robot | Security Info Watch
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot patrols human office facilities autonomously along fixed routes, but human interaction and issue handling are performed by a remote human pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor corridor monitoring in a structured facility. Does not transfer to preschool hall/cafeteria duty because exceptions are handled by a remote human pilot and the robot performs no physical caregiving of children.

sources.title: Promobot Announces the First-Ever Childcare Robot
sources.claim: The only 'childcare robot' deployment found in a daycare is an autonomous service robot that answers questions, provides navigation and entertains children; it performs no supervision, physical assistance or safety intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue in a preschool/daycare setting; capability does not transfer to monitoring duties because the robot is an information/entertainment kiosk on wheels with no ability to manage or physically assist a group of small children.

sources.title: Don't miss the bus: BCSC uses new robot to demonstrate safety rules
sources.claim: The only school-bus-related robot in schools is 'Buster the School Bus,' a remote-controlled animated prop used to teach bus safety, not a system that loads or unloads children.
sources.transferJustification: Directly adjacent to bus loading/unloading duty, but it is a teleoperated educational puppet; it cannot escort, buckle or release children and so supports no positive judgment.

roles.title: Kindergarten Teachers, Except Special Education
roles.description: Teach academic and social skills to kindergarten students.

tasks.label: Establish and enforce rules for behavior and policies and procedures to maintain order among students.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare children for later grades by encouraging them to explore learning opportunities and to persevere with challenging tasks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Instruct students individually and in groups, adapting teaching methods to meet students' varying needs and interests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Teach basic skills, such as color, shape, number and letter recognition, personal hygiene, and social skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Demonstrate activities to children.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Art/craft and fine-motor demonstration: at the art table or under a document camera, the teacher shows 5-20 five-year-olds how to cut along a line with child scissors, spread glue, fold paper, tear, tape, string beads or color inside lines, narrating each step and repeating slowly for children who missed it.

Literacy/numeracy demonstration: modeling letter and number formation stroke by stroke on a whiteboard, chart paper or worksheet; showing how to use counters, unifix cubes, pattern blocks or a ten-frame; holding a big book and tracking print with a finger while children watch from the carpet.

Movement, music and gross-motor demonstration: leading a hand-motion song or finger play, showing dance steps, stretches, jumping-jack style warm-ups, or how to play a circle/PE game or use playground equipment, with children copying the motions.

Routine and self-care demonstration: showing how to wash hands at the child sink, use a tissue, zip a coat and use the 'flip trick', tie shoes, carry a lunch tray, sit criss-cross, walk in line in the hallway, and pack a backpack/cubby.

Cleanup and materials-management demonstration: modeling how to put blocks and toys into labeled bins, stack chairs, wipe a table with a sponge, sharpen a pencil, close markers, and return center materials to the shelf.

Science/sensory demonstration: pouring water or sand between containers at the sensory table, planting a seed in a cup of soil, mixing paint colors, dropping food coloring into water, or handling a simple magnet/balance-scale investigation while children watch.

sources.developer: Italian Institute of Technology (CONTACT unit) / University of Genoa
sources.title: Who will you imitate? Studying reciprocal influence in children-robot groups during an imitation game
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid, running programmed behaviors, led a motor-imitation ('mime the action' / music) game with groups of four schoolchildren in a real school classroom: it stated the rules, named each action and performed its own version of the gesture for children to copy; children matched the robot's standard gestures in 98.6% of music-game trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading a gesture-imitation/dance game. It is the same act as demonstrating a movement activity to children - the robot performs the motions in front of a group of children in a classroom and the children copy them - so performance carries over to hand-motion songs and warm-up routines.

sources.title: UBtech Alpha Mini 2 - Terra-Robotics
sources.claim: Alpha Mini is a commercially sold small humanoid used as a classroom teaching aid that walks, dances and performs exercise routines with its head, arms, legs and ..., i.e. it can physically model movement activities for children to imitate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing dance/exercise routines in front of children in classrooms. Modeling body movements for children to copy is exactly the movement-demonstration instance; the objects (none) and precision required are the same.

sources.developer: EPFL CHILI Lab and INESC-ID/GAIPS, Univ. of Lisbon
sources.title: A social robot to enhance children's handwriting skills
sources.claim: The CoWriter system is an autonomous robot-child handwriting system in which a NAO physically produces written letters/words with a stylus on a tablet during one-to-one sessions with children; a human facilitator is typically present in the sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted handwriting practice. The robot's physical act - forming letter shapes with an arm on a writing surface while a child watches - is the same act as demonstrating letter formation, with the same objects (stylus/writing surface) and precision.

sources.title: Kids learn to write by teaching robots | Teaching & Learning
sources.claim: CoWriter was trialled with young schoolchildren in ordinary primary-school classrooms, showing the robot operating in a school setting with children of near-kindergarten age.
sources.transferJustification: Same as the CoWriter item above: it establishes the setting (school classroom, 6-8 year olds) in which the robot's letter-writing demonstration occurred.

sources.title: Are Google's New Gemini Robotics Models the Key to Smarter, More Adaptable Robots?
sources.claim: Gemini Robotics, a vision-language-action model, controls bimanual arms to carry out long-horizon, highly dexterous paper-manipulation tasks such as folding an origami fox on a laboratory workbench, autonomously and responsive to spoken instructions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous paper folding at a bench. Kindergarten craft demonstrations use the same deformable materials (paper) and comparable precision, so a system that folds paper autonomously could perform a paper-craft demonstration at a presentation station.

sources.developer: Peking University EPIC Lab and collaborators
sources.title: ScissorBot: Learning Generalizable Scissor Skill for Paper Cutting via Simulation, Imitation, and Sim2Real
sources.claim: ScissorBot is a learned policy that lets a robot arm hold and operate scissors to cut curves accurately on paper that is hung with its top edge fixed, trained in simulation and transferred to real hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting paper along a drawn line with scissors - the core physical act of a kindergarten cut-and-paste demonstration - performed with the same tool and material, but only with the paper fixtured for the machine.

sources.system: pi-0 (π0) generalist robot policy on mobile and fixed bimanual manipulators
sources.title: Our First Generalist Policy (π0)
sources.claim: The pi-zero generalist policy autonomously performs multi-step tidying and object-handling tasks, including bussing a table by putting dishes in a bin and ..., packing a bag, and folding laundry, in uncut single-policy runs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing a table and sorting items into bins. This is the same physical act as demonstrating classroom cleanup (placing toys/materials into labeled bins, clearing a table), with comparable object sizes and precision.

sources.developer: University of Bremen / research group (published in Springer LNCS)
sources.title: Accurate Pouring with an Autonomous Robot Using an RGB-D Camera
sources.claim: An autonomous pouring system on a PR2 robot tracks liquid level with an RGB-D camera and adjusts the pour rate to fill a cup to a specified height, demonstrated in repeated laboratory trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: controlled liquid pouring into a container. Demonstrating a water-table or measuring activity to children requires the same act with the same containers and tolerances, performed at a table where the vessels are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens
sources.claim: Keeko, a 45-60 cm wheeled screen-faced robot, has been placed in more than 600 Chinese kindergartens where it presents stories, songs and logic games to young children; content is loaded by the teacher and the robot has no manipulator arms.
sources.transferJustification: Context only: shows commercial robots operating inside kindergarten classrooms, but Keeko has no arms and delivers screen/audio content, so it cannot substantiate physical demonstration of an activity.

tasks.label: Read books to entire classes or to small groups.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Guide and counsel students with adjustment or academic problems or special academic interests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Observe and evaluate children's performance, behavior, social development, and physical health.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide a variety of materials and resources for children to explore, manipulate, and use, both in learning activities and in imaginative play.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Before children arrive (or between rotations), the teacher sets up learning centers in the classroom: pulls labeled bins from shelves and the supply closet, and lays out counting bears, pattern blocks, puzzles, magnifiers, books, letter tiles and writing tools on low tables and rug areas so each center is ready for use.

During a whole-group or small-group lesson the teacher hands out materials to 18-24 seated five-year-olds: dry-erase boards and markers, ten-frames and counters, glue sticks, safety scissors, playdough balls, then walks the room passing out extras and swapping broken or incorrect items while the lesson proceeds.

Between sessions the teacher refreshes and rotates the imaginative-play areas: restages the dramatic-play corner (dress-up clothes on hooks, kitchen props, doctor kit), returns unit blocks to their shaped shelf outlines, sets out puppets and small-world figures for a new theme.

While children are actively engaged in imaginative play, the teacher responds in the moment: fetching more blocks, tape, paper tubes or fabric that a child requests for a construction, offering a new prop to extend a play scenario, and moving among moving children in a crowded room.

Preparing messy/sensory and art activities: pouring tempera paint into cups, filling the water/sand table, portioning clay or playdough, setting out brushes, paper, aprons and sponges at the art table so children can freely explore the media.

End-of-activity reset and replenishment: sorting a jumble of mixed manipulatives, crayons, game pieces and loose parts back into their labeled bins, restacking books, and restocking consumables (paper, glue, markers) from the storage closet for the next day.

sources.title: pi_0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 model drives a mobile manipulator that autonomously tidies kitchens and bedrooms in homes never seen in training, picking up clothing and objects from floors and surfaces and putting them away; the developers state the system is far from perfect and often makes mistakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying / putting objects away. It is the closest published analog to arranging and putting away assorted classroom objects in an unstructured, people-occupied room; cited to show the state of the art above E1 is research-grade (10-15 minute horizons, frequent errors), below teacher reliability.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and transfers individual products of widely varying shape and size between totes inside fenced fulfillment-center workcells, at production scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating and transferring assorted small goods. Classroom manipulatives, books, art supplies and game pieces are comparable in size, weight and variability to warehouse items, and the placement precision required (into a tray or labeled bin) is comparable or lower.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick cells autonomously pick items from mixed-SKU totes and place each item into the correct order cubby of a put wall, i.e. commercial robotic kitting of assorted items into per-recipient trays inside a fixtured cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking and put-wall kitting. Assembling per-child or per-center trays of manipulatives and supplies from bulk bins is the same operation with comparable objects and tolerances; sorting mixed items back into labeled bins is its inverse.

sources.system: Blendid / Jamba by Blendid robotic kiosk
sources.title: More California colleges install Blendid robotic smoothie kiosks
sources.claim: Blendid operates enclosed autonomous robotic kiosks on US college campuses that assemble and dispense made-to-order food and beverages, handling cups, portioning and pouring liquids, and presenting the finished item to the person who comes to the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: enclosed robotic cell that portions and pours liquids into cups and presents finished items to people who approach it. Supports the E1 rendering of paint-cup and sensory-media preparation and of handing prepared material sets to users at a fixtured station.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators run autonomously in more than 25 US ..., fetching and delivering supplies and medications through corridors and elevators; this deployed institutional mobile manipulation is point-to-point transport rather than arranging assorted loose objects on tables and shelves.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous supply fetch-and-deliver inside an institutional building. Shows what deployed E2 mobile manipulation actually covers (tote and bag transport) and, by contrast, that setting out and putting away many loose small items in an occupied room is not yet covered.

sources.title: Our First Generalist Policy (pi-0)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0 policy autonomously folds laundry, grasping, flattening and stacking deformable clothing, using either a fixed pair of arms or a mobile robot, shown in uncut video from a single autonomous policy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of deformable garments at a fixed workstation. Dress-up clothes and fabric props in the dramatic-play area are comparable deformable objects with lower precision requirements than neat folding.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid with Optio AI tutor
sources.title: US Firm's Humanoid Robot Teaching Assistant to Support 500 Students in 2026 | eWeek
sources.claim: Humanoid robots entering US classrooms in 2026 are conversational tutoring platforms: the Realbotix school pilot places an embodied AI that answers questions and reinforces lessons, with no demonstrated handling of classroom materials.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as context on the robots actually placed in classrooms as of 2026: stationary social/tutoring systems with no object handling, so no cited system supports an E2 classroom judgment for this task.

tasks.label: Maintain accurate and complete student records and prepare reports on children and activities as required by laws, district policies, and administrative regulations.

tasks.label: Establish clear objectives for all lessons, units, and projects and communicate those objectives to children.

tasks.label: Plan and conduct activities for a balanced program of instruction, demonstration, and work time that provides students with opportunities to observe, question, and investigate.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-group instruction block in the kindergarten classroom: ~20 five-year-olds on the rug for calendar, phonics, or an interactive read-aloud; teacher holds up a big book/chart, points to text, uses pocket-chart cards and manipulatives, poses questions, calls on children, and continuously manages attention and behavior.

Teacher-led hands-on demonstration followed by guided practice: teacher lays out materials and models a procedure (sink/float tub, planting seeds in cups, mixing paint colors, cutting and gluing a shape collage, counting bears on a ten-frame), then children replicate it while the teacher monitors safety (scissors, water, small parts) and corrects technique.

Work-time / learning-center rotation: teacher sets up 4-6 centers (blocks, sand-water table, writing, art, math bins), distributes materials, sets timers, circulates to question and scaffold investigation, redirects off-task or conflicting children, handles spills and toileting requests, and runs cleanup and transition.

Small-group guided instruction at a kidney table: 5-6 children with differentiated literacy or math manipulatives (letter tiles, counters, decodable books) while the rest of the class works independently; teacher prompts, observes, adjusts difficulty on the fly, and takes informal assessment notes.

Planning and material preparation in the classroom/workroom: sequencing a balanced day of instruction, demonstration and work time against state standards, then copying, cutting, laminating, sorting and bagging manipulatives into center bins and labeling trays.

Outdoor or off-classroom investigation: leading the class on a neighborhood nature walk, schoolyard garden bed planting, or playground gross-motor/observation activity, carrying and distributing clipboards and magnifiers while keeping 20 children together and safe.

sources.title: Realbotix to Deploy First Humanoid Robot and AI Teachers Assistant in U.S. School District
sources.claim: The most advanced 2026 humanoid deployment in a US public school is a conversational teacher's assistant/tutor plus an M-Series humanoid used for engagement; it supports teachers with high-school STEM students and does not handle classroom materials or run instruction blocks itself.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system to 'conducting instruction' in a real school; cited to show the deployed role is conversational assistance to a human teacher, with no material handling or whole-class conduct.

sources.system: Social robots in education (NAO, Pepper, iPal, Keeko, Snow and 38 other models)
sources.developer: various (SoftBank Robotics, Aldebaran, AvatarMind, Keeko and others)
sources.title: Social robots for education: a global analysis of deployments in real scenarios
sources.claim: A 2026 documentary analysis of 206 real social-robot deployments across 28 countries (including kindergartens) finds their functions are edutainment, entertainment, teaching programming, and psychological support - not conducting a teacher's instructional program.

sources.system: Social robots in education (survey of deployed models)
sources.title: Social robots for education: a global analysis of deployments in real scenarios
sources.claim: The same 2026 review reports that current educational robots remain limited in interpreting social cues, speech recognition, and selecting appropriate actions for learners - the core competencies needed to conduct a responsive kindergarten activity.

sources.system: Social robots for education (NAO and similar tutoring robots)
sources.developer: Belpaeme et al. (Ghent/Plymouth), SoftBank Robotics hardware
sources.title: Social robots for education: A review | Science Robotics
sources.claim: A large review and meta-analysis of social robots as educators concludes robots do well only on restricted topics and are expected to assist, not replace, a human teacher.
sources.transferJustification: Robot tutoring of children is the nearest related task to conducting kindergarten instruction; the review shows scope is limited to narrow, pre-scripted content delivered beside a human teacher.

sources.title: Efficacy of a Robot-Assisted Intervention in Improving Learning Performance of Elementary School Children with Specific Learning Disorders
sources.claim: A controlled school intervention using the NAO robot with elementary children reported recurring technical failures despite efforts to maximize the robot's autonomy, indicating child-facing robot lessons are not yet reliable enough to stand in for a teacher.
sources.transferJustification: Robot-delivered lessons to school children is the related task; reliability shortfalls there carry over to conducting kindergarten instruction, which demands higher robustness with younger, less predictable learners.

tasks.label: Confer with parents or guardians, other teachers, counselors, and administrators to resolve students' behavioral and academic problems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Organize and lead activities designed to promote physical, mental, and social development, such as games, arts and crafts, music, and storytelling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-class circle time in the kindergarten classroom: teacher gathers ~20 five-year-olds on the rug, reads/tells a story with props and voices, pauses to ask comprehension and prediction questions, calls on children, redirects wandering or disruptive children, and closes with a shared activity.

Arts and crafts session in the classroom: teacher pre-cuts and lays out paper, paint, glue, scissors and manipulatives, demonstrates the steps, distributes materials to tables, circulates to help individual children hold scissors, spread glue, and fix mistakes, manages spills, then runs cleanup and displays work.

Music and movement block: teacher hands out rhythm sticks/shakers, leads songs with gestures and a keyboard or recording, teaches a simple dance or fingerplay, keeps tempo, adapts when children lose interest, collects and stores instruments.

Gross-motor games in the gym, multipurpose room, or school playground: teacher sets out cones, balls, or a parachute, explains rules, forms teams, demonstrates the movement, referees turns, supervises safety (falls, collisions, equipment misuse), and packs up.

Small-group / learning-center rotation and structured play in the classroom: teacher sets up 4-5 centers (blocks, dramatic play, sensory table, puzzles, writing), rotates groups on a timer, joins groups to scaffold play and language, mediates sharing conflicts, and resets materials between rotations.

sources.system: Social robots used in education (NAO/Pepper-class platforms, as reviewed)
sources.developer: Multiple (review published in Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Frontiers | Social robots: a meta-analysis of learning outcomes
sources.claim: A 2025 meta-analysis of social robots in education reports that speech recognition and perception with young children remain inaccurate, so studies frequently substitute Wizard-of-Oz teleoperation for genuine autonomous deployment.

sources.system: NAO humanoid robot (storytelling in classroom settings)
sources.developer: Aldebaran / SoftBank Robotics (study by university researchers)
sources.title: Once Upon a Time… Acquisition of Second Language Vocabulary Through Robotic Storytelling in Classroom Settings
sources.claim: In classroom second-language storytelling studies with young children, the NAO robot acts as a teacher assistant delivering prerecorded stories with songs and motor activities, alongside a human teacher who runs the class.

sources.system: Autonomous robot learning companions (NAO with 'sandtray' touchscreen)
sources.developer: Plymouth University / L2TOR-affiliated researchers (Baxter et al.)
sources.title: Robot education peers in a situated primary school study: Personalisation promotes child learning
sources.claim: Two autonomous robots ran as one-on-one touchscreen-based learning companions inside primary school classrooms for two weeks without experimenter supervision; the role is individual tutoring, not leading a whole class activity.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led one-on-one tutoring games in a school classroom. It shows autonomous child-facing operation is possible in an E2 school setting, but the interaction is a seated screen-mediated dialogue with a single child, with no materials handling, group management, or safety supervision.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid ('Sally') with Optio AI tutor
sources.title: US firm to deploy humanoid robot teaching assistant in New York schools
sources.claim: A 2026 US school pilot places a humanoid robot plus AI tutor in classrooms explicitly as a teaching assistant supporting teachers, with high school students, not as an activity leader for young children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: embodied AI assisting classroom instruction. It is the most recent US school humanoid deployment, but it serves high school students in a supporting role, so it does not substantiate a robot organizing and leading kindergarten activities.

sources.developer: Oregon State University (CoRIS Institute, Fitter/Logan labs)
sources.title: Robot buddies encourage children to stay physical activity - Earth.com
sources.claim: GoBot, a custom mobile assistive robot, elicited physical activity from young children using a simple autonomous routine that matched a teleoperated condition for engagement; it moves to prompt children rather than organizing and running a rule-based group game.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-prompted physical play with young children. It is the closest system to leading movement games, but it only elicits following/chasing behavior from individual children under adult supervision, with no rule explanation, turn refereeing, equipment setup, or safety supervision of a class.

sources.system: Pepper social robot group activity sessions
sources.title: Promoting activity in long-term care facilities with the social robot Pepper: a pilot study
sources.claim: In a long-term care pilot, the Pepper robot led seated group activities only with healthcare professionals continuously present to keep the environment calm and safe.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot leading a group song/exercise activity in an institutional facility. It is the strongest 'robot leads a group' evidence, but participants are cooperative adults, staff remain present throughout, and the robot neither distributes materials nor manages behavior.

tasks.label: Meet with parents and guardians to discuss their children's progress and to determine their priorities for their children and their resource needs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Use computers, audio-visual aids, and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-group circle-time lesson at the interactive whiteboard/projector: teacher wakes the classroom computer, opens a phonics or calendar slideshow, advances slides, plays short audio/video clips, calls individual 5-year-olds up to touch or write on the board, and keeps ~20 children seated and attending on the carpet.

Read-aloud / story time supplemented with AV and props: teacher projects the book pages via document camera or a digital book, reads aloud with expression, holds up and manipulates puppets, picture cards or flannel-board pieces, and pauses to ask comprehension questions and respond to children's answers.

Hands-on math or science lesson: teacher demonstrates counting bears, ten-frames, pattern blocks or a science object under a document camera projected to the class, then sets out and distributes bins of manipulatives to tables, circulates to help, and collects materials afterward.

Music-and-movement or listening-center activity: teacher plays songs or a movement video through speaker/screen, hands out scarves, shakers or headphones, models the movements with the class, and manages children moving around the room.

Before/between lessons, empty or nearly empty classroom: teacher connects laptop or document camera to the projector/flat panel by cable, powers the display on, cues up the slideshow or video, checks sound level, and pulls charged tablets from the charging cart onto a tray for the next activity.

Mid-lesson equipment handling with the whole class present: passing out and collecting tablets/headphones to seated children, adjusting volume, re-pairing or restarting a frozen device or unresponsive smartboard while continuing to hold the group's attention.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens
sources.claim: Keeko, a small autonomous wheeled robot with a screen face and no arms, was deployed in several Chinese kindergartens telling stories and posing logic problems to children as a teacher's assistant; it presents content on its own screen and cannot handle books, props, or classroom AV equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed system to 'using AV to supplement a presentation' in a kindergarten: it delivers narrated screen content to young children in a real classroom, but it is armless and only supplements a human teacher, so it cannot run the teacher's media-supported lesson or handle equipment and materials.

sources.title: RoboBuddy in the Classroom: Exploring LLM-Powered Social Robots for Storytelling in Learning and Integration Activities
sources.claim: RoboBuddy, an LLM-powered social robot, ran teacher-designed storytelling and language activities with 27 children (mean age 6.4) at an international school for one week, but teachers controlled the prompts and every generated utterance required human approval before reaching the robot; the robot performed no manipulation of classroom materials.
sources.transferJustification: Represents the state of the art for robot-delivered, media-supplemented lesson content with kindergarten-aged children; the human-in-the-loop control and total absence of object handling show the frontier falls short of a teacher running an AV-supplemented lesson.

sources.system: AppMuTT connector-mating framework on an industrial robot arm
sources.title: AI-based Framework for Robust Model-Based Connector Mating in Robotic Wire Harness Installation
sources.claim: An AI-based framework autonomously performs precise electrical connector mating (search and insertion under force and visuotactile control) for wire-harness installation in an industrial robot cell, running as programs on standard industrial controllers at millimetre tolerance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: plugging an HDMI/USB cable into a laptop, document camera or projector is a connector-mating insertion of comparable size and precision; with the devices fixtured and the cable presented, as an E1 setting would present them, the capability transfers.

sources.system: KUKA KR AGILUS machine tending cell (Waybo pre-engineered cells)
sources.title: Robotic Machine Tending Cells for CNC Automation | KUKA Canada
sources.claim: Commercial fenced machine-tending cells run unattended: a KUKA KR AGILUS picks blanks from an infeed conveyor, regrips them precisely in a squaring fixture, waits for the machine cycle, then unloads the finished part and cleans the fixture.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking rigid presented objects from a known infeed, placing them precisely and operating machine controls is the same class of action as taking charged tablets from a rack onto a tray and pressing a display's power button when the equipment is fixtured and presented at E1.

tasks.label: Meet with other professionals to discuss individual students' needs and progress.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Instruct and monitor students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injuries and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Art and fine-motor materials in the classroom: teacher demonstrates safe scissor grip, glue/paint/marker use and cap replacement at tables of 4-6 five-year-olds, circulates during the activity, physically corrects grips, redirects a child running with scissors, and supervises returning materials to labeled bins.

Learning-center manipulatives, books and blocks: teaching and enforcing handling and cleanup routines (no throwing blocks, turning pages carefully, sorting counters into trays), monitoring 20+ children across centers, and stepping in when a tower is about to topple onto someone or a book is being torn.

Classroom technology and shared equipment: instructing children to carry tablets/Chromebooks with two hands, plug and unplug headphones and chargers, use the listening center, and monitoring for dropped or mishandled devices during a 20-minute rotation.

Playground, gym and gross-motor equipment during recess/PE on school grounds: teaching slide, climber, ball and scooter rules; scanning a moving group of kindergartners outdoors; physically catching, steadying or separating children to prevent falls and collisions.

Higher-hazard or messy activities: sensory bins, water/sink routines, science and cooking activities, class pet or plant care; instruction on careful handling and cleanup, close-proximity supervision, immediate physical removal of a hazard (spill, broken item, small part in a child's mouth).

Off-campus field trip or bus: instructing children in careful use of borrowed or unfamiliar equipment (museum exhibits, farm tools, seat belts, walking rope) in a setting the school does not control, and monitoring the group closely to prevent injury or damage.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens
sources.claim: Keeko, an autonomous small mobile robot deployed in Chinese kindergartens, tells stories and poses logic problems to children; it is armless and does not handle classroom materials, demonstrate tool use, or supervise children's safe handling of equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed classroom robot working with kindergarten-age children. Cited as negative context: its demonstrated scope (verbal storytelling and quizzes, no arms) excludes instructing or monitoring children in the use and care of physical equipment, so capability does not transfer to this task.

sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics / Thomas Sievers (Univ. of Lübeck)
sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom
sources.claim: Field testing of the humanoid social robot Pepper as a teaching assistant with children from kindergarten age upward in German schools concludes that current robotic systems are not robust enough for autonomous continuous use in ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid robot acting as a classroom teaching assistant with children including kindergarten age. Cited as negative context — even the purely verbal instruction portion is not yet reliable unattended, and no material handling or safety supervision is demonstrated.

sources.title: New York School District Plans To Bring Humanoid Teacher Robot Into The Classroom
sources.claim: The 'Sally' humanoid teaching assistant being introduced at a rural New York district is a seated conversational robot supporting 11th-12th grade coding/robotics courses; it does not move about the room, handle classroom materials, or supervise young children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid teaching assistant in a US school. Cited as negative context: the most advanced announced US school humanoid is stationary and verbal, with no ability to demonstrate equipment use, circulate among children, or physically prevent injury.

sources.title: Schools & Higher Education | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots patrol school and campus grounds providing video monitoring and a call box for people to summon human security; they observe premises and escalate to humans rather than instructing or physically intervening with students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous monitoring inside an institutional school setting. Cited as negative context: the deployed capability is perimeter/anomaly video surveillance escalated to human staff, not instruction of five-year-olds or physical prevention of injury and damage.

tasks.label: Prepare objectives and outlines for courses of study, following curriculum guidelines or requirements of states and schools.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Assimilate arriving children to the school environment by greeting them, helping them remove outerwear, and selecting activities of interest to them.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Typical mild-weather morning arrival: 18-24 kindergarteners enter the classroom over 10-15 minutes; the teacher stands at the door greeting each child by name, reads mood and appearance, reminds each to hang a light jacket and backpack in a cubby, collects take-home folders, and steers each child to a morning tub or table activity matched to that child's interests.

Winter arrival: children come in wearing heavy coats, snow pants, hats, mittens and boots; the teacher physically helps individual children pull off wet outerwear, frees stuck zippers, pairs and stores gloves, helps change into indoor shoes and hangs dripping items on hooks, all while continuing to greet other arriving children.

A child arrives distressed - separation anxiety, crying, clinging to a parent, or upset from the bus ride; the teacher kneels to the child's level, comforts them physically (hug, hand-hold), takes the backpack and coat off for them, and walks them to a preferred calming activity such as playdough or blocks until they settle.

Door or car-line handoff: the teacher receives the child from a parent or bus aide at the classroom door or curb, takes lunch boxes, notes, medication or show-and-tell items, exchanges a brief word with the adult, escorts the child in and gets them started on an activity.

New, late, or individually-supported arrival: a first-week student, a child arriving mid-activity, or a child using a mobility device or adaptive clothing; the teacher gives an individualized welcome, shows or helps with cubby and belongings, removes outerwear as needed, and pairs the child with a peer and an activity already underway.

sources.system: MIT CSAIL robot-assisted dressing system (state estimation algorithm, robot arm)
sources.developer: MIT CSAIL Interactive Robotics Group with Honda Research Institute Europe and University of Edinburgh
sources.title: Robots dress humans without the full picture | MIT News
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robot-assisted dressing is a laboratory demonstration in which a robot arm pulls a jacket sleeve onto the arm of a cooperative, largely stationary adult participant, using force-based estimation of the hidden elbow; it does not address removing garments from moving children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing. It is the closest demonstrated capability to 'helping children remove outerwear' - manipulating a deformable garment around a human limb - so its lab-only scope, cooperative stationary subject and single-sleeve scope bound what is possible for coat removal from an active five-year-old.

sources.system: Dual-arm garment manipulation / dressing system (Baxter-class dual-arm robot)
sources.developer: Fan Zhang and Yiannis Demiris, Imperial College London
sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The best reported garment-dressing success rates come from a dual-arm robot putting hospital gowns on a static medical manikin in a laboratory, not on live, moving people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing of a person. Comparable objects (soft garments) and precision, but the subject is an inert manikin in a lab; a kindergarten arrival involves an unrestrained child, so performance does not carry over.

sources.system: SoftBank/Aldebaran Pepper social robot in schools
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics / United Robotics Group (studies reviewed by Cazorla et al.)
sources.title: Exploring the implementation of the Pepper social robot in formal education: a scoping review
sources.claim: Social robots deployed in formal school settings act as supervised tutoring aids; a 2026 scoping review of Pepper in education reports limited effective autonomy and the need for constant teacher supervision, with speech recognition failures in ambient classroom noise.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: social robot interaction with children in classrooms. It is the closest evidence for the greeting/activity-selection half of this task; its documented dependence on constant teacher supervision shows the arrival routine could not be run autonomously at worker quality.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid | The Robot Report
sources.claim: General-purpose humanoids marketed for varied household object handling still depend on scheduled human teleoperation for most tasks, with only partial onboard autonomy in 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid manipulation of everyday soft goods and clutter. Even the leading consumer humanoid relies on remote human operators, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment for handling coats, backpacks and children.

tasks.label: Collaborate with other teachers and administrators in the development, evaluation, and revision of kindergarten programs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare materials, classrooms, and other indoor and outdoor spaces to facilitate creative play, learning and motor-skill activities, and safety.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily indoor setup of learning centers before students arrive: reading the day's plan, pulling manipulatives (counting bears, pattern blocks), books, puzzles, crayons, glue, paper from cabinets and closets, counting out per-child sets, and distributing/arranging them at 4-6 tables or floor stations in a cluttered kindergarten classroom, typically in a 15-30 minute window.

Producing teaching materials in the classroom or school workroom: copying and collating worksheets, cutting paper and card stock, die-cutting and laminating name tags, letter cards and center labels, trimming laminated sheets, assembling packets and take-home folders, labeling bins and making bulletin-board/anchor-chart displays.

Reconfiguring the room and floor space: moving tables and chairs aside or into new groupings, repositioning rugs, shelves and easels to open a circle-time or movement area, and returning furniture to the teaching layout afterward.

Setting out and later collecting gross-motor / play equipment indoors (mats, cones, hoops, balance beams, balls) and outdoors on the school playground (balls, chalk, hoops, riding toys hauled from a shed or bin), arranging them into activity stations or an obstacle course.

End-of-activity and end-of-day reset: gathering scattered materials and toys and sorting them back into labeled bins and shelves, clearing and wiping tables, sanitizing shared toys and surfaces, and sweeping/vacuuming or mopping the classroom floor and rug area.

Safety preparation and hazard sweep: walking the classroom and playground to spot and remove hazards (broken toys and small choking-size parts, spills and wet slides, glass or litter in the mulch, damaged climbers, loose hooks, blocked exits), securing cords, outlets and heavy furniture, and reporting or fixing what is found.

sources.title: pi_{0.5}: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv)
sources.claim: The pi-0.5 vision-language-action model autonomously drives a mobile manipulator through 10-15 minute multi-stage cleanup of kitchens and bedrooms in homes never seen in training, showing generalist pick-and-place of everyday clutter in unstructured rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying. Comparable in kind to gathering and relocating classroom materials (varied everyday objects, mobile pick-and-place), but demonstrated as research-lab runs in homes, not as timed, per-plan classroom setup.

sources.title: Figure's Humanoid Robot Picks Up Toys, Wipes Surfaces in New Demo
sources.claim: A Figure 03 humanoid running Helix 02 autonomously tidied a cluttered living room, picking ... toys, sorting them and wiping surfaces.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: room tidying and surface wiping. Same object class (toys, small items) and same kind of clearing/wiping work as a classroom reset, though shown as a short staged home demo rather than sustained facility duty.

sources.title: T7AMR Robotic Floor Scrubber | Tennant Company
sources.claim: Tennant T7AMR autonomous robotic floor scrubbers are deployed in K-12 school facilities, cleaning floors without an operator in a working school building.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: floor cleaning in a school. Covers only the floor-cleaning portion of the classroom reset instance; the machine does not pick up or sort objects or wipe tables.

sources.developer: HKUST (Guangzhou) Robotics and Autonomous Systems Thrust
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator (arXiv)
sources.claim: ALORE, a legged manipulator system, autonomously rearranged large furniture (chairs, tables, bins) to specified target poses in real indoor building spaces, running 40 minutes and repositioning 32 chairs without a failure, including long routes through narrow passages.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: furniture rearrangement in institutional indoor space. Same objects (chairs, tables, bins) and same goal (moving furniture to a target room layout) as reconfiguring a classroom.

sources.system: Danfoss kitting cell with Roboception rc_visard 3D vision
sources.title: Case Studies: Automated Kitting Solution with 3D Robot Vision
sources.claim: Danfoss Drives runs a production kitting cell in which a robot uses 3D stereo vision to pick small parts presented in the cell and place them into kits with sub-millimeter precision at 25-second cycle times.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial kitting. Assembling per-child sets of small classroom items into trays and placing them at fixed positions is the same pick-place-into-kit operation, given fixtured presentation as an E1 setting provides.

sources.system: Automatic laminators (e.g., FoilGlazer II / auto-feed laminating systems)
sources.title: Automatic Laminators for High-Volume Use | MyBinding.com
sources.claim: Commercial automatic laminating systems in schools and print shops take a stack of sheets from an automatic feeder and laminate and trim them unattended, with an automatic internal cutter.

sources.title: Post-Printing Automation for Printing Industry | DEVELOP LLC
sources.claim: Robotic post-press cells automate collating, folding, cutting, binding and ... of printed sheets, and robotic laminating machines apply laminate consistently in high-volume print finishing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: print finishing. Copying, collating, cutting and laminating classroom worksheets and cards is the same paper-handling work on the same media, performed with the stock presented to the machine.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators operate in more than 25 US ... and had completed over 300,000 autonomous pharmacy deliveries, fetching and transporting supplies through corridors and elevators in a working human facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetch-and-deliver of supplies inside an institution. Shows transport of materials to a room is solved at E2, but Moxi carries closed totes and does not lay out or arrange varied loose materials.

sources.title: Angsa Robotics Uses Swift to Increase Efficiency of Autonomous Trash Picking Robots
sources.claim: Angsa Robotics' outdoor robot autonomously navigates grass and gravel green spaces, parks and open-air festival grounds, detecting and collecting small litter items such as cigarette butts and bottle caps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor litter removal from lawns/gravel. Covers only the debris-pickup fraction of a playground safety sweep; it does not inspect play equipment condition or judge hazards.

sources.title: The robots we saw at CES 2026 - Engadget
sources.claim: Clutterbot's Rovie is a consumer floor-clutter robot shown at CES 2026 that uses computer vision to identify toys left on the floor, scoop them with a tray-and-sweeper mechanism and deposit them in a designated bin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: floor toy pickup in homes. Relevant to clearing a classroom floor, but it consolidates everything into one bin rather than sorting materials back into labeled storage.
