tasks.label: Organize and label materials and display children's work in a manner appropriate for their sizes and perceptual skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-year / new-unit setup in the kindergarten classroom (children absent): teacher applies printed picture-and-word labels to storage bins, shelf edges, cubbies and hooks, then sorts crayons, scissors, glue sticks, counters and manipulatives into the labeled containers, placing them on low open shelving within a five-year-old's reach.

Routine reset of learning centers (daily/weekly): gathering scattered blocks, puzzle pieces, pattern blocks, letter tiles and books from floor, tables and rug, returning each to its correct labeled bin, straightening the leveled classroom-library book bins, and restocking table supply caddies.

Mounting flat student work on a bulletin board or hallway display: trimming paintings/writing samples, mounting on construction-paper backing, arranging them in rows at child eye level, stapling or pinning them up, and adding a printed title and child name labels.

Displaying three-dimensional and craft work: hanging mobiles, paper chains and yarn-strung projects from the ceiling grid or a strung clothesline with clips, and arranging clay figures, dioramas and paper-plate masks on a display shelf with name cards.

Producing the labels and signage themselves: printing or hand-lettering bin labels, center signs and word-wall cards, laminating them, cutting out letters and shapes, and affixing them with tape, velcro or magnets to bins, charts and center stands at child height.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks individual, diverse products with vision and suction and places them into destination totes; it is deployed in Amazon fulfillment centers and handles over 200 million unique ... varied shape, size and weight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level sortation into totes. Transfers to 'organize materials into labeled bins' — comparable small, varied, unfixtured objects (toys, DVDs, packaged goods vs. manipulatives), comparable placement precision, in a fenced purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Amazon Testing Robotic Arm that Identifies Individual Products | Vision Systems Design
sources.claim: Sparrow picks items out of a cluttered source tote and consolidates them, densely packed, into a destination tote, dealing with clutter rather than fixtured single parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: consolidating cluttered mixed inventory into bins. Same core act as returning mixed classroom manipulatives to their bins; clutter tolerance is the relevant transferable property.

sources.title: Robotic cell for precise sticker application on aluminium wheels - ELVAC Vision
sources.claim: A vision-guided robotic cell picks a flat adhesive label/sticker with a suction cup and applies it to a vision-located position on a workpiece with 0.1 mm accuracy, verifying placement with a camera.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise vision-guided placement and adhesion of a flat sheet item onto a located surface. Transfers to affixing labels to bins and mounting flat paper work onto a backing board — same suction handling of thin flat media and far tighter precision than a classroom display requires.

sources.title: Labelers | Print and Apply Labeling | Label Applicators | Videojet
sources.claim: Commercial print-and-apply labeling systems generate labels on demand and ... and pallets in line, with no human placing each label.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand printing and automatic application of identifying labels to containers. This is the labeling half of the classroom task performed on containers presented by a conveyor.

sources.title: Library Automation Solutions | Lyngsoe Library Systems
sources.claim: Lyngsoe's Sort Mate 2000 automated materials-handling system reads returned library items and routes each book to a designated tote, bin or cart; it is installed in libraries worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting books into designated destination bins. Directly comparable objects (children's books) and the same 'each item to its labeled bin' output as straightening a leveled classroom library.

sources.system: Zünd cutter with Over Cutter Camera (OCC)
sources.title: Zünd sets optical registration in high gear - FESPA
sources.claim: Zünd digital cutting systems use an over-cutter camera to capture registration marks automatically and then cut printed graphics to shape without operator intervention; used in commercial print/sign shops.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated trimming/cutting of printed sheets and letters to shape. This is the 'make the labels, signs and cut-out letters' portion, on the same paper/card media.

sources.title: Automation for Paper & Printing Industries | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC supplies robots used in the paper and printing industries for handling finished print products and for precise application of glues and adhesives on labels, books and packaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling of printed sheets/products plus adhesive dispensing in a fixtured cell — the mechanics of backing and adhering children's flat artwork to a display panel.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage shelves in Japanese convenience stores, deployed to hundreds of FamilyMart stores with remote monitoring and occasional remote intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Closest system operating in an E2 human facility (a retail store) that places goods onto shelves; cited to bound the E2 judgment — it runs on a fixed rail inside a cooler with a known SKU set, so it does not substantiate labeling, display or roaming classroom tidy-up.

tasks.label: Prepare for assigned classes and show written evidence of preparation upon request of immediate supervisors.

tasks.label: Plan and supervise class projects, field trips, visits by guests, or other experiential activities and guide students in learning from those activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classroom hands-on project or learning-center activity: teacher gathers and sets out materials (paint, glue, scissors, blocks, seeds, sensory bins) for 18-24 five-year-olds, launches the activity, circulates among tables to demonstrate technique, manage sharing and conflicts, prevent spills/injury, prompt observation and vocabulary, then leads a whole-group debrief and displays or documents the work.

Off-site field trip (zoo, farm, children's museum, fire station, pumpkin patch): pre-trip permission and logistics, loading a bus, repeated headcounts, escorting the class and chaperone groups through parking lots, crowded exhibits, restrooms and lunch, handling a lost child, upset stomach or meltdown, drawing children's attention to target content, and a follow-up discussion or drawing activity back in class.

In-class visit by a guest (firefighter in gear, dentist, police officer, parent reader, animal handler): teacher arranges the room and seating, preps expectations with the children, keeps a rug full of kindergarteners attentive and safe around the guest and equipment, facilitates question-taking, thanks the guest, and guides a follow-up drawing/writing or discussion.

On-campus outdoor experiential activity: planting and tending the school garden, a nature walk or scavenger hunt on school grounds, weather or shadow observations on the blacktop, or a walk to the school library/cafeteria for a purpose; teacher supervises movement of the group outdoors, hands out tools and clipboards, monitors weather and safety, and guides observation and recording.

Multi-week culminating project or classroom event (100th-day stations, market day, class performance or family science night): teacher plans with grade-level colleagues, assembles and preps materials, briefs parent volunteers, runs rotating stations with children and adults moving through the room, and helps children explain their learning to visitors.

sources.developer: University of Lübeck (T. Sievers) / SoftBank Robotics
sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom
sources.claim: State-of-the-art humanoid social robot (Pepper) tested with children from kindergarten age upward in German schools acted as a teacher's assistant in small groups with the teacher and class continuing separately; the author concludes current robots are not robust enough for autonomous continuous use in ....
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system to the task: a robot placed in a real classroom with kindergarten-age children. It performs conversational lesson support only, with the human teacher retaining supervision, materials handling and behaviour management.

sources.system: social robots in classrooms (review of field studies, incl. NAO, Pepper)
sources.developer: various (review by Rosanda/Smyrnova-Trybulska et al. in Educational Research Review)
sources.title: The use of social robots in classrooms: A review of field-based studies - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: A systematic review of field-based studies of social robots in real classrooms finds robots are seldom left to run autonomously for more than a few days and that real classroom conditions remain difficult for them.
sources.transferJustification: Directly surveys robots deployed in the task's setting (K-12 classrooms), establishing that autonomous, sustained classroom operation has not been achieved.

sources.system: Nao and other social robots for education
sources.developer: Belpaeme et al. (Science Robotics review); SoftBank Robotics
sources.title: Social robots for education: A review | Science Robotics
sources.claim: The authoritative review of social robots in education characterises their demonstrated role as tutor or peer learner in narrow learning interactions, not as supervisor of class activities.
sources.transferJustification: Defines the demonstrated envelope of educational robots (one-to-one or small-group tutoring), which does not extend to planning, materials handling, group supervision or off-site escorting.

sources.title: Robots can learn how to support teachers in class sessions - University of Plymouth
sources.claim: A robot teaching assistant trained by a teacher via SPARC was able to support young pupils autonomously in one specific educational activity, but only within that pre-taught tablet-based activity alongside a human teacher.
sources.transferJustification: Best-case autonomous classroom support with young children; scope is a single scripted-learning activity per child, not planning, setting up, supervising a whole class, or leading an off-site trip.

sources.title: US: BMW deploys Figure 03 humanoid at smart factory for logistics
sources.claim: The most capable general-purpose humanoid deployments as of mid-2026 are in fenced/industrial logistics work brought to the robot, not people-filled care or education settings.
sources.transferJustification: Frontier general-purpose mobile manipulation: sorting known parts in a controlled plant. Comparable object handling exists, but the environment is engineered and person-free, unlike a classroom of kindergarteners.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: Consumer humanoids intended for unstructured, people-present environments still rely on human teleoperators for complex tasks; autonomy is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that open-ended mobile manipulation among people and unfixtured objects (the physical side of running a class project) is not yet autonomous even in a home.

tasks.label: Select, store, order, issue, and inventory classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-/end-of-year setup: teacher unpacks delivered cartons of classroom supplies (crayons, glue, paper reams, manipulatives, books, art materials) in an empty kindergarten classroom, sorts them into labeled bins, cubbies, cabinet shelves and high storage, and discards packaging.

During instruction: issuing materials to 18-22 five-year-olds - setting out crayon boxes, scissors, glue sticks, worksheets, whiteboards or snack items at each table or handing them to each child, then collecting, sorting and stowing them afterward, amid moving children, spills and dropped items.

Periodic inventory and ordering: checking what remains in classroom cabinets and the school supply room (pencils, paper, paint, tissue), noting shortages, selecting items within a small budget from catalogs, and submitting a requisition through the district's ordering system.

Fetching and returning shared equipment/supply bins: walking to the school supply room, workroom or shared closet, collecting a tote of manipulatives, reams of copy paper or a cart of devices, carrying it back to the classroom, and returning it afterward through school corridors.

Routine restocking of the classroom: before/after school, refilling table caddies, cubbies and art shelves from the classroom closet, replenishing paper in the printer/paper cabinet, re-labeling and tidying storage bins in an empty room.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously picks and stows individual, diverse inventory items into fabric storage pods in production fulfillment centers, including high and low bin rows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse put-away. Storing supplies into labeled bins is the same act - grasping varied small consumer goods and placing them into a designated storage compartment - at comparable precision, in a purpose-built cell where the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously identifies and transfers individual items of many types from containers into specific totes in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking for order fulfillment. Issuing/kitting supplies into per-table or per-child sets is the same operation on comparable objects (small stationery-scale goods) when work is fixtured and presented on conveyors.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cartons from trailers and places them ... conveyors in commercial DHL warehouse operations, using vision to handle disordered box stacks without pre-programming.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carton unloading. Receiving a shipment of classroom supplies starts with moving cartons off a pallet or truck to a work point; Stretch does this autonomously on comparable boxes where the work is brought to the machine.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously retrieves supplies from hospital supply closets and delivers them to rooms, operating commercially in occupied hospital corridors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetch-and-deliver. Fetching a supply tote from a school storage room and carrying it to a classroom involves the same objects (bagged/boxed consumables, totes), the same placement precision, and the same kind of institution-controlled corridors.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi is deployed in 30+ US hospitals with over a million deliveries and 100,000 autonomous elevator rides; roughly a third of its work is delivering supplies and equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply logistics at scale. Establishes worker-quality reliability and volume for autonomous supply transport inside an institutional building, which is what the fetch/return instance requires.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robot autonomously scans shelves in operating grocery stores to count stock, detect out-of-stocks and feed replenishment decisions; deployed fleet-wide at 17 Harmons stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory audit. Counting stock and flagging what must be reordered is the inventory step of this task; Tally does it autonomously where shelving is standardized and labeled, i.e. where the stock is presented to the machine.

sources.title: ORB: Operating Room Bot, Automating Operating Room Logistics through Mobile Manipulation
sources.claim: Research mobile manipulator ORB autonomously restocks operating-room supplies onto shelves and retrieves items from shelves, but at 96% and 80% success in experiments, i.e. demonstration-level reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking and retrieval of clinical supplies inside an institutional room; it is the closest published attempt at storing and issuing supplies in a human facility, and its reliability is still below worker quality.

sources.system: pi-0.5 vision-language-action model on mobile manipulator
sources.title: Physical Intelligence on X: pi-0.5 open-world generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 model performs multi-step tidying and cleaning in previously unseen real homes, but as a research demonstration rather than a deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tidying and putting away varied objects in as-found rooms. It is the strongest current evidence for handling clutter in an unstructured room, and it remains lab-demo grade, which bounds claims for an active kindergarten classroom.

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as assisting in school libraries, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cafeteria duty at kindergarten lunch: supervising 40-80 five-year-olds in the school cafeteria for ~25 minutes — opening milk cartons, yogurt tubes and squeeze packs, wiping spills, watching for choking and allergen swaps, redirecting behavior, escorting a child to the restroom or nurse, then lining the class up and dismissing it.

Hall duty, transitions and recess/playground supervision: walking the class through corridors in a line, monitoring stairwells and bathrooms during passing times, redirecting wandering or crying children, tying shoes, opening doors, retrieving dropped items, and watching the playground for injuries and conflicts.

Arrival and dismissal duty at the bus loop / car line: outdoors in all weather, matching each kindergartner to the correct bus number or parent vehicle, holding hands crossing the loop, managing backpacks, coats and lunchboxes, buckling/handing off children, and keeping the group clear of moving vehicles.

Accompanying and assisting the class during its weekly library period: helping children choose appropriate picture books, keeping them seated for the read-aloud, running the checkout desk for the class, and keeping order among 20 five-year-olds in the stacks.

Library materials handling with no students present (covering for the librarian or during prep): checking in the bin of returned books, sorting them by section, reshelving them in call-number order, and pulling requested titles for classroom collections.

Clerical/administrative paperwork support: running class-set copies, collating and stapling packets, folding and stuffing weekly take-home folders, newsletters and permission slips, and sorting returned forms for the office.

sources.title: Florida School Deploys Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot is deployed on school campuses, where it patrols and records vehicle and pedestrian traffic; it observes and streams video but does not physically guide, assist or care for children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: campus surveillance patrol. It is the closest deployed system to hall/cafeteria/grounds 'monitoring', but it only surveils; it cannot open food packaging, redirect a five-year-old, or escort children, so it does not transfer to kindergarten supervision duty.

sources.title: Crossing guard robot: What to know – NBC Bay Area
sources.claim: The CrossBot robot crossing guard, a university prototype, uses sensors and cameras to detect traffic and signals pedestrians when it is safe to ...; it does not escort, hold, or hand off children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: school-zone crossing supervision, the nearest analogue to bus loading/unloading duty. It is a signaling prototype, not a system that matches children to buses, manages belongings, or physically shepherds them, so capability does not carry over.

sources.title: The Future of Robotic Crossing Guards
sources.claim: A commentary on robotic crossing guards notes that current robotic systems cannot match ... guard's judgment or read behavioral cues from children and drivers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: supervising children near traffic; the source is used only to support negative judgments on child-supervision instances.

sources.system: Miller Nichols Library automated storage and retrieval system (ASRS)
sources.title: The Robot - UMKC Libraries
sources.claim: Academic libraries operate automated storage and retrieval systems in which robotic cranes autonomously store and retrieve library materials from a purpose-built bin rack and deliver them to the service desk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reshelving and retrieving library books. Same objects (books) and same purpose as the reshelving/pulling-titles portion of library duty, performed autonomously in a purpose-built rack-and-crane environment.

sources.title: Automated Retrieval System (ARS) - University Library - Santa Clara University
sources.claim: Santa Clara University's library Automated Retrieval System uses three robotic cranes moving among 11,328 bins to retrieve electronically requested items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library materials storage and retrieval, i.e. the shelving/pulling component of assisting in a library, executed autonomously in a machine-built stack environment.

sources.title: Automated Library Sorting Conveyors | Lyngsoe Systems
sources.claim: Lyngsoe's Sort Mate 2000 automated material handling system is installed in public libraries, where returned items are checked in and routed into sorting bins without staff handling each item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: checking in and sorting returned books — the first half of library materials handling — done by a purpose-built conveyor/sorter that patrons feed through a book drop.

sources.title: Streamline mail processing with a folder inserter | Quadient
sources.claim: Quadient folder-inserter machines automatically feed, collate, fold, insert and seal document sets for offices and mailrooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collating and stuffing take-home packets and forms. Identical objects (loose sheets, envelopes/folders) and identical operation, performed by a machine that the work is fed into.

tasks.label: Provide students with disabilities with assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Getting a low-tech assistive device or adapted material to a child's workspace during a lesson: fetching the slant board, adapted scissors, pencil grip, fidget, magnifier, wobble cushion or noise-reducing headphones from a cubby/bin and setting it on the child's desk or table spot at the right moment in a busy kindergarten classroom.

Setting up and troubleshooting supportive technology: positioning/mounting an AAC speech tablet or switch within the child's reach on a tray or desk, turning it on, opening the right board/app, plugging in chargers and swapping batteries, pairing and clipping on an FM/remote-mic hearing system, adjusting volume or magnification.

Restroom assistance: escorting the child down the hall, opening/holding doors, stabilizing or transferring the child onto a toilet or adapted seat, managing clothing and fasteners, wiping/hygiene, handwashing at a low sink, and cleaning up after accidents.

Hands-on body support in the classroom: putting headphones, a weighted vest, splint or brace on the child, hand-over-hand guidance with an adapted tool, lifting/transferring the child between wheelchair, carpet, adaptive chair or stander, and spotting the child in a walker or gait trainer.

Moving the already-seated child and their equipment along building routes: pushing the wheelchair from the classroom to the cafeteria, gym, library or nurse, holding fire doors, waiting at the elevator, parking the chair at a table.

Assistance in non-standard settings: playground and recess equipment, field trips and museum outings, loading/unloading the accessible bus, and fire/lockdown drills where the child and their equipment must be moved on an evacuation route.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Signs Multi-Year Agreement with Staples to Deploy AI-Powered Picking Robots in Fulfillment Centers
sources.claim: RightPick is a commercially deployed, autonomous item-handling robot that picks diverse small items (including office supplies) presented in totes at a fixed station and places them into a target container, with human interventions reduced by 80%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse piece-picking. Transfer: the office-supply items Staples ships match kindergarten assistive materials in size, weight and fragility, and selecting the right item presented in a fixture and placing it at a designated spot is the E1 form of 'provide the child with the device'.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Moxi mobile manipulators autonomously fetch and deliver items (pharmacy, lab, supplies) through occupied hospitals, including autonomous elevator rides, deployed in more than 30 US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply delivery. Transfer: shows autonomous fetch-and-transport of small items through a staffed institutional building, the logistics half of getting a device to a classroom; it does not show selecting a small object from a cluttered cubby or placing it beside a moving five-year-old.

sources.title: Precise and Dexterous Robotic Manipulation via Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning
sources.claim: Autonomously learned policies performed precise insertion and fastening tasks (USB grasp-insertion, RAM insertion, cable clipping) on fixtured workpieces at 100% success over 100 evaluation trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: electronics assembly. Transfer: plugging a charge cable into an AAC tablet, seating a device in a mount and clipping a cable are the same class of small-connector insertion at millimetre precision, on parts presented in a known pose as an E1 cell would present them.

sources.title: Rocsys reveals new partners for its robotic charging solutions
sources.claim: Rocsys ROC-1 robotic chargers autonomously plug in and unplug charging connectors on electric terminal tractors without human intervention, in commercial port and depot operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic EV plug-in. Transfer: locating a socket by vision and inserting a connector reliably is the core physical act in charging and connecting a student's communication device or hearing system, shown at commercial reliability in a bay built for the machine.

sources.title: Unifi Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs carry seated passengers on pre-mapped routes through airport terminals with pedestrian traffic and return to base unoccupied; deployed at Detroit, LAX, MIA, SEA, Schiphol and other airports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: airport passenger mobility assistance. Transfer: moving an already-seated person along fixed corridors of an institutional building past pedestrians is the same act as wheeling a seated student from classroom to cafeteria; the source notes hands-on boarding stays with staff.

sources.title: Eldercare robot helps people sit and stand, and catches them if they fall
sources.claim: MIT's E-BAR body-support robot demonstrates sit-to-stand from a toilet, lifting a person from the floor and fall catching, but the prototype is driven by remote control rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical transfer and toilet assistance for adults. It marks the state of the art for body-contact assistance - a remote-controlled laboratory prototype - so it cannot support a positive judgment for transferring or toileting a child.

sources.title: This Robot Toilet Comes to You When You Need to Go (It's Absurdly Expensive, Though)
sources.claim: A mobile robot toilet for people with disabilities was unveiled at a 2026 assistive-devices expo; it drives to the user, but the user must get onto it and the system is an expo showcase rather than a deployed caregiving robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: toileting support. Even taken at face value it brings a fixture to the user; it does not undress, transfer, wipe or wash a five-year-old, so it cannot substantiate completion of restroom assistance.

tasks.label: Prepare materials and classrooms for class activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Copy room / workroom before or after school: teacher duplicates the day's paper materials for ~25 students — runs originals through the copier, makes double-sided copies, collates multi-page packets, staples them, sometimes guillotine-cuts sheets in half and sorts into per-table piles.

Classroom or prep counter: assembling and laying out hands-on lesson materials — counting out manipulatives (counters, dice, base-ten blocks), art supplies (glue sticks, scissors, colored paper), or science-kit items into a tray/bin per table group, then placing a set at each of 5-6 desk clusters.

Classroom furniture and space: pushing desks into pods or a U, clearing floor space for a carpet circle, moving tables and chairs for a station rotation or a testing layout, setting up learning-center furniture, putting chairs up or down.

Fabricating instructional display pieces: printing and cutting name tags, word-wall cards, labels, flashcards and center signs, laminating them and trimming the laminate, assembling sets of task cards.

Mounting and refreshing classroom displays: stapling backing paper and borders to bulletin boards, posting student work and anchor charts on walls, hand-writing the day's agenda/objectives on the whiteboard or chart paper.

Setting up the day's equipment and clearing surfaces: wheeling out and plugging in the tablet/laptop cart, connecting the projector or document camera and cueing the media, handing out devices and headphones, wiping and clearing tables before a messy activity, restocking supply caddies and sharpening pencils.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks individual, varied consumer items out of source containers and places them into designated totes at production scale in fulfillment centers — the core motion of assembling a per-group kit of classroom supplies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-item picking into totes. Transfers to counting out and boxing classroom supplies into per-group trays — comparable small rigid objects, low precision demands — but only in a fenced, item-presented station.

sources.title: I visited Amazon's robot factories and got an inside look at how it builds and trains them
sources.claim: Amazon's Hercules drive units autonomously lift and reposition heavy standardized storage pods to commanded locations on a fenced robotic floor, repeated at fleet scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving standardized furniture-sized units to commanded positions. Transfers to rearranging desks/tables only if the furniture is standardized and floor-marked as in a purpose-built robotic floor; it does not transfer to an as-found occupied classroom.

sources.system: Danfoss kitting cell with Roboception rc_visard 3D vision
sources.title: Case Studies: Automated Kitting Solution with 3D Robot Vision

sources.title: Robots now wipe tables, sort trash, open doors at Google offices

sources.transferJustification: Related task: table wiping and object tidying in an office. Shows only isolated sub-steps of surface prep were achieved in a human facility, not whole multi-step room setup; the program was later wound down.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point supply delivery inside a human institution. It establishes transport in an E2 facility only; Moxi does not lay out, arrange or set up materials at workstations.

sources.title: Avidbots Designs Fully Autonomous Cleaning Robots for Airports and Hospitals
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor scrubbers are deployed in schools and other large facilities, cleaning floors without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor cleaning in schools. Establishes what is actually deployed in school buildings today — floor-level cleaning only, with no manipulation of classroom materials, furniture or equipment.

instances.label: Whole-class direct instruction with digital media: in a classroom of ~24 children, the teacher runs a slide deck, interactive-whiteboard activity or short video on the projector/panel, advances and pauses it, annotates on the board, and questions students while the media plays.

Live demonstration with physical visual aids: the teacher holds up and manipulates objects (a big book, base-ten blocks or fraction tiles, a plant, a map, a science apparatus), often under a document camera projected to the class, narrating and turning/pointing to details as children watch and respond.

Pre-lesson setup and troubleshooting of AV gear: connecting a laptop to the projector/panel via HDMI or USB-C, powering on and calibrating the interactive board, hooking up speakers or a document camera, loading a media file or swapping a dead cable, usually in a quiet or empty classroom.

Distributing, collecting and re-docking equipment for a media-supported activity: handing out tablets/Chromebooks from a charging cart, headphones and manipulative kits to students, then gathering them, returning them to slots and plugging in chargers.

Small-group/center rotation media use: setting up listening stations, tablets with a reading or math app and headphones, then circulating among stations to relaunch audio, fix a wrong app screen and redirect children while the rest of the class works.

sources.system: Xiaomo humanoid robot (Spirit AI) at CATL Zhongzhou plant
sources.title: China's CATL marks trailblazing deployment of humanoid robots at scale on the factory floor
sources.claim: Spirit AI's Xiaomo humanoid robots are deployed at scale on CATL's battery assembly line, autonomously plugging in high-voltage connectors with a vision-language-action model and a reported 99% success rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: connector insertion on a production line. Plugging an HDMI/power cable into a projector or panel involves comparable objects (mating electrical connectors), comparable precision (millimetre alignment with compliance), and is substantiated only where the port and cable are presented in known, fixtured positions.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm is deployed in fulfillment centers, autonomously detecting, selecting and moving individual varied products from containers into specific totes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse item picking and placing. Sorting tablets, headphones and manipulative kits into and out of containers/slots involves objects of comparable size and fragility and comparable placement precision, but only when the items and receptacles are presented to the arm in fixtured containers.

sources.system: Standard Bots Core and other machine-tending cobots
sources.title: Cobot machine tending: Everything you need to know
sources.claim: Collaborative robots are sold and used commercially for machine tending, autonomously loading and unloading parts at fixtured CNC machines, presses and molding ... inside work cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine tending. Establishes that at E1 the work (parts, fixtures, machine controls) is presented in known positions and a robot can grasp, place and actuate equipment repeatably — the mode in which cable-plugging and item-stowing sub-actions of AV setup would arise.

sources.title: Humanoid robot makes test lecture at primary school in E.China, inspiring students to engage in 'deeper learning'
sources.claim: A 1.4 m humanoid 'Xiao An' delivered a science lesson at a Hefei primary school as a teaching assistant alongside the human teacher; the company described it as the first public trial and said stability still needs improvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering classroom instruction with media. Cited to show the state of the art for robot-led lessons in a real elementary classroom is a supervised one-off trial beside a human teacher, not autonomous worker-quality delivery.

sources.system: Social robots in education (NAO, Pepper and similar tutors)
sources.developer: various (meta-analysis, Frontiers in Robotics and AI)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered tutoring in schools. Cited as counter-evidence: even narrow robot tutoring in classrooms frequently depends on human operators, so it cannot substantiate autonomous delivery of a media-supported class lesson.

tasks.label: Provide a variety of materials and resources for children to explore, manipulate, and use, both in learning activities and in imaginative play.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Setting out manipulatives for a lesson: teacher pulls tubs of counting cubes, base-ten blocks, pattern tiles, mini whiteboards and markers from classroom cabinets, counts out complete sets, places a tub at each of five or six table groups or hands sets to 20-25 seated children, then collects, re-sorts and re-shelves at the end. Children present and moving.

Stocking and refreshing centers and shelves before/after school: refilling construction paper, glue sticks, crayons and pencils, replacing dried markers, rotating books in the classroom library, restocking the art and sensory bins, and setting up dramatic-play props (dress-up clothes, play kitchen items, blocks) in an idiosyncratic, cluttered classroom.

Setting up a hands-on science/STEM or art activity: filling cups with water, portioning soil and seeds, laying out magnets, thermometers, hand lenses, paint and brushes into kits at lab tables, handing them to groups, assisting during use, then washing and putting materials away.

Responsive mid-activity provision while teaching: passing out worksheets, scissors and glue, handing a child a replacement pencil or a different-level book, fetching a specific manipulative for a struggling student, distributing and collecting Chromebooks/tablets from a cart, all amid an active classroom of children.

Outdoor/off-site provision: carrying bins of clipboards, collection bags, hand lenses and garden tools to the schoolyard, garden or a park for a nature exploration lesson; setting out recess/play equipment; handing out materials on a field trip in a setting the school does not control.

Fetching and hauling bulk supplies: pushing a cart of paper reams, boxes of workbooks and bins of donated recyclables from the school supply room, office or storage closet through corridors to the classroom, and receiving deliveries.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously identifies and picks individual diverse products out of containers and places them into totes for specific orders, operating in fulfillment centers (purpose-built robotic work areas).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order kitting/singulation. Assembling a set of assorted small classroom items (cubes, tiles, markers, glue sticks) from bins into a tub is the same pick-and-place of varied small objects at comparable precision, and is what a purpose-built cell would present for this task.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan picking/stowing robot handles roughly three quarters of the item types stocked in fulfillment centers at human-comparable speed, calling a human only when it cannot handle an item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing/retrieving varied consumer goods into and out of fabric pods. Demonstrates that varied small-object handling reaches human-comparable throughput only inside the purpose-built pod-and-fixture environment.

sources.title: RightPick 4 piece-picking system from RightHand Robotics built to handle bigger items
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics sells the RightPick autonomous piece-picking system as a service to warehouse operators; the current generation handles larger and heavier items with reduced need for human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial each-picking of heterogeneous SKUs from totes into order containers — the same operation as assembling and presenting sets of assorted classroom supplies when the materials are fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocks refrigerated shelves with bottles and ... in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously in normal operation with remote human teleoperation only for error recovery; it relies on a pre-registered shelf layout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing shelves so that people can take items. Closest fielded analog to restocking classroom supply shelves, but limited to uniform bottles/cans, an installed fixed work zone and a pre-scanned layout — it does not transfer to varied classroom items on as-found shelving.

sources.title: Meet Moxi: Why We Invested in Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously travels hospital corridors, opens doors, rides elevators and picks up and delivers supplies, medications and lab specimens; deployed in more than 30 US hospitals with over one million deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply fetch-and-deliver among moving people. Directly comparable to hauling boxes/bins of teaching supplies from a school storeroom through corridors to a classroom.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent reported over 300,000 pharmacy deliveries by Moxi by May 2025, on top of one million total hospital deliveries and 100,000 autonomous elevator rides, in existing hospital buildings without facility modification.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (institutional supply transport); establishes deployment scale and reliability sufficient for worker-quality substitution on hauling runs.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Introduces Servi Q
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots autonomously run food and bus tables among seated guests in restaurants, hotels and other venues without changing the floor plan, though staff load and guests unload the trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wheeling trays to occupied tables in a people-filled facility. Shows navigation-among-people transfers, but the robot neither selects nor places the items, so it cannot complete material distribution end to end.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 vision-language-action model autonomously performs multi-step rearranging and cleanup tasks in entirely new, unseen homes, but its success is inconsistent.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up and placing everyday objects in unstructured rooms. Nearest evidence for E3 object handling, but it is a research demo with acknowledged unreliability, so it does not meet worker-quality completion.

tasks.label: Plan and supervise class projects, field trips, visits by guest speakers or other experiential activities, and guide students in learning from those activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hands-on class project in the teacher's own elementary classroom (e.g., multi-day science investigation, diorama/poster build, planting seed trays): teacher sets out and distributes scissors, glue, soil, measuring tools; demonstrates steps; circulates among 5-7 tables of 20-28 children helping, correcting technique, managing spills, tool safety and off-task behavior; then gathers the class to debrief what was learned.

Off-site field trip with ~25 students to a zoo, museum, farm or historic site: teacher loads and counts students on the bus, walks the group through parking lots, sidewalks and exhibit halls, manages restroom and lunch logistics, keeps physical custody of every child, handles a scraped knee or a wandering student, prompts observations and questions during the visit and leads the post-trip reflection.

On-campus experiential activity outside the classroom: school garden work, nature walk on school grounds, STEM/field day station, or science fair setup — teacher moves the class through hallways and outdoors, sets up and hands out equipment, supervises children spread over an open area, and guides them in recording and discussing what they observe.

Guest speaker or in-school presenter visit (firefighter, author, local historian): teacher arranges the visit, preps students with questions, escorts and seats the class in the classroom, library or gym, manages attention and behavior during the talk, facilitates Q&A, and runs the follow-up reflection and thank-you letters.

Classroom-based virtual experiential activity: teacher books a virtual field trip or video guest speaker, sets up the projector/laptop and student devices, seats and supervises the class during the session, troubleshoots the technology, keeps children on task, and leads the debrief connecting the experience to the unit.

sources.title: Lindsey the Tour Guide Robot - Usage Patterns in a Museum Long-Term Deployment (IEEE Xplore)
sources.claim: The closest deployed autonomous analogue to leading a group through a venue is a museum tour-guide robot: Lindsey navigates a museum autonomously every day, delivers guided tours and information to adult visitors, but exercises no custody of, or responsibility for, children and does not set up or supervise hands-on work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guiding a visitor group through a venue, the closest analogue to leading a field trip. It substantiates only autonomous navigation plus scripted narration in a mapped indoor institution; it does not substantiate supervising minors, managing behavior and safety, or guiding learning.

sources.system: Knightscope K5 / school-deployed autonomous security robots

sources.claim: Autonomous security robots patrol school premises but only stream video to human officers; monitoring premises is not supervision of children, and no manipulation or intervention is performed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping watch over an institutional site. Cited to show the ceiling of deployed school-premises robotics — passive video patrol referred to humans — which does not carry over to custodial supervision of an elementary class or to any physical intervention.

sources.title: The AV1 robot is helping sick children attend school | CNN Business
sources.claim: Robots physically present in school classrooms today are remote-presence devices operated by a person, not autonomous supervisors; the AV1 is placed on a desk by the teacher and driven by the absent pupil.

tasks.label: Organize and label materials and display students' work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-year (or end-of-year) classroom setup: teacher sorts mixed supplies — crayons, glue sticks, scissors, whiteboard markers, math manipulatives, dice, task cards — into bins, caddies, shelves and cubbies in her own classroom, then writes or prints labels (word + picture) and affixes them to bins and shelf edges.

Ongoing weekly upkeep during the school year: re-sorting the classroom library back into leveled/genre bins, returning manipulatives and center materials to their labeled tubs after use, relabeling folders, trays and mailbox slots as groups change; done around furniture and sometimes with students present.

Building a classroom bulletin-board display of student work: cutting and stapling backing paper, adding border trim, trimming/mounting ~25 varied papers (writing samples, paintings, projects) in an arrangement, stapling them to the cork board with name cards and a cut-letter title.

Hallway or common-area display: mounting student work in a corridor board or glass display case outside the room, often reaching above head height on a stool, coordinating with a grade-level theme and school display rules.

Prepping and labeling per-student lesson materials: collating multi-page packets, assembling and name-labeling individual baggies/kits (letter tiles, counters, book bags), then placing them into student mailboxes, desks or table caddies before the lesson.

sources.title: Ambi Robotics to Deploy Sortation Systems at Numerous OSM Worldwide Warehouses in U.S. - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: AmbiSort A-Series robotic cells autonomously pick mixed items (polybags, flats, boxes) from a conveyor or bin feed and sort them into designated destination bins/sacks in commercial parcel warehouses, with one operator overseeing three to four cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sortation of heterogeneous small goods into labelled destination bins. Transfers to organizing classroom supplies because the objects (small mixed consumer items), the required precision (drop into an open bin), and the fixtured feed-and-bin-wall cell are the same class of problem.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Piece-Picking System for Warehouse Order Fulfillment | Supply & Demand Chain Executive
sources.claim: RightPick 4 performs autonomous piece-picking of individual items, explicitly including office-supply SKUs, placing them into destination totes/orders in fulfillment operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking of office supplies into totes. The handled objects (markers, glue sticks, small boxed items) and the pick-and-place precision match sorting classroom supplies into bins; the demonstrated environment is a fixtured picking cell.

sources.title: Labelers | Print and Apply Labeling | Label Applicators | Videojet
sources.claim: Print-and-apply labeling systems automatically generate variable-data labels on demand and apply ... to cases, cartons, totes and pallets on a conveyor line without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic printing and application of adhesive labels to containers. This is the labeling half of the teacher task (making a label and sticking it on a bin/tote), with the same objects (printed adhesive labels, plastic totes and cartons) and tighter placement precision.

sources.system: Lyngsoe Sort Mate 2000 / bibliotheca flex AMH sorters
sources.title: Library Automation Solutions | Lyngsoe Library Systems
sources.claim: Library automated materials handling systems automatically check in returned books and route each item to the correct destination bin, cart or tote in deployed public libraries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting books by category into labelled bins. Objects (paperback and hardcover children's books), the sort-to-bin action, and the accepted output (each title in its correct bin) match re-sorting a classroom library into leveled bins on a purpose-built line.

sources.developer: Multiple (e.g. inserter vendors; Catdi Printing production line)
sources.title: Automatic Document Inserter | Storage Solutions
sources.claim: Commercial document inserters and mailing lines automatically fold, collate multi-piece personalized packets and kits and insert them into envelopes, with variable-data personalization per recipient.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: collating personalized multi-piece packets. Same objects (loose printed sheets), same required output (a complete, correctly ordered, name-identified packet per person), on a fixtured feeder line — the machine equivalent of a teacher collating and name-labeling student packets.

sources.title: Fanuc-powered robotic cell automates furniture upholstery process
sources.claim: A vision-guided industrial robot cell autonomously stretches, staples and trims flexible sheet coverings onto furniture components in a fixtured production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided stapling of flexible sheet material to a substrate. It substantiates only the fastening sub-step of a bulletin-board display; no cited system composes a multi-piece student-work display (layout, borders, trimmed mounts, cut-letter title).

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as school library assistance, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hallway/transition duty in an elementary school: standing at the classroom door or a corridor post during arrival, passing periods, restroom breaks and dismissal; keeping 20-30 children walking in line, redirecting runners, separating pushing or fighting students physically, picking up dropped items, escorting a crying or injured child to the office, holding doors for classes.

Cafeteria duty: supervising 100+ K-5 students in a lunchroom for 25-40 minutes — managing the serving line, opening milk cartons and packaging for younger children, wiping up spills and handling dropped trays, watching for allergy items and choking, resolving conflicts, dismissing tables and checking that they are cleaned.

Bus loading/unloading duty: escorting classes from the building to the bus loop, verifying each child boards the correct bus by name/route, helping kindergarteners with backpacks and bus steps, holding children back from moving buses, handing off students to drivers or waiting parents, working outdoors in rain, snow, wind and noise.

Recess/playground and arrival car-line duty: supervising children on playground equipment in an open outdoor area, watching for injuries and rough play, retrieving balls, blowing the whistle and lining classes up; or opening car doors in the drop-off loop and walking children safely across the drive.

School library assistance with students present: covering or helping during a class library period — reading aloud or shepherding a class, helping children locate age-appropriate books, operating the circulation desk to check items out to students, keeping the room orderly and quiet.

School library back-of-house assistance without students: processing a bin of returned books — checking each item in against the catalog record and sorting the items onto carts by section/destination for reshelving.

sources.title: Florida School Deploys Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot has been deployed on a school campus; its school use case is autonomous patrol of parking lots and structures, monitoring and recording vehicle and pedestrian traffic and acting as a mobile call box — it does not supervise, direct, or physically assist children.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to hall/campus monitoring by a school employee. It shows the state of the art is passive patrol and recording in outdoor lots, not supervision of children, verbal redirection, or physical intervention, so capability does not transfer to hall, cafeteria, bus or playground duty.

sources.title: Schools & Higher Education | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope markets school deployments specifically for parking lots and structures, with the robot monitoring and recording traffic rather than managing student behavior.
sources.transferJustification: Same monitoring family as hall/bus/playground duty; the scope of the commercial offering (outdoor lots, recording, call box) bounds what deployed patrol robots do and shows they do not perform student supervision duties.

sources.claim: Automated Materials Handling Systems (purpose-built conveyor-and-diverter machines) check in returned library items by RFID and sort them to destination bins at production volumes in operating libraries.
sources.transferJustification: The teacher's library-returns duty is the same operation — check an item in and route it to the right cart/section. The machine handles identical objects (books, media) to the same accuracy standard, in a purpose-built induction-and-sort layout.

sources.system: Lyngsoe IMMS / Sort Mate automated sorting
sources.title: Maximized Efficiencies and Material Turnaround at Sacramento Public Library
sources.claim: Lyngsoe's library automation software and sorters are installed at thousands of sites, sorting mixed RFID and barcoded material streams and reducing staff handling of returns.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborates that automated check-in and sorting of returned library materials is a mature commercial capability, matching the returns-processing portion of school library assistance.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid with Optio AI teacher's assistant
sources.title: Realbotix to Deploy First Humanoid Robot and AI Teachers Assistant in U.S. School District
sources.claim: Humanoid robots entering US schools are conversational teaching-assistant pilots (a stationary M-Series bust plus AI tutor software), not mobile systems that supervise children in halls, cafeterias, or bus loops.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest robotic presence in elementary/secondary schools. It is a fixed conversational platform for classroom engagement, with no locomotion, manipulation, or crowd-supervision capability, so it cannot cover the monitoring or student-assistance duties in this task.

tasks.label: Select, store, order, issue, and inventory classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily issuing and collecting of lesson materials in an occupied classroom of ~22 K-5 students: passing out worksheets, whiteboards, pencils, glue, tubs of math manipulatives and art or science kit pieces to desks/table groups, replacing missing or broken pieces mid-lesson, then collecting everything back and returning it to shelves while children move about.

Receiving and storing supply deliveries: opening cartons of paper, notebooks, crayons, glue and workbooks in the classroom or shared supply room; sorting heterogeneous items into labeled bins, tubs, drawers and cabinets; shelving overflow in a closet; refilling student supply caddies.

Periodic inventory/audit (start and end of year, or before a district equipment sweep): counting textbooks, readers, tablets and consumables; opening cabinets and bins to check that science/math kits are complete and equipment undamaged; recording counts and losses on a district form or spreadsheet.

Selecting and ordering: walking the classroom cabinets and school supply room to see what is low, choosing items from vendor catalogs/online within a small budget, submitting a requisition to the office, and later checking the delivered cartons against the packing slip.

Issuing and collecting shared durable equipment with per-student accountability: Chromebooks/tablets from a charging cart, library books, headphones, PE and music equipment; checking devices back in, plugging them to charge, noting damage, and tracking who has what.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously stows heterogeneous individual items into crowded fabric pod compartments (and picks them back out) in production fulfillment centers, handling roughly three quarters of stocked item types.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stow/pick. Transfers to 'store' and 'issue' classroom supplies: the same class of small consumer goods (boxes, books, packaged stationery-scale items) is grasped from a tote and placed into a divided bin compartment, the manipulation a teacher performs when putting supplies into labeled bins - but only where goods and bins are presented in the machine's fixtured pod system.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon Sparrow autonomously picks individual products out of cluttered mixed totes and places them into specific destination totes for particular orders in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking/kitting for orders. Transfers to 'issue' supplies: building a per-recipient set of small items from bulk stock is the same operation as making up a per-student materials kit, provided the stock is presented to the machine in totes as a purpose-built cell does.

sources.title: Library Automation Solutions | Lyngsoe Library Systems
sources.claim: Lyngsoe automated materials handling systems in libraries take items returned by patrons, check them in against the library system and sort them mechanically into totes, bins or carts without staff handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library circulation returns handling. Transfers to 'issue and inventory' of classroom books/equipment: items are received from individual users, logged against the borrower record, and sorted to a storage destination - the accountability and re-shelving loop of a Chromebook cart or class library, but only at a purpose-built induction point.

sources.title: SpartanNash deploys Simbe Tally robots in 60 more grocery stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning robot deployed at scale in US grocery chains, producing shelf-level stock counts that feed stocking and ordering decisions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory auditing. Transfers to 'inventory' and the stock-check part of 'order': the robot traverses aisles of shelved, labeled stock and outputs counts/out-of-stocks used for replenishment, the same output a supply-room count produces - but only for open, labeled shelving, not closed cabinets or loose items in bins.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Tally remains in active commercial deployment as of late 2025, running across 17 stores of the Harmons grocery chain after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Same as the other Tally item: retail shelf inventory auditing, cited to establish that the deployment is current rather than a one-off pilot.

sources.title: Telexistence to install AI re-stocking robots in 300 convenience stores across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocks beverage shelves inside operating FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously with occasional remote human correction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking in a human retail facility. Marks the current E2 frontier for stocking work: a fixed-base robot handling one standardized product family (bottles/cans) in a machine-friendly cooler, which does not extend to unpacking mixed school supplies into cabinets.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent's Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously runs supply, lab and pharmacy deliveries through the corridors and elevators of more than 30 US hospitals, with over a million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply transport. Shows what is achieved at E2 inside a people-filled institution - point-to-point transport of totes - but not the per-recipient handing out, unpacking into cabinets, or counting this task requires.

sources.title: 100% Self-Service Automated Kiosk Checkout Laptops, Tablets, Power Chargers and More
sources.claim: Automated device-dispensing kiosks issue and take back laptops and tablets with per-user accountability and charging, and are sold and installed in schools, libraries and campuses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: self-service device lending. Covers the 'issue and inventory equipment' loop (authenticate user, release device, accept return, charge, log custody), but only as a fixed machine users come to, not distribution around a classroom.

sources.title: Verity, On, Maersk pilot RFID tech with autonomous drones in warehouse inventory management - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous inventory drones fly unaided in warehouses to scan barcoded stock locations and report counts, including an RFID-augmented program run with On and Maersk.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cycle counting racked stock. Transfers to 'inventory' of classroom stock only where items sit in standardized, tagged locations, as a purpose-built stockroom would present them.

tasks.label: Provide students with disabilities with assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During a lesson in a general-ed elementary classroom of ~22 children, the teacher gets a specific student their assistive tech and adapted materials: hands over and wakes/positions an AAC speech tablet on its mount, clips on the FM/DM transmitter for a hard-of-hearing child, sets out a slant board, pencil grip, large-print book or magnifier, opens the right app/page, and checks the child can reach and use it while continuing to run the class.

Assisting a student with a disability to the restroom and back: prompting/escorting an ambulatory child who needs supervision, or pushing/steadying a child who uses a wheelchair, walker or crutches down the corridor, holding and latching doors, waiting, sometimes helping with clothing, hand-washing or calling for the aide, then returning the child to the lesson.

Positioning and equipment support in the classroom: helping a child out of a wheelchair onto the carpet or into a classroom chair, seating them in adaptive seating or a stander, fastening straps/harness, attaching or removing a wheelchair tray, repositioning a slumped child, retrieving a dropped device or crutch.

Off-lesson device readiness at the teacher's desk or a classroom charging station, with no child present: plugging AAC tablets, hearing-aid FM transmitters and switch toys in to charge, swapping batteries, wiping devices down, checking cables/mounts, and putting them back in the storage cabinet for the next day.

Facility access on campus beyond the classroom: getting a student with a disability through the cafeteria line with a tray, onto or around playground equipment at recess, into the gym or assembly seating, and to the bus loading zone at dismissal, amid crowds of moving children.

Off-site field trip or community outing: helping a student with a mobility, visual or cognitive disability navigate an unfamiliar museum, park or sidewalk route, manage curbs, uneven ground and unmarked accessible entrances, and use unfamiliar restrooms, while keeping the child with the group.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a person with impaired mobility through a building to a destination. It bears on the restroom/campus-access instances, but covers only the transport leg for a self-boarding adult who selects a destination — not transfers, door handling, hygiene help, or supervision of a young child.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous item transport inside a structured institution. It shows only that a robot can carry an item to a location in a building; it does not show handing a device to a specific child and setting it up for that child's use.

tasks.label: Prepare materials and classrooms for class activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Copy room / workroom before or between classes: teacher runs off class sets of worksheets, quizzes, article packets and exit tickets on the school copier for 4-6 sections (~120-150 students), collating multi-page packets, stapling, sorting into per-period stacks, reloading paper and clearing jams.

Own classroom in the 10-15 minutes before a period: setting out the day's materials at 28-32 student desks or table groups - handouts, lab sheets, name cards, manipulatives (rulers, protractors, mini whiteboards, novels), Chromebooks pulled from the cart - onto desks that already hold student clutter.

Reconfiguring the room for the day's activity: pushing 30 student desks and chairs from rows into pods, a seminar circle, or testing rows; clearing floor space; setting up 5-6 numbered rotation stations around the perimeter; pushing in chairs and resetting the layout between periods.

Science or hands-on activity prep at the lab bench / prep sink: portioning solutions and consumables into cups and dropper bottles, assembling 8-10 identical group trays (beakers, graduated cylinders, balances, microscopes and slides, dissection kits, goggles), setting up a demo apparatus, and placing trays at lab benches.

Setting up classroom technology and board displays: connecting laptop to projector/document camera and speakers, loading the slide deck and video, checking Chromebooks are charged, writing the day's agenda, objective and warm-up problem on the whiteboard, posting anchor charts or word walls.

Fetching and moving materials around the building: pulling consumables and equipment from the department storage room, book room or supply closet, hauling bins/carts of materials down corridors and up elevators to the classroom, gym or shared lab, and restocking classroom supply bins (markers, paper, glue, calculators).

sources.title: MultiFunction Finisher (MFF) Specifications
sources.claim: Xerox production/office finishers automatically collate and staple printed output into finished sets under machine control, the core of producing class sets of packets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production document finishing. Same objects (loose letter-size sheets) and the same accepted output as a teacher's class set (collated, stapled multi-page packets), produced inside a purpose-built paper path.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick systems autonomously pick mixed items from totes and place them into designated cubbies to build kits, deployed commercially in fulfillment operations across three continents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated kitting. Repeatedly building identical kits from a limited set of small items into fixed target positions is the same operation as assembling per-group material sets or lab trays, at comparable object size and placement precision.

sources.title: 4 cool facts about Hercules, the small-but-mighty robot in Amazon's fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Hercules drive units autonomously locate, lift and transport heavy inventory pods to commanded positions on a purpose-built warehouse floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repositioning furniture-scale free-standing objects. Lifting a pod (up to 1,250 lb) and driving it to a commanded spot on a marked floor is the same operation as moving standardized desks into a commanded layout when desks and floor are built for the machine.

sources.title: Opentrons Announces a Flex Proteomics Workstation for Automated Mass Spectrometry Sample Prep
sources.claim: Opentrons Flex liquid-handling robots perform automated reagent portioning and sample preparation and are in routine use across thousands of institutional labs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laboratory sample prep. Dispensing measured liquids into arrayed labware on a fixtured deck is the same operation, at tighter precision, than portioning solutions into per-group cups and dropper bottles for a middle-school lab.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (KUKA KMR iiwa based)
sources.title: AI-driven mobile robots team up to tackle chemical synthesis - University of Liverpool
sources.claim: The Liverpool 'mobile robotic chemist' worked autonomously for eight days in a working chemistry laboratory, moving between stations and operating human-scale lab equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous laboratory workflow execution. Shows a mobile manipulator handling vials and labware between benches in a real lab, but only at stations surveyed and arranged for it, which bounds transfer to varied classroom kit assembly.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi autonomously picks supplies from hospital supply closets and delivers them to units and patient rooms; the fleet has passed 1 million picks, 300,000 pharmacy deliveries and 100,000 autonomous elevator rides across 30+ US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply fetch and delivery. Retrieving items from a stocked storeroom and moving them through corridors and elevators to a destination room is the same operation as pulling materials from a school storage room to a classroom, lab or gym.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence TX SCARA robots autonomously restock refrigerated shelves in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, succeeding over 98% of the time with remote human fallback for rare failures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking inside a human-use facility. Placing standard consumable items onto known shelves from a supply of crates matches restocking classroom supply bins, though only for uniform items and fixed shelf geometry.

sources.title: Alphabet's X has 'Everyday Robots' test fleet that autonomously performs office maintenance tasks
sources.claim: Alphabet's Everyday Robots fleet performed autonomous tidying tasks - sorting trash, wiping tables, opening doors - across occupied Google offices in the Bay Area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tidying and object handling in an occupied human workplace - the nearest analogue to resetting or restocking a classroom, though it was a pilot fleet and the program ended in 2023.

sources.title: Scribit Design - Scribit Shop
sources.claim: Scribit is a commercially sold write-and-erase wall robot that reproduces uploaded text and vector content on whiteboards, glass or plaster walls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: writing and erasing content on a vertical whiteboard. Putting the day's agenda and objective on the classroom board is exactly this operation, on the same surface and marker medium.

sources.system: Rocsys M1 / Rocsys autonomous charging arm
sources.title: Rocsys raises $13M raise for hands-free robotaxi charging
sources.claim: Rocsys' rail-mounted robotic arm uses computer vision to locate a vehicle's charging inlet and mate the connector autonomously, in port and fleet-depot installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connector mating. Locating a socket by vision and inserting a plug is the operation needed to connect a projector or document-camera cable, though at coarser tolerance than an HDMI/USB-C port.

sources.claim: Figure's humanoid inserted sheet metal parts into fixtures in a real BMW production environment, and Figure reports Helix-02 robots running multi-minute manipulation tasks over full shifts without resets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained autonomous pick-and-place in a work facility. Supports fixtured placement of known objects at industrial stations; the demonstrated settings are company- or plant-controlled cells, not occupied classrooms.

instances.label: Hall/passing-period duty: teacher stands at classroom door or hallway intersection between periods, visually scans a crowd of 100+ 11-14 year olds, tells stragglers to move along, checks passes, separates horseplay or a shoving match, walks a non-compliant or distressed student to the office, reports by radio.

Bus loading/unloading and arrival/dismissal duty: outdoors in the bus loop or car line in all weather; keeping students on the sidewalk and back from moving buses, directing them to the correct bus, stopping traffic for crossers, helping with dropped items, handling late buses and parent pickups.

Library/media-center coverage, student-facing portion: staffing the desk during a period, keeping order among students in the space, helping students locate a title or use the catalog, approving passes and helping with printing.
Library/media-center coverage, materials-handling portion: checking in returned books, sorting them, and getting them back into their storage locations from a return cart.

Other assigned supervision/administrative posts: study hall or detention monitoring, restroom/hall sweeps, morning entrance and locker-bank posts, assemblies and fire-drill line management, dance/game chaperoning, occasional office or attendance coverage.
