sources.claim: Figure 02 humanoids running the Helix policy performed an hour of uninterrupted autonomous package sortation on a conveyor line, handling boxes, poly bags and flat envelopes and orienting barcodes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating and sorting flat, floppy paper items (envelopes/flats) presented on a conveyor — the same manipulation problem as collating and distributing sheets of student paperwork, in a purpose-built conveyor cell.

sources.title: bookBot and Collections | James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
sources.claim: The Hunt Library bookBot is an automated storage ... stores and retrieves up to two million books and other items on demand in place of open stacks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: storing an organized, indexed book collection and returning any title on request — the storage-and-order-keeping function of maintaining a classroom library, achieved only in purpose-built racking.

sources.title: Telexistence Deploys AI and Remote-Controlled Robots in 300 Convenience Stores, Utilizing Azure
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots are installed in the backrooms of roughly 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, where they detect depleted beverage shelves and restock them automatically, with remote human takeover when AI stocking fails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing uniform items onto display shelving in a retail store. Shows shelf-filling autonomy exists only where a rail-mounted machine, fixed shelf geometry and standardized SKUs are engineered around the robot, not for arbitrary room shelving.

sources.title: TidyBot: personalized robot assistance with large language models | Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: TidyBot, a research mobile manipulator, tidies real rooms by picking up objects and putting them away according to learned user preferences, succeeding with 85% of objects in real-world tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting away varied objects in an as-found room — the closest analogue to tidying and organizing a classroom. Cited to show that in-room organizing is still a research demo at ~85% success, below worker-acceptable reliability.

tasks.label: Select, store, order, issue, and inventory classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-lesson issuing and collecting of materials in the teacher's own classroom: passing out worksheet packets, class-set textbooks, novels, calculators, lab kits or art supplies to ~28 seated middle schoolers within a minute or two, then collecting and re-stacking them at the bell, with backpacks, moving students and shifted desks in the aisles.

Receiving deliveries and storing supplies: opening boxes of paper, notebooks, markers, science consumables delivered to the room or stockroom, breaking them down, and putting them away by category into classroom cabinets, closets, drawers and stockroom shelving, some high or crowded.

Periodic count of durable, tagged, shelved items: class textbook sets in the book room, Chromebook/laptop carts, calculator sets, reconciling barcoded counts and condition against the school's inventory list at end of term.

Checking and counting loose consumables and small equipment inside closed classroom cabinets, drawers and lab cupboards: glue sticks, markers, rulers, beakers, probeware, mixed bins with no fixed arrangement, noting shortages and damage.

Selecting and ordering: reviewing what is running low, choosing curriculum-appropriate items from vendor catalogs and district-approved lists within a small budget, and submitting requisitions/purchase orders through the district system.

Start-of-year individual issue and end-of-year collection of textbooks and 1:1 devices: scanning each copy/device to the individual student's record, noting condition, distributing to ~120-150 students across sections, and reclaiming and reconciling them later.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously navigates operating grocery stores, scanning shelves to capture product availability, price and placement data used to correct out-of-stocks; deployed across 17 Harmons stores after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory and out-of-stock detection. It transfers to counting shelved, labeled classroom/stockroom stock and flagging what needs reordering: same act of traversing a human-occupied facility, reading labels on shelved goods, and reconciling counts to a stock record.

sources.title: UPS deploys Verity warehouse drones for inventory tracking
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous drones fly warehouse aisles unattended to count and locate inventory, deployed commercially with UPS Supply Chain Solutions and reported at ~99.9% accuracy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. Counting tagged, shelved items and reconciling them to a records system is the same operation as an end-of-term textbook/device count, performed inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from containers and trailers at DHL sites (10 units across three countries by mid-2025, up to 700 cases/hour), with an agreement covering 1,000+ more units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading delivered cartons. This is the intake half of 'receive and store supplies' — same boxes of paper/consumables — but it delivers cases to a conveyor in a purpose-built cell, not into cabinets in a room.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking arms are deployed across Staples' North American fulfillment centers, gripping individual office/school supply items of varying shape and size at a presented pick station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking of office-supply SKUs (the very items a teacher stocks and issues) at a fixtured station; it substantiates machine handling of these objects when the work is presented to the machine, i.e., the E1 counterfactual.

sources.title: How AutoStore Works - Everything You Need to Know
sources.claim: AutoStore grid robots autonomously store and retrieve inventory bins and present them to operator ports for picking or replenishment, with near-perfect pick accuracy; the system is in commercial use across hundreds of installations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage, retrieval and perpetual inventory of small goods. Storing, issuing and counting supplies is exactly what an AS/RS does once the goods are decanted into its bins — the purpose-built (E1) form of this task.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi autonomously fetches and delivers supplies, lab specimens and medications through occupied hospital corridors and elevators; deployed in more than 25 ... with over one million deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply transport in a staffed institution. It shows autonomous point-to-point delivery of supplies at E2, but the accepted output is a drop-off, not putting items away in cabinets or issuing them to individuals.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated shelves with bottled and ... drinks in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, under remote monitoring with human teleoperation used only when the robot fails.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking inside a human retail facility. It is the closest deployed analogue to putting supplies away, but it works on one standardized product class at a fixed, pre-registered cooler shelf, not heterogeneous items in varied cabinets.

sources.title: 21st Century Libraries: Changing from the Ground Up
sources.claim: LaptopsAnytime automated dispensing kiosks store, charge, dispense and take back laptops and tablets unattended for individual borrowers in academic and public libraries and schools, handling more than four million device ... worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated device lending. Issuing a device to a named individual and recording the loan, then accepting and re-storing it, is the machine form of a teacher's device/textbook issue — but it happens inside a purpose-built enclosure with items in known bays.

sources.system: School supply vending machine (Haile Middle School)
sources.title: New school supplies vending machine meets Haile Middle students' needs
sources.claim: A school-supply vending machine funded by two teachers was installed at Haile Middle School to dispense pencils, paper and other supplies to students unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended dispensing of classroom consumables to middle schoolers. It substantiates issuing supplies when items are pre-loaded into fixed, purpose-built bays and the student comes to the machine (the E1 counterfactual), not distribution at desks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide students with disabilities with assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-lesson setup or troubleshooting of a named student's supportive technology in a 25-30 student classroom: pairing an FM/DM hearing transmitter, launching and configuring text-to-speech / speech-to-text / screen reader on the student's Chromebook or iPad, swapping batteries or chargers, mounting or repositioning an AAC device on a wheelchair tray, pushing an enlarged-print or digital copy of the day's materials.

Distributing and positioning low-tech assistive devices and adapted materials at the student's own workstation: slant board, pencil grip, adapted scissors or manipulatives, magnifier, noise-reducing headphones, wobble cushion, raised-line paper; adjusting desk/chair height and placing items within the student's reach, prompted by the IEP and by watching the student struggle.

Retrieving a needed device or consumable from elsewhere in the building mid-period - a charged iPad from the AT charging cart, a talking calculator from the resource room, a replacement charger or hearing-aid battery from the office - selecting the correct item and getting it into the student's hands before the activity ends.

Accompanying a student who uses a wheelchair or has limited mobility along a familiar route inside the school (classroom to elevator to another classroom, or to the accessible restroom door) at a time when halls are relatively clear: steering or pushing the chair, holding doors, calling the elevator, carrying the student's materials.

The same mobility/facility-access help under crowded or dynamic conditions: passing period with hundreds of students in the corridor, fire drill or evacuation, bus/field-trip loading, retrieving a dropped crutch or walker, steadying an unsteady student on stairs or a wet floor.

Personal-care level restroom access assistance per the student's IEP: escorting the student into the accessible restroom, managing door and stall, steadying or assisting a transfer, helping with clothing/hygiene as directed, supervising for safety and dignity, and returning the student to class.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulator, is deployed in more than 25 ... and has completed over a million intra-facility deliveries of small items, navigating crowded corridors and riding elevators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching and delivering small supplies inside an institutional building. It bears on the instance of bringing a device from an AT cart or office to a classroom - same class of object (handheld items), same class of environment (corridors, elevators, people present) - but Moxi is loaded by staff and drops items into a bin rather than selecting a specific student's device and handing it over.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to acquire hospital logistics provider Diligent Robotics - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi's arm lets it open doors and operate elevators, and it operates routinely in very crowded indoor human environments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous door-opening and elevator use while moving through an occupied institutional building, the navigation component of escorting or delivering inside a school; it does not cover physical assistance to a person.

sources.title: BayCare Expands Autonomous Hospital Delivery with New Relay Robots at Winter Haven Hospitals
sources.claim: Relay delivery robots autonomously transport lab specimens, pharmaceuticals and supplies point-to-point in hospitals and hotels, with a reported 99.8% delivery success rate in a 2025 pilot at ~50 deliveries per day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reliable autonomous item transport within a staffed institutional building, comparable to walking a charged device from a storage room to a classroom; the recipient must remove the item from the robot's secured bin, so handover to and setup for a specific student is not covered.

sources.title: BD and Henry Ford Health Sign Pharmacy Automation Partnership to Revolutionize Medication Storage and Prescription Delivery
sources.claim: BD Rowa Vmax is a commercially deployed robotic storage and dispensing system that automatically retrieves a specified boxed item from structured storage and delivers it to the dispensing point in a pharmacy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: on-demand retrieval of a specified small item from a purpose-built fixtured store and presentation of it to a waiting person. This is the E1 form of 'issue the student the device they need' - comparable objects (small boxes/handheld items), comparable precision, and a machine-built storage and delivery path.

sources.title: These speedy BD robot arms store and retrieve medications in seconds - Drug Delivery Business
sources.claim: The Rowa Vmax robot arm autonomously stores and retrieves boxed pharmaceuticals in high volume.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the BD news release: fixtured pick-and-present of a specified small item, the E1 analogue of handing a student the assistive item called for by their plan.

sources.title: Unifi Aviation Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs carry mobility-impaired passengers along pre-mapped routes through airport terminals without an attendant, then return to base by themselves; the service is live at DTW, LAX, MIA, SEA, Schiphol and others.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a seated person with a mobility impairment along a mapped route through a busy institution-controlled building, which is what a teacher does when pushing a student's chair from class to class; the passenger must board and leave the chair unaided, so transfers, doors at stalls and hands-on support are not covered.

sources.title: Detroit Metro Airport Is Testing Autonomous Wheelchairs
sources.claim: More than 100 WHILL autonomous wheelchairs are in service at US airports and have completed over 400,000 autonomous rides; each chair drops the passenger and returns to base automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Scale and reliability evidence for the same related task (autonomous transport of a mobility-impaired person inside a controlled facility).

sources.title: Classroom robot helps keep kids with learning disabilities on track
sources.claim: Robots used with students with learning disabilities in classrooms are social/instructional platforms run from an instructor's tablet, not systems that handle devices or physically assist students.
sources.transferJustification: Closest school-based robot evidence found for supporting students with disabilities; it is instructor-triggered and non-manipulative, so it cannot substantiate device setup, handout, or facility-access assistance.

roles.description: Teach occupational, vocational, career, or technical subjects to students at the middle, intermediate, or junior high school level.

tasks.label: Instruct students individually and in groups, using various teaching methods, such as lectures, discussions, and demonstrations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-class direct instruction in a middle-school CTE classroom (e.g., intro to careers, safety rules, business/computer or engineering concepts): teacher lectures with slides/board to 25-30 adolescents, poses questions, checks understanding, adjusts pacing, and manages behavior for a 45-minute period.

Hands-on demonstration in a shop, lab, kitchen or ag classroom: teacher physically performs a procedure with real tools and materials (threading a sewing machine, soldering a joint, setting up a scroll saw or 3D printer, knife skills, wiring a circuit) while narrating each step, showing common errors, fielding student questions, and enforcing safety with students crowded around the bench.

Individual and small-group instruction during lab/project work: teacher circulates among workstations, diagnoses a particular student's mistake in an unfinished workpiece or code, re-demonstrates the technique hand-over-hand or on the student's own materials, and gives corrective feedback tailored to that student, including students with IEPs/504 accommodations.

Facilitated group discussion or collaborative activity (design brainstorm, career-exploration discussion, team project critique) in the classroom: teacher poses prompts, calls on students, moderates turn-taking and off-task behavior, synthesizes responses on the board.

Instruction delivered outside the standard classroom: school greenhouse/garden plot, an off-campus farm, job-site visit or partner workshop, where the teacher demonstrates and explains a procedure amid variable weather, layouts and bystanders.

sources.system: Xiao An humanoid classroom robot (Hefei AI education application)
sources.developer: Local Hefei enterprise / Hefei city government project
sources.title: Humanoid robot makes test lecture at primary school in E.China, inspiring students to engage in 'deeper learning'
sources.claim: Frontier classroom humanoid: a 1.4 m humanoid 'Xiao An' delivered a trial science lecture at a Hefei primary school, but it served as a teaching assistant working with the human teacher, not as the instructor of record; autonomy of its lesson delivery is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering a science lesson to a class of children. It is the closest analogue to middle-school classroom instruction, but the robot only assisted a human teacher for a single trial lecture, so it does not substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.system: Social robots in education (NAO and similar platforms, review of the field)
sources.developer: Belpaeme et al., Science Robotics review
sources.title: Social robots for education: A review | Science Robotics
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of social robots in education: robots match human tutoring only on restricted tasks and function as tutors or peer learners, not as autonomous classroom teachers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot tutoring of school-age children. Establishes the ceiling of the field — narrow, restricted-content tutoring — which is well short of instructing a full CTE class with demonstrations and individualized coaching.

sources.system: NAO / Pepper social robots in classrooms
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics (platforms); review by Neumann et al. citing Woo et al.
sources.title: Do Robotic Tutors Compromise the Social-Emotional Development of Children?
sources.claim: Review evidence that commercially available social robots (NAO, Pepper) cannot be integrated into classrooms without extensive human support and resource mobilization.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered classroom instruction/tutoring. Directly bears on whether a robot could substitute for a teacher's instructional role in a school classroom.

sources.developer: Korea Institute of Science and Technology (KIST)
sources.title: The World As We Speak - Language Magazine
sources.claim: The largest deployed 'robot teacher' program (Engkey, 29 units in Daegu schools) relied on remote human teachers in the Philippines for the interactive avatar version; the autonomous version only ran a preprogrammed elementary English curriculum alongside classroom teachers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led language instruction to elementary classes. The most extensive school deployment to date, and it was teleoperated or narrowly scripted, showing that classroom instruction has not been completed autonomously.

sources.title: TeachBot: Towards teaching robotics fundamentals for human-robot collaboration at work
sources.claim: TeachBot is an autonomous robotic ... lectures and physically demonstrates movements to teach manufacturing workers robotics fundamentals — a fixed, single-topic curriculum delivered one-on-one at a workstation, not multi-student class instruction with adaptive feedback and safety supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instructing a human learner via lecture plus physical demonstration. Closest analogue to a CTE demonstration, but it teaches only its own scripted robotics module to adult trainees, with no tool handling, student questioning, or class management.

sources.system: SoftBank Pepper social robot in a school
sources.title: "It's Important to Think of Pepper as a Teaching Aid or Resource External to the Classroom": A Social Robot in a School
sources.claim: A three-week embedding of a Pepper robot in a school concluded the robot is best treated as a teaching aid or resource external to the classroom rather than a substitute for teacher-led instruction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained in-school use of a humanoid social robot with children. Shows that even multi-week school deployments position the robot as an adjunct resource, not as the instructor.

tasks.label: Prepare materials and classrooms for class activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hands-on tech-ed / engineering / woodshop lab prep: before a project period the teacher lays out hand tools, fasteners, wood or plastic stock, safety glasses and project folders at each of 6-10 workbenches, loads filament in the 3D printers, sets up the bandsaw/drill press guards and checks that shared machines are ready.

Paper and consumable prep: teacher photocopies worksheets, rubrics, safety contracts and project plans, collates and staples per-student packets, and sets one packet plus pencils/rulers/calculators at each seat or station before the bell.

Computer lab / device and AV prep: unlock and roll out the Chromebook/laptop cart, put a charged device at each seat, wake devices and load the day's software or CAD/coding project, connect and focus the projector or panel, and re-dock/plug devices for charging.

Family & consumer sciences lab prep: portion flour, sugar, eggs, produce into bowls for each of 4-6 kitchen stations, set out mixing bowls, measuring cups, cutting boards and utensils, preheat ovens; or thread and test sewing machines and cut fabric/pattern pieces per station.

Room reconfiguration and reset between back-to-back classes: push desks/tables from rows into pods or activity stations, clear leftover projects, scraps and stray supplies off work surfaces, wipe benches, restage supply bins at each pod, and post signage/agenda.

Kit assembly for a project unit: counting and sorting small components (robotics/electronics parts, sensors, seedlings and soil cups, health-science supplies) into one labeled bin or tray per team, replenishing consumables from the storeroom.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously identifies, picks and places individual products of widely varying shape, size and weight in production fulfillment centers, sorting and consolidating items into totes/containers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking and consolidating diverse items into order containers in a purpose-built robotic cell. Transfers to assembling per-station trays/bins of classroom supplies and small components: comparable object variety and size, comparable place precision (into a container), and the same kind of fixtured, machine-built workcell.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics — Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick system is a commercial piece-picking cell used for automated kitting, picking very small items and placing them into designated cubbies/containers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse kitting. Preparing a project kit or station tray for each student team is the same operation — pick specified small items from source totes and place a set into a labeled container — at the same precision and object scale, in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: FANUC CRX Cobots for Machine Tending & Part Transfer
sources.claim: Collaborative robots are commercially deployed to load and unload machine tools autonomously, letting a machine run without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine tending. Readying shop equipment (loading stock/consumables into a machine, presenting workpieces at a station) is the same load/present operation with comparable objects and tolerances, in a cell built around the robot.

sources.title: The Rise of Robotics: Automating Wide Format Print Production
sources.claim: Durst's P5 Robotics system uses KUKA arms to pick individual sheets, including thin paper-like stock, off a stack, register them and place them precisely for the next production step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sheet handling in print production. Handling and precisely placing individual sheets/stacks of paper is the manipulation core of preparing and setting out copied handout packets, with the same material and placement precision, in a purpose-built line.

sources.system: FANUC robots for paper and printing
sources.title: Automation for Paper & Printing Industries | FANUC America
sources.claim: Industrial robots are commercially applied in the paper and printing industry to transfer paper stacks and printed sheets between presses, cutters and finishing (collating/binding) equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: paper handling in print finishing lines. Copying, collating and stacking per-student packets is the same class of material handling at the same precision, performed in a machine-built line rather than a classroom.

sources.system: Chef Robotics food assembly robot / ChefOS
sources.title: Food Assembly Robot Startup Chef Robotics Raises $43M Series A as it Reaches 40 Million Meal Milestone
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' arms autonomously portion and plate ingredients into containers on food-production lines at customer sites, having assembled over 40 million meals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic portioning of varied ingredients into trays on a production line. Setting out measured ingredients in bowls for each kitchen station is the same dispense-and-place operation with the same materials and portion tolerances, when the containers are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Jack In The Box Is The Latest Restaurant Chain To Test Miso Robotics' Kitchen Automation
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy 2 works a restaurant fry station using computer vision and AI, and has been installed in White Castle and Jack in the Box kitchens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating fixed kitchen equipment (fryer, drink station) at a purpose-built station. Readying cooking appliances and moving food containers in a foods lab involves the same equipment interaction, though Flippy is installed as a dedicated station rather than roaming a lab.

sources.system: Digit (Agility Robotics) at GXO Logistics, Flowery Branch, GA
sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid has run full-time in a live GXO fulfillment workflow for over a year, autonomously unloading totes from mobile robots, loading conveyors and stacking containers at floor locations, passing 100,000 totes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid tote staging in a human-scale facility. It is the closest deployed evidence for moving bins of materials to stations in a human work building; it is limited to uniform totes at a fixed, marked station, which is why it does not extend to setting out heterogeneous classroom materials.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in more than 30 US hospitals, autonomously delivering medications, lab specimens, supplies and equipment through corridors and elevators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetching and delivering supplies inside an institutional building (E2). It shows what mobile manipulators reliably do in such settings — point-to-point transport of packaged items — and not the fine, multi-object arrangement of a classroom, bounding the E2 judgment.

sources.title: Avidbots releases floor-scrubbing robot for industrial spaces
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor scrubber ... commercially deployed to clean large facilities including schools, with over 1,000 robots in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor cleaning inside school buildings. It covers only the floor-cleaning fragment of a room reset; it involves no manipulation of furniture, materials or work surfaces, so it cannot substantiate completing a classroom reconfiguration.

tasks.label: Adapt teaching methods and instructional materials to meet students' varying needs and interests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Use computers, audio-visual aids, and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard middle school CTE classroom lesson (e.g., business/computer applications, health science): teacher logs into the classroom computer, projects a slide deck and short video on the interactive panel/projector, advances slides, plays/pauses and rewinds video, adjusts volume and lighting, and switches between browser tabs and student-facing apps while narrating and responding to ~25 adolescents.

AV and computer setup/troubleshooting around a lesson: waking or powering the projector/interactive panel, connecting a laptop via HDMI/USB-C dongle, pairing speakers or a wireless mic, wheeling in and distributing a Chromebook/tablet cart, plugging in chargers, and fixing devices that won't display for students mid-class.

Live hands-on demonstration in a CTE lab/shop supplementing a presentation: placing a workpiece, hand tool, food item, circuit board or 3D-printed part under a document camera or on a demo bench, manipulating it step-by-step while narrating, and passing samples around the room for students to inspect.

Setting up and running equipment stations that students use immediately after the presentation: loading filament and starting 3D printers, threading sewing machines, laying out robotics kits, soldering stations or lab trays at each bench, verifying each works, and swapping materials between class periods.

Presentation in a non-standard setting: portable AV cart and laptop for a gym/auditorium assembly, a tablet/speaker in the school greenhouse, garden or ag plot, or a laptop and printed handouts at an off-site work-based-learning visit, with variable layout, lighting, power and network.

sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics / university researchers (Rosanda et al.)
sources.title: Robot NAO integrated lesson vs. traditional lesson: Measuring learning outcomes on the topic of "societal change" - British Journal of Educational Technology
sources.claim: Research deployments of the NAO social robot in real classrooms have the robot autonomously speak lesson material with gestures as a teaching-assistant-like presenter; the robot does not operate classroom computers, projectors or physical demonstration materials, and is not programmed to answer student questions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering instructional content in a school classroom. It does not substantiate this task because the robot never handles the computer, AV equipment, or physical materials that the task consists of; it only speaks and gestures.

sources.system: SoftBank Pepper in a Special Educational Needs school
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics / University of Hertfordshire-affiliated researchers
sources.title: "It's Important to Think of Pepper as a Teaching Aid or Resource External to the Classroom": A Social Robot in a School for Autistic Children
sources.claim: A three-week embedded deployment of a Pepper social robot in a school found that its automatic perception of a classroom of children was unreliable outside the lab and had to be replaced with human operation, and the robot functioned as a resource outside normal classroom teaching rather than running classroom technology.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-supported instruction in a real school. Shows that even perception-only classroom autonomy degrades with real classes; the robot performs no manipulation of AV gear or materials, so it cannot substantiate this task.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid / Optio AI teacher's assistant, Salamanca City Central School District
sources.title: US Firm's Humanoid Robot Teaching Assistant to Support 500 Students in 2026 | eWeek
sources.claim: The most advanced 2026 humanoid deployment in a US school is a seated, conversational Realbotix M-Series robot plus an AI tutor avatar; it engages students by speech and facial expression and does not manipulate classroom computers, projectors, or lab materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: embodied assistant in a live classroom. It does not transfer: the system is a conversational, largely stationary robot with no demonstrated autonomous manipulation of presentation equipment or teaching materials.

sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic insertion of a cable into a port is demonstrated commercially only in single-purpose, fixtured settings (vehicle charging bays with rail-mounted arms and vision), currently in pilot with large-scale deployment planned later.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cable plugging. It does not transfer to classroom AV setup: the connector, port geometry and approach are fixed and purpose-engineered, whereas classroom work means varied dongles, laptops, panel menus and ad-hoc troubleshooting.

tasks.label: Instruct and monitor students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injuries and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Technology/engineering (STEM-maker) lab: teacher demonstrates safe operation and care of hand tools, soldering irons, 3D printers, laser cutter, and robotics kits to a class of ~25 twelve-to-fourteen-year-olds, then circulates among rotating stations enforcing eye protection, correcting grip and machine settings, stopping horseplay, and shutting down misused machines before damage or injury occurs.

Family & Consumer Sciences foods lab: teacher demonstrates knife skills, range/oven/mixer use, hot-pan handling, and cleaning/sanitizing of equipment; then supervises 5-6 kitchen units simultaneously during a lab period, intervening for burns, cuts, unattended burners, and improper cleanup or storage of utensils.

FACS textiles lab: teacher demonstrates threading, needle changes, iron/pressing safety, and machine care (lint, tension, oiling); supervises ~25 sewing machines running at once, clearing jams, preventing needle-through-finger incidents and machine damage from forcing fabric or wrong settings.

Industrial-tech/woodshop with powered equipment: teacher gives machine-specific demonstrations (scroll saw, drill press, sander, band saw), administers safety check-offs, verifies guards and push sticks, and continuously circulates during work time, physically stopping machines and correcting stance/feed to prevent injury.

Business/computer applications or digital-media lab: teacher instructs students in proper handling, transport, charging-cart storage and cleaning of Chromebooks, cameras, microphones and headsets, and monitors the class to prevent cable yanking, screen damage, spills, and mishandling during the period.

Agriculture/greenhouse or health-science lab on school grounds: teacher demonstrates and supervises use of pruners, trowels, potting/irrigation equipment, small animals or lab glassware and simulation manikins; monitors students working in a greenhouse or outdoor school plot in variable weather.

sources.title: TeachBot: Towards teaching robotics fundamentals for human-robot collaboration at work
sources.claim: TeachBot is a fully autonomous robotic instructor built on a collaborative arm that lectures and physically demonstrates to a single adult trainee at a fixed training station how to use a robot; it is a research prototype teaching about the robot itself, with no supervision of a class or intervention in learners' tool handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instructing a human in the use of a machine. Transfer fails for this task: TeachBot teaches one adult about the single robot it embodies at a purpose-built station, and neither monitors a class of children handling saws, ranges or sewing machines nor intervenes to prevent injury or equipment damage.

sources.title: Florida School Deploys Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)
sources.claim: Knightscope K5 autonomous security robots are commercially deployed on school campuses, where they patrol grounds and parking areas and act as a mobile call box; they observe and report but do not instruct anyone in equipment use or physically intervene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous monitoring of a school facility. Transfer fails: the K5 patrols outdoor campus areas for security anomalies; it has no manipulator, gives no equipment demonstrations, and cannot detect or stop unsafe tool use inside a shop or kitchen lab.

sources.title: US firm to deploy humanoid robot teaching assistant in New York schools
sources.claim: Realbotix's Optio AI teaching assistant and M-Series humanoid are being piloted in a New York school ... for classroom engagement and tutoring; the role is conversational academic support, not hands-on equipment demonstration or lab supervision, and the degree of autonomy is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot as classroom teaching assistant. Transfer fails: the pilot covers tutoring and engagement dialogue with a human teacher present; nothing in it shows demonstration of tool use, monitoring of students at machines, or injury prevention.

sources.title: AI-powered safety assistance system
sources.claim: The Altendorf Hand Guard is a commercial AI-camera safety device mounted on sliding table saws that detects a hand in the danger zone and automatically triggers a protective response; it is a machine guard, not a system that instructs or supervises students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated injury prevention at one machine. Transfer fails: it protects a single saw reflexively and delivers no instruction, no care-of-equipment coaching, and no supervision of a class across multiple machines and materials.

instances.label: Technology/engineering-STEM exploratory lab in a middle school: teacher opens with a ~10-minute framing of the design challenge, then physically demonstrates a tool or process at the front bench (hot-glue gun and safety, calipers, leveling/loading a 3D printer, wiring a micro:bit circuit), then releases 24-30 twelve-year-olds to team build time, circulating to question, prompt investigation, troubleshoot builds, and redirect off-task or unsafe behavior.

Family & Consumer Sciences foods or sewing lab: sanitation/safety review, a live teacher demonstration at a demo station (knife cuts, measuring and mixing, threading a machine and winding a bobbin), then rotating student teams working at kitchen or sewing stations for ~25 minutes while the teacher monitors heat sources and needles, fields questions, and inspects product quality.

Business/computer applications or career-exploration class in a computer classroom: projected step-by-step software demonstration, short guided practice, then independent or paired project work with the teacher circulating to question students, prompt investigation, resolve hardware/peripheral problems, and keep the class on task.

Agriculture, greenhouse, or industrial-arts shop period: a safety and technique demonstration on a machine or process (scroll saw, drill press, sanding, plant propagation, small-engine teardown), followed by student work at benches with the teacher granting tool permissions, supervising machine use, questioning students about what they observe, and stopping unsafe practice.

Planning and preparation before class (prep period, empty classroom/lab): designing the week's balanced sequence of instruction, demonstration, and work time against state CTE standards; assembling and staging demonstration materials and per-station kits; testing equipment and consumables so the investigation will work for every group.

sources.system: Realbotix 'Sally' humanoid / Optio AI teacher's assistant
sources.title: Can a Humanoid Robot Help Teach High School?
sources.claim: The most-publicized US school humanoid, Realbotix's 'Sally' at Salamanca City Central School ..., is a stationary seated android providing conversational learning support; it explicitly does not replace the classroom teacher and performs no tool handling, demonstration, or lab supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: this is the state of the art for a robot 'conducting' school instruction, and it is limited to seated conversation, so it cannot deliver the demonstration and work-time components.

sources.title: Can a Humanoid Robot Help Teach High School?
sources.claim: The same deployment is described as a stationary, seated robot with upper-body movement and facial expressions only, confirming no locomotion or manipulation capability needed to demonstrate hand skills or circulate during student work time.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the physical envelope of the leading classroom humanoid: it cannot manipulate tools or materials, which the demonstration and work-time parts of this task require.

sources.system: CARE customized assistive robot-based education system
sources.developer: Khalifa University / research consortium (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: CARE: towards customized assistive robot-based education
sources.claim: The strongest peer-reviewed case of an autonomous classroom education robot (CARE) delivered adaptive verbal/digital instructional content to a handful of elementary pupils in a research trial; it did not plan a program, demonstrate hands-on technical skills, or manage a full class during work time.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task (autonomous delivery of instruction in a classroom); it substantiates only content delivery to a few students, not the demonstration, physical setup, and supervised work-time components of this task.

sources.developer: Realbotix / Salamanca City Central School District
sources.title: Salamanca Superintendent sets the record straight on AI-powered robot coming to the classroom
sources.claim: District leadership publicly characterized the classroom robot as an assistive tool rather than a substitute for teaching, indicating no deployed system conducts a class session at worker quality.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: confirms the deployed system does not conduct instruction in place of the teacher.

Teacher assembles instructional materials for upcoming lessons — slide decks, project instruction sheets, worksheets, station cards, parts/ingredient lists — and organizes copies and files so the class can run as planned.

tasks.label: Provide students with disabilities with assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In the CTE classroom/computer lab, the teacher provides an individual student their assistive technology at the start of a lesson: retrieving the student's AAC tablet, laptop with screen reader, adapted keyboard/switch, magnifier, or FM hearing system from a cabinet or charging cart, placing and angling it on the student's desk or wheelchair mount, powering it on, connecting it, and confirming the student can operate it.

In the shop/kitchen/greenhouse lab, the teacher supplies and sets up adapted tools and workstation modifications for hands-on work: adapted scissors or one-handed jigs, clamps that stabilize a workpiece, raised or lowered bench, non-slip mats, guarded equipment, and positioning the student's wheelchair or stool safely at the bench amid other students and running machines.

Mobility and access assistance inside the school building: pushing or steering a student's manual wheelchair between the lab and another room, opening and holding heavy doors, carrying the student's materials, retrieving a dropped crutch or walker, guiding a student with low vision along a changed route, and accompanying the student to the accessible restroom door during a crowded passing period.

Restroom/personal-care level assistance for a student with significant physical disability: getting the student into the accessible stall, steadying or assisting a transfer, managing clothing and hygiene, and returning the student to class on schedule (often shared with a paraprofessional or nurse).

Fetching, returning, and swapping equipment between rooms in the school building: bringing a charged device or spare battery from the resource/AT room or charging station to the classroom, returning borrowed equipment, or carrying a device to the AT specialist's office.

Off-campus or outdoor CTE activity (community job-shadow site, worksite tour, greenhouse/ag plot, field trip): providing the student's device, adapting it to the unfamiliar site, and assisting the student over curbs, gravel, thresholds and into unfamiliar restrooms that are not kept to any standard.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator, autonomously fetches and delivers supplies, medications and lab specimens within hospital buildings, riding elevators and working around people; deployed commercially in 25+ US hospitals with over 1.25 million autonomous deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital point-to-point retrieval and delivery of small supplies. Transfers to the school instance of fetching a charged device, spare battery or piece of equipment from a resource room to a classroom: comparable small handheld objects, comparable precision (grasp from a drawer/cart, place at a delivery point), and the same class of institution-controlled indoor corridors, doors and elevators shared with people.

sources.title: Unifi Launches WHILL Autonomous Service at Detroit Airport
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous personal mobility chairs are deployed commercially at airports, where a passenger with reduced mobility boards at a designated station, selects a destination, and the chair drives itself along the concourse and returns empty to base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a mobility-limited person across an institutional facility. It bounds, rather than substantiates, the school escort instance: the rider must board and transfer unaided on a mapped route, and the chair does not open doors, handle the student's own wheelchair or mobility aids, guide a student with low vision, or assist inside a restroom.

sources.system: Stretch RE1 with SIRA handover demo
sources.title: Pickup and Handover Object to Person Using ArUco Markers - Stretch Forum
sources.claim: Autonomous robot-to-human handover of an everyday object by a mobile manipulator exists only as a laboratory demonstration built on fiducial markers, not as a deployed capability in occupied human facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-to-human object handover, the core physical act in giving a student an assistive device. Cited to show the state of the art is a marker-based lab demo, not delivery of a personal device set up and verified for a specific student in an occupied classroom.

sources.title: Yueban Xiaoban is a self-driving robot toilet for people with limited mobility
sources.claim: A self-driving robot toilet intended to remove the need to travel to a restroom was shown at a 2026 trade expo for mobility-impaired users; it is an exhibited product concept rather than a system documented completing toileting assistance in institutional service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: toileting support for people with limited mobility. Cited only to bound the restroom-assistance instance: it is an expo demo with unverified autonomy and does not perform transfers, clothing management or hygiene assistance for a student.

instances.label: Issue and recover tools/materials during class: in a middle-school shop, FCS, or robotics lab, hand out hand tools, power tools, kits, project stock and PPE to ~28 students at the start of the period, then collect, wipe down, and account for every item on shadow boards, tool boxes and bins before dismissal, chasing down missing items.

Receive and store deliveries: unpack cartons of lumber, fabric, food, filament, electronics kits and consumables, check contents against packing slips, break down boxes, and shelve items in the correct labeled cabinet, bin or drawer, with chemicals/hazardous and high-value items placed in locked storage.
Count consumables and materials held on labeled open shelving and racks in the lab/storeroom against the stock list, recording quantities and flagging shortages.

Asset inventory of tools, kits, laptops/tablets and small equipment kept in drawers, cabinets, tool boards and carts; verify each against the district asset/fixed-equipment list, note damaged or missing items, and reconcile the record.

Routine maintenance and upkeep of classroom equipment: sharpen or change blades and drill bits, oil and re-thread sewing machines, clear 3D-printer nozzles and level beds, clean ovens/mixers and shop vacuums, inspect cords, guards and safety switches, replace filters, and tag out equipment needing repair.

Determine what is running low by walking the lab and checking bins/shelves, compare vendor catalogs and prices, spec items to the curriculum and safety rules, prepare purchase requisitions within the CTE budget, and follow up on backorders and substitutions.

sources.title: RoboCrib® VX1000 | Industrial Vending Machine | Snap-on AutoCrib®
sources.claim: Snap-on AutoCrib RoboCrib industrial dispensing machines, with attached AutoLocker FX modules, automatically issue tools, consumables, power tools and laptops to badge-identified users from a purpose-built point-of-use machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing and checking in tools at an industrial tool crib. Same object classes (hand tools, power tools, consumables, laptops) and the same accountability standard (who has what, returned or not) as issuing tools to a class, with the storage purpose-built around the machine.

sources.system: AutoCrib industrial vending systems / Intelliport RFID crib
sources.title: AutoCrib Vending Systems – Toolneeds
sources.claim: AutoCrib vending and RFID crib systems issue and take back tools and supplies on ID/fingerprint identification, tracking every transaction and providing full issue-and-return accountability with no attendant present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tool-crib issue/return and perpetual inventory in industry. The accounting output (who took which tool, what came back, what is missing) is the same output a CTE teacher must produce at the end of a lab period and at inventory time.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trailers and containers in DHL distribution centers, in commercial multi-site deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving and unloading delivered cartons. Same first step of the teacher's receiving instance (getting mixed cases off a pallet/truck and onto conveyance) with comparable box sizes and no fixturing of individual cartons.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot picks and stows individual items of roughly three quarters of stocked item types into fabric storage pods at speeds comparable to employees, deployed at fulfillment centers in Spokane and Hamburg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level put-away into storage. Placing heterogeneous small goods into designated storage compartments is the core of shelving classroom supplies, but only where the storage and item presentation are engineered around the robot.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally, an autonomous shelf-scanning robot, is deployed across grocery chains (17 Harmons stores; ~1,000 stores overall) where it audits product availability, placement and pricing on shelves during normal store operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counting and verifying stock on shelves in a human-occupied facility. Comparable objects (boxed/packaged consumables on labeled shelving), comparable output (counts and shortages reconciled to a list), and the robot navigates aisles shared with people.

sources.title: Simbe upgrades vision platform with AI-powered capabilities
sources.claim: Simbe's vision platform detects products running low on shelf before they go out of stock, enabling proactive replenishment ordering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: walking the storeroom to see what consumables need reordering. Same physical act (visually assessing quantity remaining in labeled storage) producing the same trigger for a replenishment order.

sources.title: How GEODIS Solved a Costly and Labor-Intensive Inventory Problem with Gather AI
sources.claim: Gather AI's autonomous drones scan warehouse racking, reading barcodes, lot codes and box counts and reconciling them against the WMS; at GEODIS one operator's drone completes 1,200 location scans per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cycle counting stock in a human work facility. Produces the same reconciled count-versus-record output required by a storeroom inventory, in a facility kept to a working standard rather than built around the robot.

sources.system: KUKA KR CYBERTECH grinding/polishing cells (Liow-Shye / Atlantic Chef)
sources.title: Automated grinding and polishing by robot | KUKA
sources.claim: More than 30 KUKA KR CYBERTECH robots grind and polish kitchen knife blades in a knife manufacturer's production cells, replacing operator-dependent hand sharpening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting an edge on a blade held against a grinding wheel — the same physical operation as sharpening a chisel or plane iron, but only as an isolated sub-step of the teacher's maintenance instance.

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as school library assistance, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hallway duty during middle-school passing periods: teacher stands at an assigned corridor/stairwell post, physically present among 100-400 moving 11-14 year-olds, checks hall passes, keeps traffic moving, redirects horseplay, separates a shoving match, escorts a defiant or upset student to the office, radios for help.

Cafeteria duty during one or two lunch waves: circulates among crowded tables, keeps lines orderly, enforces seating/noise/phone rules, opens stubborn containers and helps with spills or dropped trays, watches for allergy/choking incidents and fights, dismisses tables and checks trash/tray return before the bell.

Bus loading/unloading duty in the bus loop or curbside at arrival and dismissal, in rain, cold or heat: keeps students behind the line, directs them to numbered buses, helps with backpacks/instruments/projects, stops students crossing behind buses, coordinates with drivers and administrators, handles late buses and misrouted students.

Other assigned supervision coverage inside the building: study hall or detention proctoring, covering another teacher's class or an assembly, restroom/locker-bank sweeps, monitoring a testing session - maintaining order, taking attendance, and responding to incidents.

Library/media center assistance during a duty period: staffs the circulation desk, checks materials in and out, helps students locate books and use equipment, supervises students working at tables, resets computers/printers and tidies the space.

Back-of-house library materials handling only: a cart of returned books and media is processed - items checked in, sorted, and put back into their storage locations - plus pulling requested titles for staff and students.

sources.title: Florida School Deploys Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)
sources.claim: Knightscope's K5 Autonomous Security Robot, an autonomous patrolling machine, was deployed on a central Florida school ...; it provides mobile surveillance, detection and alerting for human security staff rather than supervising or directing students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security patrol on a school campus. It is the closest deployed system to hall or bus-loop duty, but it only streams video and raises detections; it does not check passes, direct children, help with spills or physically intervene, so it does not carry over to student supervision at worker quality.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor security robot autonomously patrols corridors of human-occupied facilities such as offices, but incidents are handled by remote human specialists in a command center; the robot performs no physical intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: indoor building patrol in a structured human facility (E2), the same class of setting as a school corridor or cafeteria. Capability is limited to navigation, sensing and escalation to remote humans, so it does not transfer to supervising and physically managing middle-school students.

sources.system: Miller Nichols Library automated storage and retrieval system ('the Robot')
sources.developer: Library ASRS installed at UMKC Libraries (Dematic-type crane system)
sources.title: The Robot - UMKC Libraries
sources.claim: Academic libraries run deployed automated storage and retrieval systems in which a robotic crane autonomously stores returned items in bins and retrieves requested items to a pick-up station, inside a purpose-built high-density vault.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library materials storage and retrieval. Same objects (books, bound volumes) and same accepted output (returns placed back in their storage location, requested titles produced), but only in a purpose-built bin-and-crane vault rather than open stacks.

sources.system: Lyngsoe Sort Mate automated materials handling / book sorter
sources.title: Automated Material Handling for Libraries | Efficiency Solutions
sources.claim: Commercial library automated materials handling systems autonomously check in and sort returned items into bins and carts, but returning items to the shelves remains manual work for staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library circulation and returns processing. Shows that even in heavily automated libraries open-stack shelving and patron-facing service remain human work, supporting the negative judgment for the media-center duty instance.

instances.label: Reproducing paper materials for the day: teacher takes worksheets/quizzes/reading packets to the school copy room or workroom, runs class sets on a copier, collates, staples, sorts by class period, and stacks them for distribution.

Physically configuring the classroom for the day's activity: moving 25-32 student desks and chairs from rows into pods, a seminar circle, or lab stations; clearing surfaces of leftover clutter and student belongings; resetting the room afterward, often in the 4-5 minutes between periods.

Setting up instructional technology and displays: powering on and connecting laptop/document camera to the projector or panel, loading the lesson slides, testing audio and video, writing the agenda/objective/warm-up on the whiteboard, and posting anchor charts or word walls.

Staging materials at each seat or station before students arrive: placing a handout, textbook, calculator, mini-whiteboard, Chromebook, novel, or art/manipulative kit at each desk or group table, and collecting them again at the end.

Subject-specific lab or activity prep: assembling and setting out lab trays with glassware, chemicals, specimens, microscopes, probes or art/shop materials at each bench station; mixing solutions to concentration; checking that gas/water/equipment work and safety gear is in place.

Fetching and transporting supplies across the building: retrieving copies from the copy room, a Chromebook cart from the library, a book set or lab kit from a storage closet or department office, and bringing them to the classroom, sometimes via elevator or across wings.

sources.system: Xerox / Plockmatic PowerSquare 160 inline booklet finishing system
sources.title: Booklet Folding & Stapling Machine: PowerSquare™ - Xerox
sources.claim: Commercial production print/copy systems with inline finishing automatically collate, fold and staple printed sets into finished booklets with essentially no operator intervention once the job is submitted — the machine handles the paper in a purpose-built feed/finish path.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production printing with inline finishing. A teacher's copy-room instance is the same physical operation on the same objects (loose sheets collated and stapled into per-student sets); the machine's output is the accepted output of the instance.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products of widely varying shape and size in fenced workcells inside fulfillment centers, sorting and consolidating items into totes/orders at commercial reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking and consolidation of diverse retail items. Assembling per-student material sets (one handout, one calculator, one manipulative per tray) is the same pick-and-place of small varied objects into presented receptacles, at comparable precision, when the receptacles are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously fetches and delivers supplies, medications and lab samples through hospital corridors, including autonomous elevator rides, at large deployed scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-building supply fetch-and-delivery in an institutional facility. Carrying copies, kits or book sets from a school copy room or storage closet to a classroom is the same errand — same building type, same load class, same corridor/elevator navigation among people.

sources.title: Agility Robotics’ Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid works in commercial operation at a GXO logistics facility, autonomously picking totes off mobile robots, loading conveyors and stacking containers; it has moved over 100,000 totes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repetitive tote/container transport and placement inside a structured facility. Moving bins of classroom supplies between staging points is the same load handling, though Digit's workflow is a fixed, mapped route with known pick and place points.

sources.developer: HKUST (Bi, Zhang, Chen, Zhao, Li, Ma)
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator
sources.claim: ALORE, a legged manipulator system, autonomously rearranges large objects such as chairs, ... target positions, completing 8 continuous loops rearranging 32 chairs in about 40 minutes without failure; the system assumes approximate target positions and feasible grasp regions are provided.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous rearrangement of chairs and tables to specified target poses — the same physical operation as reconfiguring classroom furniture into pods or a circle, on the same object class, though demonstrated in a controlled indoor test space with target positions and grasp regions supplied.

sources.title: Opentrons introduces Flex Prep: A no-code robot offering the simplicity of a pipette with the versatility of a liquid handler
sources.claim: The Opentrons Flex Prep liquid-handling robot executes user-defined pipetting workflows — sample transfer, reagent aliquoting, dilution — autonomously on a fixed labware deck, and is sold commercially to thousands of institutions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated preparation and aliquoting of reagents into labware. Preparing and portioning solutions for a school chemistry lab is the same liquid-handling operation when the labware is presented on the machine's fixtured deck.

sources.system: Mobile robotic chemist (Burger et al., Nature 583:237)
sources.title: Professor Andy Cooper receives Royal Society Professorship to develop mobile robotic chemist
sources.claim: A mobile robotic chemist operated autonomously for days at a time inside a chemistry laboratory built for humans, navigating between workstations and operating benchtop instruments to run experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of vials and operation of lab stations in a human-scale laboratory. It shows in-lab sample handling, but the stations, vial racks and positions were engineered for the robot, so it does not substantiate laying out varied glassware and specimens across a school lab's benches.

sources.title: This robot learns to clean your space just the way you like it | Stanford University School of Engineering
sources.claim: TidyBot, a mobile manipulator using LLM-based preference reasoning, put away objects in real rooms with an 85% success rate — well below the reliability a school would accept for pre-class setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tidying and object put-away in as-found rooms — the closest published analogue to clearing and staging a classroom; cited to show the reliability gap at the E2/E3 end, not to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Provide students with disabilities with assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-class setup and adjustment of supportive technology for an individual student: clipping on / pairing an FM or hearing-assist transmitter, mounting and repositioning an AAC device or switch on a wheelchair tray, opening and configuring a laptop/tablet with text-to-speech or speech-to-text, positioning a magnifier or slant board, and checking the student can actually operate it that period.

Providing prepared adapted materials and charged devices to specific students: retrieving braille or large-print copies, a charged laptop, noise-cancelling headphones, an adapted calculator or manipulatives from a classroom cabinet and getting them to the right student's desk at the start of class.

Hands-on physical assistance in the classroom or at the door: moving desks and clearing an aisle for a wheelchair or walker, steadying a student who is unsteady on their feet, helping a student in or out of a seat, retrieving a dropped cane, AAC device or backpack and placing it back in the student's hands, holding doors during transitions.
Escorting or transporting a mobility-impaired student along school corridors during class time to the accessible restroom, nurse's office or elevator, and back to the classroom.

Assisting with the restroom itself: opening and holding a heavy accessible-stall door, maneuvering the student and chair inside, waiting nearby, and providing transfer, clothing or hygiene support as the student's plan requires before returning to class.

Accessibility assistance away from the standard classroom: field trips, science labs and athletic fields, bus loading, and evacuation/fire drills - carrying or handing over the student's device and helping them over curbs, ramps, uneven ground and unfamiliar buildings.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi performs commercial autonomous mobile manipulation in hospitals: it picks supplies out of supply closets ... delivers them to patient rooms without human control, navigating corridors, doors and elevators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetch-and-deliver of small light items inside an institutional building. Retrieving a prepared assistive device or adapted materials from a cabinet and bringing them to a student in a classroom involves comparable objects (sub-kilogram supplies), comparable grasp precision, and the same class of environment (mapped corridors and rooms occupied by people).

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is a fielded commercial product rather than a demo: more than 25 US hospitals, over one million deliveries including ....

sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. with Unifi Aviation / Wayne County Airport Authority

sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a seated mobility-impaired person between two points inside a crowded institutional building. Escorting a wheelchair-using student from a classroom to the accessible restroom area is the same act at shorter range, with the same passenger-safety requirement and comparable corridor conditions.

sources.title: WHILL and Envoy Deploy Autonomous Service at U.S. Airports
sources.claim: The WHILL autonomous mobility service is commercially installed in US airport terminals (American Airlines at LAX and MIA), not only in trials.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms commercial maturity of the person-transport transfer argued in evidence 2.

sources.title: Bear Robotics embraces automation to improve frontline | BILL
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi autonomously runs food and items to specific tables in restaurants and similar venues, with several thousand units deployed at chains such as Denny's and Chili's.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously bringing items to named, seated people in a furniture-cluttered room built for humans. Handing a charged device or a large-print packet to a student at an assigned desk involves the same navigation among chairs and people and the same item-to-person transfer.

sources.system: HAT (Head-Worn Assistive Teleoperation) with Hello Robot Stretch
sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon RCHI Lab / Hello Robot
sources.title: Independence in the Home: A Wearable Interface for a Person with Quadriplegia to Teleoperate a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: State-of-the-art assistive mobile manipulation for people with severe motor impairments (Hello Robot Stretch in the home) is delivered by direct human teleoperation interfaces, not autonomous execution.
sources.transferJustification: Shows that personal, body-adjacent assistive manipulation for disabled users - the closest published analogue to fitting a device on a student or steadying them - remains continuously human-driven, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Towards human-centered AI and robotics to reduce hospital falls: finding opportunities to enhance patient-nurse interactions during toileting
sources.claim: Toileting assistance is characterized by clinicians as inseparable from human judgment and interpersonal care; no robotic substitute exists in practice.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the restroom-assistance instance; used only to support a negative judgment.

tasks.label: Instruct and monitor students in the use of equipment and materials to prevent injuries and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Science practical (chemistry/biology/physics): teacher gives pre-lab safety briefing and hands-on demonstration of Bunsen burners, glassware, hot plates, reagents or dissection tools, then circulates among 25-30 teenagers during the lab, enforcing goggles/gloves, correcting grips and technique, stopping horseplay, shutting off gas, and handling spills or breakage.

Physical education / health class in gym, weight room or on the field: teacher instructs on correct use of weight machines, free weights, gymnastics apparatus and sports gear, sets/checks equipment adjustments, monitors form during use, spots students, and stops unsafe use or overloading.

Art, music or general elective classroom: teacher demonstrates and supervises use of X-Acto knives, scissors, hot glue guns, clay and kiln tools, paints and solvents, or band instruments, correcting handling and care to prevent cuts, burns and damage to instruments and materials.

General academic classroom with school technology and consumables: teacher instructs students on handling laptops/tablets from carts, chargers and cords, projectors, calculators and classroom supplies, and monitors use to prevent dropped devices, damaged screens, and misuse.

Off-campus or outdoor work: field trip, outdoor environmental sampling with nets, probes and waders, or an off-site event where the teacher briefs students on equipment use and monitors them in a setting whose layout and conditions are not controlled by the school.

sources.system: Laboratory Safety Assistant (LSA) framework, socially assistive robot
sources.developer: Academic research team (Hasnine, Indurkhya, Ahmed; IEEE ARSO 2024 / Springer 2025)
sources.title: Socially Assistive Robot as Laboratory Safety Assistant for Science Students (IEEE ARSO 2024)
sources.claim: A research framework proposes a socially assistive robot that detects student behaviours violating lab guidelines (e.g., not wearing goggles or gloves) during science experiments and triggers dashboard-based interventions; it is a research prototype, not a system that instructs, demonstrates or physically intervenes.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system to 'monitor students in the use of equipment to prevent injuries': it targets the same school-laboratory setting, but covers only detection of a few pre-specified rule violations, so it does not substantiate whole-task completion.

sources.system: Optio AI teacher's assistant and Realbotix M-Series humanoid
sources.developer: Realbotix Corp. with Salamanca City Central School District
sources.title: Realbotix to Deploy First Humanoid Robot and AI Teachers Assistant in U.S. School District
sources.claim: The first announced US school-district humanoid deployment is a tutoring/teacher's-assistant pilot planned for fall 2026; it provides conversational curriculum support, not instruction or monitoring of students' equipment use.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of the art for humanoid robots physically present in secondary classrooms; it is an announced pilot for tutoring, providing no evidence of demonstrating equipment use or supervising students to prevent injury or damage.

sources.developer: Israeli university research lab (Krakovsky et al.)
sources.title: Between Fear and Trust: Factors Influencing Older Adults' Evaluation of Socially Assistive Robots
sources.claim: A robotic physical training coach demonstrates exercise routines and tracks a single seated user's movements in a laboratory setting with older adults; it does not supervise groups, set up gym equipment, or spot users.
sources.transferJustification: Related task of instructing and monitoring a human performing physical activity; transfer fails because it is one-on-one, in a lab, with no gym equipment, no group supervision and no capacity to spot or physically intervene.
