instances.label: Daily/weekly hand-out and collection of classroom materials during class: worksheets, novels, calculators, whiteboards, Chromebook-cart devices, art or manipulative kits passed to ~30 students at desks or lab tables, collected at the bell, counted, and returned to labeled bins and cabinets in an occupied, cluttered classroom.

Start/end-of-term issue and collection of textbooks and devices: teacher pulls numbered/barcoded books or Chromebooks from a book room or cart, issues each to a named student, records the number against the roster, then collects them at term end, checks condition, and stacks them in the storage room.

Science-lab or art-room preparation: teacher sets out glassware, probeware, dissection trays, chemicals or art supplies at 8-10 stations before a period, checks kits for completeness, and afterward washes/returns items and locks chemicals and sharp tools in the prep-room cabinet per safety rules.

Selecting and ordering supplies from vendor catalogs/district requisition systems, then receiving the delivery: hauling boxes from the front office, opening cartons, checking contents against the packing slip, and shelving mixed consumables (paper, markers, notebooks, kits) in a classroom closet or department supply room.

Periodic inventory: counting shelved textbooks, calculators, lab equipment and consumable stock in the classroom/book room against a district list, flagging missing, damaged or expired items, and recording counts in a spreadsheet or asset system.

sources.title: Keyed By Tally, Simbe Helps Grocers With Inventory, Workforce Issues
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robot autonomously scans store shelves during open hours, identifying stock levels, out-of-stocks and pricing at ~99% accuracy; deployed commercially across grocery chains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory audit. Same core act as inventorying classroom stock \-controlled building among people, recognizing items on shelves, comparing them to a master list, and reporting missing or misplaced stock.

sources.title: Independent US grocer Harmons deploys Simbe Tally inventory robot across 17 of its locations
sources.claim: Tally is deployed in multiple US grocery chains, e.g. live across 17 Harmons stores after a five-store pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf-stock auditing in a human-use facility; establishes commercial-grade reliability of autonomous inventory counting in an E2 setting comparable to a school book room or supply room.

sources.developer: A*STAR with Singapore National Library Board
sources.title: Automated robot that scans library shelves using laser mapping and radio tags can ensure no book is misplaced again
sources.claim: AuRoSS, an autonomous RFID shelf-scanning robot, navigated library stacks and reported missing/misplaced books with up to 99% accuracy in real Singapore library trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library shelf-reading/inventory. Books are the same objects a teacher inventories (class sets of textbooks), and the setting — an institution-run building with standard shelving — matches a school book room.

sources.title: Stow: Robotic packing of items into fabric pods
sources.claim: Amazon's robotic stow system autonomously places diverse items onto densely packed shelves, performing over 500,000 stows in a working fulfillment center at rates approaching human operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse putaway. Storing supplies means placing many small, varied consumer-type objects (books, boxes, packaged goods) onto shelves without damage — the same manipulation, at a station where the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow arm autonomously picks individual items of many types from containers and places them into specific totes in fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: piece-picking/kitting. Assembling per-student or per-station sets of supplies and re-sorting returned items is the same pick-and-place of varied small goods into designated bins at a purpose-built station.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cartons from trailers, handling mixed stacks and fallen boxes; DHL made the first commercial deployment and has since expanded it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading cartons from a delivery. Receiving a school supply order involves the same mixed corrugated cases moved off a pallet or truck to a conveyor or shelf, presented to the machine as in a dock cell.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage shelves and was deployed to 300 FamilyMart convenience stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking inside a human-use retail store. Shows autonomous placement of standardized packaged goods on fixed shelving, but only from a rail-mounted cell handling one product form, not free navigation of a varied storeroom.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent's Moxi mobile manipulators autonomously fetch and deliver supplies and medications inside 25+ US hospitals, exceeding one million deliveries including 300,000 ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply delivery. Establishes autonomous transport and hand-off of supplies in a staffed institutional building, but not per-person distribution to seated people or shelving of mixed stock.

sources.system: Library RFID automated materials handling sorter
sources.developer: library AMH vendors (FE Technologies, P.V. Supa and others)
sources.title: Main Library Introduces Automated Book Return
sources.claim: Library automated materials handling systems check returned items in by RFID and mechanically sort them into designated bins without staff handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: checking in and sorting returned books. Textbook collection at term end is the same operation — identify each book against a borrower record, register the return, route it to the right bin — in a purpose-built sorter.

sources.title: AutoCrib ® Industrial Vending Solutions
sources.claim: AutoCrib industrial vending/dispensing units issue tools and supplies to identified employees and automatically log every transaction for inventory control; installed in 20,000+ locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-of-use issuing of supplies with per-user accountability. Issuing calculators or kits to students and tracking who holds what is the same dispense-and-record function, with users coming to a fixed machine.

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as school library assistance, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hall duty during passing periods: teacher stands at an assigned corridor/stairwell post in the school building, greets and visually screens the stream of students, checks hall passes, tells students to move along or remove hoods/phones, disperses crowding, verbally de-escalates arguments or scuffles, walks a defiant student to the office, and reports incidents. Loud, dense, fast-changing crowds of adolescents.

Cafeteria/lunch duty: teacher circulates through a crowded lunchroom for one period, keeps line order, enforces seating and cleanup rules, responds to spills, food-throwing, and conflicts, watches for a student in distress (choking, allergic reaction, bullying), authorizes bathroom trips, and dismisses tables at the bell.

Morning arrival and afternoon bus/car-line duty: teacher stands outdoors on the bus loop or at an entrance door in whatever weather, directs students to the correct bus, keeps them on the sidewalk and out of moving traffic, signals drivers, hurries stragglers, and stays until the last bus clears.

Library/media center coverage: teacher staffs the school library for a period or covers for the librarian — supervising students who are working or browsing, keeping noise and phone use in check, checking materials out and in at the circulation desk, helping a student locate a title or database, reshelving returned books and straightening shelves.

Other assigned supervision: study hall or detention proctoring, in-school-suspension coverage, restroom and locker-bay sweeps, assembly/pep-rally and fire-drill supervision, and monitoring an entrance or main office — taking attendance of the group, keeping students on task and in place, and handling whatever comes up.

sources.system: Team 1st Technologies autonomous security patrol robot
sources.title: Santa Fe rolls out robot to help keep schools safe
sources.claim: Santa Fe Public Schools piloted an autonomous wheeled security robot from Team 1st Technologies that patrols school grounds and streams 360-degree video to human security officers; it monitors and notifies but does not perform teacher-style supervision, rule enforcement, or physical redirection of students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous security patrol of a school campus. It is the closest deployed analogue to hall/grounds monitoring, but it delivers only observation and alerting to humans, so it does not carry over to a duty that requires enforcing rules and intervening with students.

sources.system: Autonomous security robots (Knightscope K5 and comparable patrol robots)
sources.title: Security Robots vs. Human Guards – Which is more effective
sources.claim: Commercially deployed autonomous security robots (e.g., Knightscope K5 class machines) observe, record, and alert, but cannot physically intervene with people — the capability at the core of hall, cafeteria, and bus-duty supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: guard patrol in human-occupied facilities. Establishes the ceiling of deployed mobile supervision robots — sensing and alerting only — which is below what monitoring duty requires.

sources.title: Researcher designs robot to help children cross streets safely
sources.claim: CrossBot, a Fresno State research prototype robotic crossing guard, uses sensors and AI to detect pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles in school zones and issue alerts; its designer states it is meant to complement rather than replace human crossing guards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: student pedestrian-safety supervision at school zones, the nearest analogue to bus-loading duty. It only detects and warns; it cannot marshal students to buses or manage the loading zone, so capability does not transfer.

sources.title: Working Alongside Robots at the Library
sources.claim: Library shelf-scanning robots such as AuRoSS in Singapore public libraries autonomously inventory shelves at night with high accuracy, but they cannot reshelve books; human librarians must retrieve and reshelve the flagged items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library shelf maintenance. It covers only an after-hours inventory sub-step of library coverage and explicitly excludes reshelving and any student-facing circulation or supervision work.

sources.title: Superintendent clarifies use of AI-powered robot in Salamanca schools
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid robot announced for US secondary schools, Realbotix's M-Series 'Sally', is a stationary conversational classroom assistant in a limited pilot starting fall 2026 — not a mobile supervision or duty-post system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid robot presence in a secondary school. Shows that school-deployed humanoids are conversational classroom aides, providing no evidence of autonomous crowd supervision or physical student management.

roles.description: Teach occupational, vocational, career, or technical subjects to students at the secondary school level.

tasks.label: Instruct students individually and in groups, using various teaching methods, such as lectures, discussions, and demonstrations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-class lecture/discussion in a CTE classroom on underlying theory (electrical theory, business law, safety codes, anatomy) delivered with slides, whiteboard, and Q&A to ~20-30 secondary students of mixed ability; purpose is conveying and checking understanding of concepts.

Live skill demonstration in a shop/lab bay (running a weld bead, mounting a tire, sectioning a chicken, styling hair, wiring a receptacle) with students gathered around, narrated step by step and followed by questions; purpose is showing students how a procedure is performed and why.

Individualized instruction while students work at benches, stations, or computers: circulating, watching a student's technique, asking diagnostic questions, re-explaining, and coaching corrections one-on-one.
Small-group / project-team instruction: guiding 3-5 students through a build, case study, or lab exercise with Socratic questioning, differentiated re-teaching, and group discussion.

Instruction delivered outside the home classroom - clinical rotation, co-op/work-based learning site, career-tech competition prep, or online/hybrid session - where the teacher explains and discusses with individuals or small groups in a workplace or remote setting.

tasks.label: Establish and enforce rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order among students.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Prepare materials and classroom for class activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Trade shop/lab setup (auto tech, welding, woodworking, manufacturing): before the period the teacher stages stock (steel coupons, lumber, engine components) at each bench or booth, lays out hand tools and consumables from the tool crib, sets up/checks machines and jigs, positions PPE and fire extinguishers, and posts task sheets at stations. Room is cluttered, layout varies by project, students' prior-period leftovers must be cleared.

General CTE classroom or computer lab (business, IT, marketing, engineering-drafting): boots and logs in workstations, loads software/files, sets up projector and demo hardware, rearranges desks/tables into project groups, distributes worksheets, laptops, calculators or robotics kits to each seat, writes the agenda on the board.

Culinary arts / hospitality teaching kitchen: pulls ingredients from cooler and dry storage, portions and stages mise en place for 6-8 student stations, lays out utensils, pans, cutting boards, scales and recipe cards, preheats ovens and ranges, sets out sanitizer buckets and towels.

Health science, cosmetology, or early-childhood lab: positions mannequins/task trainers on beds or chairs, sets out per-station supply kits (gloves, BP cuffs, syringes, shears, mannequin heads, dolls), sanitizes surfaces and instruments, stages skills-check paperwork and consumables at each station.

Materials production away from the classroom (school workroom/copy room): duplicates handouts, safety sheets, rubrics and exams; collates, staples or hole-punches class sets; assembles per-student packets and mixed-item material kits pulled from supply cabinets; boxes them by class period.

Agriculture CTE (greenhouse, land lab, ag mechanics shop, animal science): fills and stages flats/pots with media, sets out seed, fertilizer and hand tools on greenhouse benches, stages feed and handling equipment in the barn, sets up plots or welding stations for the day's ag-mech activity; conditions vary with weather and livestock.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Moxi is an autonomous mobile manipulator deployed in dozens of US hospitals, doing point-to-point fetch-and-deliver of supplies, specimens and pharmacy items along mapped corridors; it delivers items to a drop point rather than setting up a room or laying out equipment at workstations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply delivery. It is the strongest existing case of an autonomous mobile manipulator working inside a human institutional facility (E2), and it bounds what such systems do there: transporting containers, not staging tools and consumables across many stations.

sources.title: Implementing Piece-Picking Robots into Micro-Fulfillment Centers
sources.claim: RightPick piece-picking cells autonomously pick mixed items from presented totes into destination totes in fulfillment centers, with kitting named as a supported workflow; the cell is purpose-built, with items brought to the robot by ASRS or AMRs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order fulfillment kitting. Assembling a per-student packet/kit from a set of stocked items is the same operation on comparable small objects with comparable precision, provided the inputs are presented in bins as in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: OSARO automates Zenni fulfillment center
sources.claim: OSARO robotic pick-and-place/bagging systems were deployed in Zenni's fulfillment center to ready orders autonomously, showing commercial-grade robotic assembly and packing of small consumer items in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order packing/kitting. Packing sets of small items into a container at commercial reliability transfers to assembling class sets of handouts and small supplies when inputs are presented to the machine.

sources.system: Xerox Production Ready (PR) Booklet Maker Finisher (Versant/Iridesse presses)
sources.title: Production Ready Finisher and Production Ready Booklet Maker Finisher Specifications
sources.claim: Production digital presses with inline finishers automatically produce collated, stapled, folded and saddle-stitched sets from a submitted job, i.e. the machine itself performs the collating and stapling of class-set packets without a human handling each sheet.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial print finishing. Producing collated, stapled packets is precisely the paper-materials half of classroom material preparation; the machine is a purpose-built paper-handling system with the job brought to it.

sources.title: We've Raised a $43.1M Series A to Accelerate Our AI-Enabled Robot Deployments
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' arms autonomously portion and assemble food ingredients into trays on production lines in food manufacturing plants at large scale, but they are fixed-line cells whose hoppers are loaded by humans and which do not set up a kitchen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: food portioning/assembly. It is the closest deployed analogue to staging mise en place, and shows the capability exists only on a purpose-built line, not as station setup inside a working kitchen.

sources.title: GXO Signs Industry-First Multi-Year Agreement with Agility Robotics
sources.claim: Digit humanoids are commercially deployed in GXO warehouses moving totes between cobots and conveyors under fleet orchestration; the work is repetitive container handling at fixed presentation points, not multi-object staging of a room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse tote handling. It bounds what deployed humanoids do in facilities today: single-object transfers between defined stations, well short of laying out tools and consumables across many student stations.

sources.title: π0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 mobile manipulator performs multi-stage tidying in previously unseen kitchens and bedrooms, the closest research result to setting a room in order, but the developers report frequent errors and it is a research demonstration, not a deployed system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying/object rearrangement. It is the nearest analogue to arranging a room's objects for use, and its acknowledged error rate shows worker-quality room preparation is not yet met.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading general-purpose robot aimed at human living/working spaces, relies on remote human experts for complex chores; its autonomy falls well short of the promised capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household chores including fetching and tidying. Because it is teleoperated for complex tasks, it cannot support a positive judgment for autonomous classroom preparation.

sources.system: survey of leading humanoid/manipulation platforms (Figure, Optimus, Digit, others)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026
sources.claim: A 2026 systematic capability assessment of leading robot platforms finds that manipulation demonstrations generally depend on controlled setups and narrow object sets, with transfer to new objects and contexts rarely demonstrated; warehouses/factories where the environment is designed around the robot remain the clearest near-term ground.
sources.transferJustification: General capability assessment used only to bound positive judgments; it covers the multi-step, multi-object manipulation that classroom and shop preparation would require.

sources.title: Realbotix to Deploy First Humanoid Robot and AI Teachers Assistant in U.S. School District
sources.claim: The first humanoid robot deployed ... US school district is a social teaching-assistant platform placed in classrooms for student engagement and AI tutoring; it does no physical preparation of materials or the room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: classroom support. Shows that the only humanoid actually deployed in secondary classrooms is an interaction device, providing no evidence of robotic material or room preparation in schools.

tasks.label: Instruct students in the knowledge and skills required in a specific occupation or occupational field, using a systematic plan of lectures, discussions, audio-visual presentations, and laboratory, shop, and field studies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classroom theory block in any CTE field (business, health science, auto, ag, IT): teacher delivers a planned lecture with slides/video, runs discussion and Q&A, checks understanding, writes/draws on the board, distributes and collects materials, and manages a class of 20-30 teenagers for a 50-90 minute period in a standard school classroom.

Trade/industrial shop session (welding, automotive, construction, HVAC): teacher physically demonstrates a procedure on live equipment (striking an arc, torquing a fastener, cutting a rafter), then circulates among 15-25 students at benches and machines, hands-on correcting grip/technique, checking work, enforcing PPE and lockout, and shutting down equipment on the shop floor.

Health science, culinary, or cosmetology lab: teacher demonstrates a skill on a manikin, patient simulator, food, or mannequin head (vitals, transfers, knife cuts, sanitation, styling), then supervises students practicing on deformable/perishable materials in a school lab, correcting technique and enforcing hygiene and safety standards.

Business/IT/engineering-technology instruction in a computer or design lab: teacher demonstrates software or CAD on a projector, distributes and sets up hardware (kits, printers, controllers, robotics trainers), then moves station to station troubleshooting individual students' varied work in a school computer lab.

Agriculture/animal-science or small-engine applied lab on school grounds: teacher demonstrates and supervises students in a greenhouse, school farm/livestock barn, or power-mechanics bay, handling plants, animals, and machinery while keeping a class of teenagers safe.

Field study or work-based learning: teacher leads students off campus to a jobsite, clinic, farm, or employer facility (or an outdoor FFA/SkillsUSA field exercise), narrating and demonstrating occupational practice on site while supervising students in a setting the school does not control.

sources.system: Social robots in education (43 robot models incl. NAO, Pepper), survey of 206 real deployments
sources.developer: Ferrer & Aymerich-Franch (survey of many developers: SoftBank Robotics and others)
sources.title: Social robots for education: a global analysis of deployments in real scenarios
sources.claim: A worldwide documentary survey of real-world social-robot deployments in education finds 206 cases across 28 countries, with robots functioning as edutainment devices, programming-skill teachers, and psychological support — not as the instructor of record delivering a full course of instruction.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about robots placed in classrooms to support instruction — the closest existing analogue to this task; it shows deployed roles are narrow supplements, not delivery of a systematic instructional plan.

sources.title: Social robots for education: a global analysis of deployments in real scenarios
sources.claim: The same 2026 survey reports persistent technical limits (social cues, speech recognition, selecting actions from learner needs) and that teachers judge educational robots not qualified to replace educators.

sources.developer: University of Plymouth / Aldebaran-SoftBank NAO platform

sources.claim: Best-case fully autonomous classroom deployment: two autonomous NAO-type robots ran unsupervised in primary-school classrooms for two weeks, but only as one-on-one learning companions on narrow subject content, not as the teacher running lectures, labs, or shop work.
sources.transferJustification: Robot-delivered instruction in a real school classroom is the same activity class as this task; it bounds what autonomous classroom robots achieve — dyadic tutoring on narrow content, no lab/shop instruction.

sources.transferJustification: Most advanced current humanoid-in-a-classroom deployment; it is a stationary conversational torso used as an assistant, showing no capability for demonstrating occupational skills or supervising a shop.

tasks.label: Instruct and monitor students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injury and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-unit safety demonstration in a high school shop (woodshop/metals/welding): teacher dons PPE, sets up the table saw, lathe or MIG welder, demonstrates guards, stance, stock handling and shutdown on a real workpiece in front of 20+ teenagers, answers questions, and checks that each student can restate and show the safe procedure before being cleared to use the machine.

Circulating and monitoring during hands-on lab time: teacher moves continuously around a shop or automotive bay where 15-25 students work simultaneously on machines and vehicles, scanning for missing eye protection, loose clothing, crowding, improper feed or grip; verbally correcting, physically stopping a machine or repositioning a student's hands, and pausing the class when needed.

Equipment care and end-of-period cleanup supervision: instructing students on cleaning, lubricating, blade/bit changes, battery and cord care, chip and scrap disposal; supervising tool check-in against a shadow board or crib list, inspecting returned tools for damage and tagging out defective equipment.

Health science, culinary or cosmetology lab: demonstrating and monitoring safe handling of sharps, autoclaves, hot ranges, fryers, mandolines, chemicals and shears; sanitation and glove protocol; correcting students during timed hands-on practice with real food, clients or manikins.

Agriculture or construction CTE outside the classroom: greenhouse, farm shop, livestock area or an off-campus jobsite/work-based-learning visit where the teacher instructs on chainsaw, tractor PTO, nail gun or livestock-handling safety and monitors students amid changing terrain, weather, vehicles and third parties.

Business/IT or engineering-drafting classroom: instructing on careful handling and care of laptops, 3D printers, ESD-sensitive components, soldering irons and cameras; monitoring students at fixed workstations and correcting misuse that risks damage rather than injury.

sources.title: Company Behind AI Companion Robots for Intimacy Enters Us Schools With Humanoid Classroom Teacher
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid robot actually placed in a US secondary classroom is a seated, immobile conversational teaching assistant that supports a human teacher in coding/robotics lessons; it cannot move around the room, operate shop equipment, or supervise students at machines.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system to 'instructing students'; cited to show that even the state-of-the-art classroom humanoid is stationary, assists rather than replaces the teacher, and cannot demonstrate or monitor equipment use.

sources.system: Laboratory Safety Assistant (LSA) framework on a socially assistive robot
sources.title: Socially Assistive Robot as Laboratory Safety Assistant for Science Students
sources.claim: Robotic supervision of student lab safety exists only as a research framework that detects unsafe student behaviors (e.g., missing PPE) during experiments and issues social prompts; it does not instruct in equipment use, physically intervene, or carry a class.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = monitoring students for unsafe behavior in a school science lab. Transfer fails: it is a detection-only research prototype with no instructional delivery, no machine-specific demonstration, and no physical intervention capability.

sources.title: Campus Security Inspection Robot Based on YOLO Algorithm
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic monitoring in institutional buildings is limited to navigating fixed routes and flagging hazards such as fire, smoking or falls; no instruction or hands-on correction of people is involved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = patrolling a school facility and detecting hazards. Transfer fails: detection and alarming is a sub-step of monitoring; it provides no instruction, no judgment of technique, and no safety intervention at a machine.

sources.system: Quadruped robot with 6-axis arm and generative AI for lab monitoring
sources.title: Autonomous Monitoring of Pharmaceutical R&D Laboratories with 6 Axis Arm Equipped Quadruped Robot and Generative AI
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile monitoring of laboratory equipment status has been demonstrated with a quadruped plus arm in pharmaceutical R&D labs, i.e. watching equipment rather than teaching or supervising people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = monitoring equipment condition in a structured lab. Transfer fails: it monitors instruments, not students; it neither instructs nor prevents human injury.

sources.system: Figure 02/03 at BMW Spartanburg; Apptronik Apollo at Mercedes-Benz
sources.title: Humanoid Robots on the Factory Floor: Figure 03 BMW & Apptronik Apollo Mercedes Deployment
sources.claim: Commercially deployed humanoids perform narrow, repetitive part-handling on fenced or dedicated automotive production stations; their demonstrated competence is material handling, not demonstration-based teaching or supervision of people.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to establish the ceiling of current autonomous physical capability: repetitive part presentation in an engineered industrial station. It does not substantiate demonstrating varied shop machinery to students or supervising them.

tasks.label: Use computers, audio-visual aids, and other equipment and materials to supplement presentations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classroom lecture in a CTE classroom: teacher operates a laptop and ceiling projector or interactive flat panel to supplement a presentation — waking the machine, selecting inputs, launching slides, playing a training video, advancing slides while talking, adjusting volume/focus, and troubleshooting a dropped HDMI/wireless-cast connection mid-lesson with ~25 students present.

Shop or lab presentation supplemented by a live equipment demonstration: the teacher runs the actual trade equipment (MIG welder, lathe or CNC mill, sewing machine, kitchen range, engine analyzer, CPR mannequin, hair mannequin) and passes around physical samples, cutaway parts, or specimens while narrating the point being taught, adapting the demo to student questions.

Pre-class setup and takedown in an empty classroom/shop: wheeling in the AV cart, connecting laptop, document camera and speakers, powering and aligning the projector, queuing media, and laying out demonstration models, tools, samples and handouts on the demo bench and student desks; then reversing it after class.

Device-based supplement in a computer lab or 1:1 classroom: distributing/setting up Chromebooks, tablets, VR headsets or simulation software (e.g., welding simulator, CAD, EHR sim), logging stations in, casting the teacher screen, and circulating to fix technical problems while the presentation continues.

Off-site or non-standard venue: presenting with portable AV at a career fair, industry partner site tour, advisory-committee meeting, or community/parent night — unfamiliar room and equipment, improvised cabling, variable lighting and seating, plus carried demonstration materials.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: The most capable deployed mobile manipulator in a human institutional facility (hospitals) does fetch-and-deliver of supplies, autonomously navigating corridors and riding elevators; it does not operate AV/computer equipment or run instructional demonstrations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = hospital supply delivery in an E2 facility. It shows autonomous mobile manipulation is real in institution-controlled buildings, but the handled objects (totes, supply bags) and the action set (grasp, transport, press elevator button) do not transfer to plugging AV cables, driving a computer UI, or demonstrating trade equipment to a class, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: Humanoid robots complete 11-month project at BMW plant | Repairer Driven News
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous humanoid work is a single repetitive part-handling job inside an automotive plant, run for months on a fixed station — not multi-step equipment setup or live demonstration in a people-filled room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = sheet-metal part loading in a body shop. Demonstrates sustained autonomous humanoid manipulation, but only on one fixtured, repetitive presentation of identical parts; it gives no evidence of the varied object handling, cable/interface work, or audience-directed demonstration this task requires.

sources.title: Frontiers | CARE: towards customized assistive robot-based education
sources.claim: A fully autonomous classroom robot has been run with school students, but it is a screen-and-camera social platform that presents and assesses content; it performs no manipulation of AV equipment, tools, or teaching materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robot-delivered tutoring in a classroom. The robot's output is speech and on-screen content — under the rating rules a screen/speaker platform is effectively software-only and does not act on the physical world, so it cannot substantiate the equipment- and materials-handling part of this task.

sources.title: US Firm's Humanoid Robot Teaching Assistant to Support 500 Students in 2026 | eWeek
sources.claim: The first US school-district humanoid deployment is an AI teaching-assistant avatar plus a stationary Realbotix M-Series robot used for classroom engagement; it has no capability for handling classroom equipment or materials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = AI tutoring/engagement in a high school. It is the closest thing to a robot in the instance's own setting, but it is a conversational face-and-screen unit with no dexterous manipulation or mobility, so it cannot perform AV setup, equipment demonstration, or materials handling.

sources.title: Breaking the humanoid robot delusion – Computerworld
sources.claim: Independent review of 2025 humanoid demonstrations finds many public showings are human-operated rather than autonomous, so demonstration footage of general-purpose household/office manipulation does not establish autonomous capability.

instances.label: Trades shop/lab class (welding, automotive, construction, manufacturing): teacher plans the day's sequence, gives a short whiteboard intro, performs a live hands-on demonstration at the bench or bay (setting a bead, torquing a fastener, running a machine), then releases 15-25 teens to work stations, circulating to answer questions, correct technique, enforce PPE/lockout rules, and stop unsafe acts.

Health science, culinary, cosmetology, or early-childhood lab: teacher demonstrates a skill on a manikin, mannequin head, or prep station (vitals, knife cuts, sanitation), narrates rationale, then supervises paired student practice at stations, checking off competencies and handling spontaneous questions and mistakes.

Business/IT/digital media computer lab: teacher models a workflow on the projected screen (code, CAD, spreadsheet, video edit), assigns investigative project work time, circulates among desks troubleshooting individual machines and student work, and runs a closing share-out.

Classroom theory block plus the planning itself: writing/adjusting the lesson and activity sequence to standards and available materials, then delivering direct instruction with discussion, guided questioning, worksheets/handouts, and a formative check for understanding before the next lab day.

Setup and safety orientation for an activity: prepping and laying out consumables, tool kits and station materials, verifying machine guards and equipment function, then conducting the safety demonstration and quiz before students are allowed to work.

Off-site or outdoor instructional activity (agriculture greenhouse/farm plot, building-trades jobsite house build, clinical or work-based learning rotation): teacher stages the activity in a variable, uncontrolled setting, demonstrates in situ, and supervises students investigating and working under changing conditions.

tasks.label: Provide students with disabilities with assistive devices, supportive technology, and assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retrieve and deliver an assistive item to a student inside the school building: fetch a loaner laptop or charged AAC/speech device from the resource room or office, a large-print or braille packet, or a handheld magnifier, and bring it to the student's seat in the CTE classroom or computer lab during class.

Set up and fit supportive technology to the individual student: connect an adapted keyboard, switch or trackball; mount a device on a wheelchair tray or workbench; pair an FM/DM transmitter with hearing aids; adjust screen-reader, magnification or captioning settings; then check with the student that it is reachable, legible and usable, and troubleshoot on the spot.

Adapt CTE shop/lab equipment and provide adaptive tools: fit an adaptive grip, jig or clamp to a hand tool; lower or raise a workbench or machine; reposition a guard, stool or task light; lay out an accessible alternate workstation in a cluttered welding, auto, culinary or wood shop, checking fit against the student's reach and grip.

Accompany a student with a mobility or vision impairment to a destination in the building and back: from the shop to the accessible restroom, elevator or another lab, through corridors that are crowded at passing periods, and return the student to the work area.

Hands-on personal assistance: steady or support a student during a sit-to-stand or chair-to-stool transfer, push and position a manual wheelchair at a bench, hold or open a heavy restroom door and help the student inside, adjust clothing, or catch a student who loses balance.

Off-campus work-based learning, job shadow, community field trip, greenhouse or outdoor lab: place a portable ramp, assist the student over uneven ground, gravel or curbs, find and enable access to a restroom in an unfamiliar business, and improvise accommodations at a site the school does not control.

sources.title: New autonomous wheelchairs at Miami International Airport
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous personal mobility devices carry passengers who need mobility assistance to a self-selected destination through airport concourses without an attendant, at roughly 120 rides a day at Miami International Airport.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a person with a mobility impairment to a destination inside a large public building. It transfers to escorting a student to a restroom or lab because the payload (a seated person), speeds, pedestrian traffic and corridor-and-doorway layout are comparable.

sources.title: WHILL Expands Global Autonomous Mobility Network with Heathrow Airport Launch
sources.claim: The same autonomous mobility service runs at 26 airports and facilities worldwide with over a million autonomous rides, using 360-degree sensing and obstacle detection to navigate crowded public buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: person-transport to a chosen destination inside an institution-controlled facility, at commercial scale, which is the escort component of assisting a student to reach facilities.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator, autonomously fetches and delivers medications, lab specimens and supplies between rooms in more than 30 US hospitals, riding elevators on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving an item from a storeroom or pharmacy and transporting it to a destination elsewhere in a staffed building. It transfers to bringing a loaner device or print materials from a school resource room to a classroom: similar object sizes, similar corridors, doors and elevators, no fixturing.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is described as one of the largest commercial ..., with roughly 100 robots and 1.25 million autonomous deliveries across 25+ hospital facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms the scale and autonomy of the same fetch-and-deliver capability cited for delivering assistive items inside an institutional building.

instances.label: At a desk/classroom computer, the CTE teacher reviews unit test scores, competency checklists and shop-project rubrics to identify students below standard, then writes an individualized remediation plan (re-teach objectives, modified assignments, practice packets, retest schedule) for a machining, welding, health-science or business course.

One-on-one after-school or study-hall tutoring re-teaching theory content the student failed — Ohm's law and circuit calculations, blueprint/print reading, medical terminology, accounting entries — using worksheets, worked examples, verbal explanation, questioning and corrective feedback.

Small-group re-teaching inside the school shop/lab during class or open-lab time: the teacher re-demonstrates a hands-on competency (running a weld bead, taking a blood pressure on a manikin, wiring a receptacle, disassembling a small engine), then observes and coaches students through repeat practice and signs off competency when the standard is met.

Coordinating remediation with special-education/504 staff, counselors and parents: reviewing IEP accommodations, adapting the remedial plan and industry-certification prep materials, and documenting progress in the district data system for MTSS/RTI review meetings.

Assigning, monitoring and troubleshooting online/credit-recovery or self-paced modules (e.g., certification practice software, LMS remediation units), checking dashboards, prompting students who stall, and re-testing them on missed competencies.

tasks.label: Select, order, store, issue, and inventory classroom equipment, materials, and supplies.

instances.label: Issuing during a class period in a CTE shop/lab: teacher unlocks the tool crib and cabinets and hands out hand tools, meters, PPE, and project stock to 20-30 students, tracks who has what, and collects and checks items back in at the bell.

Periodic physical inventory of tools and durable equipment: counting against shadow boards, drawers and cabinets, scanning asset tags on welders, laptops, mannequins and engine stands, noting damaged or missing items, and reconciling with district asset records.

Receiving and storing deliveries: cartons and pallets arrive at the loading dock or classroom door; teacher unpacks, verifies against packing slips, and stows consumables and bulky stock (lumber, sheet metal, filament, PPE, gas cylinders) in the storeroom, racks and cabinets.

Routine reordering of consumables: walking the storeroom to check what is running low, choosing items and vendors from catalogs/contract lists, and entering requisitions in the district purchasing system against the program budget.

Non-routine selection and specification of new equipment or curriculum materials: matching items to course competencies and safety codes, comparing quotes, measuring shop space and utilities, and shepherding approvals - largely deliberation and paperwork.

Perishable and regulated program stock: culinary/agriculture food deliveries inspected for quality, temperature and dates, labeled and FIFO-rotated in walk-in coolers and dry storage; auto/ag shop chemicals and fuels stored in flammables cabinets with SDS and disposal records.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-of-use tool/PPE issue in industry. Same act as issuing shop tools and supplies to users - machine-controlled retrieval and handover of the same classes of objects (hand tools, gauges, gloves, fasteners) with per-user authorization.

sources.title: Industrial Vending Machine Products from Snap-on AutoCrib
sources.claim: AutoCrib machines control issue and return of tools, MRO items, PPE and gauges by badge or fingerprint, keeping a per-user record of every item taken and returned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial tool-crib attendant duties (issue, return, inventory control). The CTE teacher's issuing/return-checking of tools to students is the same transaction with the same object classes and accountability requirement.

sources.title: AutoCrib ® Industrial Vending Solutions | TENAQUIP
sources.claim: AutoCrib point-of-use dispensing machines for industrial supplies are installed at more than 20,000 locations worldwide, indicating mature, routine deployment rather than a demo.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes deployment scale for the dispensing/inventory-control systems cited for issuing and inventorying tools and supplies.

sources.title: Level 5™ ATC from Snap-on® Industrial Breaks New Ground in Tool Management
sources.claim: Snap-on Level 5 Automated Tool Control cabinets photograph each drawer with built-in cameras and automatically determine which tools were removed or returned, logging it to the user; used in aviation MRO tool cribs with automatic locking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: aviation MRO tool accountability. It performs exactly the CTE inventory step - verifying every hand tool is present in its pocket and flagging missing/misplaced items - on identical objects (wrenches, drivers, sockets) in purpose-built cabinets.

sources.title: How Fastenal Vending Machines Work for Businesses - Engineer Fix
sources.claim: Industrial vending systems monitor on-hand levels of the items they hold and automatically raise replenishment orders when stock falls below a minimum threshold, removing the manual reorder step.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: consumable replenishment in industrial stores. The stock-sensing and reorder-trigger are the same operations the teacher performs when checking the storeroom and submitting a requisition for routine consumables.

sources.date: 2024-2025 (product coverage); installed at health systems including UCSF
sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare: Transforming Pharmacy Storage with BoxPicker - RXinsider
sources.claim: BoxPicker is a robotic high-density storage and retrieval system installed in hospital pharmacies that stores incoming stock, controls access, and retrieves packages by robotic picking while tracking inventory and expiry dates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pharmacy stockroom management (store, issue, inventory of small boxed supplies). Same three operations on comparably sized packaged goods, with tighter accountability than a school storeroom demands.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads mixed cases from trailers and containers in commercial DHL warehouses, handling mixed stack configurations and fallen boxes at up to 700 cases per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: inbound case handling at a dock. It covers the receiving half of 'store' - taking heterogeneous cartons off a delivery and moving them into the facility's storage flow, the same physical act as taking a supply delivery in at school.

sources.title: Walmart to deploy Fox Robotics autonomous forklifts across four distribution centers - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Walmart is deploying FoxBot autonomous forklifts at four distribution centers to unload trailers and move pallets between the dock and storage without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dock-to-storage putaway of palletized goods. Bulky CTE stock (lumber, sheet metal, cased consumables) arrives palletized, and this is the same move-and-store operation under machine control.

sources.system: Kardex Shuttle VLM automated tool crib
sources.title: How to Build an Automated Tool Crib Storage Solution - Kardex
sources.claim: Automated tool cribs built on vertical lift modules automatically store and retrieve tools, securing them and logging every transaction to a user ID, replacing manual logging and open shelving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial tool-crib storage and retrieval. Same objects (shop tools and supplies) stored and issued from a purpose-built machine with automatic inventory records, which is the E1 form of the teacher's store/issue/inventory duties.

sources.title: How a robot named Tally is helping BJ's boost the customer experience
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously navigates retail sales floors to scan shelves and audit inventory; it is deployed across BJ's Wholesale Club's 244 clubs and in grocery chains such as Harmons.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf inventory audit in a structured human facility. It marks the limit of E2 inventory automation - camera passes over planogrammed, barcoded shelf faces, with no ability to open cabinets or drawers or assess tool condition.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated shelves with bottles and ... in 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, running on a rail inside the beverage cooler with rare remote intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking inside a human-run facility. It marks the limit of E2 storing automation - a rail-mounted arm handling uniform bottles and cans, not mixed cartons of shop supplies put away in cabinets.

sources.title: 80% Reduction in Managing Student Devices | LocknCharge
sources.claim: Smart locker systems deployed in US school districts automatically distribute and collect student devices with self-authenticated access and an automatic transaction record for each issue and return.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing school-owned equipment to students. Corroborates that machine-mediated issue/return with automatic records already serves secondary students, though items must be pre-loaded into purpose-built compartments.

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as school library assistance, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Assigned hall duty: teacher stands at a corridor post during passing periods, greets and redirects students, checks hall passes, disperses crowds and blocked doorways, intervenes in horseplay or a shoving match, escorts a student to the office, and reports incidents.

Cafeteria duty during lunch waves: supervising a few hundred teenagers, keeping serving lines orderly, addressing throwing food/phones/leaving trash, responding to spills, allergy or choking incidents, dismissing tables and releasing students to next period.

Morning arrival / afternoon bus loading-unloading duty at the outdoor bus loop: directing students to the correct bus, keeping them behind the curb line and out of traffic, assisting a student with mobility needs, coordinating with drivers and parents, in rain, cold or dark.

Covering the school library/media center for a period: checking materials out to students at the circulation desk, helping students find a resource or fix a printer/Chromebook, supervising quiet study and computer use.

Library/media center materials handling during a duty period with few or no students present: emptying the book drop, checking in returned items, sorting them and re-shelving carts, shelf-reading for misplaced items.

Other assigned supervisory/administrative duties: proctoring study hall or detention, supervising standardized testing, ticket-taking or crowd supervision at a school event, covering another teacher's shop/lab during open hours, greeting and signing in visitors at a duty station.

sources.title: Autonomous Security Robots Are Starting to Patrol Schools and Cities, Despite Controversies - The Debrief
sources.claim: Team 1st Technologies' autonomous security robot patrolled Santa Fe High ... grounds in a pilot, providing 360-degree live video to human security officers; it surveils and deters but does not interact with or manage student behavior.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: campus security patrol. It is the closest deployed analogue to hall/cafeteria/bus supervision, but transfer is limited: it streams video for humans rather than checking passes, redirecting students, or intervening.

sources.title: Santa Fe High School tests out new security robot
sources.claim: The Santa Fe High School patrol robot is described as fully autonomous with seven cameras, able to handle weather, inclines and obstacle avoidance while patrolling school property.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor campus patrol, adjacent to bus-loop duty. Establishes autonomous navigation of school grounds but no capability to marshal students onto buses or keep them out of traffic.

sources.title: School and Transit Clients Expand Knightscope Contracts - Silicon UK
sources.claim: Knightscope autonomous security robots are sold and deployed under service contracts to school districts and other institutions, performing patrol and monitoring functions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial security patrol in school facilities. Shows autonomous mobile robots operating in E2 school settings, but the accepted output is detection/alerting, not supervision of students.

sources.system: bookBot (Dematic automated storage and retrieval system)
sources.title: bookBot and Collections | James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
sources.claim: The Hunt Library bookBot is a deployed automated storage and retrieval system ... stores library items and retrieves any requested item for delivery to a service desk, replacing human shelving and retrieval in a purpose-built machine bay.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library materials shelving and retrieval. Same objects (books/media) and same accepted output (item correctly stored and produced on request), performed with the work brought to a purpose-built machine.

sources.title: North Carolina State University bookBot — Library Technology Guides
sources.claim: The bookBot delivers any of up to two million stored items within five minutes of an online catalog request, i.e. it performs the retrieval function of library shelving staff at production reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving and re-storing library materials, the materials-handling core of school library assistance; comparable objects and precision, at higher throughput than a human shelver.

sources.system: Lyngsoe Sort Mate / Library Mate automated material handling (AMH)
sources.title: Library Automation Solutions | Lyngsoe Library Systems
sources.claim: Lyngsoe Systems sells deployed automated material handling systems for libraries that check in returned items and route/sort them automatically into bins for re-shelving, integrated with self-service check-out kiosks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library circulation check-in and sorting of returns, which is the bulk of the materials-handling side of library duty; identical objects and the same accepted output (items checked in and sorted for shelving).
