tasks.label: Prepare classrooms with a variety of materials or resources for children to explore, manipulate, or use in learning activities or imaginative play.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Morning setup of 4-6 learning centers in a self-contained SPED kindergarten room: pulling counting bears, links, unifix cubes, magnetic letters, puzzles, sorting trays, leveled books and task cards from labeled shelves and setting a differentiated set out at each low table per the day's lesson plan, around child-sized furniture and existing clutter.

Sensory and adaptive materials prep: filling sensory bins/tables with rice, beans, water beads or sand plus scoops and hidden objects; laying out fidgets, weighted lap pads, pencil grips, slant boards; building velcro picture-symbol schedules, first/then boards and tactile/braille-labeled items individualized to each child's IEP.

Art and messy-activity setup: pouring paint into cups, clipping paper to easels, portioning playdough, setting out glue, scissors, brushes and collage bits as one tray per child, covering tables, and putting drying racks and smocks in reach.

Dramatic/imaginative play area refresh: rotating theme props (play kitchen food, doctor kit, vehicles, dolls), hanging or laying out dress-up clothes, arranging soft toys, puppets and blocks on low open shelves so items are visible and inviting.

Restocking and organizing: hauling tubs of consumables from a storage closet or shared workroom to the classroom, replenishing labeled shelf bins, sorting returned materials back into the right bins, relabeling and staging materials for the next unit.

Off-classroom setup: arranging gross-motor or sensory-diet equipment (mats, tunnels, balance beam, cones, therapy balls) in a gym, motor room or playground area, or staging materials in a therapy/resource room before a pull-out session.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics, Inc.: RightPick 3 Order Fulfillment System - Material Handling 24/7
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick 3 is a commercially sold autonomous piece-picking system that transfers a wide variety of small ... one at a time between totes at up to 1,200 items/hour, and is explicitly used for kitting workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic kitting/order fulfillment. Assembling a specified assortment of small rigid objects (blocks, letters, bears, books, task cards) into a tray or bin is the same pick-and-place operation on comparable objects and precision, performed in a fixtured goods-to-robot cell.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand's kitting workflow assembles repeated, slightly varied sets of items from a limited product range - the same operation as building per-center or per-child material sets - and is in commercial use across three continents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated kitting. Preparing a center's materials is functionally a kit build: a fixed list of small items assembled into a container to a specified content standard.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks individual items from totes in fulfillment centers and handles over 200 million distinct product types of varying shape, size and weight.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: singulating and placing diverse consumer items in a fenced workcell. Classroom manipulatives and supplies fall inside the size/shape/weight envelope Sparrow already handles from presented totes.

sources.title: Robotic Barista Precision Systems : Robotic Coffee System
sources.claim: Artly's Barista Bot is a deployed, fully automated robotic arm system in compact kiosks that handles cups and pours liquids to a consistent quality standard, with a vision feedback loop on each cup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cup handling and liquid dispensing in a purpose-built kiosk. Filling paint cups and setting them on a tray involves the same cup grasping and controlled pouring at looser tolerance than latte art.

sources.title: Robots deployed for re-stocking shelves in convenient stores | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated shelves with bottled and ... drinks from a purpose-built rail-mounted workspace behind the cooler, mass-deployed to hundreds of Japanese convenience stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous shelf replenishment from presented stock. Refilling labeled classroom bins/shelves with standard items is the same pick-from-stock, place-to-slot operation when the stock is presented to the machine.

sources.system: Accutek automatic volumetric / weight filling machines
sources.title: Bottle & Liquid Filling Machines | Inline Filling Systems
sources.claim: Automatic volumetric, piston and vibratory weight filling machines are standard commercial equipment for dosing free-flowing granular and liquid products into containers on a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dosing granular media into containers. Filling a sensory bin with rice, beans or water beads to a target quantity is the same bulk-dosing operation done by these machines when the bin is presented on a line.

sources.system: Humanoid robots evaluated in the 2026 AI Index / Behavior-1K challenge
sources.developer: Stanford HAI (evaluation of multiple developers' systems)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots' 88% Fail Rate: Completing Home Tasks
sources.claim: Stanford's 2026 AI Index finds that today's humanoid robots safely and fully complete only about 12% of real ..., with the best Behavior-1K challenge teams reaching roughly 25% acceptable-quality success.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence bounding in-room, human-scale object arrangement (tidying, placing objects on furniture) at worker-quality reliability.

sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 mobile manipulator can be tasked to clean rooms in homes never seen in training, picking up and placing objects, but the developers state it is far from perfect ... frequently errs in both planning and motor execution.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available evidence for autonomous multi-object arrangement in a room built for people (picking up toys/objects and placing them); cited to show research-level, sub-worker reliability.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously performs supply and pharmacy deliveries in over 25 US hospitals, exceeding one million deliveries, navigating corridors and elevators among people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous transport and drop-off of supply totes inside a structured human facility. Shows E2 navigation/transport is solved, but manipulation is limited to grasping bagged/toted loads, not item-level arrangement.

sources.title: Figure AI humanoids sort 28,000 packages in 24-hour autonomous test
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 humanoids ran a continuous autonomous package-sorting operation at a customer warehouse station for nearly 40 hours, handling tens of thousands of packages at near-human speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained autonomous pick-and-place at a fixed, purpose-built station; shows worker-rate endurance only for presented, uniform items, not for roaming arrangement of varied classroom materials.

tasks.label: Provide assistive devices, supportive technology, or assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Restroom/toileting assistance for a kindergartner with a disability: walking or wheeling the child to the school restroom, managing clothing fasteners, supporting or transferring the child on and off a toilet or changing table, changing a pull-up, wiping/hygiene, handwashing, and returning to class, with the child moving unpredictably and sometimes resisting.

Providing and setting up supportive technology in the classroom: mounting a speech-generating AAC tablet on a wheelchair tray or desk, powering it up and opening the right communication board, positioning a switch or eye-gaze unit within the child's reach, adjusting it during the lesson, swapping batteries, and troubleshooting when the child knocks it out of place.

Physical positioning and mobility assistance inside the school: transferring a child between wheelchair, floor mat, adaptive chair, and stander; fastening straps, harnesses, and AFO braces; pushing the chair or spotting a child using a walker/gait trainer through hallways, doorways, and thresholds to the gym, therapy room, or cafeteria.

Distributing and fitting low-tech adaptive materials and sensory supports at the child's work area: pencil grips, slant boards, adapted scissors, weighted vest, noise-cancelling headphones, magnifier or large-print/braille materials, and checking that a hearing aid or FM/DM system is on, paired, and worn correctly.

Assisting access to facilities outside the classroom under less controlled conditions: lifting a child into an adaptive playground swing or onto equipment at recess, carrying and opening a cafeteria tray and containers, helping a child on and off the bus lift at arrival and dismissal, and arranging access at off-site field-trip venues.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare, Diligent Robotics to bring last-mile delivery to hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously transports lightweight supplies through hospital corridors and elevators and drops them off for staff; it is deployed at more than 25 ... with over 1 million deliveries. It is the closest deployed analogue to bringing equipment through an institutional building, but it does not fit devices to a person or provide personal care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item transport and drop-off inside a structured human facility. It substantiates autonomous navigation and delivery in E2 buildings, but not the child-facing manipulation, fitting, or personal-care steps this task requires.

sources.title: Meet the Robot That Nurses Unplugged - Proof News
sources.claim: Reporting on Moxi in hospital use describes frequent navigation and elevator failures requiring human help, indicating deployed mobile manipulators still need staff rescue in busy institutional corridors.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (institutional delivery); shows the reliability limits relevant to whether such a system could serve kindergarteners at worker quality.

sources.system: WHILL Autonomous Model / Autonomous Drive System
sources.title: WHILL Autonomous Service Expands North American Footprint with Alaska Airport Debut
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchairs are commercially deployed in airport terminals (LAX, MIA, SEA, DTW, ANC and others), driving passengers with reduced mobility along mapped routes from curb to gate with trained ground staff support. They carry self-directing adult passengers and perform no transfers, toileting, or supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a mobility-limited person through a structured facility. It covers only the transport leg for a cooperative adult rider, not transfers, strapping, or restroom assistance for a five-year-old.

sources.system: physically assistive robots (systematic review of the field)
sources.title: Physically Assistive Robots: A Systematic Review of Mobile and Manipulator Robots That Physically Assist People with Disabilities
sources.claim: A 2024 systematic review of physically assistive robots (mobile and manipulator robots that physically assist people with disabilities with ambulating, dressing, personal hygiene, eating) characterizes such robots as only recently becoming feasible, i.e., research-stage rather than deployed personal-care systems.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the ADL-assistance family (hygiene, dressing, transfers) required by this task's personal-assistance instances; establishes that no deployed autonomous system performs them.

sources.system: robotic dressing assistance systems (soft robotic self-wearing garment study)
sources.title: Self-Wearing Adaptive Garments via Soft Robotic Unfurling (arXiv)
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing (relevant to putting on braces, vests, or coats and to clothing management during toileting) remains a research problem; current approaches rely on rigid manipulators that struggle with deformable garments and safe physical contact.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: garment handling on a human body, needed for clothing management in toileting and for fitting vests and braces; the literature shows it is still a laboratory problem, not a deployed capability.

sources.title: Physical Support for Students | Disability Services | Wright State University
sources.claim: Even where an assistive robot is used in an institutional setting, human staff still perform the provisioning and setup: Wright State University's Obi robotic feeder program requires a dining services staff member to set the device up for the user before the meal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making an assistive device available and usable to a person with a disability inside a facility. It shows the provisioning/setup act itself is still performed by human staff, not by a robot.

sources.title: 1X Neo Home Robot: Teleoperation Today, Autonomy Tomorrow
sources.claim: The leading home humanoid marketed for household physical help, 1X's NEO, performed fetching and tidying tasks by teleoperation during a press demonstration, with scheduled remote human operators covering tasks its onboard autonomy cannot handle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general object handling and helping people in everyday settings. The most capable general-purpose candidate is teleoperated, so it cannot support positive judgments for device setup or personal assistance.

tasks.label: Organize and display students' work in a manner appropriate for their perceptual skills.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly classroom bulletin-board refresh in a kindergarten special education room: take down the previous unit's pieces, then mount ~15-25 pieces of children's paper artwork and worksheets (varied sizes, crayon/paint, sometimes crumpled or torn) with staples, pins or tape, adding large-print, high-contrast name/title labels at child eye level.

Adapting a display for a student who is blind or has low vision: producing a tactile/raised-line or braille-labeled version of the work, mounting on high-contrast backing, and placing it low and within reach for tactile exploration; also enlarging or re-contrasting work for a student with cortical visual impairment.

Organizing accumulated work into individual portfolios, folders, cubbies and take-home packets: sorting loose papers by child, hole-punching/filing in binders, ordering chronologically for conferences, labeling folders with picture symbols and names.

Hallway or school-wide display outside the classroom, plus arranging three-dimensional projects (clay figures, paper-plate crafts, block photos) on a shelf or display table with labels and adequate spacing.
Digital display of work: photographing or scanning each child's piece, uploading to a class app/portfolio site, and projecting selected work on the classroom screen for whole-group sharing.

sources.title: Document Scanning & Digitization Services | Ripcord AI-Powered Robotics
sources.claim: Ripcord's proprietary robotic workcells autonomously handle heterogeneous stacks of paper - detecting and removing staples, unfolding pages, opening envelopes - and feed sheets for imaging in the company's purpose-built digitization facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic paper handling for digitization. Transfers to organizing/displaying children's paper work because the objects are the same class (loose, variable, sometimes stapled or folded sheets) and the required action is damage-free single-sheet separation and precise placement.

sources.title: Ripcord robots remove tedium, paper cuts from digitizing records
sources.claim: Ripcord machines take stacks of paper, remove staples and separate and place single sheets at roughly one sheet per second onto a conveyor for scanning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: de-stapling and single-sheet feeding. The hardest physical element of mounting or filing children's work is separating one flexible sheet from a pile without tearing it; this system does that at commercial reliability inside a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Ripcord uses robotics to digitize records, processes and avoid paper waste
sources.claim: In Ripcord's California factory, robots with computer vision sort pages and digitize documents at a scale of hundreds of millions of pages per year, with humans handling exceptions only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic sorting and imaging of loose documents. Directly covers the physical capture step of digitally displaying student work and the sheet-sorting step of building per-student portfolios.

sources.title: Amazon introduces Sparrow—a state-of-the-art robot that handles millions of diverse products
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products drawn from millions of diverse, unpackaged and deformable items inside fenced warehouse cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking novel, previously unseen items of varied size and rigidity from a presented bin. Transfers to picking up children's craft objects and paper pieces presented to a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force/tactile sensing to pick and stow about 75% of warehouse items into shelf pods at human-comparable speed, i.e. placing varied items into a compartmented storage surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact-rich stowing of diverse items into shelf compartments. Comparable to arranging small craft objects on a display shelf or placing work into cubbies, with force control that limits damage to fragile items.

sources.title: Robot Labeler | TOPPAN Infomedia Inc.
sources.claim: Camera-guided robotic labelers automatically apply printed labels to specified locations on product surfaces in production lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vision-guided application of a printed paper label to a defined position on a surface. This is the same physical operation as affixing a sheet of work, or a large-print name label, to a display panel at a specified spot.

sources.title: Optimizing Apparel Order Fulfillment – OPEX SURE SORT
sources.claim: OPEX Sure Sort uses autonomous iBOT vehicles to carry individually inducted items to designated bins or ... in an array of destinations, with scanning and pack-to-light error checking.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level sortation into a wall of destination bins. Sorting each child's papers into that child's folder/cubbie is the same operation - identify the item, route it to the correct one of many labeled compartments.

sources.title: Single-Sheet Separation from Paper Stack Based on Friction Uncertainty Using High-Speed Robot Hand
sources.claim: A high-speed robot hand demonstrated reliable separation of a single sheet ... standing stack of paper using friction-based finger motion.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dexterous separation of individual sheets. Supports the sheet-picking element of mounting and filing children's paper work when the stack is presented to the machine.

tasks.label: Organize and supervise games or other recreational activities to promote physical, mental, or social development.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Small-group structured play in a self-contained kindergarten special education classroom: teacher selects and sets out turn-taking games (board games, matching games, pretend-play centers) for 4-6 students with autism, intellectual disability, or speech/language delays; seats and positions students, models and prompts turns, uses hand-over-hand assistance and visual supports, adapts rules on the fly, and redirects off-task or disruptive behavior until the activity ends and materials are put away.

Adapted gross-motor / motor-room or gym session: teacher lays out an obstacle course, parachute, bean bags, scooters or balls; leads 6-12 kindergarteners with physical, sensory, or motor delays through the activity; physically spots, supports, or repositions children with low tone, braces, or walkers; adjusts equipment heights and distances; monitors for falls and fatigue; packs equipment away.

Outdoor playground recess/free-play supervision: teacher escorts the class outside, organizes a group game (tag, duck-duck-goose, ball toss), monitors safety on climbing structures and swings, facilitates play between students with disabilities and typically developing peers, intervenes in conflicts, prevents elopement from the yard, and handles scrapes or upsets before lining the class up to return.

Inclusive/co-taught activity in a general education kindergarten room: whole-class circle games, movement songs, or center rotations with 20+ children; the special education teacher organizes an adapted version so 2-4 IEP students can participate, positions and prompts them, cues peers to include them, and provides behavior support while the general education teacher runs the activity.

Behavior/sensory escalation during a recreational activity: a student becomes dysregulated mid-game, elopes, grabs equipment from a peer, or begins a meltdown; the teacher redirects, offers a sensory or calming alternative, physically guides or blocks as trained under the behavior plan, keeps the rest of the group's activity running, and documents the incident.

sources.title: LuxAI - Award winning social robots for autism and special needs education
sources.claim: QTrobot for Schools is a commercially sold social robot used in special education classrooms; it autonomously runs pre-built educational modules and generates session reports, but it is explicitly an assistive tool integrated by a teacher, support worker, or therapist rather than a supervisor of children.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed system to robot-led recreational/social-skill activities for children with disabilities; cited to show the frontier is a teacher-operated tabletop tutor, not organization and supervision of live group games.

sources.title: VITA: A Multi-modal LLM-based System for Longitudinal, Autonomous, and Adaptive Robotic Mental Well-being Coaching
sources.claim: QTrobot's hardware is a 90 cm child-sized humanoid with static legs and limited arm degrees of freedom, so it cannot walk to a play area, set out or retrieve play equipment, spot a falling child, or physically assist a child's participation.
sources.transferJustification: Hardware description bounding what the leading commercial special-education robot can physically do during games: no locomotion, no equipment handling, no physical support of a child.

sources.system: In-home social robot (Jibo-based) for ASD intervention
sources.developer: MIT Media Lab / Personal Robots Group
sources.title: Improving social skills in children with ASD using a long-term, in-home social robot
sources.claim: A long-term in-home study with an autonomous social robot ran structured social-skill activities with autistic children, but always as a triadic interaction with a ... present rather than as independent supervision of children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot-led social-skill activity with a child with a disability); shows even the most autonomous long-duration deployments require a supervising adult and cover only seated one-child activities.

sources.system: iCub/humanoid robot in children-robot imitation game study
sources.title: Who will you imitate? Studying reciprocal influence in children-robot groups during an imitation game
sources.claim: Group human-robot game research places a robot as a participant in a four-child imitation game in a controlled study setting; the robot is a play partner among children, not the organizer or safety supervisor, and children disregard it when its behavior is atypical.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot in a multi-child group game); cited to show group-game research remains short controlled sessions with adults present and no robot responsibility for supervision or safety.

tasks.label: Instruct and monitor students in the use and care of equipment or materials to prevent injuries and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-class or small-group lesson on safe use and care of everyday classroom fine-motor materials (child scissors, glue sticks, crayons, markers, blocks, manipulatives) in a self-contained or inclusion kindergarten room: the teacher demonstrates the grip and technique with the actual tool, uses hand-over-hand or physical prompting with students who have motor or intellectual disabilities, watches 6-12 five-year-olds continuously, and physically intervenes when a child points scissors at a peer, mouths or throws materials, or breaks crayons; ends with a supervised put-away/cleanup routine.

Instructing and monitoring an individual student in the use and care of adaptive/assistive equipment - walker, gait trainer, wheelchair, stander, long cane, hearing aids or FM system, braillewriter, AAC speech device, adapted seating - checking that it is used correctly and not damaged, steadying the child, correcting positioning, and stopping unsafe use before a fall or a broken device.

Instructing and monitoring students in careful handling of classroom technology and sensory equipment (iPads/switches/headphones, listening centers, therapy balls, platform swings, weighted items, sensory-room gear), including modeling gentle handling, supervising turn-taking, and physically redirecting a child who swings, drops, or bangs the equipment.

Safety instruction and active supervision on playground, gym, or adapted-PE equipment during recess/motor time on school grounds: reviewing rules at the slide, climber, and swings, spotting and physically supporting students with balance or coordination difficulties, and blocking or catching a child heading into an unsafe use.

Life-skills routines with tools and consumables - snack utensils, cups and pouring, toothbrushes, art paint and brushes, classroom jobs - teaching proper use, cleaning, and storage, with hand-over-hand assistance and continuous monitoring for choking, spills, cuts, or damage to materials.

sources.title: The School District of Manatee County Becomes First in Florida to Adopt RoboKind's Robot and Social-Emotional Curriculum for Students with Autism
sources.claim: Milo, a small tabletop social robot, is deployed in US school districts to deliver social-emotional/communication lessons to students with autism, always alongside an educator who acts as facilitator; it does not handle classroom equipment or supervise safety.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot in special education for young children; cited to show the scope of real school deployments - seated lesson delivery to one child at a time, with a human facilitator - which does not extend to demonstrating tool use, hand-over-hand prompting, or preventing injury and damage.

sources.system: autonomous social robot deployment (Kupaei et al., HRI 2026)
sources.title: Social Robots on the Loose: Supporting Children's Independent Learning in the Wild (Proc. 21st ACM/IEEE HRI)
sources.claim: A 2026 HRI study reports autonomous social robots placed in classrooms supporting children's independent learning without direct supervision; the robots deliver conversational learning interactions, not physical instruction or safety supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous child-facing tutoring in a school (E2 setting). Cited as the ceiling of demonstrated autonomy with children; the interaction is speech/screen based with no manipulation of tools, no hand-over-hand guidance, and no injury-prevention monitoring, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: social robots in classrooms (review of field studies)
sources.title: The use of social robots in classrooms: A review of field-based studies
sources.claim: A review of field-based studies finds social robots are rarely used in real classrooms and rarely run autonomously for more than a few days, with safety issues seldom addressed.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that sustained autonomous classroom operation by robots - a prerequisite for continuously monitoring kindergarteners' equipment use - has not been demonstrated.

sources.developer: academic HRI researchers (ACM CHI/HRI workshop paper)
sources.title: Expert Insights on Robots for Safeguarding Children: How (not) and Why (not)?
sources.claim: Expert-elicitation work on robots for safeguarding children reports that current perception and speech capabilities are inadequate for robots to autonomously monitor children and detect concerning situations in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic monitoring of children for safety. The same perception limits apply to continuously watching a kindergarten group and detecting unsafe tool use before an injury occurs.

tasks.label: Perform administrative duties, such as school library assistance, hall and cafeteria monitoring, and bus loading and unloading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hall/transition monitoring: standing corridor duty and escorting a line of kindergarteners with disabilities between classroom, restroom, and specials; redirecting running or dysregulated children, blocking elopement toward exits, hand-holding and physical prompting, walking an upset child to the office.

Cafeteria duty during kindergarten lunch: opening milk cartons and packaging, prompting/assisting students with feeding and utensil use, watching for choking and allergy exposure, wiping spills, managing noise and behavior, dismissing tables and prompting tray cleanup.

Bus loading/unloading duty in the outdoor bus loop at arrival and dismissal: matching each child to the correct bus, hand-holding across the loading zone, handing off to drivers/aides, securing harnesses or car seats, assisting a wheelchair lift, in rain, cold, and traffic with parents present.

Other assigned supervisory coverage: morning car-rider line, recess/playground duty, restroom checks, covering another teacher's group — watching a mixed group of young children, intervening in conflicts, first-aid triage of scrapes, counting and accounting for every child.

Library duty, student-facing portion: bringing the kindergarten class to the school library, helping children choose picture books at their level, running them through check-out, keeping the group seated for a read-aloud and quiet in the stacks.
Library duty, clerical materials-handling portion: checking in returned books, sorting them, and reshelving/stocking picture books and readers on the library's shelves and carts.

sources.date: 2017 (case story; system in ongoing production use)
sources.title: Maximized Efficiencies and Material Turnaround at Sacramento Public Library
sources.claim: Lyngsoe Sort Mate automated material handling system at Sacramento Public Library automatically checks in and sorts returned library items into a 40-bin sort in the library's central sorting room, deployed in production at high volume.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library circulation materials handling. The teacher's library-assistance duty consists of checking in, sorting and reshelving the same class of objects (books/media); the AMH machine performs the check-in and sort autonomously once items are inducted into purpose-built conveyor equipment.

sources.title: bookBot and Collections | James B. Hunt Jr. Library | NC State University Libraries
sources.claim: The Hunt Library bookBot is a robotic automated storage and retrieval system ... stores and retrieves up to 2 million books from bins in a purpose-built vault on catalog request, in daily operation since 2013.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelving and retrieving library books. It substitutes for the shelving/retrieval part of library assistance, handling identical objects, but only where books are stored in machine-readable bins in a purpose-built racking vault rather than on open school-library shelves.

sources.title: This Robot Librarian Locates Haphazardly Placed Books
sources.claim: AuRoSS, an autonomous shelf-scanning robot demonstrated in Singapore public libraries, navigates the stacks at night and detects misfiled books with about 99% accuracy, but only flags them for human staff to reshelve.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library shelf-reading. Shows the limit of in-stacks library robotics in a real (E2) library — inventory scanning only, with the physical reshelving left to staff — so it does not substantiate completing library assistance at E2.

sources.title: Schools & Higher Education | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope's autonomous security robots marketed to schools patrol and record in parking lots and structures; they are surveillance platforms with no manipulation or child-supervision capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: campus patrol/monitoring. The closest deployed analogue to hall and lot monitoring; it records and alerts but cannot escort, redirect, or physically intervene with kindergarteners, so it does not complete the monitoring instances.

sources.title: Salamanca pauses use of educational robot
sources.claim: A July 2026 school-district pilot of a lifelike 'teacher's assistant' robot in New York was paused; the state teachers' union raised hallway, cafeteria and bus-loop monitoring and chasing a student who leaves class as duties the robot plainly could not be relied on to perform.
sources.transferJustification: Directly concerns the same duties (hallway, cafeteria, bus-loop monitoring) in a US K-12 setting as of July 2026; the most advanced school-deployed humanoid is a stationary instructional avatar, confirming no robotic system performs these supervisory duties.

tasks.label: Control the inventory or distribution of classroom equipment, materials, or supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: During instruction, hands out and collects individual learning materials directly to/from kindergarteners with disabilities seated at tables or on the carpet: adapted scissors, crayons, worksheets, manipulatives, snack items, sensory tools; matches each child's IEP-specified adapted item to the right child, withholds hazards, prompts and hand-over-hand assists, then reclaims items as children move on. Children move unpredictably, grab, drop, and mouth items.

Before or between lessons, prepares and sets out material sets: assembles per-student or per-table kits of supplies from the classroom's stock, loads trays/bins, and places them at tables and learning centers, replenishing consumables (paper, glue sticks, markers) at each station so the activity can run.

End-of-day/weekly reset: sorts returned mixed manipulatives, blocks, cards, and writing tools back into their labeled bins and cubbies, refills consumable stock on open shelves, discards broken items, and arranges the storage shelving so materials are findable next day.

Periodic stock control: walks the classroom cabinets, closet, and shelving to check what is on hand and what is low (partially used glue bottles, crayon boxes, laminated card sets, paper reams, wipes), records levels on a form/spreadsheet, and submits a requisition or supply order to the school office.

Manages adaptive/assistive equipment issued to individual students: checks out and issues FM/hearing systems, AAC speech devices, braille materials, adaptive seating, weighted vests; fits or positions them on/for the child, verifies they function, charges and sanitizes them, and logs which device is with which student.

Receives supply deliveries: collects or accepts cartons of ordered materials from the school office/central storeroom, moves them through hallways to the classroom, opens and unpacks them, checks contents against the order, and puts items away in the classroom closet and on shelves.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking arm is deployed commercially across Staples' North American fulfillment centers, picking office/school-supply SKUs of varied shape, size, weight and packaging out of bulk containers and placing them into destination totes in a fixtured workcell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking/kitting of small office and school supplies. The physical operation — recognizing heterogeneous small supply items presented in a bin and placing each into the correct destination container — is the same as assembling per-student material kits and sorting returned classroom supplies into labeled bins, at comparable object size and precision, when the work is presented to the machine.

sources.title: KNAPP and Covariant Partnership Advances AI Robotics for more Efficient Warehouses
sources.claim: KNAPP's Pick-it-Easy Robot powered by Covariant autonomously picks single articles from supply containers and places them into designated target totes in live warehouse operation for up to 14 ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: goods-to-robot item picking into order totes. Sorting mixed small items into correct destination containers is the same manipulation as kitting supplies per student or returning manipulatives to labeled bins, once containers are fixtured and presented.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously scans store aisles multiple times per ... record product availability and shelf stock, and is deployed across operating grocery chains (e.g., 17 Harmons stores).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory auditing. It substantiates autonomous stock-level counting and low-stock flagging on open, labeled, planogrammed shelving — the counting/reordering half of inventory control — but depends on standardized barcoded product presentation rather than a classroom's cabinets and partially used consumables.

sources.title: UPS deploys Verity warehouse drones for inventory tracking
sources.claim: Verity's autonomous inventory drones perform fully autonomous inventory checks in warehouses, deployed at UPS Supply Chain Solutions' Kentucky facility to track racked inventory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse cycle counting. It shows autonomous stock counting and record generation at worker quality when stock is stored in standardized, labeled locations — the inventory-count-and-record portion of this task under a purpose-built presentation.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch works autonomously to unload cartons from trailers onto conveyors, handling mixed stacking and fallen boxes; DHL had 10 units deployed commercially across three countries by June 2025, unloading up to 700 cases per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carton unloading at a receiving dock. Receiving and breaking down delivered supply cartons is the same physical operation — grasping and moving mixed boxes from a delivered stack onto a conveyor/staging point — at comparable weight and precision when the delivery is presented to the machine.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated shelves with bottled and ... drinks from crates, mass-deployed to hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment from crates. Refilling standardized consumable stock into fixed shelf slots is the same operation as replenishing classroom consumables, but the robot runs on a rail in a purpose-built backroom cooler lane with uniform, known items.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi autonomously transports supplies and pharmacy items through hospital corridors and elevators, deployed in more than 25 ... with over one million completed deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-to-point supply delivery inside an institutional building. It substantiates autonomous transport of supply loads through staffed corridors (the fetch-and-carry leg of distribution), but the robot delivers a closed load to a station; it does not select or hand individual items to people.

tasks.label: Plan or supervise experiential learning activities, such as class projects, field trips, demonstrations, or visits by guest speakers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In-class hands-on project with a kindergarten special-education group (5-12 children with autism, intellectual, sensory or physical disabilities, plus paraprofessionals): teacher plans an adapted project (planting seeds, sensory/science exploration, cooking, art), lays out and adapts materials per IEP (adapted scissors, braille/tactile labels, visual schedules), then supervises the activity live — hand-over-hand prompting, redirecting elopement, managing scissors/hot or messy materials, de-escalating meltdowns, and running cleanup.

Off-site field trip (zoo, farm, pumpkin patch, fire station, children's museum): teacher arranges accessible transport and chaperone ratios in advance, then supervises the trip — bus/van loading with wheelchairs and harnesses, continuous headcounts, holding hands near traffic and crowds, toileting and feeding support, managing sensory overload in a public, unpredictable venue, and returning every child safely.

In-school demonstration or guest speaker visit (firefighter in gear, dentist, therapy dog, community helper) in the classroom or multipurpose room: teacher schedules and briefs the visitor, pre-teaches the routine, positions students (wheelchairs, front-row for low-vision, interpreter sightlines), and supervises during the visit — prompting participation, managing noise/startle reactions, and physically redirecting children who approach equipment.

Planning and coordination episodes with no live activity: selecting the experience and tying it to IEP goals, writing the lesson/activity plan, permission slips and allergy/medical forms, booking accessible buses and venue accommodations, assigning paraprofessionals and related-service providers, risk assessment, and follow-up communication with families and administrators. Desk and meeting work.

Walking trip or school-grounds experiential activity: nature walk on campus, school garden planting, walk to a neighborhood library or post office, or a playground-based demonstration. Teacher plans the route and supports, then supervises children on sidewalks and uneven ground — line formation, hand-holding, wheelchair pushing, weather and stranger management.

sources.title: QTrobot for special needs education - LuxAI S.A.
sources.claim: QTrobot is a commercial tabletop humanoid used in special-needs education that autonomously delivers a scripted social/language curriculum to a child, alongside (not instead of) an educator; it has no mobility or capacity to supervise a group or intervene physically.
sources.transferJustification: Closest cited system to the task's population (kindergarten-age children with disabilities) in the task's own setting; cited to establish the ceiling of autonomous classroom robots — dyadic seated interaction, no material handling, no group supervision.

sources.title: Robot education peers in a situated primary school study: Personalisation promotes child learning
sources.claim: Two autonomous social robots ran as learning companions in primary-school classrooms for two weeks without experimenter supervision, showing autonomous child-facing tutoring is possible in a school, but limited to seated learning interaction rather than activity supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-classroom tutoring of children) in the same E2 setting; cited to show what autonomy in a school classroom currently covers — dialogue-based learning support, not safety supervision, material setup, or physical prompting.

sources.title: The AV1 robot is helping sick children attend school | CNN Business
sources.claim: The AV1 school robot is a desktop telepresence device fully controlled in real time by the absent student; it has no arms or mobility and cannot supervise or physically assist anyone.

sources.developer: Global Bridge Holdings with Gunma University
sources.title: Day care facilities test robots as high-tech solution to alleviate staffing shortages - The Japan Times
sources.claim: The most advanced childcare-facility robot deployments perform greeting, facial-recognition identification and vital-sign monitoring in nursery schools; supervision of the children remains with staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (supervising young children in an institutional childcare facility) in an E2 setting; cited because it marks the limit of deployed capability — passive monitoring and greeting, with no physical intervention or group safety management.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University / University of Bonn
sources.title: The Interactive Museum Tour-Guide Robot - Robotics Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
sources.claim: An autonomous mobile robot guided hundreds of museum visitors along tours over a multi-day deployment, establishing autonomous group-leading and navigation in a crowded public venue, but with no responsibility for anyone's safety or conduct.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (leading a group of people through a public venue) — the navigational core of a field trip. Cited to show that even this best case covers only wayfinding and narration, not headcounts, hand-holding, toileting, restraint, or bus loading of children with disabilities.

sources.date: 2025 (analysis of consumer NEO launch and Expert Mode teleoperation)
sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: State-of-the-art general-purpose humanoids intended for unstructured human spaces still depend on human teleoperators for complete multi-step chores, so autonomous set-up, adaptation and cleanup of classroom project materials is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (multi-step object handling in rooms built for people) bearing on the materials-handling half of running a class project; cited as a negative bound on autonomous mobile manipulation in human settings.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (robot acting as a teaching assistant in a US school) in an E2 setting; cited to show the deployed frontier is a conversational avatar, which cannot supervise an experiential activity.

tasks.label: Prepare classrooms with a variety of materials or resources for children to explore, manipulate, or use in learning activities or imaginative play.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Before school in a self-contained elementary special-ed classroom, the teacher pulls manipulatives, adapted books, worksheets, visual supports and counters from labeled bins and cabinets and sets out differentiated sets at 3-5 small-group stations, matching each student's IEP level.

Making and assembling adapted materials: printing picture symbols/communication icons, laminating, cutting them apart, applying Velcro dots, assembling file-folder tasks and task boxes, and labeling bins for the coming week.

Preparing sensory and imaginative-play areas: filling a sensory bin with rice, beads or water and hiding target objects, laying out playdough, fidgets, scoops/tongs, dramatic-play props and switch-adapted toys.

Restocking and organizing supplies: replenishing crayons, glue, paper, wipes and snack items from a supply closet, refilling classroom bins and shelves, checking what has run out, returning materials to labeled storage.

Setting up assistive technology and adaptive equipment: producing braille/tactile materials on an embosser, charging and mounting AAC devices, attaching switches and mounts, positioning slant boards, adapted seating and FM systems for specific students.

Resetting the room between activities or at the end of the day: returning scattered materials to labeled bins, wiping tables, clearing the floor and moving furniture between circle-time, centers and testing configurations.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Integrations and Workflows
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick is a commercially deployed, AI-driven piece-picking system that picks a wide range of small items from presented totes into order containers, explicitly marketed and used for automated kitting workflows in fenced/guarded warehouse cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse kitting. Assembling per-station sets of small classroom manipulatives (counters, cards, dice, adapted books) from source bins into trays is the same pick-list-driven, small-object pick-and-place at similar precision, when the materials and trays are presented to the machine as in an E1 cell.

sources.title: How RightHand Robotics is using RealSense computer vision technology... - RealSense
sources.claim: RightPick2 cells run with one human supervising a fleet of several robots picking thousands of SKUs, i.e. autonomous operation with occasional human intervention rather than teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the limited-intervention criterion for the kitting evidence used for classroom material set assembly.

sources.title: ABB Adds 8 kg Model to IRB 360 FlexPicker Line - Automate.org
sources.claim: ABB's IRB 360 FlexPicker delta robots are long-standing commercial vision-guided pick-and-place robots that load loose items into trays and containers and kit assorted products on packaging lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: primary food packaging. Placing assorted small objects into a presented container (sensory-bin objects, scoops, props into a tub) is the same vision-guided placement of irregular light items into containers on a conveyor.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocking robots were mass-deployed to 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, autonomously replenishing refrigerated shelves with bottles and ... around the clock, with the vendor monitoring remotely.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf replenishment. Refilling classroom consumable bins from cartons is the same repetitive transfer of uniform stock items from presented crates onto fixed shelf positions, at lower speed and precision than the store case.

sources.system: Robot PortaTable 130 (Robotfactory) with Zünd digital cutter
sources.title: Allies in Print: End-of-Line Automation | Digital Output Magazine
sources.claim: Print-finishing lines use collaborative robots integrated with digital cutting tables to automatically load and remove cut sheet material, alongside automated feeders and stackers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: digital print finishing. Producing adapted materials (print, laminate, die-cut picture symbols, stack and sort cards) is exactly print-finishing work; the same fixtured cells handle flat laminated sheets at equal or better precision.

sources.title: Products | AccuPlace
sources.claim: Commercial print-and-apply label applicators automatically print and apply pressure-sensitive labels ... products with placement accuracy of about ±0.05 mm.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic label application. Applying adhesive Velcro dots/labels to laminated symbol cards and bin labels is the same pressure-sensitive adhesive placement on presented flat stock, at far looser tolerance.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (π0.5)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 is a research vision-language-action model that autonomously cleans kitchens and bedrooms in homes never seen in training, but its developers state it is far from perfect ... frequently errs.

sources.title: Robot provides personalized room cleanup | Stanford Report
sources.claim: TidyBot, a mobile manipulator that puts objects away in a room according to learned user preferences, achieved about 85% correct put-away of objects in real-world tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting objects away in a lived-in room. Its 85% success shows autonomous room-level material handling remains below the reliability a school would accept for classroom reset.

sources.title: Figure 03 Review 2026: Price, Release Date & Is It For Sale? | RoboZaps Blog
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 household demonstrations (dishwasher, living room and bedroom tidying, January-May 2026) are company-reported as fully autonomous but occur in Figure's own environments, with no independent worker-quality deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying by a humanoid. Checked as the frontier candidate for arranging objects in a human-built room; the evidence is staged demos, not deployment at worker reliability in a classroom.

sources.developer: Realbotix / Salamanca City Central School District
sources.title: Salamanca Superintendent sets the record straight on AI-powered robot coming to the classroom - WKBW
sources.claim: The humanoid robot being piloted in a US school district classroom is a stationary AI teaching assistant that does not move around the room, i.e. deployed classroom robots do not handle or lay out learning materials.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about robots in classrooms: shows that the robots actually placed in classrooms are social/instructional interfaces without material-handling capability.

tasks.label: Establish and enforce rules for behavior and procedures for maintaining order among students.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Start-of-year (or new-unit) establishment of classroom rules and routines in a self-contained elementary special education room: teaching and modeling 3-5 expectations, posting visual rule charts and picture schedules, rehearsing routines (lining up, hand raising, transitions, materials handling) with 6-12 students with autism, intellectual disability or emotional disturbance, including nonverbal/AAC users; requires modeling with bodies and objects and physically arranging the room and supports.

Daily enforcement of rules and order during ordinary instruction and transitions in the self-contained/resource room: proximity control, verbal and gestural prompts, running a token economy or point sheet (handing out tokens/moving chart pieces), redirecting off-task or disruptive children, physically guiding a wandering child back to a seat, removing distracting objects, and directing paraprofessionals.

Implementing an individual behavior intervention plan for one student (FBA-based): antecedent supports, differential reinforcement, planned ignoring, prompting through a break/calm-down routine, hand-over-hand or gentle physical prompting, escorting the child to a break space, and recording data - while the rest of the class keeps working.

Escalated behavior or crisis: a child becomes aggressive, throws furniture/objects, or elopes from the room. Teacher de-escalates verbally, physically blocks or guides the student, clears peers to a safe area, applies a trained hold/escort if required by policy, then re-establishes order and reviews expectations afterward.

Enforcing rules and procedures outside the classroom on school premises: hallway transitions, cafeteria, recess/playground, assemblies and bus lines, supervising students with disabilities amid crowds of general-education peers, keeping the group together, prompting compliance and intervening when a student bolts or conflicts with a peer.

sources.title: Robot QT faces a classroom challenge of keeping kids focused | AI Magazine
sources.claim: QTrobot used with students with learning disabilities in a Canadian public school to help them stay focused; the robot was directed by a human instructor via tablet during the sessions rather than managing the class itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustaining student attention/engagement in a special-needs classroom. It is the closest published in-classroom behavior-support use, but the robot works on instructor-selected activities with individuals while a human keeps order, so it does not transfer to establishing and enforcing rules for a whole class.

sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom
sources.claim: A humanoid social robot (with LLM speech) trialled as a teaching assistant in real school lessons; the author reports current robots are not robust enough for autonomous continuous use in ..., especially with noise and groups.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisting/leading classroom activity. Directly probes the same environment (a school classroom with a group of children) and reports the state of the art falls short of unsupervised continuous operation, so it cannot support supervising or enforcing rules among students.

sources.developer: Plymouth University / EU L2TOR-era classroom study (PLOS ONE)
sources.title: Robot education peers in a situated primary school study: Personalisation promotes child learning
sources.claim: Autonomous social robots were embedded in two primary-school classrooms for two weeks without experimenter supervision, acting as learning companions for children - showing autonomous robot operation in a school classroom, limited to one-to-one tutoring interactions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous one-to-one tutoring in a classroom. It establishes that autonomous robots can persist in the E2 classroom setting, but the robots only run tutoring dialogues; they neither set behavioral expectations nor redirect, prompt or physically manage children, so capability does not transfer to rule enforcement.

sources.title: Schools & Higher Education | Knightscope
sources.claim: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robots are marketed and deployed on school campuses, patrolling parking lots and structures and acting as a mobile call box; they detect and report but do not interact with or manage student behavior.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintaining order/security on institutional premises. Autonomy and outdoor campus deployment are real, but the robot only patrols and relays alerts to human security; it cannot instruct children, deliver reinforcement, redirect a child or intervene physically, so it does not transfer to enforcing classroom or school behavior rules.

sources.title: Can Robots Help Autistic Children Better Their Academic Performance?
sources.claim: RoboKind's Milo is used in US special education classrooms to teach social-emotional lessons, with a human facilitator selecting and running each lesson from an iPad while sitting with the student.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: teaching social/behavioral skills to elementary students with autism, the population in this task. The robot is operator-driven and works one-to-one under a facilitator who remains responsible for behavior management, so it cannot substantiate autonomous rule setting or order maintenance.

tasks.label: Provide assistive devices, supportive technology, or assistance accessing facilities, such as restrooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary special-ed classroom: teacher provides and sets up a student's supportive technology for a lesson — hands over the speech-generating/AAC device or iPad, clamps or mounts it on the wheelchair tray or slant board, positions a head/hand switch within the child's reach, powers it on, opens the right board/app, and adjusts angle and volume as the child moves and reacts.

Restroom access for a student with a physical or intellectual disability: escorting or wheeling the child to the accessible stall, transferring them to the toilet or supporting them on an adapted seat, managing clothing and fasteners, hygiene and clean-up, hand washing, and re-seating in the wheelchair — done on the child's schedule, often with resistance or unpredictable movement.

Physical mobility and positioning assistance in and around the classroom: lifting/transferring a child between wheelchair, floor mat, stander, adapted chair or gait trainer; strapping and adjusting positioning equipment; hand-over-hand support for a child with a walker on stairs, thresholds, or playground equipment.

Escorting/transporting a student to a facility within the school building: pushing a manual wheelchair or walking beside a student down corridors to the cafeteria, therapy room, restroom door, or bus loading zone, opening/holding doors and using the accessible route, during passing periods with other children around.

Sensory assistive devices for students who are blind/low-vision or deaf/hard-of-hearing: checking and inserting hearing aids or cochlear processors, changing tiny batteries, pairing and clipping on an FM/DM transmitter, setting up a braille display or magnifier, and handing out tactile/brailled materials fitted to the child.

Fetching, delivering and distributing assistive equipment and adapted materials around the school: collecting charged AAC devices, adapted keyboards, communication binders, adapted books or equipment from the resource/therapy room or storage, bringing them to the classroom, and setting them out at students' places before an activity.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics hits 1M picks with Moxi robot in healthcare settings - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi, a mobile manipulator with an arm, autonomously fetches and delivers supplies, specimens and medications inside hospitals, operating doors and elevators; deployed commercially at scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fetch-and-delivery of small items through corridors of an institution-controlled facility. Transfers to fetching charged AAC devices and adapted materials from a school resource room to classrooms — same object scale, same building-scale navigation and drop-off precision.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi's hospital deployment scale as of early 2026: nearly 100 robots, 25+ facilities, over 1.25 million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes maturity/reliability of the delivery capability cited for the school materials-delivery instance.

sources.title: WHILL Launches Autonomous Services at Munich Airport
sources.claim: WHILL autonomous wheelchairs carry seated passengers to a chosen destination through an airport terminal under their own navigation, then return to base; staff assist with boarding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting a seated person with limited mobility along an accessible route inside a crowded, institution-controlled building. Transfers to wheeling a student down school corridors to the cafeteria or restroom door — same passenger-carrying navigation among pedestrians.

sources.title: WHILL Autonomous Service Expands North American Footprint with Alaska Airport Debut
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchair service is in commercial operation at US airports, e.g. Anchorage from March 2026, alongside earlier Haneda and Munich deployments.
sources.transferJustification: Confirms deployed, non-demo status of the passenger-transport capability used for the escort instance.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Sparrow autonomously identifies and picks individual, varied consumer items out of containers and places them into designated totes inside a fenced, purpose-built fulfillment cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: selecting a specific item from presented stock and placing it at a defined hand-off point. Transfers to an E1 counterfactual where devices and adapted materials are fixtured and presented for pick-and-present, matching object size and placement precision.

sources.title: Hello Robot Unveils Stretch 4: A Simply Useful Robot that Puts People First
sources.claim: Hello Robot's Stretch, the leading assistive mobile manipulator piloted with people with severe mobility impairment, performs fetching tasks under user control from a phone app rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as the state of the art for in-situ assistive manipulation near a disabled person; because it is operator-driven it cannot support positive judgments for device set-up, personal care, or transfers.

sources.title: 2A2-U06 Development of High-functionality Nursing-care Assistant Robot ROBEAR for Patient-transfer and Standing Assistance
sources.claim: ROBEAR, the best-known patient-transfer robot, remains a laboratory prototype evaluated in experiments on lifting a person between bed and wheelchair; no autonomous deployed transfer robot exists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a person. Cited to show the capability exists only as an operator-guided prototype, so it cannot support the transfer/positioning or restroom instances at any tier.

tasks.label: Instruct students in daily living skills required for independent maintenance and self-sufficiency, such as hygiene, safety, or food preparation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hygiene/self-care routine instruction embedded in the school day: teaching handwashing, toothbrushing, nose-blowing, toileting and grooming at the classroom sink or school restroom to elementary students with intellectual, autism-spectrum or physical disabilities; teacher models the steps, uses a prompting hierarchy including hand-over-hand physical guidance, fades prompts, manages resistance or behavior, cleans up, and records IEP data.

Food-preparation lesson in a classroom life-skills kitchen or on a rolling cart: making a snack or simple meal (spreading, pouring, using a microwave/toaster, an adapted knife, measuring), with the teacher setting up materials, demonstrating each step, physically guiding small hands, enforcing safety around heat and blades for 2-6 students at once, and running clean-up.

Safety instruction in the classroom and school building: lessons and role-play on fire/tornado drills, stranger safety, poison and medicine safety, playground and bus safety, using visuals, social stories and practice; teacher adapts pacing and communication mode (sign, AAC, braille), redirects behavior, and checks comprehension of each student.

Dressing and personal-management instruction woven into daily transitions: coats, zippers, buttons, shoes, backpack and lunch-tray handling in the classroom, cubby area and cafeteria; teacher provides graduated physical assistance, positions students with motor impairments, and prompts independence while the rest of the group is in motion.

Community-based instruction outing with a small group: walking on public sidewalks and crossing streets safely, buying a snack item at a nearby grocery store, ordering at a counter; teacher supervises safety in traffic and crowds, cues each step of the routine, and manages unexpected behavior in an uncontrolled public setting.

sources.title: The School District of Manatee County Becomes First in Florida to Adopt RoboKind's Robot and Social-Emotional Curriculum for Students with Autism
sources.claim: RoboKind's Milo humanoid is commercially adopted by US school districts and delivers verbal social-emotional/social-skills lessons to students with autism in group or one-to-one sessions, but it works alongside educators, does not manipulate objects, and its curriculum is social-emotional rather than hygiene, dressing or food preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available system to robot-delivered instruction of children with disabilities in an elementary school; cited to show that even the most mature school deployment covers verbal social-emotional lesson delivery beside a teacher, not hands-on daily-living-skills instruction.

sources.developer: University of Glasgow / Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham
sources.title: Handwashing robot helps schoolkids make a clean break with bad habits
sources.claim: The Pepe handwashing robot, the best-known school hygiene-teaching robot, was wall-mounted over a primary school handwashing station but was tele-operated by researchers to speak to pupils and point them to a poster; it provided no physical guidance and supplemented rather than replaced teachers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly targets hygiene instruction to primary-school children, the closest match to the hygiene instance; cited to show the demonstration was teleoperated and non-manipulative.

sources.developer: multiple (Frontiers in Robotics and AI review)
sources.title: Social robots: a meta-analysis of learning outcomes
sources.claim: A 2025 meta-analysis of social robots for learning notes that the evidence base includes studies where the robot served only as an assistant to a human teacher and studies where the robot was controlled by a human operator (Wizard-of-Oz), indicating that classroom teaching robots generally are not autonomous instructors.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the general literature on robots delivering instruction to learners; establishes that reported teaching performance frequently depends on human operators or a supervising teacher, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of instructional instances.

sources.title: Helping children with autism understand the world with Kaspar the social robot
sources.claim: Kaspar, a humanoid used in specialist schools for children with autism and learning difficulties, is positioned as an educational companion used within a school partnership rather than as an autonomous teacher of self-care or life skills.
sources.transferJustification: Special-school robot working with the same student population; shows the role is companion/prompt delivery in research partnerships, not autonomous whole-lesson instruction with physical prompting.

sources.title: Figure AI's Helix 02 Completes 4-Minute Autonomous Kitchen Task, Setting New Humanoid Robotics Benchmark
sources.claim: Frontier humanoid manipulation in a kitchen reached a four-minute fully autonomous dishwasher-loading task in January 2026, demonstrating object handling in a human kitchen but nothing resembling supervising or teaching a child through a cooking routine.
sources.transferJustification: Kitchen manipulation is the physical component nearest to the food-preparation instance; cited to bound the state of the art — a short scripted-scope autonomous chore demo, with no capability for co-active instruction, physical prompting of a child, or safety supervision.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Confer with other staff members to plan or schedule lessons promoting learning, following approved curricula.
