tasks.label: Maintain inventory of instructional equipment, materials, or aids.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic physical count/audit of the adapted PE equipment inventory in a school gym or storage room: open bins and count loose items (bean bags, spot markers, adapted balls), verify large items (scooter boards, balance beams, bolsters, adapted bats) on shelves, hooks and floor stacks, note missing or misplaced items, and reconcile against the district equipment list.

Routine put-away and restock after lessons: gather cones, hoops, therapy balls, scooter boards, weighted vests, resistance bands from the gym/multipurpose room floor and carts, return each to its labeled bin, rack or shelf in the storeroom, and note consumables or items running low.

Safety inspection and upkeep of equipment: check ball inflation and inflate as needed, inspect straps/harnesses on gait trainers and adapted trikes, check mats and switches for tears or wear, clean/sanitize shared and mouth-contact items, tag or pull damaged items from circulation and log repair/replacement needs.

Receiving new orders in the school storeroom: unbox deliveries of adapted equipment and materials, check contents against the packing slip, apply district asset tags/labels, enter items in the inventory system, and shelve them in the correct location.

Itinerant caseload logistics: assemble and replenish the traveling kit of equipment carried between two or more school sites, verify kit contents against a checklist, load/unload the cart or vehicle, and track which items are on loan to classroom teachers, therapists or families.

sources.title: Independent US grocer Harmons deploys Simbe Tally inventory robot across 17 of its locations
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally is an autonomous shelf-scanning inventory robot commercially deployed in grocery stores, capturing shelf-level data on product availability and placement — autonomous inventory auditing inside a facility built for people, but keyed to barcoded/planogrammed retail shelving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory auditing. It is the same act as an equipment count — traverse aisles, identify stock, report discrepancies — and shows what autonomous counting requires (labelled, uniformly shelved goods), which is why it does not carry to unlabelled gym equipment in bins and on hooks.

sources.title: AuRoSS: An Autonomous Robotic Shelf Scanning system (IEEE)
sources.claim: AuRoSS, an autonomous RFID shelf-scanning robot used in Singapore public libraries, navigates stacks and generates reports of missing and misplaced items — autonomous inventory reconciliation of instructional materials in an institutional facility, but only for RFID-tagged items neatly shelved in rows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: library shelf-reading/inventory of instructional materials. Same output (count plus missing/misplaced report) for a school-like institution, showing tagged, row-shelved items are the precondition — not met by loose adapted PE gear in bins.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sequoia containerized storage system uses mobile robots, gantries and robotic arms to identify and store received inventory in fulfillment centers, maintaining item-level inventory records — inventory identification and put-away performed with the work containerized and brought to purpose-built machinery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse receive/stow and inventory identification. It is the machine-side equivalent of counting, tagging and shelving instructional equipment: each item is identified, recorded and placed in a known location, with the work presented to the machine.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Piece-Picking System for Warehouse Order Fulfillment
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick 4 autonomously picks and places diverse items, including items it has never seen ..., at fixed robotic workstations in warehouses — item-level sortation into totes/containers with minimal human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse piece-picking/sortation. Sorting presented items into designated bins is the machine analogue of returning equipment to its labelled bin and of picking a kit list, with comparable object variety when items are presented in totes.

sources.title: DHL Supply Chain Achieves First Commercial Deployment of Boston Dynamics' Stretch Robot to Unload Trailers and Containers in the Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads mixed stacks of cases from trailers and containers onto conveyors at DHL sites, handling recovery from fallen boxes; DHL had ten units deployed for case unloading across ... by mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving/unloading incoming shipments. Cartons of ordered equipment arriving at a dock are the same objects and the same act (take cases off a delivery, place for downstream put-away) as receiving an equipment order, when presented at a purpose-built dock.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid has moved more than 100,000 ... a GXO warehouse, autonomously picking totes on and off mobile robots, loading conveyors and stacking containers within an engineered workflow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: container handling and staging for transport. Moving and stacking totes of stock is the machine equivalent of loading a containerized equipment kit onto a cart, but only within a purpose-built, mapped workflow.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks beverage shelves in FamilyMart convenience stores, running under its GORDON AI in normal operation with rare remote human takeover — autonomous shelf replenishment of uniform items from a fixed installation inside a human retail facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking. Placing stock into known shelf positions is the same act as returning equipment to labelled bins, but the demonstrated system is a fixed arm handling uniform bottles/cans, not a mobile robot handling assorted gear.

sources.title: Tennibot – The Ultimate Robotic Tennis Ball Collector
sources.claim: Tennibot is a commercially sold autonomous robot that detects and collects tennis balls on a court while avoiding people — the only fielded example of autonomous collection of sports equipment from a playing surface, and it handles only balls.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: post-activity collection of loose sports equipment on an institution-controlled court. It shows the scope of what is fielded at E2 — one object class into an onboard hopper — not the multi-object gather-and-shelve work of a PE storeroom.

instances.label: Copy room of an adult-education center or community college shortly before class: instructor pulls a master worksheet/reading packet, runs 15-30 copies on the shared copier, collates, staples or three-hole-punches the sets, and stacks them by class section.

Prep/workroom: making hands-on ESL materials - printing and cutting picture/vocabulary flashcards and cut-up sentence strips, laminating them, sorting the pieces into envelopes or bags, one set per small group.

Classroom in a school, library or college building 10-20 minutes before class: moving tables and stackable chairs from rows into small-group clusters, a U-shape or a conversation circle for the day's activity, and often restoring the layout afterward for the next tenant.

Same classroom: writing the agenda/objectives and vocabulary on the whiteboard, putting a handout packet, name tent, dictionary or manipulative at each seat, taping up chart paper/word walls, laying out realia at learning stations.

Setting up instructional technology: placing and powering the laptop, plugging HDMI/USB-C and power into a projector or wall TV, connecting speakers or a document camera, lowering the screen, logging in and cueing audio/video, or booting and logging in the computer-lab stations.

Off-site / itinerant class (workplace ESL, church basement, shelter, union hall, jail classroom): hauling in a rolling bag of materials, taking the room as found, clearing and rearranging whatever furniture is there, setting up a portable board or projector, then breaking it all down.

sources.title: Duplo System 5000 Bookletmaker | Fingerprint Digital
sources.claim: Commercial collating/booklet-making finishing systems take printed sheets and automatically produce collated, stitched document sets at production volumes - the same physical output as a teacher's stapled handout packets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: print-shop production of collated, stitched document sets. Same objects (loose printed sheets), same accepted output (a correctly ordered, fastened set), and school-district print shops in fact produce teacher packets this way.

sources.claim: Inline production booklet-making runs from the digital press through fold/stitch/trim to a stacker with little or no operator ... - unattended machine-controlled production of finished document sets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended print finishing. It substantiates that once the job is presented in the purpose-built line, sheet handling, ordering and fastening complete under machine control without step-by-step human command.

sources.title: Duplo DC-618 Slitter Cutter Creaser | All-in-One Print Finishing
sources.claim: A fully automated slitter/cutter/creaser converts printed sheets into finished cards (business cards, greeting cards, tickets) in a single pass, self-setting from barcode and register marks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated card production. Flashcards and sentence strips are printed card stock cut to size; the machine handles the same media, the same cutting precision and the same set-based output.

sources.system: Automatic cut-sheet laminators (Foliant; MultiLam Burst Auto)
sources.title: Commercial Laminating Machines | Foliant Dealer Michigan | Mid-State Litho
sources.claim: Automatic laminating machines feed, laminate, ... as standard daily production equipment in print rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production lamination of cut sheets. Teachers laminate the same media for durable flashcards; auto-feed, trim and sheet separation cover the steps the instructor otherwise does by hand.

sources.system: ALORE (legged manipulator with hierarchical RL whole-body controller and TAMP planner)
sources.developer: HKUST (Guangzhou) - Bi, Zhang, Chen, Zhao, Li, Ma
sources.title: ALORE: Autonomous Large-Object Rearrangement with a Legged Manipulator
sources.claim: A legged manipulator autonomously rearranged large furniture - chairs, tables and bins - to target positions and orientations, including 32 chairs in 8 continuous loops over ~40 minutes with no failures and a ~40 m transport route.

sources.system: Ori robotic furniture (Pocket Closet / Cloud Bed)
sources.date: 2019 rollout into apartment buildings; product still sold
sources.title: Ori Systems' robotic furniture system transforms apartment living | New Atlas
sources.claim: Commercially installed robotic furniture reconfigures a room's layout under machine control, moving a full wall/closet unit across the room on a powered rail at the touch of a ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: changing a room's furniture layout on command. It shows that where the room is built around the machine (rails, known unit, designated end positions), furniture-scale layout changes complete under machine control - the E1 form of classroom furniture setup.

sources.title: Hyster trucks to use Rocsys robotic charging
sources.claim: Vision-guided robotic arms autonomously find a vehicle inlet and insert a heavy charging connector; deployed for hands-free charging of electric terminal tractors at a container terminal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connector insertion into a socket whose pose must be found by vision. Cited only as partial coverage of AV cabling - it does not cover powering, source selection, image/audio verification or login.

sources.title: Figure AI humanoids sort 28,000 packages in 24-hour autonomous test
sources.claim: The frontier of autonomous humanoid work inside a human work facility is a fixed station doing one repetitive handling motion - picking packages and placing them barcode-down on a conveyor over a 24-hour run.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to characterise the state of the art for autonomous humanoid manipulation inside a work facility: a single fixtured station task rather than multi-step room preparation, which is why the E2 judgments here are negative.

instances.label: Start-of-term textbook/workbook issue: ABE/ESL instructor picks level-appropriate titles from the program's approved list, submits a requisition, then carries boxes from the program storage room to the classroom, hands the right title/level to each of 15-25 adult learners, logs each copy on a sign-out roster, swaps damaged copies mid-term and collects books at term end. Setting: classroom in an adult education center or community college.

Routine classroom consumables: instructor orders pencils, notebooks, folders, dictionaries, dry-erase markers, copy paper through a district/office-supply portal or coordinator; receives and opens delivered cartons, stocks the classroom cabinet, and hands items out to individual students during class as needed. Setting: adult education center classroom and supply room.

Duplicated handout/worksheet packets for a unit: instructor selects pages from workbooks and curriculum files, copies/collates/staples sets at the staff workroom copier, sorts them into level-specific piles, and distributes the correct packet to each seated student at class start. Setting: staff workroom plus classroom.

Project and loaned-equipment issue: instructor orders and assembles per-student kits or equipment for a project or workforce unit (calculators, Chromebooks, hotspots, USB drives, chart paper, lab or craft items), checks each item out to a named student, then collects, inspects and inventories returns at the end. Setting: adult education classroom/resource room.

Off-site community class: ESL/ABE class held in a church hall, workplace break room, shelter, library meeting room or apartment community room; instructor loads bins of books and supplies into a car, transports them, sets them out on whatever tables exist, issues materials to students, then repacks and removes everything after class. Setting varies site to site and is not kept to any working standard.

sources.system: D-Tech LendIT / EnvisionWare 24-Hour Library automated library kiosks
sources.date: 2019-06 (product line in continued library deployment through 2025)
sources.title: All-Hours Access | American Libraries Magazine
sources.claim: D-Tech LendIT / EnvisionWare 24-Hour Library automated lending kiosks issue physical books and media to card holders and record the loan automatically; an onboard robot places loaded items into the machine's slots and returns are auto-checked-in. This is machine-controlled issuing of books with circulation tracking, in a purpose-built dispensing enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated library lending. Transfers because the objects are the same class of item (books/media of textbook size), the required precision is item-level retrieval and hand-over to a named borrower, and the output — the right item issued to the right person with a recorded loan — is the same output the instructor produces when issuing course texts.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout – GeekWire
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and picks individual products out of mixed totes and places them into trays inside fulfillment centers, covering a large share of Amazon's item catalog (which includes books and school/office supplies).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking in order fulfillment. Transfers to selecting and assembling course materials because the items (books, notebooks, pens, calculators) are the same everyday retail objects, the placement precision required is tote-to-tray, and the work is presented fixtured on conveyors — the E1 presentation.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics (deployed by DHL Supply Chain)
sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trailers and containers at DHL sites, identifying boxes with computer vision without pre-programming; 10 units were in commercial service across three countries as of June 2025 at roughly 700 cases per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: receiving and unloading cartons. Transfers to the receiving half of this task (cartons of textbooks and supplies arriving on a pallet or truck) — same box sizes and weights, same destacking motion — but only where the load is presented to the machine at a dock, not carried through a school building.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously fetches and delivers supplies and medications inside hospitals, deployed at more than 25 ... with over one million deliveries including ... and 100,000+ autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply delivery. Shows autonomous point-to-point transport of supplies in a structured human facility (E2), but the hand-off is a secured bin that a staff member unloads — it does not pick, match and issue individual items to each of a room of recipients.

sources.title: The SmartStore Vending Program – Industrial Vending for the Masses (Fastenal)
sources.claim: Fastenal's FAST Solutions industrial vending machines (SmartStore) dispense consumable supplies to workers at the point of use under machine control, with badge-logged issuance and consumption-driven replenishment ordering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-of-use supply issuance with automatic reordering. Transfers to issuing classroom consumables (pens, notebooks, markers) because the items are comparable small goods, issuance is per-person and logged, and reorder is triggered by recorded usage — the 'order and issue' output. The stock sits in fixtured coils/slots, i.e. an E1 presentation.

sources.title: Library Automation Solutions | Lyngsoe Library Systems
sources.claim: Lyngsoe library automated materials handling systems check items in at RFID kiosks and mechanically route each item to a designated bin, trolley or cart, sorting printed materials into destination sets without manual handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sorting of books and printed items. Transfers to sorting course materials/packets into level-specific sets: identical media, item-level identification and routing, in a purpose-built conveyor-and-bin machine.

sources.system: BG Robotic Product Sortation / robotic each picking
sources.title: Berkshire Grey Introduces Next Generation Robotic Product Sortation Solution for Scalable, Touchless Order Fulfillment
sources.claim: Berkshire Grey's robotic each-picking and product-sortation systems autonomously pick, sort and pack individual items into outbound order ... operator interaction, i.e. machine assembly of per-order sets of mixed consumer goods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic kitting/order assembly. Transfers to assembling per-student project kits (calculator, notebook, handouts, USB drive) — same object classes, same requirement that each container hold a specified item set — provided goods are presented to the cell in totes.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocking robot was deployed to hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores to autonomously restock beverage shelves, operating in the store's fixed-geometry back cooler with remote human assistance for the small fraction of failed picks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking inside a human retail facility. Shows machine stocking only for uniform products on fixed, known shelf geometry served from a dedicated back-of-cooler rail; it does not open mixed shipping cartons of assorted school supplies or stock arbitrary classroom cabinets.

sources.system: imageRUNNER ADVANCE multifunction printers with finishers; Xerox Production Ready Booklet Maker Finisher
sources.title: Finishing - Canon imageRUNNER ADVANCE C5255/C5250 user manual
sources.claim: Standard office multifunction copiers automatically collate multi-page copy sets, and production finishers automatically staple and bind them, producing finished document sets from a loaded original and paper trays under machine control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated document reproduction and finishing. Transfers to producing worksheet/workbook packets: the paper is presented fixtured in feeders and trays, and the accepted output — collated, stapled, level-specific sets — is exactly what the instructor produces at the workroom copier.

instances.label: Adult ed / community-college ABE or ESL classroom: instructor retrieves an assistive item from a cabinet or AT cart — large-print or braille handouts, a handheld or video magnifier, an FM/assistive-listening receiver, a laptop or tablet loaded with text-to-speech — carries it across the room and hands it to the student at their seat before or during class.

Same classroom: instructor sets up and configures the supportive technology for the individual student — plugs in and boots the device, launches and adjusts a screen reader, speech-to-text or magnification settings, fits the headset/FM receiver on the student, angles the monitor or magnifier, and troubleshoots when the device fails mid-lesson.

Institution-controlled building (adult learning center, community college, library classroom wing): instructor escorts a student who uses a wheelchair, walker or cane from the classroom down the corridor to the accessible restroom or elevator — clearing the path, pushing or steadying the chair, holding doors, waiting, and escorting back — without personal-care contact.

Hands-on personal support at the restroom or in the classroom: steadying a student during a transfer or at the stall door, supporting an unsteady student's weight, helping a student who has slipped or fallen, repositioning a student in a chair.

Instructor acts as sighted guide for a blind or low-vision student through the facility — walking them to the restroom, testing room or exit, warning of obstacles and door swings, and orienting them to the room layout.

Off-site community adult-education site (church hall, shelter, union hall, workplace, family-literacy room) taken as found: instructor helps the student with a mobility or vision impairment get in the door, over a threshold or step, down an unmarked hall past stacked chairs to whatever restroom is usable, and back.

sources.title: Meet Moxi: Why We Invested in Diligent Robotics — Diligent Robotics
sources.claim: Moxi, an autonomous mobile manipulator, travels to a location inside a hospital, picks up supplies or medications, and delivers them elsewhere in the building — the same fetch-and-hand-over pattern as issuing an assistive device to a student in a classroom.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply delivery. Objects (small kits, pouches, tablets/boxes) and precision are comparable to handing a magnifier, headset or tablet to a person; both occur in a people-occupied institutional building with a human taking the item from the robot.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi's deployment scale and autonomy: nearly 100 robots in 25+ US hospitals with over 1.25 million autonomous deliveries completed, operating alongside people.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Moxi uses its arm to open doors and press elevator buttons autonomously while moving through occupied hospital corridors, having logged 110,000 autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: door and elevator operation en route to a delivery. It substantiates the door-holding/elevator-calling element of escorting a student to a restroom inside an institutional building.

sources.title: RELAY ROBOTICS Secures $10 Million Financing
sources.claim: Relay delivery robots operate fully autonomously in hotels and healthcare buildings, riding elevators on their own and bringing items to a person's location, with over a million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item delivery to a person inside a human-occupied facility. Comparable payloads (small devices, printed materials) and the recipient takes the item from the robot, matching hand-off of an assistive device.

sources.title: Unifi Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport

sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a mobility-impaired person through a facility. Same output as a teacher walking a student to the restroom — the person is conveyed safely to a chosen destination inside an institution-controlled building among pedestrians.

sources.title: How Autonomous Wheelchairs Work | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous wheelchair routing inside airports is planned around destinations such as restrooms, using pre-scanned facility maps and existing infrastructure without layout modification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conveying a person to a restroom inside a large public building, which is exactly the facility-access assistance the instructor provides.

tasks.label: Instruct students individually and in groups, using various teaching methods, such as lectures, discussions, and demonstrations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Group hands-on studio class (pottery, painting, jewelry, sewing, cooking) of 8-15 adults at a community art center, craft studio or teaching kitchen: instructor demonstrates the technique live with real tools and materials at a demo station, then circulates, inspects each student's in-progress work, gives individual verbal and hands-on correction (grip, pressure, tool angle), and re-paces the lesson for mixed skill levels.

One-on-one lesson (piano, guitar, violin, drawing) of 30-60 minutes given in the teacher's home studio or at the student's house: the teacher plays/draws the passage as a model, listens to or watches the student attempt it, diagnoses errors by ear and eye, physically adjusts posture and hand position, and improvises new exercises on the spot.

Group lecture-and-discussion class for adults (conversational language, local history, personal finance, computer skills, book discussion) in a library, community-center or adult-ed classroom: present material with board or slides, pose questions, facilitate discussion, answer unpredictable questions, and manage a group of 10-25 learners for 60-90 minutes.

Recreational movement or performance class (social/ballroom dance, kids' movement, martial arts for enrichment, improv/theater) in a dance or activity studio: demonstrate sequences at speed and broken down, mirror the class, cue music, watch bodies and correct alignment individually, and adapt the routine to the group's ability.

Off-site or outdoor enrichment session (gardening workshop in a community garden, urban sketching outing, nature photography or birdwatching walk): demonstrate technique in situ with tools or cameras, lead the group over uneven ground and through changing weather, and give improvised individual coaching on whatever the site presents.

sources.system: Social robots for education (NAO, Pepper and similar platforms), Belpaeme et al. review
sources.developer: University of Plymouth / Ghent University, Yale, University of Tsukuba
sources.title: Robots will never replace teachers but can boost children's education | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed review of 100+ studies of social robots (NAO-class) in education concludes robots are effective only on narrow topics and that technical limits confine them to teaching-assistant/tutor roles rather than leading instruction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is classroom instruction of students by a robot; it is the same activity (instructing individuals and groups with lectures, discussion and demonstration), so the finding that robots cannot carry the instructional role transfers directly to self-enrichment teaching.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is instructing students in a classroom, the same activity as this task; the robot's scope is limited to supporting activities and homework help alongside a human teacher, showing no system takes over lesson delivery.

sources.system: Generative AI-powered social robots in education (expert Delphi assessment)

sources.transferJustification: Related task is robot-delivered teaching; the panel's assessment concerns exactly the substitution of a robot for the instructing worker, which is what this task requires.

sources.claim: Global survey of real-world social-robot deployments in education finds persistent technical barriers in social-cue interpretation and speech recognition, with robots used to support rather than conduct teaching.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is social-robot instruction in schools; the deployments surveyed are the closest real-world analogue to a robot instructing self-enrichment learners, and they remain support tools under human teachers.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is supervising an individual music-practice session, the nearest robotic analogue to a one-on-one music lesson; it shows the state of the art stops at motivational prompting and does not reach modelling, diagnosing and correcting technique.

instances.label: Art/craft/hobby class in an already-furnished community-center, school, or studio room: teacher lays out per-seat material sets (paper, paints, brushes, glue, scissors, clay balls, kit bags), fills water cups, distributes handouts and name tags, puts sample pieces on each table.

Full room reconfiguration just before class: move and group tables and chairs into the needed layout, clear floor and shelves, cover surfaces with paper or cloth, hang displays/reference sheets, wheel out easel or cart, connect and test laptop/projector and screen.

Advance bulk materials preparation in a prep room, storeroom, or the teacher's own workspace: photocopy and collate handout packets, assemble 12-25 identical student kits into bags/trays, pre-cut paper, fabric, or wood pieces, portion clay and paint into cups, label everything.

Teaching-kitchen mise en place for a cooking, baking, or wine class: portion ingredients into per-station bowls and trays, stage knives, boards, bowls and measuring tools at each station, preheat ovens/stovetops, sanitize counters, plate a demo example.

Movement or music class setup in a studio, rec-center gym, or band room: clear and mop the floor, lay out mats, blocks, straps or apparatus at spacing, arrange chairs and music stands in a formation, distribute sheet music and percussion, set up and test the sound system, amps, and lighting.

Off-site class setup in a space taken as found: private home, rented hall, church basement, park, garden plot, or campsite. Teacher unloads gear from a car, sets up folding tables and portable equipment, and improvises a layout around whatever furniture, terrain, and power are available.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout – GeekWire
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks individual, highly varied consumer products out of source containers and places them into specific totes inside a fenced/protective structure in fulfillment centers — the same operation as assembling per-student material sets from bulk supplies in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level order picking/kitting. Transfers to preparing class material sets because the objects (small, mixed, non-uniform consumer goods) and the required precision (place each item into a designated tray/tote position) match, and both are done from presented bins in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Danfoss kitting cell with Roboception rc_visard 3D vision
sources.title: Case Studies: Automated Kitting Solution with 3D Robot Vision | Roboception GmbH
sources.claim: A production kitting cell at Danfoss Drives uses a vision-guided robot to assemble assortments of different parts picked from supplier pallets into different trays, with 3D vision handling shifted/tilted pallet contents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial kitting. Assembling a tray of mixed parts is the same operation as assembling a student supply kit or a per-seat material tray: mixed small items, modest placement precision, work presented in bins/pallets inside a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Breaking: Chef Robotics raises $43m Series A to scale AI-enabled robotics in meal assembly
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI meal-assembly arms autonomously portion and place multiple ingredients with ... and tray positions on conveyors, deployed commercially across more than a dozen food production facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production meal assembly. Portioning deformable, variable food ingredients into designated tray compartments is the same physical operation as mise en place for a cooking class (measured ingredient portions staged per station), at comparable precision, in a fixtured line.

sources.title: AI-powered robot enhances meal assembly in food manufacturing
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' meal assembly system adapts to variable ingredient types in real time using a three-camera vision system that tracks conveyor speed and trays for ..., and holds NSF certification for food-contact use.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: substantiates that portioning of variable ingredients into presented trays is autonomous and production-grade, not a scripted demo.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in 25+ US hospitals and has completed over 1.25 million autonomous ... of medications, lab samples, and supplies — the most mature mobile manipulation in a structured human facility, but limited to fetching and dropping off closed payloads, not arranging rooms or laying out materials at seats.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound E2 capability: the leading commercial mobile manipulator in an institution-controlled building performs point-to-point item transport, which does not cover furniture layout, AV setup, or per-seat material placement.

sources.title: Figure Humanoid Robots Sort Packages Non-Stop in 24/7 Demo
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 humanoids ran multi-hour fully autonomous shifts sorting tens of thousands of packages at a warehouse station, showing endurance and reliability only for a single repetitive, station-bound manipulation task in a logistics facility.
sources.transferJustification: Cited to bound humanoid capability as of mid-2026: sustained autonomy exists for one fixed, repetitive handling task at a prepared station, not for open-ended multi-step room preparation.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 can direct a mobile manipulator to tidy a kitchen or bedroom in homes not seen in training, but this is a research model performing coarse cleanup, not reliable worker-quality setup of a space.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying in unseen spaces. Nearest evidence for arranging a found space, but it is a research demonstration with partial task success, so it does not support worker-quality completion of class setup at E3 or E2.

sources.title: 1X Neo Home Robot Teleoperation Today, Autonomy Tomorrow
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading consumer robot for unstructured homes, relied on remote human pilots for the manipulation tasks demonstrated to press, with autonomy limited to simple actions.
sources.transferJustification: Cited as negative evidence for E3: setup work in homes and other found spaces is currently done by teleoperation, which cannot support a positive judgment.

Recreational cooking or baking class in a teaching kitchen: instructor plans the menu and mise en place, demonstrates knife skills and technique at a demo station, then students work at stations while the instructor moves between them, tastes, corrects timing and heat, enforces safety, and fields questions.

Private or small-group music lesson (guitar, piano, voice) in a music-school studio: instructor plans progression, demonstrates passages on the instrument, models posture and fingering, listens and corrects in real time, and supervises in-lesson practice.

Discussion/lecture-style adult enrichment class (conversational language, personal finance, local history, computer skills) in a community-college classroom or library meeting room: instructor plans the lesson, presents material, runs paired or small-group activities at tables, and fields open questions.

Children's hands-on enrichment program (nature/garden club, STEM-build session, summer camp activity) run at a park, garden, nature center, or school yard: instructor plans and sets out the activity, demonstrates, then supervises 10-20 children exploring, building, and investigating outdoors, managing safety and behavior.

sources.developer: L2TOR consortium (Tilburg/Utrecht/Plymouth); robot by SoftBank Robotics
sources.title: Second Language Tutoring Using Social Robots: A Large-Scale Study
sources.claim: A NAO social robot acted as a (nearly) autonomous tutor delivering a series of seven pre-designed English-vocabulary lessons one-on-one to preschool children in schools; learning gains matched a tablet app rather than exceeding it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered tutoring lessons. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to conducting a program of instruction, but lessons are pre-authored, one-on-one and screen-mediated, with no physical demonstration using materials and no supervision of student work time, so it does not transfer to conducting an enrichment class.

sources.claim: A humanoid robot plus AI avatar was deployed in a US school district in a supporting teacher's-assistant and engagement role alongside human teachers, not as the instructor conducting a class.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: classroom instructional support. The unit is a stationary conversational humanoid used for engagement; it does not plan and run sessions, demonstrate manual technique, or supervise hands-on work, so it cannot stand in for the teacher conducting the class.

sources.system: Pepper robot activity sessions in long-term care facilities
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics (pilot study by long-term care researchers)
sources.title: Promoting activity in long-term care facilities with the social robot Pepper: a pilot study
sources.claim: Attempts to have a social robot lead structured group activity sessions inside institutional care facilities still depend on human operator control rather than autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading a structured group activity session for an audience inside an institution, the closest analogue to conducting a group class. It remains Wizard-of-Oz operated, which under the autonomy rule cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: FRIDA's robotic arm using AI models to paint pictures ows its name also to Frida Kahlo
sources.claim: A robot arm can autonomously execute a painting from a supplied image or prompt, but a human selects canvas and palette and the robot provides no instruction, feedback, or supervision of learners.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing the art-making act an instructor would demonstrate. It covers only the manual sub-step under human-specified parameters; it does not narrate technique, answer questions, or critique student work, so it does not complete the instance.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: culinary manipulation of the kind a cooking-class demonstration requires. Autonomy is unestablished and the demo involves no students, no teaching sequence, and no supervision of learners' stations, so it cannot substitute for conducting a cooking class.

instances.label: Lecture-style enrichment class (local history, personal finance, language, photography theory) in a community-center, library, senior-center or adult-ed classroom: teacher arrives early, wheels over or connects a laptop to the installed projector/TV by HDMI or wireless casting, powers the display, checks speaker volume, dims lights/closes blinds, opens the slide deck, then advances slides and cues short video/audio clips at the right moments through a 1-2 hour class, troubleshooting no-signal or sound problems live in front of students.

Hands-on studio or workshop class (watercolor, pottery, cake decorating, woodworking, floral design) in a craft studio or teaching kitchen: teacher lays out demonstration materials, tools and samples at each station, positions a document camera or tablet on a stand so a close-up of hands/technique projects to a screen, plays reference images or a technique video, hands out printed patterns/recipes, and swaps materials and re-cues media between steps while students work.

Private one-to-one enrichment lesson in a private home (piano/guitar teacher at the student's house or teaching in the teacher's own living-room studio): sets up a tablet or laptop with sheet-music apps, metronome and backing tracks, positions a small Bluetooth speaker and music stand, cues and pauses recordings during the lesson, occasionally records the student on a phone for playback, and handles accessories and printed music.

Online or hybrid enrichment class run from the teacher's home or a small studio: sets up laptop, webcam, ring light and microphone, mounts an overhead camera to show hands and materials, joins the video platform, shares screen, plays media, switches camera angles mid-class to show a demonstration, and fixes audio/video and connection problems as they arise.

One-off or off-site class in a borrowed venue room (museum classroom, hotel meeting room, church hall, cruise-ship lounge, park pavilion): teacher hauls in a portable projector, screen, powered speaker and laptop, finds outlets, runs an extension cord, improvises a table or cart, tests a microphone and sound in an unfamiliar room, then runs the media through the session and packs everything out afterward.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid + Optio AI teaching assistant
sources.title: US Firm's Humanoid Robot Teaching Assistant to Support 500 Students in 2026
sources.claim: The most advanced classroom-deployed humanoid in a US school district is a conversational, expressive upper-body robot used for face-to-face interaction and Q&A; nothing in the deployment involves setting up or operating classroom AV equipment, connecting laptops/projectors, or handling instructional materials.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot in the same setting (a school classroom, an E2 facility). It shows the state of the art for classroom robots is speech and social interaction, not operation of AV equipment or handling of teaching materials, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Figure AI, Agility Digit, Tesla Optimus, Unitree H1/G1 (industry review)
sources.title: Humanoid Robots in Industrial Manufacturing: What They Can (and Can't) Do in 2026
sources.claim: As of 2026 the best autonomous humanoid manipulation is confined to a narrow set of material-handling, bin-picking and simple assembly tasks at a handful of factory pilot sites; no general-purpose system is documented setting up or operating presentation equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general-purpose humanoid manipulation in industrial settings. Cited to bound the state of the art; the demonstrated repertoire (material handling, bin picking) does not include multi-step AV setup, computer operation, or live media cueing during a class.

sources.system: MIT CSAIL tactile cable-manipulation system (GelSight gripper on robot arm)

sources.claim: Autonomous insertion of an audio plug into a jack has been demonstrated only as a laboratory research result with a specialised tactile gripper on a fixtured arm — a single sub-step of AV setup, not a whole classroom AV instance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cable/connector insertion, a sub-step of connecting a laptop to a projector. It is a lab bench demonstration on a fixtured arm and covers only one motion, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole AV-supplementation instance.

Continuing-education classroom course (language, writing, local history) at a school, library, or college adult-ed program: instructor picks a textbook/workbook, places the order with a bookstore or vendor, prints handout packets, and issues books and packets to each enrolled student on the first night, tracking who received what.

Recreational cooking or baking class in a teaching kitchen: instructor chooses recipes, orders or shops for ingredients and small equipment, then portions ingredients and sets out per-student mise en place trays and tools at each workstation before class.

Independent instructor teaching at varied sites (private homes, rented church halls, parks, pop-up venues): buys supplies at a retail store, loads and transports them by car, unloads at the site, and distributes kits and tools to participants in whatever space is available.

Music, dance, or hobby studio: instructor selects and orders sheet music, method books, loaner instruments or equipment, then issues items to individual students from studio storage and logs the loans/returns.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously identifies and picks individual items of many types out of containers and places them into the correct order totes inside fulfillment centers - the same act as pulling selected books/supplies from stock and assembling per-recipient sets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: e-commerce order picking/kitting. Transfer holds because the objects (books, paper goods, small consumer items) and the required precision match 'issuing' course materials, and the act is selecting listed items from stock and grouping them per recipient.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Signs Multi-Year Agreement with Staples to Deploy AI-Powered Picking Robots in Fulfillment Centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick item-handling system is deployed commercially by Staples to automate autonomous piece-picking in office-supply fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking office/school supply SKUs to order. The item mix (pens, paper, notebooks, small kits) is essentially the supply list of a self-enrichment course, so picking and packing performance carries over to assembling and issuing course materials.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Piece-Picking System for Warehouse Order Fulfillment
sources.claim: The RightPick 4 generation is stated to enable autonomous piece-picking across verticals that explicitly include general merchandise and office supplies, with increased autonomy and reduced human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mixed-SKU piece picking. Craft, art, and classroom supplies fall inside the same object class (general merchandise/office supplies) and require no greater precision.

sources.system: Automated Storage and Retrieval System ('The Robot'), Miller Nichols Library

sources.claim: Academic library automated storage and retrieval systems use robotic cranes that, on an electronic request, locate the requested book and bring it to a pick-up station for the patron - a deployed, purpose-built book-issuing machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving and issuing requested books from stored stock. Objects (bound books) and the fetch-to-a-pickup-point workflow are the same as issuing course textbooks; only the surrounding structure differs.

sources.title: Chef Robotics and Packline Partner on End-to-End Meal Production Automation
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI food-assembly robots are deployed in food production facilities where they portion ingredients into moving trays, surpassing 100 million servings produced since first deployment at Amy's Kitchen in 2022.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning varied ingredients into individual trays on a line. This is the same physical act as setting out per-student mise en place portions for a cooking class, with comparable ingredient variety and portion precision.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator is deployed in 25-30+ US hospitals doing autonomous pharmacy, lab, and supply deliveries (1 million+ deliveries), but its work is transporting bagged/tote'd payloads point-to-point, not unpacking shipments or distributing individual items to people at tables.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply logistics in a structured human facility (E2). Cited to mark the ceiling of demonstrated E2 mobile manipulation: transport with limited single-arm grasping, short of stocking closets and issuing per-student materials.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid, the leading commercial humanoid deployment, has moved over 100,000 totes ... a GXO facility, handling totes on and off AMRs, loading conveyors, and stacking containers - i.e., coarse container handling, not distribution of individual small items to people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: humanoid material handling in a logistics facility. Cited to bound what deployed general-purpose robots do outside fixtured cells; the workflow is fixed tote routes, not selecting and issuing varied supplies in a classroom.

tasks.label: Conduct classes, workshops, and demonstrations, and provide individual instruction to teach topics and skills, such as cooking, dancing, writing, physical fitness, photography, personal finance, and flying.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Arts/crafts/hobby workshop at a community art center, rec center, or craft store studio (painting, pottery, jewelry, woodworking, floral): instructor demonstrates technique with tools and materials at the front, then circulates among 8-15 students, diagnosing problems in their work and giving hands-on correction, while managing tools, kilns, and cleanup.

Music, dance, or performing-arts group class or private lesson in a studio (guitar/piano, ballroom, ballet, drama): instructor demonstrates on the instrument or performs the steps, watches learners' posture, hand position, and timing, physically adjusts or partners with them, and adapts pacing to each learner.

Hands-on cooking or beverage workshop in a teaching kitchen at a community college, kitchen store, or cooking school: instructor demonstrates knife skills and a recipe at a demo station, then supervises students cooking at their own stations, correcting technique, enforcing food and knife safety, and troubleshooting dishes.

Knowledge/discussion enrichment class in a classroom, library meeting room, or continuing-ed room (creative writing, personal finance, language, genealogy, computer/smartphone literacy): instructor presents material, uses whiteboard/slides/handouts, facilitates discussion, critiques student work, and answers open-ended questions.

Outdoor or technical recreation instruction taken as found (photography walk downtown, gardening class in a plot, sailing/scuba, introductory flight lesson in a light aircraft): instructor demonstrates in situ, supervises learners on live equipment, adapts to weather and site conditions, and intervenes for safety.

Light exercise/recreation enrichment session in a senior center or adult day-care activity room: instructor leads seated stretching and simple movement routines, plus songs, quizzes, or games, for a seated group of older adults with facility staff present.

sources.title: News on Aging | ILC-Japan — The Future of the Robot-led Nursing Care
sources.claim: PALRO, a small humanoid from Fuji Soft, is used as the exercise instructor at a Yokohama adult day-care facility, leading the assembled group of older adults through spoken and gestured exercise routines each morning as part of the facility's program.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on task: PALRO conducts a recreation/exercise session for a group, the light-fitness variant of this teaching task.

sources.title: コミュニケーションロボット PALRO ビジネスシリーズ 高齢者福祉施設向けモデル（富士ソフト）
sources.claim: PALRO is sold commercially for eldercare facilities as recreation host and health-exercise instructor, running a day's recreation program (songs, quizzes, games, 10+ exercise routines) after a single spoken cue, in over 1,200 Japanese senior facilities.

sources.title: Humanoid robot makes test lecture at primary school in E.China, inspiring students to engage in 'deeper learning'
sources.claim: A 1.4 m humanoid 'Xiao An' delivered a trial science lesson at a Hefei primary school, but only as a teaching assistant working alongside the human teacher; the report does not establish autonomous conduct of the class.
sources.transferJustification: Closest analogue to conducting a knowledge-based class; shows current classroom humanoids assist a human teacher rather than conduct the session.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid ('Sally') with Optio AI assistant
sources.title: Salamanca Superintendent sets the record straight on AI-powered robot coming to the classroom
sources.claim: The Salamanca, NY school district's AI humanoid classroom robot is being introduced as an assistant, with the superintendent stating it will not replace human teachers.
sources.transferJustification: Most recent US classroom humanoid deployment; establishes the role is assistance, not conducting instruction.

sources.title: World's first robotic personal trainer guides gym-goers through exercise programme | UWE Bristol
sources.claim: A Pepper-based fitness coach prototype from Bristol Robotics Laboratory guides a single gym user through a treadmill programme with voice prompts and gestures, personalised to heart rate and mood; it is a research prototype, not a deployed class instructor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (one-on-one exercise coaching); cited to show the state of the art for robot instruction of physical skill is a single-user treadmill prototype, not class instruction.

sources.title: Miso and Roboworx Team to Deliver Comprehensive Restaurant Automation Solutions
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy Fry Station autonomously runs the frying process in commercial fast-food kitchens, installed in roughly 20 restaurant locations, showing autonomous food manipulation in a purpose-fitted kitchen but no instructional role.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (cooking) cited only to show that autonomous cooking manipulation exists in fixtured kitchens; it covers a sub-step and provides no demonstration, explanation, or supervision of students.

tasks.label: Instruct and monitor students in the use and care of equipment and materials to prevent injury and damage.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Arts/crafts class at a community arts center or studio (pottery, painting, jewelry, glass): teacher demonstrates safe handling of the wheel, kiln, cutters, torches, solvents and brushes on real materials, then circulates among 8-15 students, correcting grips, stopping unsafe actions (hand near a moving wheel, overloaded kiln shelf), and showing clean-up and tool-care routines at the end of the session.

Recreational cooking or baking class in a teaching kitchen (retail cooking school, rec center, community college): instructor demonstrates knife grip, mandoline guard, hot pans, mixers and ovens on real food, then monitors multiple stations for cuts and burns, physically intervening (moving a hand, turning off a burner) and showing washing and storage of equipment.

Private or small-group music lesson in a studio or school room: teacher shows how to hold, tune, assemble and clean the instrument (bow rosin, reed care, drum hardware, piano lid), watches the student's hands and posture, corrects grip physically, and checks that instruments and cases are handled and stored without damage.

Hobby woodworking, metal or makerspace class in a shop run by a community college or makerspace: mandatory safety orientation with hands-on demonstration of table saw, lathe, laser cutter and 3D printer including guards, push sticks, PPE and lockout; continuous floor supervision with authority to stop a machine or a student, plus teaching blade and bit care.

Outdoor or field recreational class (kayaking, sailing, horseback riding, gardening, fly casting): instructor fits and demonstrates gear (PFD, paddle, tack, hand tools), demonstrates rinsing and storage, and monitors participants spread over water, trail or plot under changing weather, intervening physically to prevent injury to people, animals or gear.

Class held in a non-dedicated space taken as found: a rented church hall, library room, pop-up craft workshop, or the teacher's or a student's home (sewing machines, hot glue guns, soldering irons, craft blades brought in for the day); teacher sets up the equipment, briefs on safe use, and supervises in a layout that changes every session.

sources.system: Realbotix M-Series humanoid + Optio AI teacher's assistant
sources.title: Realbotix to Deploy First Humanoid Robot and AI Teachers Assistant in U.S. School District
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid deployed into a US classroom to date is a conversational AI teacher's-assistant pilot; the robot supports interactive engagement and dialogue and shows no handling of tools, no demonstration of equipment use, and no physical supervision of students at equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered classroom instruction. Cited to bound the frontier - classroom robots interact by speech and screen and do not handle class equipment or supervise safety, so this cannot substantiate completion of the rated task.

sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics platform; study reported in arXiv:2508.05646
sources.title: A Humanoid Social Robot as a Teaching Assistant in the Classroom (arXiv:2508.05646)
sources.claim: A social humanoid robot linked to an LLM presented new learning content to high-school student groups in a research study; the platform is a stationary-torso speech agent and did not instruct in the handling of physical equipment or monitor students for hazards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot instruction of students in a classroom. Verbal content delivery does not transfer to demonstrating and supervising the physical use and care of tools and materials, so it supports no positive judgment here.

sources.system: Laboratory Safety Assistant (LSA) socially assistive robot framework
sources.title: Socially Assistive Robot as Laboratory Safety Assistant for Science Students (IEEE Xplore 10557826)
sources.claim: A research framework using a socially assistive robot detects student behaviors that could cause laboratory accidents (for example missing PPE) and issues reminders in a university teaching lab; it is a prototype, does not demonstrate equipment use, and cannot physically intervene.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: monitoring students to prevent injury and equipment damage during hands-on instruction. It is the closest match found, but it is a study-stage rule-compliance prompter with no tool demonstration, no physical intervention and no evidence of autonomous worker-quality supervision.

sources.system: LSA framework / socially assistive robot for science laboratories
sources.title: Social Robot Assistive Intervention for Science Students to Prevent Laboratory Accidents
sources.claim: A 2025 follow-on publication of the same socially assistive lab-safety concept frames the robot as an assistive intervention against student-caused injuries and asset damage in science labs, confirming the concept remains at research-intervention stage rather than deployed supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preventing student injury and equipment damage during hands-on instruction. Shows the state of the art in robotic student-safety supervision is a prompting prototype, far short of instructing in equipment use and care at worker quality.

instances.label: Cafeteria lunch duty in an elementary or middle school: the substitute watches 100+ students in a noisy lunchroom for 25-40 minutes, enforces seating and noise rules, opens milk cartons and packaging for young students, watches for allergy and choking risks, breaks up food-throwing and shoving, gets spills cleaned, dismisses tables and checks the area before the next lunch wave.

Outdoor recess/playground duty at an elementary school: the substitute patrols an open blacktop, field and play structure with 40-150 children in varying weather, keeps children inside boundaries and off unsafe equipment, mediates disputes and reports bullying, responds to falls, scrapes and nosebleeds and escorts an injured child to the nurse, then blows the whistle and lines the class up to return.

In-building transitions: escorting the class in a line to specials (gym, art, library), restroom and locker breaks, hallway/passing-period duty checking passes and moving students along, plus morning arrival and afternoon dismissal duty at the bus loop or car line, matching students to the correct bus or guardian.

Large-group supervision in gym, auditorium or media center: monitoring an assembly, pep rally, study hall or test overflow room; seating and counting students, keeping order and phones away, and leading the class out in order during a fire or lockdown drill with an accurate headcount.

Off-site field trip chaperoning: riding the bus with students, taking repeated headcounts, keeping an assigned small group together through a museum, zoo, park or theater, escorting restroom trips, supervising a bag lunch, handling a lost or ill child, and returning all students to the bus on schedule.

sources.system: Team 1st Technologies autonomous security robot (Santa Fe High School, New Mexico pilot)
sources.title: Autonomous Security Robots Are Starting to Patrol Schools and Cities, Despite Controversies - The Debrief
sources.claim: An autonomous security robot piloted at a US high school patrols the campus and streams 360-degree video to human security officers, and can approach and verbally warn suspicious persons, but supervisory judgment and any intervention remain with human officers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: security patrol inside a school. It is the closest fielded school-premises robot, but it only surveils and alerts humans; it does not manage student behavior, count or line up a class, help with food or equipment, or respond physically to an injured child, so it cannot substitute for a supervising adult at recess, lunch or transitions.

sources.system: Avatar robots in elementary classroom field trial
sources.title: Encouraging classroom activities for children using avatar robots: a field trial (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: A nine-day field trial placed avatar robots in a Japanese 5th-grade classroom where they interacted with children during lessons and recess; the robots were run continuously by multiple remote human operators rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot present among schoolchildren during class and recess, the same social setting as this task. It shows the state of the art for robot presence with children still depends on continuous human teleoperation, so it cannot support an autonomous positive judgment.

sources.developer: University of Pisa / Research Center E. Piaggio (Alter-Ego platform)
sources.title: Next-Gen Museum Guides: Autonomous Navigation and Visitor Interaction with an Agentic Robot (arXiv:2507.12273)
sources.claim: An autonomous guide robot navigated a real museum and led visitors along routes with LLM-based question answering, evaluated with 34 participants, with reported limitations in comprehension and responsiveness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading people through a public venue, the closest analog to shepherding a class on a field trip. It guides self-directed adult visitors along mapped routes; it does not take headcounts, keep children together, escort restroom trips or assume duty of care, so it does not carry over to chaperoning.
