tasks.label: Distribute or collect tests or homework assignments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Secondary classroom (grades 6-12), ~25-30 students at desks in rows: sub hands a counted stack of worksheets/quizzes to the first student in each row (or walks the rows placing one per desk), then at the bell collects papers passed forward, squares the stack, and leaves it on the regular teacher's desk with a note.

Elementary classroom (K-5), 20-25 young children at table groups: sub distributes worksheets or packets, sometimes pre-named sheets that must go to the right child, while children move about and desks/floor are cluttered with supplies and backpacks; finished work is gathered into a tray or turn-in folder.

Collecting homework at the start of a period: sub circulates among desks taking papers that students pull from folders, notebooks or backpacks (loose, crumpled, torn spiral edges), checks off who turned work in on the roster, and keeps the sets separated by class period.

Distributing and collecting devices and consumables: sub unlocks the Chromebook/tablet cart, hands out numbered devices (plus pencils, calculators, lab handouts) to each student, then collects them at the end, verifies the count, and re-docks each device in its charging slot.

Secure/standardized testing session: sub distributes numbered, barcoded test booklets and answer sheets to assigned seats per a seating chart, keeps materials secure during the session, then collects every booklet and answer sheet, reconciles counts against the roster, and returns the sealed materials to the test coordinator.

sources.title: Scaling Helix: a New State of the Art in Humanoid Logistics
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-controlled humanoids working at a customer logistics site autonomously singulate and place flat envelopes and deformable poly bags as reliably as rigid boxes, at ~4 seconds per item with ~95% correct label orientation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parcel singulation at a conveyor station. Flat paper envelopes are the closest commercial analogue to sheets of homework/test paper: the robot must separate one limp flat item from a presented supply, orient it, and place it accurately and repeatedly — the manipulation core of handing out and gathering paper in a purpose-built, fixtured setting.

sources.title: Watching This Humanoid Robot Sort Packages Is Quite Something
sources.claim: Independent trade coverage of the same deployment reports the Helix neural network running an hour of uninterrupted package handling, indicating sustained autonomous operation rather than scripted or teleoperated demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy and endurance for the flat-item handling evidence above, which is the transfer basis for paper distribution/collection at a fixtured station.

sources.system: Schmalz vacuum grippers / sheet-separation suction cups
sources.title: Vacuum grippers: definition, types & applications | Schmalz
sources.claim: Commercial vacuum end-of-arm tooling reliably separates a single sheet of paper or film from a stack for robotic pick-and-place, a standard industrial capability in print and packaging automation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: single-sheet destacking in printing/packaging cells. Distributing worksheets is fundamentally singulating one sheet at a time from a stack and placing it at a target position; this tooling does exactly that at industrial reliability when the stack is fixtured, i.e. under E1 presentation.

sources.title: BlueCrest Solutions | Ricoh USA
sources.claim: High-speed inserting systems select, collate and route specific printed sheets to specific named recipients at tens of thousands of pieces per hour with double-feed detection, in production mail facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: personalized document assembly and routing. 'Give the right paper to the right person' — including matching a named sheet to a named recipient and counting sets — is performed at far above worker reliability by these machines when sheets arrive fixtured in feeders, i.e. the E1 counterfactual of distribution.

sources.developer: King's College London / Monash University (Jiang, Zhang, Gomes, Do, Luo)
sources.title: RoTipBot: Robotic Handling of Thin and Flexible Objects using Rotatable Tactile Sensors
sources.claim: A robot with rotatable tactile fingertips counts layers of thin, flexible sheet-like objects and grasps a chosen number of them in a single closure, outperforming suction-only singulation in laboratory trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counting and separating thin flexible sheets. Handing out one paper per student and verifying counts on collection require exactly this count-and-singulate skill on limp paper-like material, demonstrated here in a bench (purpose-built) setup.

sources.title: Paper based exams | ePC
sources.claim: In university paper-exam workflows, machines accept and process stacks of completed answer sheets at high speed once the papers are presented to them, while human staff perform the room-level collection from candidates.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk exam-script intake. It substantiates that the collect-and-account-for-papers step is machine-executable once papers are presented at a station (E1), while confirming that the in-room gathering from seated examinees is still done by people (no E2 support).

sources.title: NCR Introduces a New Addition to its Family of Cash Recycling ATMs, the NCR SelfServ 63
sources.claim: Bulk-deposit self-service terminals accept loose stacks of banknotes and checks handed in by individual customers at a station, separating, counting and validating each sheet without an attendant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing sheets to, and accepting sheet stacks from, individual untrained members of the public at a purpose-built station. This is the closest deployed analogue to a paper hand-out/turn-in station and shows the person-facing exchange of paper can be machine-mediated when the machine defines the interface.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulators run item-delivery routes inside institutional buildings, but they transport supplies in enclosed bins/drawers between rooms rather than handing individual documents to each seated person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility delivery in a structured human facility (E2). Cited to bound what deployed E2 systems actually do — container transport between fixed points — which does not extend to per-student paper hand-out or desk-by-desk collection in an occupied classroom.

tasks.label: Distribute teaching materials, such as textbooks, workbooks, papers, and pencils, to students.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary (K-5) general classroom: sub hands a worksheet/handout to each of ~20-25 children seated at desks or table clusters, walking narrow aisles cluttered with backpacks and chairs while children move, reach, and talk; sometimes hands small stacks to table leaders to pass.

Secondary (6-12) classroom: sub retrieves the regular teacher's stack of handouts/answer sheets from the desk and passes them out to 25-30 seated teens at the start of the period, typically counting sheets per row and handing the row's stack to the front student.

Distributing supplies and durable materials: pencils, scissors, glue, rulers, calculators, art or lab materials, Chromebooks from a charging cart, or textbooks/workbooks pulled from classroom shelves and given to each student, sometimes recorded by number.

Name-matched distribution: returning graded papers or individually labeled packets to specific students, or handing out numbered test booklets and answer sheets under a testing protocol where each item must reach the right student and be accounted for.

Early-childhood or special-education/small-group setting: placing individualized, often adapted materials in front of each student at their workstation, adjusting to each student's IEP needs, prompting or hand-over-hand assistance, and managing students who mouth, throw, or refuse materials.

sources.title: Scaling Helix: a New State of the Art in Humanoid Logistics
sources.claim: Figure's Helix system autonomously picks and singulates varied parcels on a logistics conveyor cell, including thin flat envelopes and deformable poly bags, at ~4 seconds per item with high placement accuracy - i.e., machine-side handling of flat, paper-like items in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parcel singulation. Transfer is to the machine-side half of handing out materials - separating one thin, floppy item from a presented supply and placing it accurately - with comparable object class (flat envelopes/paper) and a fixtured, conveyor-fed presentation typical of an E1 cell.

sources.title: Meet Sparrow: Amazon's new item-picking robot
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual products (including flat/soft goods) from bulk containers in fulfillment centers, a deployed purpose-built picking cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level bin picking. Distributing materials requires selecting one book/workbook/pencil/packet at a time from a supply; Sparrow shows this is solved for a wide item mix when the supply is presented in a fixtured cell.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves 16,000 drinks at Las Vegas cafe
sources.claim: Richtech's dual-arm ADAM robot operates as an unattended beverage station in a Las Vegas cafe, preparing and presenting a drink to each customer in turn; it has served over 16,000 drinks ... that location.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: serving each customer at a counter. It substantiates the person-side half of distribution - a fixed robotic station repeatedly delivering one item to each individual who presents themselves - at commercial reliability.

sources.title: Automated Checkout Kiosks - LaptopsAnytime
sources.claim: Automated laptop-dispensing kiosks are installed in school and campus libraries and dispense a device to each student on demand after the student authenticates, with return and tracking handled by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing school equipment to students. Same output as the rated task for durable materials (device/textbook in each student's hands, tracked), achieved by a purpose-built machine when students are brought to it.

sources.system: Inchy's Bookworm / school book vending machines
sources.developer: Global Vending Group / Betson (school book vending machines)
sources.title: Johnston promotes literacy through innovative book vending machines
sources.claim: Book-dispensing machines are deployed in US elementary school libraries and hand a physical book out to each student who presents a token, without staff handling the item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dispensing books to students. Identical object class (textbook-sized bound books) and identical recipients; it shows the distribution step can be completed by a machine when the stock is loaded into a purpose-built dispenser.

sources.title: Asteres Announces 1,000 ScriptCenter Unit Milestone in 38 U.S. States
sources.claim: Asteres ScriptCenter automated pickup kiosks/lockers are installed at 1,000 sites in 38 states, storing pharmacist-prepared labeled packages and releasing the correct item to the correct authenticated individual.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: name-matched hand-out of a labeled paper-bag item to a specific person. Same requirement as returning graded/labeled papers - the right item to the right individual, with accountability - executed by a fixtured machine.

sources.title: Asteres, Inc. | Vendor Profile (PioneerRx)
sources.claim: The ScriptCenter system verifies items by barcode so that each stored, individually labeled package is released only to the matching person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: identity-matched item release. Supports the accuracy requirement of returning name-labeled papers or numbered test booklets to the correct student at a purpose-built station.

sources.title: Single-Sheet Separation from Paper Stack Based on Friction Uncertainty Using High-Speed Robot Hand
sources.claim: Research demonstrates a robot hand that reliably separates a single sheet from a paper stack under uncertain friction, addressing the core mechanical difficulty of handing out one sheet at a time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sheet separation from a stack. This is the precision bottleneck for handing out worksheets; the demonstration is in a fixtured bench setting, i.e., E1 conditions.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Diligent's Moxi mobile manipulator runs autonomously in hospitals at scale, but its work is point-to-point transport of supplies in locked drawers between staff pickup/drop-off points, not selecting and handing individual items to each seated person.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-facility delivery. Marks the frontier of autonomous mobile work inside structured human facilities (E2): bulk transport between fixed stops, with humans loading and unloading - which falls short of per-student hand-out.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Introduces Servi Q
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi robots autonomously run loaded trays through tight restaurant aisles to tables in thousands of venues, but humans load the trays and diners remove their own items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tray delivery among seated people in an institution-controlled room. Closest E2 analogue to walking a classroom, but it performs no picking or per-person hand-off, so it does not complete the rated task in a classroom.

sources.title: US firm to deploy humanoid robot teaching assistant in New York schools
sources.claim: The first US school-district humanoid deployment (Salamanca City CSD) uses a conversational humanoid for classroom engagement; it does not manipulate or distribute classroom materials.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only as context: the leading in-classroom robot deployment is conversational, confirming no cited system performs physical material distribution in a live classroom (E2).

tasks.label: Operate equipment such as computers or audio-visual aids to supplement presentations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Middle/high school class period: sub wakes or logs into the classroom desktop/laptop already tied to a ceiling projector or interactive panel, finds the regular teacher's slide deck, PDF or video link in the school LMS/drive, projects it, then advances slides, plays/pauses video and adjusts volume while ~25 students work; must switch apps and recover from stray clicks in real time.

Bringing the AV chain up or fixing it: press the projector/panel power button or wall control, select the right input, connect a personal or cart laptop with an HDMI/USB-C dongle, get sound routed to room speakers, lower the screen or dim lights, and troubleshoot 'no signal'/no audio before or during class.

Document camera / interactive whiteboard use: place a worksheet, textbook page or object under the doc cam, adjust zoom and focus, and annotate on the smartboard with stylus or finger while walking students through the work.

Elementary or specialist class: play a read-aloud, song or streaming clip on a smart TV or Bluetooth speaker, pair a phone/tablet to the speaker, run a listening center or CD/streaming audio, with young children moving around the room and crowding the equipment.

Student-device lesson: unlock the Chromebook/tablet cart, hand devices out to students, help with logins to the assigned online activity, then collect the devices and seat each one back in its charging slot at the end of the period.

Non-classroom school space (gym, library, cafeteria, lab, assembly): wheel in a portable projector/PA cart, run an extension cord, connect a laptop, speaker or wireless mic, and play the video or slides for a large group.

sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT is a commercially sold device-testing robot that operates a fixtured device's touchscreens, physical buttons, switches and knobs and runs full test cycles unattended for 72+ hours on a bench with adjustable device-mounting fixtures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated device UI testing. It is the same physical act a substitute performs on a computer or AV aid - pressing power/play buttons and tapping a screen on a device in a known position - executed by machine without a human in the ..., but only with the device fixtured on a test bench.

sources.title: TOUCH: Automated touch screen testing | OptoFidelity
sources.claim: OptoFidelity's TOUCH/STYLUS robotic test platforms use camera-based positioning to locate a fixtured device under test and drive touch and stylus interactions (taps, swipes, straight-line drawing) on its screen from test sequences.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: touchscreen/stylus test automation. Tapping GUI elements and drawing lines with a stylus on a fixtured panel is the same manipulation as advancing a slide or annotating on an interactive whiteboard, at finer precision, but demonstrated only on a fixtured DUT in a lab cell.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi, deployed in US hospitals, uses a single arm to open doors and physically push elevator buttons, completing over 110,000 autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pressing a fixed wall panel button inside an institutional building (E2). It shows a single, well-known button press is achievable in a structured human facility, but not GUI navigation, cabling, or media control on classroom equipment.

sources.title: Rocsys launches integrated platform to enable hands-free charging for autonomous mobility - Charged EVs
sources.claim: Rocsys' Steward automatic connection device uses computer vision and machine learning ... autonomously detect a vehicle, open the charging port, plug the connector in, charge, and unplug; deployed with port terminal and robotaxi operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connector mating. Plugging an HDMI/USB-C cable into a laptop is the same class of vision-plus-force insertion, though Rocsys works in a purpose-built charging bay with a single known connector geometry.

sources.title: Automated Connector Insertion in Automotive Wire Harness Assembly | Eureka Robotics
sources.claim: Eureka Robotics automates connector insertion in wire-harness assembly cells, using force-torque feedback to seat connectors without damaging pins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial connector mating in a fixtured cell. Establishes that small-connector insertion (the HDMI/dongle step of AV setup) is solved when the parts are presented in fixed, known positions.

sources.title: How this humanoid robot learned to make coffee by watching videos | Fox News
sources.claim: Figure 01 autonomously operated a capsule coffee machine - opening the hatch, inserting the pod and pressing the button - from an end-to-end neural network trained on human video, with no human guidance during execution.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating an appliance's lid and control button. Comparable to pressing a projector/TV power or play button, but demonstrated only as a single-station lab demo with the appliance placed in front of the robot, not in an occupied classroom.

sources.title: Laptop & Portable Charger Lending Kiosks - Drexel Libraries
sources.claim: Self-service LaptopsAnytime kiosks in the Drexel University Libraries autonomously dispense laptops and chargers to card-authenticated users and recharge each device when it is returned.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: issuing, collecting and recharging student computing devices. Same objects and accountability as handing out a Chromebook cart, but performed inside a purpose-built dispensing enclosure that users come to, not by a robot moving among seated students.

instances.label: General-education K-12 classroom: sub hands out and sets up low-tech assistive supports called for by IEP/504 accommodations - slant board, pencil grip, adapted scissors, magnifier, noise-reducing headphones, large-print or braille copy, visual schedule/communication board - retrieved from the teacher's labeled bin or the student's cubby, placed and oriented at the student's desk, and adjusted during the lesson.

Setting up or troubleshooting supportive technology during class: waking/charging a student's laptop or tablet, plugging in a charger or headphones, launching text-to-speech or an AAC app, mounting a speech-generating device on a wheelchair tray, clipping on and pairing an FM/DM transmitter for a student with hearing loss, adjusting volume or display settings.

Escorting a wheelchair-using student through school corridors to the restroom, nurse's office, resource room or bus loop during class time or a passing period: pushing or accompanying the chair, holding or opening doors, using the elevator/lift, and bringing the student back to class.

Accompanying an ambulatory student with a disability (walker, crutches, unsteady gait, low vision, seizure risk) to the restroom or another facility: walking at the student's pace, watching for hazards and other students, offering an arm or verbal guidance, waiting outside the restroom, returning to class.

Hands-on personal care in a school restroom or changing area for a student in a self-contained special-education program: managing clothing, toileting or diapering, hygiene and hand-washing, and getting the student on and off the toilet, usually with a second adult present.

In-classroom physical support in direct contact with the student: transferring between wheelchair and classroom chair, floor mat or stander using a gait belt or lift, positioning in adaptive seating, repositioning limbs, steadying a student who is unsteady on their feet.

sources.system: BD Rowa Vmax / Smart automated dispensing system
sources.title: BD Rowa - pharmacy robots and digital solutions for pharmacies
sources.claim: BD Rowa pharmacy robots autonomously store, retrieve and deliver the specific requested item to a counter or self-service collection terminal where a person picks it up, inside a purpose-built machine enclosure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: prescription dispensing. Retrieving one named item for one named person out of a large stock and presenting it for pickup is the manipulation and item-identification core of fetching a particular assistive device for a particular student; objects (small boxed/handheld items) and precision are comparable, in a purpose-built E1 enclosure.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow arm autonomously identifies and picks individual, varied products out of cluttered totes and places each one in a tray, running inside fenced warehouse workcells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse item singulation. Selecting the correct one of many small everyday objects and placing it precisely is the same manipulation as picking a named assistive device from a supply bin and setting it out; demonstrated only inside fenced, purpose-built cells.

sources.system: Rocsys ROC-1 / M1 autonomous charging robot
sources.title: Rocsys unveils next version of its robotic charging solution - electrive.com
sources.claim: Rocsys robotic charging systems use vision-guided robots to autonomously insert and remove charging connectors on parked vehicles at ports and logistics yards, with no human handling the plug.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic connector insertion. Locating a port by vision and mating a connector is the same physical skill as plugging a charger or headphones into a student's tablet or docking an AAC device on its mount; the demonstrated setting is a purpose-built charging bay.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator works autonomously in hospital corridors, using its arm to open doors and operate elevators while making point-to-point deliveries around staff and patients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital corridor logistics. Autonomous door opening, elevator operation and navigation among moving people in an institutional corridor is the environmental-navigation half of escorting a student down a school hallway to a restroom.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is one of the largest fielded autonomous mobile-manipulator deployments, with over a million completed deliveries across more than 25 hospital facilities.

sources.title: Unifi Aviation Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: WHILL self-driving wheelchairs are in commercial airport service: a passenger with reduced mobility boards at a station, selects a destination on a touchscreen, and the chair autonomously drives them there and returns itself to base.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transporting a person with a mobility impairment through a busy institutional building. Same payload (a seated person), same crowded indoor navigation among pedestrians, and the same purpose as wheeling a student down a school corridor to a restroom or nurse's office.

sources.title: How Autonomous Wheelchairs Work | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: The WHILL autonomous service depends on pre-scanned facility maps and fixed virtual pathways with defined endpoints inside a controlled venue, not on open or unstructured settings.

tasks.label: Assist students with boarding or exiting school buses.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Afternoon dismissal bus duty at an elementary school: the substitute walks a class of K-2 students from the classroom to the outdoor bus loop, keeps them in a line away from moving buses, matches each child to the correct bus number, steadies small children on the high first step, picks up dropped backpacks/coats, and confirms with the driver that every child is aboard.

Morning arrival duty at the curb: buses unload in sequence; the substitute stands at the door area, helps students step down (offering a hand or bracing a child carrying an instrument or project), hands down items left on seats, keeps the flow moving in rain/snow/wind, and directs students into the building.

Substituting in a special-education class or as a para: assisting a student with a disability onto the bus — guiding or pushing a wheelchair onto the lift platform, riding/monitoring the lift, positioning the chair and attaching tie-downs and lap/shoulder belts, or physically supporting an ambulatory student with poor balance up the steps and buckling a safety harness/vest.

Field trip loading/unloading at an off-campus site (museum, park, public street curb): counting students on and off at an unstructured curbside, holding students back from traffic, helping younger children with the steps, and handling unexpected conditions (crowds, construction, no designated loading zone).

Bus-loading-zone supervision post at a middle/high school: standing duty in the loading area, monitoring behavior, verbally redirecting and physically separating students who push or scuffle, keeping students behind the safety line, and escorting a student who missed the bus back to the office.

sources.system: May Mobility wheelchair-accessible autonomous shuttle (with Autonomous Vehicle Operator)
sources.title: Wheelchair-Accessible Autonomous Vehicles Are Here. Now What? - New Mobility
sources.claim: In wheelchair-accessible autonomous vehicle deployments, a human operator on board still provides the physical boarding assistance — helping passengers enter and exit and securing mobility devices — and the article identifies eliminating that human role as an unsolved obstacle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisting a passenger to board/exit a vehicle and securing a wheelchair. Even in the most automated vehicle-boarding setting available, the boarding assistance is performed by a human attendant, indicating no robotic system performs this physical assistance autonomously.

sources.title: Schools & Higher Education | Knightscope
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous robots deployed on school grounds are security patrol robots that monitor vehicle and pedestrian traffic in parking lots; they observe and record but perform no physical assistance to students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous presence in a school bus-loop/parking environment. It establishes that autonomous mobility in that setting is possible, but the system only surveils; it cannot guide, steady, hand-off, or physically assist children boarding a bus.

sources.title: Buster the School Bus Robot – Robotronics
sources.claim: The only school-bus robot actually used in US schools is a remote-controlled animated prop used for bus-safety education assemblies, not a system that assists students at loading and unloading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: school bus loading/unloading safety in schools. The device is teleoperated and purely didactic, so it cannot support any positive judgment about autonomously assisting students at the bus.

tasks.label: Restock teaching materials or supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Elementary (K-5) classroom: mid-lesson or end-of-day replenishing of table caddies and student supply bins with pencils, crayons, markers, glue sticks and scissors pulled from the teacher's cabinet or closet shelves; sharpening pencils; sorting loose small items back into labeled bins in an occupied, cluttered room.

Paper and printed materials: refilling the classroom printer/copier paper tray from a ream, replenishing worksheet/handout and turn-in trays with copies brought from the workroom, restocking lined and construction paper and sticky-note stock on the supply shelf.

Common consumables run: noticing tissues, wipes, hand sanitizer, paper towels or dry-erase markers are out, walking to the school supply room/workroom, collecting boxes or packs, carrying them back and placing them on the designated classroom shelf, counter or dispenser.

Secondary (6-12) classroom between periods: restocking class-set materials — calculators returned to numbered caddies, textbooks and novels back on shelves, safety goggles and glassware into cabinets, replacing spent dry-erase markers and leaving a note on shortages for the regular teacher.

Art, science or special-education room: refilling paint cups and glue containers, replenishing brushes, clay, lab consumables and sensory manipulatives into their storage tubs, and reassembling per-table kits for the next class.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Moxi, a one-armed mobile manipulator, autonomously picks supplies out of hospital supply closets and delivers them to patient rooms — commercial mobile manipulation in an institution-controlled human work facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply fetch-and-restock. Transfers to a school consumables run — same class of boxed/packaged consumables, coarse grasp-and-place precision, and an indoor institution-controlled facility with mapped stockrooms and delivery points.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics humanoid MMR performs one million deliveries - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Moxi's deployed task set explicitly includes retrieving items from central supply ... units, i.e. stocking replenishment rather than only point-to-point delivery.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: restocking nursing units from central supply. Same fetch-transport-place structure and comparable packaged-consumable objects as restocking classroom tissues, wipes and marker packs from a school supply room.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Moxi is in commercial deployment at scale (25+ US hospital facilities, 1.25M autonomous deliveries), establishing that this level of mobile manipulation works reliably in a structured human facility.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes maturity/reliability of the Moxi evidence used for the supply-run instance; same task family (indoor supply fetch and restock).

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: TX SCARA, a rail-mounted arm installed in convenience-store refrigerated cases, autonomously judges which shelves are low and restocks them with bottles and cans at up to 1,000 units/day, with remote recovery only on failure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment of rigid consumer goods from crates onto pre-registered shelf layouts. Comparable objects and placement precision to putting marker packs, boxes and class-set items onto known shelf positions when the work is presented as a purpose-built installation does.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow arm uses computer vision and AI ... and pick individual items out of containers and place them into specific totes, running in fenced fulfillment-center cells across a wide rollout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: each-picking/kitting of heterogeneous small goods into containers. Filling supply caddies or refilling a bin with pencils, glue sticks and markers is the same operation — small mixed items, coarse placement tolerance — when the caddies and stock are fixtured and presented.

sources.title: Pick-and-place robots set the pace | KUKA Global
sources.claim: Industrial pick-and-place cells perform precise fixtured loading and unloading of machines and packaging lines, the standard capability underlying fixtured tray/ream loading.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fixtured machine loading. Loading a paper ream into an open, fixtured paper tray is a rigid pick-and-insert of a known object at a known pose, within the precision such cells routinely achieve.

sources.title: pi_0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv)
sources.claim: General-purpose tidying and put-away in unstructured, previously unseen rooms is at research-demo stage: pi-0.5 cleans kitchens and bedrooms in homes not seen in training, but as a lab evaluation rather than a deployed, worker-quality service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting objects away into drawers/cabinets in novel rooms. Cited to bound the upper end: this capability exists only as a research demonstration, so it cannot support worker-quality classroom restocking at E2 or E3.

instances.label: Private in-home tutoring at the student's house: tutor clears the kitchen or dining table of dishes, mail and clutter, pulls two chairs to the right positions, lays out the student's textbook, worksheets, pencils, calculator and timer, moves distractions (TV remote, toys, phone) out of reach, adjusts a lamp, and puts everything back at the end of the session. Layout, furniture, lighting and clutter differ at every house.

Commercial learning center (Kumon/Sylvan/Mathnasium-style storefront): between back-to-back sessions the tutor resets a standard pod or table — wipes the surface, squares up chairs, returns manipulatives/whiteboards/markers to labeled bins, pulls the next student's folder and worksheet packet from a shelf and stages it at the seat. Fixed, repeated layout controlled by the franchise.

School-based tutoring (after-school or push-in) in a classroom, resource room, or school library: tutor pulls 2-6 desks or a kidney table into a small-group cluster, sets out manipulatives, whiteboards, chromebooks and leveled readers, seats students away from windows/doors, then restores the room's original desk arrangement and returns materials to the teacher's shelves.

Session in a public library study room, community center, or coffee shop: tutor picks and claims a table, arranges two chairs side-by-side, wipes crumbs, spreads out prep books, scratch paper and a laptop, angles the seating away from foot traffic, and clears the table completely at the end.

Online tutoring from the tutor's own home office: tutor arranges the desk and physical props (document camera, whiteboard, manipulatives, printed problem sets) within camera frame, positions webcam and lighting, seats the chair, and clears background clutter before the video session.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 VLA autonomously drives mobile manipulators to clean up kitchens and bedrooms in homes never seen in training — picking up clutter, putting objects away — but the developers state it is error-prone.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household room cleanup. Clearing a surface and putting loose objects in their places is the physical core of organizing a tutoring space; objects (books, cups, small items) and precision demands are comparable.

sources.title: Introducing Helix 02: Full-Body Autonomy
sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 runs a single neural policy for long-horizon, whole-room loco-manipulation, completing a four-minute kitchen task end-to-end with no human intervention or resets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: multi-step room reset (fetch, carry, place items in designated locations). Demonstrates the sustained autonomous pick-carry-place sequence needed to stage and clear a tutoring workspace.

sources.title: Living Room Ready: Watch How Figure 03 Tackles Domestic Tidying with Helix 02
sources.claim: Figure 03 autonomously tidied a living room under Helix 02, wiping tables with spray bottle and cloth, returning cushions, and putting toys away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: surface wiping and object put-away in a furnished room — the same physical acts (clear table, wipe, stow loose items) that constitute preparing a tutoring table.

sources.title: TidyBot: personalized robot assistance with large language models (Autonomous Robots)
sources.claim: TidyBot, a real mobile manipulator, learns where objects belong in a given space and autonomously puts away 85% of objects in real-world room-cleanup tests.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: personalized room tidying. Shows that when a robot is trained for one specific space (as a tutoring center or classroom would be), it can place objects in their designated locations at high rates.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots

sources.transferJustification: Related task: readying a room in a human institution for its next users, including trash pickup and door opening. Same class of environment-preparation work in a structured facility, at commercial reliability.

sources.title: Neo™ Autonomous floor cleaning machine for Educational Facilities
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor scrubbers are deployed and operate inside schools and other educational facilities alongside staff and students.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping a school's rooms and corridors to a working standard. Establishes that autonomous mobile robots reliably work inside school buildings among people, the environment of the school-tutoring instance.

sources.title: Swisslog Healthcare Partners with Diligent Robotics to Enhance Hospital Logistics
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi, a mobile manipulator with an arm, is deployed in more than 25 ... and has autonomously completed over a million fetch-and-deliver runs of supplies through occupied corridors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving supplies from storage and staging them where they are needed inside a busy institution — the material-staging half of setting up a tutoring space, at deployed reliability.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: kitting. When materials are presented in fixtures at known positions, laying out a standard set of items into a prepared workspace is exactly the collation/kitting operation these cells perform reliably.

instances.label: Private in-home session: tutor drives across town to a family's house, parks, carries books/worksheets/laptop inside, sets up at the kitchen or dining table, and runs a 60-90 minute one-on-one K-12 math or reading session with the student while parents, siblings and pets move around the house.

Public library or coffee-shop session: tutor drives or walks to a branch library, checks in for a reserved study room, and delivers a 1-hour session with a high school or college student using printed practice sets and a laptop, keeping voice low in a shared public space.

School-site session: tutor drives to a K-12 school, signs in at the front office with a visitor badge, walks to a classroom or school library, and tutors a small group of 2-4 students during an after-school or pull-out block, coordinating briefly with the classroom teacher.

Multi-stop day for a test-prep or agency tutor: driving between two or three client homes in an afternoon in traffic and weather, finding parking, hauling prep books and timed practice tests, and adapting on arrival when a student is late, sick, or the agreed workspace is occupied.

Urban travel without a car: tutor takes transit or walks to an apartment building, uses the buzzer/intercom, climbs stairs, and tutors a young child at a small table in a crowded apartment with limited workspace and background noise.

tasks.label: Organize archival records and develop classification systems to facilitate access to archival materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Processing an unprocessed personal-papers/manuscript accession in a university or historical-society processing room: unbox and survey heterogeneous fragile paper (correspondence, drafts, clippings, ledgers), decide series/subseries and internal order per provenance and original order, remove staples, pins and rubber bands, rehouse into acid-free folders and record cartons, write folder and box labels, assign collection/series numbers, and record the resulting container list.

Arranging a bulk institutional record series (personnel, case, subject, or project files) in a college archives or agency records center: applying the file plan/records classification scheme, verifying and correcting file order, refoldering and reboxing into standard containers, barcoding and labeling containers, shelving them in the assigned run, and updating the location/container register.

Organizing non-textual formats in a processing lab: sorting photographic prints, negatives, slides, maps, architectural drawings, scrapbooks and AV media by subject/date, sleeving photos in mylar or acid-free enclosures, interleaving brittle items, moving oversize sheets to flat files with separation sheets and cross-references, and labeling each enclosure.

Developing or revising the classification/arrangement scheme itself: designing the record-group/series hierarchy, numbering and controlled vocabulary, testing it against sample containers in the stacks, encoding the finding aid in ArchivesSpace/EAD, then relabeling and physically reordering the affected folders and boxes on the shelves so holdings match the new scheme.

Imposing preliminary order on records found in an uncontrolled setting: a donor's home or attic, a church basement, a departmental storeroom, or a small volunteer-run historical society, where records sit in mixed piles, filing cabinets and damaged cartons; the archivist sorts on the spot, weeds duplicates and non-records, boxes and labels material in rough order, and sketches a preliminary arrangement for transfer.

sources.date: 2020-04-22 (article); company still operating and merged with VASTEC in Jan 2025
sources.title: Ripcord uses robotics to digitize records, processes and avoid paper waste — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Ripcord operates commercial robotic work cells that take boxes of heterogeneous business records, detect and remove staples and other fasteners, unfold and singulate pages and feed them to scanners, using SCARA arms, machine vision and machine learning; output is digital images and extracted data, not physically arranged or rehoused originals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk preparation and handling of loose paper records (fastener removal, page singulation). It shows machine handling of the same class of objects in a purpose-built cell, but only in a factory-fixtured feed path, and it delivers digital surrogates rather than arranged, rehoused and labeled physical files, so it does not complete an archival arrangement instance.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically sequencing paper documents. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to putting documents in order, but it is a bench prototype on uniform clean sheets with a pre-given key; it does not appraise content, rehouse into folders, label, or box, so it cannot complete an archival processing instance.

sources.title: Archive access robot for smart archive repositories | Industrial Robot | Emerald Insight
sources.claim: A research mobile manipulator built for 'smart archive repositories' navigates repository aisles and identifies and retrieves file volumes from shelves at different levels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf-level handling of archival files in a repository. It substantiates fetching and replacing labeled file units, but not intellectual arrangement, rehousing or labeling of the contents, which are the core of this task.

sources.claim: A deployed automated storage and retrieval system files and retrieves paper record containers in a purpose-built federal records warehouse, keeping records ordered by machine-assigned locations rather than by an intellectual classification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical storage and retrieval of record containers. It shows machines can move and track boxes in a purpose-built vault, but location management by barcode is not arrangement of records into series or development of a classification scheme, and humans still prepare and file the paper into the bins.

sources.title: Automated Storage & Retrieval System (BookBot) — Temple University Libraries
sources.claim: A deployed library automated storage and retrieval system stores and retrieves 1.5 million volumes in bins on demand in a purpose-built high-density vault.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-managed ordering and retrieval of collection items. It confirms only that bins of items can be stored and fetched in a machine-built vault; item-level arrangement, foldering and classification work remains manual.

sources.title: Automatic Book Scanner or the ScanRobot developed by Treventus — The Robot Report
sources.claim: A commercial automatic book scanner turns the pages of bound volumes by itself and digitizes them at up to 2,500 pages per ... for libraries and archives, inside a self-contained machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: gentle machine handling of fragile bound archival material. It shows page-level manipulation is possible only for a bound volume clamped in a purpose-built cradle; loose, mixed-size, damaged archival papers and their rehousing are outside its scope.

sources.title: PP-Tac: Paper Picking Using Tactile Feedback in Dexterous Robotic Hands
sources.claim: A research dexterous hand with tactile sensing picks up single sheets of paper and paper-like deformable objects from flat surfaces with an 87.5% success rate in laboratory trials.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grasping individual sheets of paper. It marks the current research frontier for paper manipulation — single-sheet pickup at ~88% success in a lab — well short of damage-free handling of brittle historical documents and of any multi-step foldering, labeling and boxing workflow.

instances.label: Holdings maintenance / rehousing during processing in an archives workroom: removing rusted staples, pins and paper clips from mixed loose papers, unfolding and flattening, separating acidic sheets, sleeving photographs, refoldering into labeled acid-free folders, packing record cartons and shelving them in the stacks.

Batch digitization of loose flat paper records (correspondence, forms, reports, case files) in the repository's digitization lab: pulling prepared batches, capturing at archival resolution on production/overhead scanners, quality control of images, file naming, and returning sheets to their folders in original order.

Digitizing bound material — ledgers, minute books, scrapbooks, rare books, brittle periodicals — on a cradle/planetary scanner: supporting the binding, turning pages without damage, page-by-page capture, and QC of the resulting image set.

Batch reformatting of cassette-based and roll media: videocassettes (U-matic, Betacam, VHS), optical discs from born-digital accessions, and microfilm/microfiche rolls — load carrier, real-time or high-speed capture to preservation files, log errors, verify output.

Reformatting open-reel media: 1/4-inch audio tape, acetate discs, and 16/35mm motion picture film — inspect for mold, vinegar syndrome, and broken splices, clean and repair, thread on deck or scanner, monitor real-time transfer, and produce a preservation master.

Creating preservation surrogates of photographs, negatives, oversize maps and drawings, and three-dimensional artifacts: positioning items on a copy stand, large-format scanner, or 3D capture rig, imaging with color targets, and QC of the captures.

tasks.label: Research and record the origins and historical significance of archival materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: University special collections: archivist accessions a donated personal papers collection, interviews/reviews donor correspondence and deed of gift, researches the creator's biography in secondary sources, establishes chain of custody, and writes the provenance, biographical, and scope-and-content notes into an EAD finding aid / ArchivesSpace record.

Government or municipal archives: archivist appraises a transferred records series from an agency, traces its administrative origin through agency histories, retention schedules, and transfer paperwork, and records the administrative history and significance statement in the catalog/records management system.

Museum or historical society: archivist researches the origin of photographs, maps, or artifacts with sparse documentation — examining inscriptions, stamps, watermarks, formats, and comparing against auction records, prior owner files, and published literature — then records dating, attribution, and significance in a collections management database (e.g., for provenance/ownership-gap due diligence).

Corporate, religious, or nonprofit archives: sole archivist documents the origin and significance of internal records (meeting minutes, product files, media assets), interviewing long-tenured staff and consulting institutional publications, and writes item- or series-level notes plus a short internal report or exhibit label.

Born-digital and audiovisual materials: archivist reconstructs the origin of files from a hard drive, email account, or tape deposit using system metadata, checksums, donor statements, and playback/format identification, and records the custodial history and significance in the preservation repository's metadata.

instances.label: Collection-level appraisal of a paper collection offered to a university special collections or historical society: the archivist surveys boxes/folders of correspondence, photographs, ledgers and ephemera, assesses provenance, completeness, authenticity, condition and research value against the collecting policy, and writes an accession/appraisal recommendation.

Appraisal of an agency's or organization's records against retention schedules (NARA-style): reviewing schedule items, samples, and documentation of record series to determine permanent vs. temporary disposition and justify the determination in writing.

Appraisal of a born-digital accession (email accounts, office document shares, digital photographs, databases, disk images) performed entirely on screen using file manifests, format reports and content sampling to decide what has enduring value.

Item-level authentication of a single questioned document — a signed letter, manuscript leaf, land deed or photograph — using provenance/chain-of-custody research, comparison with known exemplars, paleographic and typographic analysis, and sometimes watermark, ink or UV examination or referral to a forensic specialist.

Monetary or market valuation of materials for a donor's tax deduction, insurance schedule, or a purchase decision: researching auction records, dealer catalogs and comparable sales, and issuing or reviewing a valuation opinion.

tasks.label: Study, examine, and test acquisitions to authenticate their origin, composition, history, and to assess their current value.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench connoisseurship examination in the museum's study/collections room: curator unpacks a newly offered painting, print, decorative-art or historic object, handles it with gloves, inspects it under raking light, loupe/UV lamp, turns it to read verso marks, labels, stamps, construction and later repairs, compares with published comparanda, and writes an attribution and condition note for the acquisition file.

Technical/scientific analysis in the institution's conservation-science lab: the object or a micro-sample is analyzed with instruments (portable/MA-XRF, FTIR/Raman, SEM-EDS, XRD, radiography) to identify pigments, alloys, fibers or minerals and to check whether materials are consistent with the claimed date and origin; result is an analytical record of composition.

Bulk small-specimen identification in a natural-history collection: large lots of small invertebrates/insects from an accessioned collection or field lot are sorted, imaged, identified, and sampled for DNA barcoding to verify identifications and locality data before accession.

Other natural-science specimen verification: fossil, mineral/gem, herbarium sheet, or vertebrate specimen examined under a stereo microscope, measured, tested for hardness/streak or matrix, and compared against type or reference material and literature to confirm identification, locality, and whether it is a composite/forgery.

Documentary provenance and value research: assembling ownership history from archival files, dealer and auction records, catalogues raisonnés, stolen-art and Nazi-era databases; pulling and handling paper files and photographs; corresponding with specialists; comparing recent comparable sale prices to assess current value; recording conclusions in the acquisition dossier.

Off-site examination of a prospective acquisition at a donor's home, dealer's gallery, auction preview, storage unit or field site: variable lighting and clutter, no lab equipment, only handheld tools (loupe, UV torch, magnet, tape, sometimes handheld XRF); curator must judge authenticity, condition and approximate market value on the spot.

sources.title: Fraunhofer IGD develops automated robotic arm to scan cultural objects in 3D, now cooperating with Phase One
sources.claim: CultArm3D is a commercial, autonomous robotic-arm scanner used in museums to generate high-resolution colour-accurate 3D models of collection objects; it performs documentation imaging of heterogeneous artefacts but produces no authentication, attribution, or valuation judgment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic 3D documentation of museum objects. It shows the state of the art for robots working with heterogeneous museum artefacts is capture/imaging under human setup; nothing in it delivers the examination-and-attribution judgment this task requires.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (Ceder/Zeng group) with Google DeepMind
sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of novel materials (PubMed abstract)
sources.claim: A-Lab is an autonomous robotic laboratory in which robotic arms move samples between dosing, heating and X-ray diffraction stations and machine-learning models interpret the diffraction data to identify the phases present, i.e. autonomous determination of a presented sample's composition.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous materials characterization. Compositional identification of an unknown inorganic solid presented at an instrument station is the same physical operation and comparable precision to the compositional testing a curator commissions on an acquisition sample.

sources.system: TIMA-X automated mineral analyzer with AutoLoader

It substantiates that a purpose-built instrument cell can take presented specimens and autonomously report their composition, the analytical deliverable of the 'test composition' part of this task.

sources.claim: DiversityScanner is a fully automated benchtop sorting robot that detects small invertebrate specimens in a mixed sample with a CNN, images and classifies them, and transfers each specimen to a well of a 96-well plate for DNA barcoding, enabling automated identification of bulk specimen lots.

sources.system: Robotic hyperspectral imaging system for cultural heritage

sources.claim: A push-broom hyperspectral camera has been mounted on a robotic arm to run automated, repeatable acquisition trajectories over cultural-heritage artefacts for material analysis, i.e. robotic acquisition of analytical imaging data on heritage objects in a laboratory setting.

sources.title: AMS2 - De Beers Group Verification

sources.claim: A MA-XRF scanner integrated with a high-precision robotic arm (Aramis, derived from remote-surgery hardware) was used in the Capitoline Museums' picture gallery to carry out non-invasive diagnostic mapping of Caravaggio's The Fortune Teller; the degree of autonomy of the arm is not established in the source.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-gallery technical examination of a painting. Autonomy is not established, so it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment; it is cited only to characterize the current state of robotic examination in museums.

tasks.label: Inspect premises to assess the need for repairs and to ensure that climate and pest control issues are addressed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine walkthrough of galleries and public exhibition halls in a museum: verifying temperature/RH readings from dataloggers and case sensors, checking HVAC diffusers and light levels, and scanning ceilings, walls and cases for water stains, condensation, cracked plaster, or damaged finishes; occupied building, fixed layout, institution controls access.

Round through collections storage rooms and vaults: narrow aisles between compact shelving and cabinets, checking under sprinkler heads and pipe runs for leaks or water intrusion, musty odor/mold, dust, blocked vents, and RH/temperature stability; contents fragile, nothing fixtured for a machine.

Integrated pest management round: examining sticky blunder traps and bait stations on floors, in corners, behind and under cabinets, at loading docks and food-service areas; counting and identifying trapped insects (clothes moth, carpet beetle, silverfish), checking objects and sills for frass or casings, and door sweeps and gaps for entry points.

Exterior envelope check of a historic museum building: roof slopes, gutters, downspouts, flashing, parapets, masonry pointing and window sills, judging what needs repair; outdoors, uneven ground, weather and access constraints, condition as found.

Back-of-house unconditioned spaces: attics, crawl spaces, basements and mechanical rooms — looking for roof leaks, condensation on ducts, standing water, humidifier/filter condition and equipment faults; low clearance, ladders, no fixed route, spaces not kept to a working standard.

Historic house museum period rooms, outdoor sculpture and grounds, or a visit to an offsite store or loan venue: cluttered interiors with open displays and fragile furnishings, layout differing site to site, plus outdoor walkarounds of structures and monuments.

sources.system: Spot (with sensor payloads, Orbit fleet software)
sources.title: Autonomous Detection of Combustible Gas | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot executes autonomous inspection rounds across a 40-acre midstream plant, performing anomaly detection, thermal inspection and gauge reading, and detected a combustible gas leak during a round.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds. A curator's premises walkthrough is the same act — a repeated route through a building capturing readings and looking for leaks, thermal/climate anomalies and equipment faults — with comparable sensing demands and no manipulation.

sources.system: Spot with Cam+ payload and Orbit visual inspection models
sources.title: Automated Visual Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot autonomously collects imagery of assets on repeat routes and applies change detection to find cracks, wear and other damage, and reads analog gauges with alerting when out of range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual condition inspection of industrial assets. Detecting cracks/wear by repeat imaging is the same perceptual job as spotting new cracks, stains or deterioration in building fabric during a curator's round.

sources.title: Robosecurity Is Here: How Robots Can Save Money and Lives – Cobalt Robotics
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor patrol robots autonomously detect leaks and spills, build maps ... temperature and humidity, flag facility problems and open facilities support tickets while patrolling occupied enterprise buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous facility-condition patrol in human-occupied buildings. It covers the same outputs a curator's climate/repair walkthrough produces — environmental readings, leak/water findings and maintenance tickets — in an indoor institutional setting.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: The Cobalt robot navigates indoor facilities autonomously on scheduled and ad-hoc routes performing security patrols and facility checks, with onboard processing and human review of flagged events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled indoor facility check rounds. Same environment class (occupied institutional building, fixed layout) and same output (route-based condition findings escalated to staff) as a gallery/storage inspection round.

sources.title: Verity, On, and Maersk pilot RFID technology with autonomous drones in warehouse inventory management
sources.claim: Verity's indoor drones fly fully autonomous scanning missions through dense floor-to-ceiling warehouse racking, performing millions of autonomous inventory checks per month across more than 100 warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous visual checking along narrow aisles of tall storage racking. Museum collection stores have the same geometry (tight aisles, tall shelving, GPS-denied, no fixtures), showing the navigation and imaging needed for a storage-room condition round is achievable.

sources.claim: Skydio drones fly autonomous 3D Scan missions to inspect structures, including whole building facades, and are used by transportation agencies for routine infrastructure inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous exterior structural inspection of bridges and building facades. The curator's envelope check (roof, gutters, pointing, flashing) asks for the same close exterior imagery and defect identification on an as-found outdoor structure.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeat autonomous condition/progress documentation rounds on an unstructured jobsite, showing a legged robot can traverse as-found premises and capture the survey data an inspection round produces.
