roles.title: Museum Technicians and Conservators
roles.description: Restore, maintain, or prepare objects in museum collections for storage, research, or exhibit. May work with specimens such as fossils, skeletal parts, or botanicals; or artifacts, textiles, or art. May identify and record objects or install and arrange them in exhibits. Includes book or document conservators.

tasks.label: Determine whether objects need repair and choose the safest and most effective method of repair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Conservation lab intake examination of a single artwork or artifact (e.g., oil painting, ceramic vessel, wooden furniture, textile): unpack, handle and turn the object, examine under raking light, UV, and stereomicroscope, do micro-tests (solvent/solubility swab tests, tapping for loose joints, probing flaking media), then judge whether treatment is needed and specify the safest reversible method (consolidant, adhesive, fill, backing).

Collection storage condition survey: technician moves through storage aisles, opens drawers/boxes, unrolls or lifts hundreds of mixed objects, checks for mold, pest damage, corrosion, tears, broken elements, and records for each whether it needs repair, what stabilization method to use, and treatment priority.

Incoming/outgoing loan condition check at the loading dock or crate room: unpack a crated object, compare it against the lender's condition report, decide whether newly observed cracks, losses, or shifted elements are pre-existing or new damage requiring repair, and choose the interim stabilization or treatment method before display or return.

Gallery/exhibit walkthrough inspection of installed objects (mounted textiles, ethnographic objects, sculptures, mounted specimens) with visitors and casework around: determine on the spot whether an observed problem (lifting paint, sagging fabric, loose mount, insect frass) needs repair and whether it can be treated in situ or must be de-installed.

Field or historic-site assessment: newly excavated archaeological finds at a dig, objects in a historic house, or outdoor monuments/architectural fragments taken as found, in variable light and weather; decide whether an item is stable enough to lift or must be consolidated/block-lifted, and choose the field stabilization method.

Batch triage of numerous similar paper-based or natural-history items in a workroom (books, prints, photographs, herbarium sheets, entomology drawers), often tied to digitization or rehousing: page through or scan each item, flag tears, brittleness, mold, detached parts, and choose a simple repair (Japanese tissue mend, hinge, encapsulation) or refer to a conservator.

sources.developer: Natural History Museum London (with Techman Robot)
sources.title: Robot-in-the-loop: Prototyping robotic digitisation at the Natural History Museum
sources.claim: The Natural History Museum, London is prototyping a Techman TM5 900 robotic ... with AI software, custom grippers, and a 3D ... to handle and image collection specimens in its digitisation workflow; the work is specimen handling, imaging, and label capture, not condition assessment or treatment selection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling and imaging of museum collection objects in a museum lab (E2). It shows the frontier of embodied automation on museum objects is pick-and-image of standardized specimens; nothing in the workflow determines whether an object needs repair or selects a repair method, so it does not transfer to this task.

sources.system: Operation Night Watch macro-XRF scanner and robotic imaging rig
sources.title: Operation Night Watch to start at the Rijksmuseum - Rijksmuseum
sources.claim: At the Rijksmuseum, automated macro-XRF and hyperspectral scanning plus a robotic high-resolution camera captured condition data on The Night Watch, but conservators and researchers interpreted the data and produced the treatment plan for restoration.
sources.transferJustification: Directly adjacent: automated instrumentation examines a museum object in a conservation studio and produces condition data, yet the determination of what needs repair and the choice of treatment remained a multi-year human expert process, showing machines complete only the data-capture sub-step.

sources.system: Spot (Boston Dynamics) at Pompeii Archaeological Park
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Parco Archeologico di Pompei
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology (Sensors/PMC)
sources.claim: A Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped conducts autonomous routine inspections at the Pompeii archaeological park, mapping inaccessible spaces and identifying structural problems, erosion and damage to support human planning of restoration interventions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heritage-site damage monitoring in an unstructured outdoor site. It covers detection of gross structural damage at building scale and feeds human decisions; it does not handle or examine movable collection objects, make repair/no-repair determinations on them, or select conservation treatment methods.

sources.system: Robotic imaging + AI transcription workflow for natural history collections
sources.title: Unlocking biodiversity data with robotic imaging and AI-driven transcription of natural history collections
sources.claim: A published robotic workflow images natural history specimens and uses AI to transcribe labels, accelerating digitisation; the automated output is metadata, not condition or treatment judgments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated batch processing of museum specimens in a collections facility, the closest analogue to batch triage. Output is label metadata; no damage determination or repair-method selection is performed, so it cannot substitute for condition triage.

sources.system: AMR/forklift-based container inspection robot (ZeniaLabs AI concepts, Sensors 24(12) 3721)
sources.title: Toward Fully Automated Inspection of Critical Assets Supported by Autonomous Mobile Robots, Vision Sensors, and Artificial Intelligence
sources.claim: Research on autonomous mobile robots for asset inspection describes a forklift-based robot that circles shipping containers and analyses potential damage and structural health in maritime ports.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic damage detection to decide whether an asset needs repair. Transfer fails: steel containers are standardized, rugged, and assessed against codified damage criteria, whereas museum objects are unique, fragile, materially heterogeneous, and require reversible-treatment selection grounded in materials science and conservation ethics.

tasks.label: Specialize in particular materials or types of object, such as documents and books, paintings, decorative arts, textiles, metals, or architectural materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paper/book/document specialty: in a museum or library conservation lab, the conservator examines a unique fragile item (manuscript, print, bound volume), surface-cleans it, mends tears with Japanese tissue and wheat-starch paste, washes/deacidifies and flattens it, then rehouses or rebinds it. Decisions are item-specific and largely irreversible.

Paintings specialty: in a studio, the conservator consolidates flaking paint, runs solvent cleaning tests under magnification, removes discolored varnish swab by swab, fills and inpaints losses to match surrounding paint, and revarnishes; each passage requires continuous visual and tactile judgment on a unique, irreplaceable surface.

Objects/decorative arts/metals/ceramics specialty: lab treatment of archaeological and decorative objects - mechanical and chemical removal of corrosion down to the original surface, desalination, adhesive joining of ceramic or glass sherds, gap fills and toning, plus fabrication of a custom mount for storage or display.

Textiles/costume specialty: lab work on a historic garment, flag, or tapestry - micro-vacuuming through screen, humidification and realignment of distorted yarns, wet cleaning where safe, stitched support with couching to a dyed sheer overlay, and mounting on a padded custom form.

Natural-history/archaeological specimen specialty: preparation lab work - removing matrix from a fossil with air scribe and air abrasive under a microscope, consolidating and gluing fragments, articulating skeletal material, or mounting botanical and entomological specimens.

Architectural/large-object specialty: work in situ on a historic building or monument - condition survey and treatment of wall paintings, plaster, masonry, or outdoor bronze and stone from scaffolding or lifts, with variable substrate, weather, dust and site access constraints.

sources.developer: Ca' Foscari University of Venice with IIT and the Archaeological Park of Pompeii (EU Horizon 2020)
sources.title: RePAIR: Results and Future Prospects of the Project Integrating Robotics and Artificial Intelligence in the Reassembly of Frescoes at Pompeii
sources.claim: RePAIR built a prototype system with two robotic arms and soft ... autonomously places digitized Pompeii fresco fragments into reconstructed positions, but it is a research prototype whose puzzle solutions were checked and corrected by archaeologists, and it covers only fragment reassembly, not conservation treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic work to a conservator's material specialty (wall-painting fragments): handling of fragile heritage fragments in a purpose-built rig. It substantiates only fragment placement under human error-correction, not a whole conservation treatment, so it does not transfer to completing a treatment instance.

sources.system: Monumental Labs robotic stone carving workshop
sources.title: A stone carving resurgence: Monumental Labs uses robotic arms for ornamental building facades
sources.claim: Monumental Labs uses seven-axis KUKA robotic arms to mill architectural stone ornament and sculpture for new build and historic restoration, but human carvers still perform the finishing passes on each piece.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fabrication/replication of architectural stone elements for restoration. It shows robots shaping new stone in a fabrication shop, not treating existing historic fabric in situ, and hand finishing is still required, so it does not carry over to architectural conservation treatment.

sources.system: Treventus ScanRobot 2.0 MDS automatic book scanner
sources.title: The Automatic Book Scanner or the ScanRobot developed by Treventus
sources.claim: The ScanRobot 2.0 MDS automatically turns pages by airflow and scans bound historic volumes at up to 2,500 pages per ... in libraries and archives - a commercial, autonomous machine that handles fragile books but performs digitization only, with no repair, washing, or rebinding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling of fragile bound volumes in a library/archive (E2 facility). Transfer fails for the paper/book specialty because page turning and imaging involve no material intervention - no tear mending, washing, deacidification, or rebinding is performed.

sources.title: Have a damaged painting? Restore it in just hours with an AI-generated "mask"
sources.claim: The state of the art in automated painting restoration is an AI-generated laminate mask printed on polymer film that a person aligns and adheres to the painting; no robot performs cleaning, filling, or inpainting on the original surface.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related to the paintings specialty (loss compensation), but it is a printing-and-lamination method applied by a human, not an embodied robot, so it cannot support a positive robotic judgment.

sources.developer: Laser Photonics and other industrial vendors
sources.title: Advanced Laser Cleaning Robotic Work Cells Turbocharge Industrial Processes
sources.claim: Commercial robotic laser-cleaning workcells remove corrosion, grease and coatings from metal parts inside enclosed industrial cells, following coordinates entered by an operator for known part geometries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: corrosion removal from metal in a fenced E1 cell. Transfer to the metals-conservation instance fails because heritage cleaning requires locating and stopping at the original surface of a unique, non-replaceable object, with patina-retention and reversibility judgments that no programmed path encodes.

sources.system: Survey of robotic systems in archaeology and cultural heritage (review)
sources.developer: University of Peloponnese / ICCS, published in Sensors (MDPI)
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic survey of robotics in archaeology and cultural heritage finds the deployed roles are survey, access to inaccessible sites, documentation and analysis, with reconstruction still at the research stage; it identifies no robot performing conservation treatment of collection objects.
sources.transferJustification: Field-wide review used as context for negative judgments: the documented robotic roles in heritage are sensing and documentation, not material intervention on objects.

tasks.label: Recommend preservation procedures, such as control of temperature and humidity, to curatorial and building staff.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Install, arrange, assemble, and prepare artifacts for exhibition, ensuring the artifacts' safety, reporting their status and condition, and identifying and correcting any problems with the set up.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Art/history museum gallery during an install period: hanging framed 2D works (paintings, prints, photographs) per the exhibit layout — measuring and marking wall positions, fitting hanging hardware or security fittings, lifting works onto the wall, leveling and aligning to sightlines, and cleaning up marks.

Installing objects into vitrines/display cases in a gallery or case-prep room: seating unique, fragile objects (ceramics, metalwork, jewelry, small sculpture, natural-history specimens) on custom-fabricated mounts, adjusting mount fit, arranging groupings and label spacing per design, then closing and sealing the case.

Installing large or heavy three-dimensional objects in a gallery: sculptures, furniture, machinery, mounted skeletons or dioramas — rigging and moving with carts/gantries/team lifts, placing on pedestals or armatures, assembling multi-part objects on site, and securing them against seismic/visitor contact.

Bench-top reassembly and layout of fragmentary artifacts in a lab or prep room before display: fitting sherds, fresco/mosaic fragments or broken elements into their correct configuration on a support so the object can be exhibited.

Preparing and mounting flexible or flat works: dressing costumes and textiles on padded mannequins/forms, mounting flags or rugs to display panels, and hinging/matting works on paper and fitting them into frames for display.

Examining and reporting object status during installation and after: unpacking and condition-checking incoming loans, documenting condition on arrival and after placement, walking the finished setup to spot problems (unstable mount, poor fit, rubbing, insecure hardware, light or climate issues) and correcting them.

sources.system: RePAIR robotic fresco reassembly system (IIT / Ca' Foscari University of Venice)
sources.developer: Italian Institute of Technology, Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Archaeological Park of Pompeii
sources.title: The research project for the reassembly of fragmented frescoes using an "intelligent robot" comes to an end | EurekAlert!
sources.claim: The EU RePAIR project built a purpose-built robotic installation at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii in which two robotic arms with soft hands automatically place digitized fresco fragments into their reconstructed positions after AI puzzle-solving; validated in initial on-site tests, partly using replica fragments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic reassembly of fragmentary archaeological artifacts. It matches the 'assemble artifacts' element of this task — gentle grasping of unique, fragile heritage objects and precise placement into a target configuration — performed in a dedicated room built around the machine at the heritage site.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan is a fixed robotic arm deployed in warehouses that autonomously picks and stows a wide variety of objects, adapting grip to fragile items, at reliability reported above 99%, operating inside a humanless zone and calling for human help on rare failures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pick-and-place of varied fragile items into compartments. It is the closest deployed analogue to seating objects in a display case, but the objects are packaged commodities in a fenced, machine-built zone, with no custom-mount seating, no aesthetic arrangement, and a damage rate tolerable to retail but not to irreplaceable artifacts.

sources.system: survey of state-of-the-art manipulation systems (Figure Helix, ByteDance GR-RL, others)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: Independent 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capability finds high-precision insertion and fine-manipulation tasks remain limited to labs, several times slower than humans, with low or unclear reliability and no demonstrated transfer to new objects or ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-precision insertion/fine manipulation with novel objects. Museum installation requires exactly this — one-off objects seated into fitted mounts or hardware — so the documented lack of transfer bounds what can be claimed for artifact installation.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robots restock beverage shelves autonomously in hundreds of Japanese FamilyMart convenience stores, succeeding automatically more than 98% of ... with remote operators handling rare failures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing goods onto display shelves inside a human-occupied commercial facility (E2). It shows autonomous display stocking exists, but only for uniform packaged drinks on a fixed rail-mounted track behind standard cooler shelves, with a toppling/misplacement rate and no condition assessment — so it does not transfer to seating unique artifacts on custom mounts.

tasks.label: Study object documentation or conduct standard chemical and physical tests to ascertain the object's age, composition, original appearance, need for treatment or restoration, and appropriate preservation method.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Documentary/comparative research on an object in the museum's collections office or library: pulling the accession file, prior treatment and exhibition records, maker's marks, catalogues and technical literature, and handling the object to match it to the records, in order to establish date, attribution, original appearance and prior interventions.

Hands-on bench examination in the conservation lab of a single unique object (painting, ceramic, textile, book, metal artifact): visual and raking-light inspection, UV fluorescence, stereomicroscopy, magnet/tactile probing of friability and structural stability, simple spot/solubility/pH tests, measurement and photography, ending in a written examination/condition report with a treatment recommendation and recommended preservation method.

Non-invasive instrumental analysis of an object in the museum lab or gallery: portable or macro XRF elemental mapping, infrared reflectography, multispectral/hyperspectral imaging or X-radiography of a painting, panel or three-dimensional object, to map pigments and materials, reveal underdrawing/hidden layers and earlier restorations.

Micro-sampling and laboratory testing: removing a micro-sample or fiber under the microscope from an artifact or specimen, preparing a cross-section/mount or dispatching material, then running standard tests (FTIR, Raman, XRD, GC-MS, polarized-light fiber ID, paper pH/cellulose tests, radiocarbon or DNA sampling of natural-history specimens) and reporting composition and deterioration state.

In-situ examination away from the lab: a historic house interior, an outdoor bronze or stone monument, an archaeological site or a borrower's venue, where the technician examines objects as found under variable light and access to judge condition, materials and need for treatment.

sources.system: Aramis robotic arm + MA-XRF scanner (INFN CHNet / Roma Tre)
sources.developer: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare (INFN Roma Tre) with Roma Tre University
sources.title: Art Under the Scanner. A Surgical Robot Examines Caravaggio - Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare
sources.claim: A medical-grade robotic arm (Aramis) carrying a macro-XRF head autonomously scanned Caravaggio's 'The Fortune Teller' at the Capitoline Museums, adapting in real time to ... painted surface to produce high-resolution chemical maps identifying pigments and an underlying composition.

sources.system: Robotic hyperspectral imaging station for cultural heritage
sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia, Centre for Cultural Heritage Technology (Venice)
sources.title: Integration of Hyperspectral Imaging and Robotics: A Novel Approach to Analysing Cultural Heritage Artefacts (Heritage 2025)
sources.claim: A push-broom VNIR hyperspectral camera mounted on a robotic arm acquired programmable, repeatable scans of planar and volumetric cultural-heritage artefacts without manual intervention, with spectral reliability comparable to established manual methods.

sources.system: Hands-Free Heritage automated two-robot 3D scanning system
sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (Venice / Industrial Robotics Facility, Genova)
sources.title: Hands-Free Heritage: Automated 3D Scanning for Cultural Heritage Digitization (arXiv:2510.04781)
sources.claim: A two-robot cell (scanner arm plus tray-handling arm) autonomously repositions and 3D-scans heritage artefacts with planned trajectories, replacing expert handheld scanning for documentation of object geometry and surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic physical examination/digitization of unique heritage artefacts. It shows autonomous handling and sensor placement around fragile unique objects in a purpose-built cell, the same manipulation class needed to present an object for physical examination, though it yields geometry rather than a condition or treatment judgment.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / UC Berkeley (Ceder group)
sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials | Nature
sources.claim: The A-Lab operates robotic arms and instruments to prepare samples and characterize products by X-ray diffraction, with machine-learning models automatically analysing the diffraction patterns to determine which phases were made.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous instrumental determination of the composition of a presented powder sample. It matches the analytical half of this task (running a standard physical/chemical test on a prepared sample and reporting composition) in a purpose-built robotic cell.

sources.title: Automated Molding Materials Testing | ZwickRoell
sources.claim: Commercial robotic testing systems load, measure and run standardized physical tests (tensile, flexure, compression, hardness) on whole lots of presented specimens overnight without human monitoring, producing traceable test results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: standard physical testing of presented specimens. It substantiates that, once a sample is fixtured and presented, a robot can execute standardized physical tests and deliver accepted measurement results unattended, which is the E1 form of 'conduct standard physical tests'.

sources.system: Total laboratory automation (robotic track systems with clinical chemistry analyzers)
sources.developer: Clinical laboratory automation vendors (e.g., Olympus/Beckman, ARUP installations)
sources.title: Automated Analyser - an overview | ScienceDirect Topics
sources.claim: Total laboratory automation systems accept specimens and robotically centrifuge, aliquot and deliver them to chemistry analyzers, with results auto-verified, in routine hospital laboratory operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine chemical testing of presented samples at accepted quality. It shows that standard chemical tests on samples brought to the machine are completed autonomously end-to-end, matching the E1 counterfactual for the laboratory-analysis portion of this task.

sources.developer: Zoologische Staatssammlung München / Karlsruhe Institute of Technology / NUS collaborators
sources.title: DiversityScanner: Robotic discovery of small invertebrates with machine learning methods (bioRxiv)
sources.claim: A fully automated station uses a robot to detect, image and measure individual small invertebrate specimens and transfer each to a microplate well for DNA barcoding, classifying them with a neural network.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling, imaging and analytical preparation of natural-history specimens. It substantiates that, in a purpose-built station, a robot can handle small collection specimens and carry them through a standard analytical test workflow used to characterize them.

sources.title: Autonomous Hyperspectral Characterisation Station: Robotically Assisted Characterisation of Polymer Degradation (arXiv:2402.11763)
sources.claim: An autonomous station combines robot-aided hyperspectral imaging with automated data analysis to non-destructively characterize the degradation of polymer material samples over time in a laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated non-destructive assessment of material degradation. It shows robotic sensor placement plus automated interpretation for deterioration state of presented samples, the closest analogue to instrumental condition characterization, though on standardized coupons rather than unique artifacts.

sources.title: A mobile instrument for in situ scanning macro-XRF investigation of historical paintings
sources.claim: The first commercial macro-XRF scanner for paintings moves its measuring head over the painting on a motorized X,Y stage to image the distribution of surface and sub-surface elements; such scanners are used routinely in museum studios (e.g., 56 automated 24-hour scans of Rembrandt's Night Watch).

tasks.label: Clean objects, such as paper, textiles, wood, metal, glass, rock, pottery, and furniture, using cleansers, solvents, soap solutions, and polishes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Works on paper, books, photographs and archival documents in a conservation lab: dry surface cleaning with soft brushes, vinyl erasers and soot sponges, then localized solvent/aqueous stain reduction or washing on a suction table. Items are unique, fragile, often torn or brittle; the technician must judge media solubility and stop before abrading the sheet.

Historic textiles and costume in a lab: low-suction vacuuming through a screen mesh, spot cleaning with surfactant or solvent swabs, and full wet cleaning of a flag or garment on a wash table. Fibers are weakened, dyes may bleed, and the object must be supported and reshaped while wet.

Metal objects in a lab: removing tarnish from historic silver with precipitated-chalk slurry and swabs, reducing corrosion on archaeological bronze/iron with solvents, chemical baths, scalpel or micro-abrasive tools. Each object is unique in shape; the crux is stopping at the original surface without abrading hallmarks, plating, or patina.

Individually treated ceramics, glass, stone/geological specimens and fossils in a lab: solvent removal of old adhesives and grime, poulticing salts, mechanical removal of matrix under a microscope with air scribes or air abrasion. Objects are one-of-a-kind, sometimes friable or previously repaired.

Bulk processing of durable excavated material in a collections/processing lab: batches of robust ceramic sherds, lithics and faunal fragments washed in water with mild soap and soft brushes or a bath, rinsed, racked and air dried before labeling. Repetitive, batch-oriented, with pre-selection of fragments too fragile to wash.

Wood, furniture, frames, and large mixed-material objects, often cleaned in situ on the exhibit floor or in a period room/historic house museum: dusting and brush-vacuuming carved and gilded surfaces, cleaning with dilute soap solutions, applying wax polish, working around installed mounts, barriers, and visitors.

sources.system: Survey of heritage/archaeology robotics (ROVINA, RePAIR, fresco service robot)
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed survey of robotics in archaeology and heritage finds conservation robotics is an emerging area centered on sensing, surveying and handling; it names no deployed robot that cleans artifacts, citing only a service-robot design study for fresco restoration and documentation projects such as ROVINA and RePAIR.
sources.transferJustification: Directly surveys robotics applied to conservation/restoration of artifacts; establishes the state of the art for the cleaning task rather than transferring from another task.

sources.system: ML-assisted acoustic monitoring of laser cleaning (IESL-FORTH)
sources.title: Machine learning assisted real-time acoustic monitoring of laser cleaning in Heritage conservation
sources.claim: As of late 2025, automating even the decision of when to stop cleaning a heritage surface is at the feasibility-study stage: an ML model was trained on acoustic signals during laser cleaning to predict the pulse at which the deposit is removed. No robot performs the whole cleaning treatment.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (cleaning heritage objects), automated sub-step only; shows the judgment element of the task is not yet automated even in the lab.

sources.system: Zenith automated ultrasonic cleaners / Advantage automatic parts washer
sources.title: Automated Ultrasonic Cleaners | Industrial Cleaning Systems
sources.claim: Commercially available multi-stage automated ultrasonic parts-washing systems clean batches of soiled parts in aqueous detergent with programmed wash/rinse/dry stages and servo-driven basket transfer between tanks, running unattended after a basket is loaded.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: batch immersion cleaning of soiled solid objects in soap/detergent solution. Transfers to bulk washing of durable excavated sherds because the objects are rigid, tolerant of immersion, cleaned in baskets, and the accepted output is simply soil-free, rinsed and dried material.

sources.system: Ultrasound-assisted cleaning protocol for archaeological pottery (ultrasonic bath)
sources.title: Ultrasound-Assisted Cleaning of Archaeological Pottery
sources.claim: Ultrasonic bath cleaning is an accepted method for archaeological pottery, but published protocol requires human pre-selection of which fragments can tolerate it plus microscopic documentation, because cavitation can abrade fragile ceramics and erase use-wear.
sources.transferJustification: Same task on the same material class; establishes that machine bath cleaning is acceptable for selected robust sherds while confirming per-object human triage is needed for fragile ones.

sources.title: Laserax Launches New Robot Cell for Laser Cleaning and Texturing
sources.claim: Industrial robot cells perform fully automated laser cleaning of rust, oxide and coatings from metal parts of varying shapes inside enclosed cells with conveyor or rotary-table part feeding.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing corrosion/soiling from metal surfaces. Cited to show the closest industrial capability; it processes identical, programmed part geometries to a production spec, not unique artifacts where preserving original surface and patina defines acceptance.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: A general-purpose vision-language-action model controlled a mobile manipulator to carry out multi-stage cleaning/tidying in homes not seen in training, including wiping surfaces and putting objects away.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household cleaning/wiping in unstructured settings. Cited for the in-situ gallery/period-room instance; object value, fragility and the precision of conservation surface cleaning are far beyond kitchen wiping, so it does not transfer.

sources.developer: Dartmouth College ENGS 89/90 team (for APSAP, Armenia)
sources.title: Automated Washing of Archaeological Artifacts: Auto-fact
sources.claim: A 2024 engineering capstone designed an automated washing/drying system for excavated pottery sherds for an active excavation project, selecting ultrasonic cleaning plus fan drying as the gentlest scalable method; it remains a proposed, unvalidated implementation.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (initial washing of excavated artifacts) applied to the bulk-sherd instance; supports that machine bath washing of robust sherds is the intended substitute for hand scrubbing.

tasks.label: Repair, restore, and reassemble artifacts, designing and fabricating missing or broken parts, to restore them to their original appearance and prevent deterioration.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Museum conservation lab: reassembling a broken ceramic, glass or stone object — removing old adhesive from break edges, dry-fitting sherds, bonding with reversible adhesive under supports, filling losses with plaster/epoxy, carving and sanding fills flush, then inpainting to match the original surface. Every object is unique and irreplaceable; damage is unacceptable.

Paper/book conservation lab: repairing a torn document, print, or bound volume — mending tears with Japanese tissue and wheat-starch paste, infilling losses (hand or leafcast), resewing a text block, reattaching boards and rebacking a binding, using a bench, weights, presses and hand tools on fragile, variable-thickness sheets.

Objects/furniture/metals workshop: repairing a wooden, metal, or composite artifact — designing and fabricating a missing element (carved, turned, cast, or 3D-printed from a scan), fitting and attaching it, consolidating corroded or split material, and toning/finishing so the repair is detectable but visually integrated.

Natural history prep lab: reassembling a fossil or skeletal specimen — gluing bone or matrix fragments, gap-filling with epoxy putty, sculpting or casting missing elements, and re-articulating/remounting a mounted specimen or taxidermy mount; work done at the bench with air scribes, adhesives, and armatures.

Textile/organics lab: stabilizing and repairing a textile, basket, or leather object — laying couched stitches or a stitched support fabric under magnification, adhesive-patching splits, reshaping distorted fibers with humidification; extremely low-force, compliant, deformable material.

On-site work at a historic house, outdoor monument, or field/excavation setting: repairing a large sculpture, architectural fragment, or period furnishing in place — scaffolding or floor-level access, uncontrolled light and weather, unknown substrate condition, public or excavation surroundings.

sources.developer: Ca' Foscari University of Venice, Italian Institute of Technology (IIT), Archaeological Park of Pompeii
sources.title: RePAIR: Results and Future Prospects of the Project Integrating Robotics and Artificial Intelligence in the Reassembly of Frescoes at Pompeii
sources.claim: The EU RePAIR project built a prototype system in which AI solves the fragment 'puzzle' and two robotic arms with soft hands automatically position fresco fragments; archaeologists remain in the loop to catch errors, and the system stops at dry placement (no adhesive bonding, loss compensation, or retouching).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic reassembly of fragmented painted plaster, the closest published analogue to reassembling broken artifacts. It substantiates only fragment placement on a purpose-built robotic table; the project explicitly frames itself as support for conservators, with human oversight and no bonding, filling, or inpainting.

sources.system: Vision-based collaborative fragment reconstruction system (cobot with vacuum suction attachment)
sources.developer: Fraunhofer IPK, Department of Machine Vision, Berlin
sources.title: A Vision Based System for Guided and Collaborative Reconstruction of Fragmented Documents
sources.claim: A Fraunhofer IPK prototype uses a collaborative robot with a vacuum suction end-effector to position fragments of damaged paper documents automatically (0.57 mm repeatability), leaving quality checking to human experts; it does not mend, infill, or rebind.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic reconstruction of fragmented paper documents, comparable objects (fragile sheet material) to document conservation. It covers only fragment positioning on a flat prepared table; the conservation steps of tear mending, loss infilling, and rebinding remain manual.

sources.system: 3D scanning and printing workflow in Getty Museum conservation
sources.title: Conservation and Mountmaking: 3-D Scanning | Getty Projects
sources.claim: Getty Museum conservation uses 3D scanning and printing to produce replacement elements missing from ornate frames, but the machine only outputs a part: the design decision, fitting, attachment, and finishing are performed by conservators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: digital fabrication of missing parts, the 'designing and fabricating missing or broken parts' sub-step. Transfer is limited: additive machines produce a part in a purpose-built machine enclosure, but no cited machine fits, adheres, or finishes the part on the artifact.

sources.system: Extended Automation System (EAS) robotic masonry restoration workflow
sources.developer: Research consortium reported in npj Heritage Science (HLRS/EAS workflow, Lanxi City case study)
sources.title: Integrating CAD and extended robotics for masonry restoration: a scalable workflow for historic and heritage buildings (HHBs)
sources.claim: A published heritage-masonry restoration workflow used a robotic arm to apply mortar and position bricks for coarse assembly of damaged wall specimens, with mixed-reality human oversight refining the work — the closest demonstrated robotic 'repair by reassembly', and only at building-masonry scale and coarse precision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic reassembly and repair of historic fabric. Objects (bricks) are standard, rigid and robust and tolerances are millimetre-scale with human MR-guided correction, so it does not transfer to sub-millimetre, no-damage repair of unique museum artifacts.

tasks.label: Perform tests and examinations to establish storage and conservation requirements, policies, and procedures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Conservation lab / collection store: hands-on condition examination of an individual object (painting, textile, ceramic, archival document, natural-history specimen) newly acquired, returning from loan, or pulled for review — unwrap and position it, inspect recto and verso under raking light, UV and magnification, gently probe for structural weakness, photograph, and issue a condition report specifying handling, mount and storage requirements. Includes batch condition surveys of objects pulled from cabinets and drawers in storage.

Non-invasive instrumental analysis of an object's materials — handheld or macro XRF elemental mapping, IR/UV imaging, imaging spectroscopy, X-radiography — set up in the conservation lab or in situ on a painting or object in the gallery, to identify pigments, metals, media and degradation products that determine treatment, display and storage requirements.

Micro-invasive testing on the object itself: taking micro-samples and cross-sections with a scalpel under a stereomicroscope, solubility and cleaning tests with swabs on discreet areas, pH spot tests on paper, salt tests on ceramics, fibre and adhesive identification — each decided case by case on a unique, fragile artifact.

Preventive-conservation monitoring rounds inside the museum: routine circuits of galleries, cases and storage rooms recording temperature, relative humidity, lux and UV readings at fixed points, visually checking for leaks, dust, mould and insect evidence, and logging the data that feeds reports setting environmental storage requirements and procedures.

Bench testing of storage and display materials in the conservation science lab: Oddy/accelerated corrosion tests on case fabrics, paints and adhesives, pH and lignin tests on boards and papers, off-gassing and accelerated-aging trials — samples prepared, sealed, incubated, measured and evaluated to set purchasing and case-construction policy.

Off-site examination taken as found: assessing an outdoor monument, historic house interior, archaeological site or a borrower's venue — inspecting fabric, mounts and surrounding conditions on uneven, unmaintained ground to establish conservation and environmental requirements.

sources.system: Aramis robotic-arm MA-XRF scanner (INFN CHNet / Roma Tre)
sources.developer: INFN (Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare), Roma Tre section
sources.title: Art Under the Scanner. A Surgical Robot Examines Caravaggio
sources.claim: A medical-grade robotic arm ('Aramis') carrying an MA-XRF head performed a non-invasive analytical examination of a Caravaggio painting inside the Capitoline Museums picture gallery, with the arm adapting in real time to ... painted surface and holding constant standoff via sensors.

sources.title: The Importance of Being Versatile: INFN-CHNet MA-XRF Scanner on Furniture at the CCR "La Venaria Reale"
sources.claim: The INFN-CHNet motorised MA-XRF scanner was brought to artworks at the CCR 'La Venaria Reale' conservation centre and to furniture in historic interiors, scanning non-planar decorated surfaces with a telemeter for distance control to characterise materials for conservation.

sources.developer: Google Cultural Institute / Google Arts & Culture
sources.title: Google Art Camera uses robotic system to take gigapixel photos of museum paintings
sources.claim: Google's Art Camera is a robotic ... rig that, once calibrated by an operator to the edges of a work, automatically scans a painting section by section with laser and sonar focusing; it has been used on artworks in museum galleries worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-resolution documentary imaging of artworks in museums. It shows robotic capture of an object's surface in a gallery, but the deliverable is imagery, not the diagnostic condition assessment the examination task requires.

sources.title: Fraunhofer IGD develops automated robotic arm to scan cultural objects in 3D, now cooperating with Phase One
sources.claim: CultArm3D is an autonomous robot-arm scanner that photogrammetrically digitises museum artefacts placed before it, planning its own views and generating high-resolution 3D models at the push of a ...; it is marketed and used for museum collection digitisation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated 3D capture of collection objects presented on a turntable. It substantiates robotic imaging of fixtured heritage objects, but not object handling, multimodal inspection, or a conservator-quality condition diagnosis.

sources.system: Spot (with Orbit fleet management and inspection payloads)
sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs autonomous, repeatable inspection missions in industrial facilities, navigating fixed routes and collecting sensor data (visual, thermal, acoustic, gauge readings) on tens of thousands of assets; arm manipulation, by contrast, was operator-driven.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine sensor-round inspection of an institution-controlled facility. Museum environmental monitoring rounds are the same activity — fixed circuits, readings and visual checks at set points in an indoor facility — with comparable sensing precision and no object handling.

sources.system: Spot at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii (Smart@POMPEI)
sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Archaeological Park of Pompeii
sources.title: Meet Spot, the Dog-Like Robot Roaming the Ruins of Pompeii
sources.claim: A four-legged Spot robot was put to work at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii, navigating the ruins autonomously to collect data on structural ... problems used to plan conservation interventions.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist (Nature 583, 237–241)
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile manipulator worked unattended in a university chemistry laboratory built for people, autonomously executing multi-step experimental workflows — sample preparation, handling of vials, moving samples between benchtop instruments and measurement — and choosing its own next experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous multi-step bench chemistry in a human lab. Museum materials testing (pH, off-gassing, accelerated corrosion trials) uses the same manipulations — vials, dispensing, sealing, shuttling samples to instruments — at comparable precision, though coupon preparation and visual corrosion rating are not demonstrated.

tasks.label: Prepare reports on the operation of conservation laboratories, documenting the condition of artifacts, treatment options, and the methods of preservation and repair used.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Direct and supervise curatorial, technical, and student staff in the handling, mounting, care, and storage of art objects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Art museum exhibition installation: the technician/conservator briefs a crew of preparators and technicians on handling protocols for a specific set of works, assigns who carries, mounts, and hangs each object, sets the sequence of work, and inspects and approves mounts and placements before the gallery opens.

Conservation lab supervision of graduate interns and student assistants: demonstrating correct support and handling of fragile works on paper, textiles, or ceramics, assigning treatment and rehousing tasks, reviewing their documentation and condition reports, and correcting technique.

Collections storage project: the collections manager/technician directs staff and volunteers through a rehousing or storage move, planning the workflow and cart routes, assigning roles, specifying housing and padding standards, and signing off on completed shelving and location records.

Incoming/outgoing loans at the loading dock and packing room: directing technical staff and contract art handlers in unpacking, condition-checking, crating, and staging of loaned art objects, and instructing couriers on handling limits and acclimation.

Small or regional museum / historic house: a single technician directs a handful of part-time staff and volunteers through a temporary exhibit change-out, giving on-the-spot instruction on object handling, mount fabrication, and return to storage.

Formal training and policy work: running handling orientations for new student workers and volunteers, writing and updating handling/storage protocols and safety rules, scheduling staff to tasks, and evaluating their performance.

tasks.label: Photograph objects for documentation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Accession/catalog photography of small-to-medium portable artifacts (ceramics, coins, tools, jewelry, small sculpture) in the museum's collections photo studio: object staged on a sweep or turntable with scale bar and color target, several standard views plus 360/photogrammetry sets, files named and attached to the collection record.

Mass digitization of standardized natural history specimens in a collections imaging lab: herbarium sheets, pinned insects, microscope slides, small fossils and shells imaged in batches at high throughput with barcode/label capture, against fixed lighting and copy-stand or conveyor setups.

Standard before/after treatment documentation of an object in the conservation lab: overall recto/verso views on an easel or table with color chart and scale, plus routine raking-light and UV-fluorescence overall shots, matched framing to prior campaigns.

Examination and in-progress documentation driven by the conservator's judgment: photomicrographs through the stereomicroscope of chosen losses, cracks, tool marks or cross-sections, targeted raking-light details of specific condition features, and shots taken at chosen moments during a treatment.

Imaging of books, bound volumes, archival documents and works on paper: page-by-page capture in a cradle or overhead scanner, handling fragile bindings, flattening and turning leaves, capturing bindings and watermarks.

In-situ documentation of large, heavy, fragile or installed objects that cannot go to the studio: paintings on gallery walls, sculpture and furniture in open storage aisles, mounted exhibits, period rooms and historic-house or field-site material, shot with portable lights and stands amid gallery/storage clutter.

sources.title: J. Paul Getty Trust puts CultArm3D-P to the test - Fraunhofer IGD
sources.claim: CultArm3D-P is an autonomous, color-calibrated photogrammetric scanner using a robotic arm and glass turntable that images museum objects, including sculpture-sized objects, fully automatically; it was trialed at the J. Paul Getty Trust in Los Angeles.
sources.transferJustification: The scanner's capture step is repeated calibrated photography of the object from many viewpoints - the same act as documentary object photography, with the same objects and color/resolution standards.

sources.title: Fraunhofer IGD develops automated robotic arm to scan cultural objects in 3D, now cooperating with Phase One
sources.claim: The commercial CultArm3D GT10 (Fraunhofer IGD with Phase One) autonomously produces high-resolution, color-faithful scans of museum exhibits at the push of a ... has been used at the Getty, REM Mannheim, MHK Kassel, Saalburg and Keltenwelt am Glauberg.

sources.title: CultArm3D, an Automated Robotic Arm That Can Scan Cultural Objects in 3D - 3Dnatives
sources.claim: With CultArm3D the object is placed on ... supplied turntable by staff and the system then runs a pre-scan and dynamic view planning to capture all visible detail in sharp, true color with the minimum number of images.

sources.developer: Istituto Italiano di Tecnologia (Centre for Cultural Heritage Technology, Venice; Industrial Robotics Facility, Genoa)
sources.title: Hands-Free Heritage: Automated 3D Scanning for Cultural Heritage Digitization (arXiv:2510.04781)
sources.claim: An automated two-robot cell (scanner robot plus tray-handling robot) performs complete high-resolution capture of cultural heritage artefacts without handheld or semi-automatic operator intervention, including repositioning of the object.
sources.transferJustification: Robotic capture of calibrated image sets of heritage artefacts on a tray is the same physical act as studio documentation photography of the same class of objects.

sources.developer: Harvard University Herbaria (Sweeney et al., TAXON)
sources.title: Large-scale digitization of herbarium specimens: Development and usage of an automated, high-throughput conveyor system
sources.claim: An automated conveyor-based imaging workflow at Harvard University Herbaria imaged and captured core data for nearly 350,000 herbarium specimens, at 35 seconds per sheet.

sources.developer: TU Darmstadt / Hochschule Darmstadt (Ströbel et al., ZooKeys)
sources.title: An automated device for the digitization and 3D modelling of insects, combining extended-depth-of-field and all-side multi-view imaging
sources.claim: DISC3D is a computer-controlled digitization device for pinned insects and other small specimens with a motorized two-axis gimbal that images the specimen automatically from any view with extended depth of field.

sources.title: Automated Product Photography Solutions for still, 3D, 360 product photos
sources.claim: Ortery's software-controlled photography systems capture stills, 360 sequences and focus-stacked images automatically once an item is placed inside, with four-axis control of camera tilt, zoom and fly-over while the object rotates on an embedded turntable.
sources.transferJustification: Automated multi-view still capture of small objects on a turntable is the same physical operation as museum object documentation photography; the Getty Villa uses this hardware for ancient glass.

sources.title: Ortery PhotoCapture 360 Product Turntable (product page, customer review)
sources.claim: The Getty Villa Museum built a 360-degree photography set for ancient glass around an Ortery PhotoCapture 360 turntable, reporting that the image quality meets its standards.

sources.title: Automatic Book Scanner | Treventus
sources.claim: The ScanRobot 2.0 MDS is an automatic book scanner that turns pages by itself with a v-shaped cradle and prism capture at up to 2,500 pages per ..., to ISO 19264-1 archival image quality.
sources.transferJustification: Page-by-page imaging of bound volumes is the book/document conservator's version of photographing objects for documentation, with the same fragile materials and archival image standards.

sources.developer: Treventus Mechatronics / University of Tulsa McFarlin Library
sources.title: McFarlin's new ScanRobot protects rare books while increasing access for students, scholars
sources.claim: The University of Tulsa's McFarlin ... has installed a ScanRobot to digitize rare books, describing it as the only such machine in the central United States.

sources.title: Google Art Camera uses robotic system to take gigapixel photos of museum paintings - DPReview
sources.claim: Google's Art Camera is a robotic ... that, once an operator has calibrated it to the edges of a ..., automatically photographs the work section by section using laser and sonar focusing; it has been used to digitize over a thousand works in museums.
sources.transferJustification: Gigapixel tile capture of an artwork in place is documentation photography of a museum object performed in the gallery, at resolutions used for conservation condition monitoring.

sources.title: Applications of Reflectance Transformation Imaging (RTI) for Books and Objects on Paper
sources.claim: A portable, automated RTI dome ... is used in a paper conservation department to photograph collection objects under many controlled light directions, documenting surface relief and condition.
sources.transferJustification: Automated multi-light capture is the mechanized form of the raking-light documentation photography conservators perform for condition records.

sources.system: Phase One Rainbow Multispectral Imaging Solution
sources.title: Phase One Rainbow Multispectral Imaging Solution | DT Heritage
sources.claim: The Phase One Rainbow multispectral solution automates capture of visible, infrared and ultraviolet image stacks of cultural heritage objects on a copy-stand imaging station.
sources.transferJustification: Automated UV/IR/visible stack capture reproduces the routine UV-fluorescence and IR documentation exposures conservators make for condition records.

tasks.label: Plan and conduct research to develop and improve methods of restoring and preserving specimens.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Bench screening of candidate treatment materials on prepared mock-up coupons in a museum conservation lab: conservator designs a test matrix (solvent gels, consolidant dilutions, adhesives, deacidification agents), prepares or obtains sample coupons (painted panels, paper strips, textile swatches, bone/plaster analogues), applies treatments by swab/brush/pipette under a stereomicroscope, then judges gloss, color, penetration, tack and residue, and records results.

Analytical characterization research in a museum conservation-science lab or studio: taking micro-samples or making non-invasive measurements on specimens, embedding and polishing cross-sections, running FTIR/XRF/SEM-EDS/optical microscopy, and interpreting spectra and images to establish degradation mechanisms and material compatibility that inform improved preservation methods.

Accelerated aging and exposure studies: placing prepared sample sets in light-fading, temperature/RH, or pollutant chambers; periodic colorimetric, mechanical, or pH measurement over weeks or months; statistical comparison of degradation rates between treated and untreated samples to set storage, display, or treatment standards.

Trial application of a candidate improved method on an actual collection object or specimen: e.g., a new consolidant on a fossil fragment still in matrix, a novel adhesive on a fragile textile, a gel cleaning test in an inconspicuous corner of a painting; unique irreplaceable object, non-standard geometry, close visual/microscopic evaluation, full documentation, performed in the lab/studio or in gallery/storage.

Field/in-situ research at an unstructured site: trialing and monitoring preservation treatments on an outdoor monument, archaeological excavation, or historic house interior; installing outdoor exposure racks or dataloggers and returning to measure; variable weather, access, and site layout.

sources.title: Meet the Autonomous Lab of the Future - Berkeley Lab News Center
sources.claim: A-Lab at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory is a purpose-built autonomous laboratory in which robotic arms carry out powder dosing, heating and characterization steps for target materials selected by researchers or AI agents, closing the loop with automated analysis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous materials-synthesis research. It transfers to conservation research because both are closed-loop experimental programs on prepared laboratory samples — formulate, treat, characterize instrumentally, interpret, and choose the next experiment — with comparable object sizes (vials, powders, coupons) and lab-bench precision.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with Google DeepMind
sources.title: New analysis raises doubts over autonomous lab's materials discoveries | Chemistry World
sources.claim: A-Lab ran independently for 17 days at about 21 experiments per day, using machine learning to plan experiments and interpret robot-collected characterization data; some of its structural interpretations were later contested, indicating the interpretive step is not yet at expert quality in all cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous synthesis plus automated X-ray diffraction interpretation. It substantiates machine planning and instrumental interpretation of samples, the same loop a conservator uses when characterizing treated coupons, while also bounding reliability of the interpretation step.

sources.title: AI-driven mobile robots team up to tackle chemical synthesis | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: Two AI-driven mobile robots at the University of Liverpool autonomously performed exploratory synthetic chemistry — running reactions, analysing products with instruments, and deciding what to do ... — reaching decisions comparable to human researchers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exploratory chemistry research with robot-executed experiments and autonomous decision making. It transfers to 'plan and conduct research' because the planning/decision element — judging which trial results are worth pursuing — is the same, though the samples are standard labware rather than heritage mock-ups.

sources.developer: Argonne National Laboratory, Center for Nanoscale Materials
sources.title: Self-driving lab transforms materials discovery | Argonne National Laboratory
sources.claim: Polybot, an AI-driven robotic platform at Argonne's Center for Nanoscale Materials, autonomously explored processing routes for polymer thin films, coating substrates, using computer vision to quantify film coverage/defects, and optimizing conductivity and defect levels without human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous coating of substrates and vision-based assessment of the resulting film. This is the closest analog to screening consolidants/coatings on prepared conservation coupons — same scale of substrate, same apply-then-inspect loop, same optical quality metrics.

sources.title: A self-supervised robotic system for autonomous contact-based spatial mapping of semiconductor properties | Science Advances
sources.claim: A self-supervised robotic probe autonomously positioned and made thousands of contact measurements across sample films for 24 hours of continuous unattended operation, mapping material properties at high throughput.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: repeated automated measurement of sample arrays. Aging studies require the same repeated instrumental measurement of coupon sets over time (colorimetry, probe contact), at comparable precision and on comparable sample geometry.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University / Emerald Cloud Lab
sources.title: Autonomous Chemistry and Materials Innovation Driven by Scientific Agents | JACS Au
sources.claim: Coscientist, an LLM-driven agent, read hardware documentation and autonomously planned reactions and generated control code for liquid-handling robots, executing and iterating on chemical experiments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous experimental design and execution on standard automated labware. It supports the 'plan' half of plan-and-conduct research, showing machine planning can drive purpose-built robotic benches through a solution-handling experimental program.

sources.title: Towards Robot Scientists for autonomous scientific discovery
sources.claim: The Robot Scientist Adam autonomously generated hypotheses, designed discriminating experiments, executed them with laboratory automation, and interpreted the results in repeated cycles, in a purpose-built automated laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: closed-loop automated scientific discovery. It is the canonical precedent that the whole plan-conduct-interpret research cycle can run on robotic lab automation when samples are presented in standard carriers.

sources.title: The initial results of Operation Night Watch - Rijksmuseum
sources.claim: At the Rijksmuseum, technical research on The Night Watch used an automated macro-XRF scanning instrument that raster-scans the painting on a purpose-made easel in the museum studio; the scanner acquires data unattended, but scan planning, mounting and interpretation remained with conservators and scientists.
sources.transferJustification: Same task family (technical research supporting conservation methods) in a museum setting. Cited only as context for the E2 setting: acquisition is instrument-automated, but experiment planning, object handling and interpretation are human, so it cannot support a positive E2 whole-instance judgment.

tasks.label: Prepare artifacts for storage and shipping.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: In a museum collections storage room or conservation lab, rehousing unique three-dimensional artifacts (ceramics, metalwork, decorative arts, small sculpture) and textiles/costume for long-term storage: assessing condition and fragile points, choosing archival materials, cutting Ethafoam cavity or tray mounts, padding with acid-free tissue, rolling textiles on tubes or supporting garments, placing in archival boxes, labeling and shelving. One-off objects, no two alike, essentially zero tolerance for abrasion or breakage.

Preparing framed paintings, works on paper, and photographs for outgoing loan shipment in the museum's packing/prep area: condition report and photography, glassine/foam-corner soft pack, backing boards, travel frames, then seating the work in a foam-lined crate with braces or tray packs, and sealing/marking the crate.

Fabricating and fitting out the container itself in a museum prep shop or crate shop: measuring the object, designing the crate/box, cutting plywood, cleats, foamcore trays and cushioning foam, carving cavities to the object's negative shape, gluing/nailing/screwing the case, adding gaskets, hardware and hinged lid, stenciling.

Rehousing natural history and archaeological material in a collections lab: sherd and bone lots into labeled archival bags/trays, fossils cushioned in cavity-cut trays or plaster jackets, herbarium sheets into species folders and cabinets, pinned insect drawers and fluid-preserved jars checked and returned to cabinets, each with catalog labels.

Preparing frozen tissue/DNA vouchers and small barcoded vials in a museum biorepository for cryogenic storage: racking labeled tubes and loading them into an automated ultra-cold storage unit that stores and retrieves them.

Off-site preparation: packing objects for transit at a lender's private home or a dealer's premises, deinstalling and packing a travelling show in a borrowing venue's gallery, or bagging/boxing finds in a field lab at an excavation. Layout unknown in advance, mixed object types, work done around other people and around building fabric.

sources.title: Stow: Robotic Packing of Items into Fabric Pods (arXiv 2505.04572)
sources.claim: Amazon's Stow robot autonomously places a wide variety of consumer items into fabric storage pods at human-comparable speed and density, with over 500,000 stows performed in a working fulfillment center — the closest deployed analogue to 'placing objects into storage', but on commodity goods with tolerated damage rates rather than unique artifacts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing diverse items into storage. It shows autonomous handling of varied objects in an institutional facility, but the items are replaceable commodities handled at measurable damage rates and without any object-specific archival housing, condition assessment, or padding, so it does not substantiate preparing unique artifacts for storage.

sources.system: Amazon automated made-to-fit box packaging machines
sources.title: Amazon to deploy automated packaging machines across Europe, reducing waste for millions of customer orders
sources.claim: Amazon's automated packaging machines measure an item, build a right-sized cardboard box around it and apply the shipping label, and are used for heavier or more fragile items; hundreds are being installed across fulfillment centres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated boxing of goods for shipment on a purpose-built line. It produces a generic right-sized corrugated box with standard void fill, not archival cushioning, cavity mounts, glassine/tissue interleaving or a condition-documented museum pack, so it does not carry over to artifact packing.

sources.system: RASCAL (Robotic Arm for Sherds and Ceramics Automated Locomotion), modified LoCoBot arm
sources.developer: Temple Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (Temple University)
sources.title: GitHub - TempleRAIL/Archeology-Robot-Arm
sources.claim: The RASCAL robotic arm autonomously detects pottery sherds against a uniform background, picks them up and places ... target locations while imaging and recording them, demonstrated for archaeological fieldwork processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling and sorting of excavated ceramic fragments. It moves robust sherds between trays on a prepared uniform-colour surface; it does not bag, cushion, label or box material to archival standard, so it covers only a fragment of preparing finds for storage.

sources.developer: Wührl et al. (Zoologische Staatssammlung München / National University of Singapore)
sources.title: DiversityScanner: Robotic discovery of small invertebrates with machine learning methods (bioRxiv v4)
sources.claim: The DiversityScanner is a fully automated benchtop sorting robot that detects small invertebrate specimens in a mixed sample, images and measures each one, and transfers it into an individual well of a 96-well microplate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated transfer of natural history specimens into standardized containers. Comparable objects (millimetre-scale specimens) and comparable precision, in a purpose-built enclosed frame; it supports racked-container specimen handling but not archival housing of dry collection lots.

sources.system: Hamilton BiOS automated -80C sample storage system
sources.title: Automation of Biobanking Activities – OpenSpecimen
sources.claim: Automated ultra-cold biorepository systems such as the Hamilton BiOS robotically store and retrieve labelled specimen tubes at -80C and are in routine use in operating biorepositories.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing labelled specimen vials into long-term storage. Same object class (barcoded tubes/racks) and same purpose (accessioning specimens into a controlled store) as museum biorepository cryo-vouchers, in a purpose-built automated store.

tasks.label: Perform on-site field work which may involve interviewing people, inspecting and identifying artifacts, note-taking, viewing sites and collections, and repainting exhibition spaces.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Repaint an emptied gallery/exhibition space between shows: patch and sand anchor holes and scars from the previous install, mask floors, trim and light tracks, apply two coats to large flat walls in the specified gallery color, and clean up. Museum-controlled premises, fixed layout, work scheduled in the changeover window.

Touch-up and detail painting in an occupied or partly installed exhibition space: brush touch-ups on case bases, plinths, pedestals, corners and trim, cutting in around installed vitrines, mounts and objects, color-matching existing paint, working within inches of artifacts on view.

Off-site visit to a private home, collector, donor or church: interview the owner about provenance and history, unwrap, handle and examine objects (frames, furniture, textiles, paintings), identify materials, maker and damage, take written notes and reference photographs, advise on care. Layout as found, clutter, pets, no institutional control.

Visit to a peer institution — another museum, historical society, library, loan venue or offsite storage facility: examine collection objects on shelves and tables, write incoming/outgoing condition reports for loans, check mounts and cases, take notes and photos, confer with resident staff. Institution-controlled premises, standard equipment.

Outdoor site fieldwork: archaeological excavation, historic structure, monument, or natural-history collecting locality. Walk and view the site, inspect and identify artifacts, features or specimens in situ, assess condition and environmental risks, take field notes, measurements and photographs, sometimes lift and pack material. Weather, terrain and site conditions as found.

sources.title: Behind the Gloss: Construction's Dirty Work Is Going Robotic — Architect Magazine
sources.claim: Okibo's EG7 is a fully autonomous, AI-guided robot that paints, applies plaster and finishes ... on interior construction sites, navigating by onboard 3D scanning without BIM data or site preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior wall painting and drywall patching/sanding on construction sites. Transfers to repainting an emptied gallery: same substrate (painted gypsum board walls), same operations (patch, sand, coat), and a museum gallery is a cleaner, more predictable interior than an active construction site.

sources.title: Okibo opens New Jersey HQ and launches EG7 robot in U.S. market — The Robot Report
sources.claim: Okibo's autonomous painting and drywall-finishing robots are commercially deployed, having covered more than one ... on major construction sites in Europe before the US launch.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: real-jobsite interior painting at scale establishes that whole-wall repainting is done autonomously rather than in a demo.

sources.title: Okibo launches EG7+, the autonomous painting robot — Building Design + Construction
sources.claim: The Okibo EG7+ performs autonomous sanding, painting and Level 4/5 drywall finishing on walls up to 24 feet, with customers reporting quality standards consistently met.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes finish quality (Level 4/5) comparable to what a museum accepts for gallery walls, and covers the patch-and-sand prep step that precedes a gallery repaint.

sources.developer: Boston Dynamics / Archaeological Park of Pompeii
sources.title: Survey on the Application of Robotics in Archaeology (Sensors/PMC)
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot is used at the Archaeological Park of Pompeii for routine autonomous inspection patrols, structural monitoring and 3D data capture, including looters' tunnels, alongside an autonomous Leica scanning drone; interpretation and archaeological judgment remain with human specialists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heritage-site inspection and documentation. It substantiates autonomous data capture at an outdoor heritage site, but not artifact handling, identification, interviewing or the professional field record the conservator's instance requires.

tasks.label: Coordinate exhibit installations, assisting with design, constructing displays, dioramas, display cases, and models, and ensuring the availability of necessary materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Shop fabrication of display furniture for an upcoming exhibition: from the exhibit designer's drawings, cutting plywood/MDF panels, building pedestals, platforms, wall panels and panel-built case bodies, edging, drilling, assembling with dowels/fasteners, and painting or laminating. Occurs in the museum's carpentry/fabrication shop with table saw, router, and spray booth.

Physical installation in the gallery: rolling cases and pedestals into position, anchoring vitrines, mounting graphic panels and vinyl text, hanging framed works to specified center-line and level, setting unique fragile objects onto mounts inside cases, and focusing track lighting, working around a fixed deadline in a finished public gallery.

Fabricating custom mounts and armatures fitted to individual objects: bending brass/steel rod, forming acrylic cradles, or scanning an artifact and producing conformal 3D-printed supports, then padding and finishing the mount so it safely holds one unique object. Done in the mount/prep shop.

Constructing a diorama or habitat group: sculpting terrain and rockwork, applying textures and foliage, arranging taxidermy specimens or artifacts in a naturalistic scene, and blending the foreground into a curved painted background. Done in the exhibit shop and on-site in the gallery.

Producing scale models, replicas and sculpted scenic elements from a digital model: CNC/robot-milled rigid foam forms, 3D-printed touchable replicas and architectural study models used in exhibit design and display.

Ensuring materials are available: checking stock of lumber, hardware, paint and archival supplies, ordering, then receiving deliveries at the dock and moving crates, sheet goods and cases by pallet jack/cart to the shop and gallery staging area within the museum building.

instances.label: Domestic ground courier trip between museums: the technician oversees final packing and dock loading of crates into a climate-controlled fine-art truck, travels with/behind the truck (overnight stops, security watch), then at the borrowing museum supervises unloading, acclimatization, uncrating, writes a condition report against the outgoing one, and oversees installation before signing the receipt.

International air courier trip: escort crates to the air-cargo terminal, witness palletization and aircraft loading on the ramp, fly on the same flight, attend customs/broker clearance and transfer to the fine-art agent's truck at the destination, then condition-check and supervise uncrating and installation at the borrowing venue.

Local or regional van run: technician packs and loads the museum van, drives across the city or region to a partner venue, commercial gallery, conservation studio or framer, negotiates varied loading docks, service elevators, doorways and street parking, carries the work in, unpacks, condition-checks and obtains a signed receipt.

Courier trip to or from a non-institutional site: pickup or return of a loan at a private collector's home, artist's studio or auction house back room; on-site soft-wrap/packing, negotiating stairs, furnished rooms and tight residential entries, condition report with the lender present, and transport back.
