tasks.label: Preserve or direct preservation of objects, using plaster, resin, sealants, hardeners, and shellac.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Paintings/polychrome surface conservation in a museum lab: under a stereomicroscope, wicking dilute resin consolidant into lifting or cleaving paint and setting it down with heated spatula/tacking iron, filling losses with gesso or plaster fill leveled and textured to match, then brushing or spraying a natural-resin/shellac varnish coat. Unique object, irreversible risk, treatment decided flake by flake.

Objects conservation bench work: rejoining broken ceramic, glass or stone fragments with Paraloid B-72 or epoxy, dry-fitting and taping joins, bulking and carving plaster/epoxy gap fills, and applying protective lacquer or wax sealant coats to metal artifacts. Each object unique in shape, fragility and prior repair history.

Natural-history/fossil preparation lab: consolidating friable bone or matrix with Butvar/Paraloid or cyanoacrylate hardener applied by brush, pipette or wicking into cracks; gluing separated fragments; building plaster-and-burlap or epoxy supports, cradles and repair jackets around irregular specimens.

Field/on-site preservation: applying plaster-and-burlap field jackets to fossils in a quarry, consolidating fragile finds in situ at an excavation, or sealing/consolidating an outdoor monument or sculpture. Uneven terrain, weather, no fixed layout, access and lighting taken as found.

Batch protective coating of a set of similar, stable items (e.g., lacquer or microcrystalline-wax coating on a group of metal artifacts or specimen mounts, sealing coats on prepared supports), racked and coated in a fume hood or spray booth in the collections lab to a specified coating and film thickness.

Book, document, frame and furniture conservation: consolidating friable media or degraded leather, applying shellac or resin coatings to a historic frame or furniture surface, and sealing/hardening localized repairs, matching surrounding gloss and color by eye.

tasks.label: Classify and assign registration numbers to artifacts and supervise inventory control.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Accessioning an individual new acquisition at an art or history museum: the technician examines a unique object (painting, ceramic, quilt, tool, taxidermy mount) received from a donor, determines its classification under Nomenclature/thesaurus terms, assigns the next accession number, creates the catalogue record with measurements, materials and photographs, and physically marks the number on the object with barrier coat and ink, a sewn tag or a tie-on tag. Work is done in a collections workroom with the object on padded supports.

Batch registration of a bulk natural-history accession in a collections lab: trays or vials of insects, shells, seeds or microfossils arrive as a mixed lot; the technician sorts and identifies specimens to taxon, assigns catalogue or lot numbers, writes/prints labels into vials, unit trays or slides, and enters the data into the collection database.

Batch registration of an archaeological or historical object lot: bags of potsherds, lithics, buttons, coins or nails from a site or estate donation; the technician sorts by type, assigns lot and item numbers, ink-marks or tags individual diagnostic pieces, re-bags with labels, and records counts and classifications in the catalogue.

Tagging and location registration during a rehousing or move: attaching barcode or RFID tags to objects, mounts and archival boxes, then scanning each item into its new shelf, drawer or rack location in the collections management system so the record shows where the object physically sits.

Periodic inventory sweep of a storage range: walking aisles of shelving, cabinets and pallet racking with a scanner, verifying that each tagged and labelled housing is present and in its recorded location, and producing a discrepancy list of missing or misplaced items for follow-up.

Supervising inventory control: assigning and checking the numbering and inventory work of volunteers, interns and junior staff, auditing catalogue entries for consistency with numbering conventions, investigating and reconciling discrepancies between records and physical holdings, and signing off inventory reports.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated triage and sorting of bulk biological specimens. It performs the two acts this task requires for bulk specimen lots — machine classification of each specimen and assignment of a unique registered position/identifier linked to a database record — on comparable small, fragile natural-history specimens.

sources.transferJustification: Same bulk-specimen triage transfer as above; shows the robotic system is in continuing real research use rather than a one-off demonstration.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: library shelf-reading/inventory. A museum inventory sweep of tagged, boxed holdings on storage shelving requires the same acts — traversing aisles, reading each item's unique ID tag in place, and reporting missing or misplaced items against the catalogue.

instances.label: Public library circulation desk checkout: a patron sets a stack of mixed items (hardbacks, paperbacks, DVD cases, magazines, a hotspot) on the desk with a library card; the worker verifies the account, clears blocks/fines, scans or RFID-reads each item, deactivates security, prints a due-date slip, pulls holds from the hold shelf, and hands the stack over, in a busy open public area.

Special, museum, or corporate library and special collections: charging out non-standard or untagged material (archival folders, rare volumes, media kits, uncataloged reports) to a named researcher or staff member, often with manual call slips, condition notes, and reading-room-only restrictions.

instances.label: Public library print/copy station: the multifunction copier reports a jam mid-job; librarian opens side and rear doors, extracts torn sheets from rollers and the duplexer, reseats the toner cartridge or swaps in a new one, refills the 500-sheet trays, wipes the scanner platen/ADF glass, closes up and runs a test copy — done on the open floor with patrons waiting.

Public-access computer area: a workstation is frozen, will not print, or lost network; librarian walks to the station, checks cables and power, force-reboots, logs in as admin, clears the session/print queue, applies pending OS or browser updates or re-images the machine from the deep-freeze/management client, wipes down keyboard and screen, and confirms a patron can log in.

Peripheral swap at the staff workbench: a mouse, keyboard, headphone set, webcam or monitor cable has failed; librarian brings the unit or spare to the desk, unplugs the dead peripheral from the USB/HDMI/power ports, plugs in the replacement from the supply cabinet, powers up and verifies it works, and logs the swap.

Meeting room / classroom AV upkeep: set up and maintain the projector, screen, microphones, speakers, laptop cart and document camera for a program — connect HDMI/USB-C and audio cables, pair a wireless mic, fix a 'no signal' or feedback problem, clean the projector filter or replace a lamp/bulb, then break down and stow the cart.

School or academic library device fleet: Chromebook/laptop/tablet carts returned from classrooms — inspect for damage, seat each device in the charging cart and confirm charging, replace broken chargers, keyboards, screen bezels or styluses, push images/updates to the fleet, re-tag and re-shelve devices in the workroom.

Media collection / digitization equipment upkeep: keep playback, duplication and capture gear running in a media lab or archive — load and unload tapes, discs and cartridges into drives and decks, run head-cleaning cartridges or cleaning discs on drives showing read errors, check capture decks and duplicators, and verify a clean read/playback afterward.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: Autonomous cable insertion into a computer's external ports has been demonstrated by Gemini Robotics 1.5 on a lab bench setup: the robot inserted and removed power, USB ... PC front panel.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cable insertion. Unplugging a dead peripheral and plugging in its replacement at a PC's external ports is the same manipulation on the same objects (USB/power/LAN connectors on a desktop machine) that a librarian performs when swapping a mouse, keyboard or monitor cable.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed connector-insertion system achieved 100% success inserting USB stick, HDMI, DisplayPort and Type-C connectors, though slowly (27 s per insertion).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: rigid connector mating in a fixtured cell. The connector types are exactly those used on library PCs, monitors and AV gear, supporting the plug/unplug portion of a bench-side peripheral swap at worker-comparable reliability.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: Humanoid robots have been deployed on CATL production lines inserting connectors attached to flexible cables into battery packs at claimed 99% reliability and human speed, in a factory production setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: production connector mating with flexible cables. It shows connector plugging can be done at production reliability and speed in a structured line, the physical core of a cable/peripheral swap.

sources.developer: Epoch AI (review of deployed and lab systems)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 — Epoch AI
sources.claim: State of the art on maintenance-like work inside computer equipment: no robot has attempted a full PC cable-assembly job, and working inside a cramped case with limited visibility remains a significant limitation even in the lab.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant negative context: reaching into machine interiors (copier paths, PC cases, AV housings) with limited visibility is the defining condition of hardware maintenance in a library.

sources.system: IBM TS4500 tape library robotic accessor
sources.title: LTO cleaning cartridge — IBM TS4500 Documentation
sources.claim: Commercial automated tape libraries autonomously maintain their own drives: the robotic accessor loads a cleaning cartridge into any drive that requests cleaning, inside a purpose-built enclosure, and also loads/unloads media for read/write verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: media-drive upkeep. Loading cartridges into drives and running a head-cleaning cartridge when a drive reports errors is the same maintenance act a media collections specialist performs on decks and drives, on the same class of media.

sources.system: robotic unscrewing cell for e-waste disassembly
sources.title: Robotic system for automated disassembly of electronic waste: Unscrewing — ScienceDirect
sources.claim: An autonomous robotic cell (UR10e arm, RealSense vision, custom screwdriver) locates and removes screws from electronic devices for e-waste disassembly; only teardown steps are automated, not diagnosis, repair or reassembly.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: opening laptops/PCs by removing fasteners. It shows the disassembly step alone is automatable in a fixtured cell, but no cited system diagnoses a fault, installs a replacement part and verifies the device boots.

sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy robot autonomously disassembles 23 iPhone models at 200 units per hour on a purpose-built recycling line — teardown only, with no repair or functional verification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of consumer electronic devices in a fixtured line. Bounds the state of the art: model-specific teardown is deployed, but repair, part replacement and verification of a working device are not.

sources.title: Rocsys Unveils Multi-Bay Charging Solution for Robotaxis
sources.claim: Rocsys autonomous charging robots plug and unplug connectors into vehicles without human intervention in commercial depots, ports and robotaxi charging bays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous connector mating in service operations. Confirms that vision-guided plug insertion, including opening a flap first, is reliable enough for commercial duty, supporting the plug/unplug core of equipment hook-up — though on much larger connectors than USB-C.

tasks.label: Train faculty and media staff on the use of software and audio-visual equipment.

instances.label: Academic library media specialist runs a scheduled hands-on workshop for a group of faculty in a smart classroom or training room, explaining and demonstrating the AV podium: projector/display switching, document camera, wireless presentation, lecture-capture and microphone use, and answering questions until instructors can operate the room themselves.

One-on-one, just-in-time coaching: a faculty member comes to the reference desk or the librarian visits their office to be walked through software — database search interfaces, citation managers, streaming-media platform, or the library's discovery layer — with the learner driving their own computer.

Training media staff and student assistants on procedures and equipment handling: how camera, tripod, microphone and lighting kits are checked out, inspected and configured, plus the circulation/reservation software used to track them; delivered as a mix of talk-through, demonstration and supervised practice in the media services area.

Remote or hybrid training webinar for distributed faculty on a newly licensed software platform (LMS-integrated video, e-reserves, institutional repository, or reference tools), delivered by screen-share with follow-up Q&A.

Producing and disseminating instructional support materials — quick-start guides, annotated screenshots, short how-to videos, signage for a new videoconferencing room — and walking staff or faculty through them so they can self-serve later.

tasks.label: Maintain inventory of audio-visual equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic physical inventory audit of the AV equipment collection in a school/academic media center storeroom or locked cage: walking the shelves and cabinets, scanning barcodes/RFID asset tags on cameras, projectors, tripods, mic kits and cases, verifying counts and locations against the asset database, and flagging missing or misplaced items.

Day-to-day circulation of single tagged devices (laptops, tablets, portable chargers, hotspots, calculators, handheld recorders): accepting the returned unit at the service point or kiosk, confirming identity and condition, recharging/resetting it, updating the circulation/inventory record, and returning it to its charging bay or shelf.

Check-in of multi-component AV kits (DSLR/camcorder kit with lens, battery, charger, SD card, cables; wireless mic set; projector cart): opening the case, verifying every component against the kit packing list, testing that the gear powers on and functions, noting damage, then restocking the case on the correct shelf.

Accessioning and records upkeep in the workroom: unboxing newly purchased equipment, recording model/serial numbers, affixing barcode or RFID asset labels, entering items into the inventory/ILS system, and marking lost, retired, or sent-for-repair items as deaccessioned.

Pulling a specific requested item from equipment storage for a patron hold, class reservation, or faculty request: locating the item by call/asset number in the cage or cabinet, verifying it is the right unit and complete, and bringing it to the service desk on time.

Verifying distributed/installed AV across the institution: walking a route of classrooms, labs, and conference rooms to confirm ceiling projectors, room carts, document cameras, remotes and cables are present and working, and reconciling with the asset list.

Same act as an AV storeroom audit - navigate aisles, read item identifiers, reconcile against the inventory record and report discrepancies - with comparable object scale and no manipulation required.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cycle counting of RFID-tagged assets (not just retail goods) in a working facility, i.e. exactly the presence/location verification step of an equipment inventory audit.

sources.claim: Commercial vision-guided robotic labeling cells apply barcode/RFID labels to products in a fixtured industrial cell and verify label presence, position and readability.

tasks.label: Assemble and arrange display materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public/school library: build a themed or staff-picks book display on a display table, endcap, or slatwall — stand ~15-30 books and media cases face-out on easels/stands, add a printed topper or sign in a holder, tidy the arrangement; done on the open floor while patrons browse.

Refresh and maintain existing displays and new-arrivals racks: pull items that were borrowed or misplaced, bring replacement titles from carts, re-face and straighten remaining items so the display stays full and presentable; repeated on a daily/weekly cycle.

Assemble a bulletin board or wall display: mount backing paper and borders, cut/arrange paper lettering and printed posters, staple or pin flyers, reading lists and student work to a cork board or wall panel, often working at height on a ladder or step stool.

Arrange an exhibit/display case: place special-collections items, artifacts, memorabilia, realia or student artwork on cradles, risers and mounts inside a locked glass case, position typed labels precisely, adjust lighting; fragile, unique, irreplaceable objects.

Seasonal/event display work: hang banners and signage, drape tablecloths, set up standees, props, string lights and window clings for a program or holiday; assemble portable display racks and event tabling in the lobby or meeting room.

Transfer: arranging multiple items face-forward in a specified layout inside a display fixture demands the same manipulation and layout fidelity as standing books face-out on a display rack, and is demonstrated commercially in fixtured lines.

sources.title: Telexistence to install AI re-stocking robots in 300 convenience stores across Japan | Robotics & Automation News
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocks refrigerated beverage display shelves from the back storage area of roughly 300 FamilyMart (and later Lawson) convenience stores in Japan, running autonomously during normal operation with remote human takeover only for rare failures.

Transfer is only partial: the objects are uniform rigid bottles and the arm is a rail-mounted installation dedicated to one cooler, so it does not substantiate mobile display work with mixed-size books on a library floor.

tasks.label: Troubleshoot problems with audio-visual equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Instruction room / meeting room in a public or academic library (or school media center): a projector, flat-panel display or document camera shows no image or the wrong source. The librarian goes to the room, checks power and the control panel, cycles inputs, gets behind the podium/cart to reseat or swap HDMI/USB-C cables and dongles, checks the laptop's display settings, reboots the device, and confirms the picture is restored before the class or program starts.

Program room, storytime space or recording studio: sound problems - a wireless handheld/lavalier mic is dead or cutting out, a mixer channel is muted or feeding back, a Bluetooth speaker will not pair, or a hearing-loop/amp has no output. The librarian swaps batteries, re-pairs or re-tunes the mic, checks gain and cable runs, moves speakers, and tests the room audio with a patron waiting.

Service desk bench check of a small standardized circulating device returned or reported as 'not working' (tablet, e-reader, camera, headphones, handheld recorder): staff power it up in a fixed spot at the desk and step through its screen, buttons, camera, speaker and microphone to confirm or rule out the reported fault, then either resolve it with a factory reset / settings change or flag the unit for removal from circulation.

Same circulating-equipment stream, but the remedy is physical and non-standard: recharge or replace a swollen battery, reseat an SD card, clean a lens or connector, replace a frayed cable or ear pad, free a stuck door, reload firmware over a cable, and re-test before returning the item to the hold shelf.

Live hybrid event or instruction session in a library conference room or auditorium: mid-session failure of the videoconference/streaming chain - webcam or PTZ camera not detected, capture card dropped, no far-end audio, screen share black, mic echo. The librarian must diagnose across camera, cabling, USB hubs, software settings and network while the meeting is running and restore it within a minute or two.

Media collections / archive or media lab: legacy and specialized playback and digitization gear misbehaving - VCR eating tape or tracking poorly, microfilm/microfiche reader lamp or film transport jammed, turntable/cassette deck with hum or one dead channel, 16mm projector loop failure, digitization station with a dead capture input. The specialist opens the unit, cleans heads/gates, clears the jam, re-threads media, checks a fuse or belt, and verifies playback quality.

sources.title: MATT for Refurbished Device Diagnostics - Automated Device Diagnostics for Refurbishment Operations | Adapta Robotics
sources.claim: MATT is a commercially deployed device-testing robot that autonomously performs the physical interaction needed to exercise a smartphone-class device held in a universal cradle - touchscreen, side buttons, front/rear cameras, microphone and speakers, charging port - and reports which functions fail; one operator supervises up to nine robots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: functional fault verification of handheld consumer devices. It exercises exactly the audio-visual functions a librarian bench-checks on a circulating tablet/camera/headset (screen, buttons, camera, mic, speaker, charging port), with comparable objects and precision, in a purpose-built cradle station.

sources.title: Rocsys unveils multi-bay hands-free charging system for robotaxis, raises $13M (Electrek)
sources.claim: Rocsys builds autonomous robotic charging arms that locate a vehicle, open the charge port and insert/withdraw the connector without a human, deployed at ports and vehicle depots.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous insertion of a connector. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to reseating an AV cable, but it handles one pre-engineered connector type at an engineered stall and performs no fault diagnosis, so it does not transfer to heterogeneous AV troubleshooting.

sources.title: Breaking Boundaries in Data Center Connectivity: Introducing Telescent's G5 Robotic Patch Panel - Data Center POST
sources.claim: Telescent's robotic patch panels autonomously make, break and re-route fibre connections inside a purpose-built enclosure in data centres, and are sold commercially to network operators.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: remote re-patching and link restoration of signal cabling. Shows connector work is automated only inside a machine-built panel with one standard connector, not on found AV installations behind podiums, carts and racks.

sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with Orbit performs autonomous routine inspection rounds in industrial facilities - thermal imaging, acoustic anomaly detection and gauge reading - detecting faults but not repairing equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous fault detection on equipment inside a structured facility. It establishes only sensor-based anomaly detection on fixed routes; it does not include diagnosing a signal-chain fault or performing the corrective manipulation this task requires.

sources.title: Meet Daisy and Taz: Apple's iPhone-Disassembling Robots | Supply Chain Digital
sources.claim: Apple's Daisy line disassembles many iPhone models at high rate in a purpose-built facility, showing that automated electronics manipulation today is fixtured, model-specific teardown rather than fault diagnosis or repair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated manipulation of consumer electronics in a purpose-built cell. Demonstrates fixtured, model-specific teardown only; no diagnosis of an unknown fault and no restoration of function, which is what troubleshooting requires.

tasks.label: Set up, adjust, and operate audio-visual equipment, such as cameras, film and slide projectors, and recording equipment, for meetings, events, classes, seminars, and video conferences.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public library meeting/community room event (author talk, community group, film screening): librarian retrieves or wheels out a portable projector or connects a display, lowers/erects the screen, plugs the visiting presenter's laptop in via HDMI/USB-C adapters, runs power and audio cables, sets up a small PA with a wired or wireless mic, tests picture and sound, and stays to troubleshoot mid-event.

Academic or school library instruction/conference room hybrid class or seminar: power up the installed system, connect the instructor's laptop or room PC, launch Zoom/Teams, select sources, position and adjust camera and microphones for in-room and remote participants, share content, and fix problems (no audio, wrong input, dropped call) while the session runs.

Recording or livestreaming a library program: set camera(s) on tripods and frame shots, place and cable microphones into a mixer/recorder, set levels, start and stop the recording, adjust framing and audio live as speakers move, then deliver the file/stream for the collection or website.

Operating an already-installed automated capture system during a scheduled lecture, class or seminar in a fixed classroom/auditorium: keeping the presenter framed as they move, following them between lectern, screen and whiteboard, switching among camera angles, and keeping the recording/stream running for the length of the session.

Legacy and media-lab equipment: threading a 16mm film projector or loading a slide carousel for a class, loading and playing DVD/VHS/cassette media for a program or patron, or setting up and adjusting a microform reader-printer or digitization station and getting it working for the user.

Off-site or outdoor library event (park movie night, bookmobile stop, community fair, class held at a partner site): haul portable gear to a setting taken as found, rig a screen or inflatable screen and projector, set up battery/generator-powered PA and mics, and adjust for wind, daylight, ambient noise and improvised power.

sources.claim: Autonomous cable/connector insertion is demonstrated on a production line only inside a workstation cell where a human loads the parts and consumables and the workpiece is fixtured.

roles.title: Library Technicians
roles.description: Assist librarians by helping readers in the use of library catalogs, databases, and indexes to locate books and other materials; and by answering questions that require only brief consultation of standard reference. Compile records; sort and shelve books or other media; remove or repair damaged books or other media; register patrons; and check materials in and out of the circulation process. Replace materials in shelving area (stacks) or files. Includes bookmobile drivers who assist with providing services in mobile libraries.

tasks.label: Reserve, circulate, renew, and discharge books and other materials.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public library circulation desk checkout: a patron brings a mixed stack (print books, DVDs/Blu-rays in locking cases, audiobook kits, board games, hotspots) to the desk; the technician charges each item to the account, deactivates the security tag, unlocks media cases, prints or emails a due-date slip, and handles in-person renewals, expired cards and account blocks. Open public floor, unpredictable patron flow.

Discharging returns: emptying the exterior drive-up book drop and interior return bins, checking each item in (backdating when needed), glancing for damage/missing discs, then routing each item to the hold shelf, the branch-transit bin, mending, or a reshelving cart. Back workroom plus vestibule of a public library branch, high daily volume.

Holds/reserves fulfillment from open stacks: running the daily pull list, walking the public shelves across floors to retrieve requested titles by call number, checking them in as holds, wrapping with a name slip, filing them alphabetically on the self-service hold shelf, and bagging in-transit items for other branches. Public stacks with patrons present.

Academic or special library reserve and closed-stack circulation: two-hour course-reserve loans issued and discharged at the service desk, paging requests for items in closed or high-density storage delivered to a pickup point, and immediate restocking of returned reserve copies during exam-period peaks. Campus library building.

Outreach circulation away from the library building: bookmobile stops at schools, senior residences, trailer parks and rural crossroads, deposit collections, and homebound delivery — checking materials out and discharging returns on a laptop/tablet at the stop, in weather, curbside or in a community room.

tasks.label: Process print and non-print library materials to prepare them for inclusion in library collections.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public or school library technical-services workroom: batch of new jacketed hardcover trade books processed in house — property stamp, barcode label, spine label with call number plus label protector, security strip/RFID tag, and a Mylar/Kapco protective cover fitted over the printed dust jacket; item record verified before the truck goes to shelving.

Public library workroom: new paperbacks, mass-market titles, prebound and board juvenile books, and jacketless hardcovers — print and apply spine label with protector and cover barcode, apply and encode RFID/security tag, ownership label, verify item record, load onto shelving truck. Dozens to a few hundred uniform items per shift.

New non-print media (DVD, Blu-ray, audiobook CD sets, video games): take discs out of vendor packaging, insert discs and cover art into the library's locking security case, label each disc and case with barcode and spine/call-number label, add RFID/security tag, record piece count.

Academic or large public library receiving area: shelf-ready vendor shipments — unpack cartons, scan and verify each item against the invoice/packing list and loaded bibliographic records, spot-check vendor-applied call-number labels, add remaining local pieces (property mark, security/RFID tag), log receipt and route to the stacks.

Serials, pamphlets, maps, government documents and similar formats: date stamp and property stamp, apply barcode/security tag, place items in pamphlet binders, vertical files, magazine covers or boxes and label the housing before adding to the collection.

Nonstandard materials in a small branch or school library: activity kits, board games, 'library of things' items (hotspots, tools, instruments), and donated or used books of varied size and condition — inventory and bag the pieces, custom-label irregular surfaces, assess condition, and assemble the circulating unit.

Academic/research library: reshelving monographs, bound periodicals, oversize volumes, and course reserves in exact LC call-number order across multi-floor stacks, including compact movable shelving ranges, tightly packed shelves requiring shifting, and items routed to reserve or off-site trays.

Circulation check-in / central sorting: items arriving from book drops, self-return, and inter-branch delivery are checked in and sorted by destination — holds shelf, home branch, floating collection, mending, discard — and loaded into bins or carts for delivery or shelving.

Technical services: copy-cataloging new arrivals (matching/editing records in the ILS or OCLC, assigning call numbers, adding item records) and physically processing them — printing and applying spine labels and barcodes at the required position, security strips, mylar jacket covers, property stamps — then routing to the new-books display.

Non-print and 'library of things': DVDs/Blu-rays/video games checked for disc presence and re-cased, CD sets and playaways verified, kits/hotspots/board games inventoried for pieces, then returned to locked media cases, secured display racks, or behind-desk storage.

Special collections, closed stacks, or off-site depository: returning archival boxes and folders, microform reels, maps, and rare volumes to their designated file drawers, trays, or high-density storage locations and recording the location in the tracking system.

instances.label: Public copier/printer/scanner in the library print area goes down mid-session: technician diagnoses the fault from a panel code or patron report, opens side/front panels and trays, extracts torn or crumpled jammed sheets from rollers and the fuser, reloads paper, swaps a toner cartridge or waste bin, closes up, runs a test print, and re-releases the patron's print job, often with patrons waiting.

Public-access PC or catalog workstation fault: machine frozen, black screen, no network, dead mouse/keyboard, or no sound. Technician goes to the carrel, power-cycles, checks and reseats power/HDMI/USB cables under the desk, swaps peripherals or headphones from a spares drawer, clears the session or reimages if needed, and verifies login, internet, and print release before handing back to the patron.

Meeting/program-room and AV equipment: set up and troubleshoot ceiling or cart projector, screen, HDMI/USB-C adapters, laptop, wireless microphone and batteries, amplifier/speakers, or a videoconference cart before a class or program; resolve 'no signal'/'no sound', re-route cables, adjust focus and levels, and confirm the presenter is running.

Circulation and staff-area equipment: self-check kiosk freeze or receipt-printer paper-roll change, RFID pad or barcode scanner not reading, label printer misfeed, book-drop/automated-sorter jam, staff desk PC or payment terminal fault; technician opens the unit, clears the obstruction, reloads consumables, restarts the client software, and tests with a live transaction.

Routine preventive maintenance rounds: opening/closing checks that power on and test every public station and printer, top up paper, clean screens, keyboards and scanner glass, tidy and secure cabling, check headphone and mouse inventory, apply/verify updates, log recurring faults, and pull or swap failing units and package them for vendor or IT repair.

sources.title: Helix-02 humanoid robot handles full 8-hour factory work shifts

sources.transferJustification: Cited as the frontier of general-purpose autonomous manipulation in human-built settings; the demonstrated tasks involve grasping rigid household objects and closing an appliance door, not opening machine panels, extracting jammed paper, or fault diagnosis, so it does not transfer to equipment troubleshooting.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is condition-monitoring rounds in a structured facility (E2). It substantiates autonomous detection of malfunctioning equipment but not the corrective physical work (panel opening, consumable replacement, cable reseating, test-and-verify) that the library instances require.

sources.title: Robotic Machine Tending Cells for CNC Automation | KUKA Canada
sources.claim: Purpose-built machine-tending cells autonomously open machine doors and load/unload fixtured parts, showing the E1 state of the art for servicing a machine: known geometry, fixtured rigid workpieces, and a pre-programmed cycle rather than open-ended fault diagnosis.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is tending a machine inside a fenced cell (E1). It shows robots can open doors and insert rigid parts at known poses, but the cycle is fixed and there is no diagnosis of an unknown fault or handling of torn paper, so it does not carry over to copier or PC troubleshooting.

sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic paper manipulation. It is the closest capability to reloading trays and clearing jams, and it is still a benchmark lab problem on flat card stock, so it does not support completing copier servicing at any tier.

tasks.label: Check for damaged library materials, such as books or audio-visual equipment, and provide replacements or make repairs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Circulation check-in inspection in a public or academic library: technician examines returned books and other print items at the desk or in the workroom for water damage, torn or loose pages, broken hinges/spines, marking, or mold, and routes damaged items to mending or to a replacement decision. Items are of every size, binding, and condition.

Bench mending in the library workroom: repairing damaged books by hand — tipping in and reattaching loose pages, taping torn pages, re-gluing hinges and spines, reattaching or replacing paperback covers, repairing dust jackets — using adhesives, mending tape, bone folders and book-repair kits, judging which technique the individual book needs.

AV media check: opening DVD/CD/audiobook-on-CD cases at check-in, verifying all discs and inserts are present, inspecting discs for scratches, running scratched discs through a disc-repair/resurfacing machine, and verifying playability before returning the item to the shelf.

Circulating technology and AV equipment: laptops, Chromebooks, tablets, hotspots, e-readers, projectors and their chargers/cases returned at the desk or kiosk — check for cracked screens or missing cords, power-on and function test, recharge, take damaged units out of circulation and issue a replacement device to the patron.

Withdrawal and replacement processing: an item judged beyond repair is pulled from the collection, records updated and a replacement copy ordered, and when the new copy arrives it is physically processed — property stamp, barcode and spine label applied, security strip inserted, mylar jacket fitted — and shelved.

Spot checks in the stacks or on a bookmobile: while shelf-reading, shelving, or working a bookmobile stop, the technician notices deteriorating or damaged items on the shelf (split spines, loose boards, mildew) and pulls them for repair or replacement review.

tasks.label: Process interlibrary loans for patrons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Borrowing side, consortium/state courier delivery: a delivery tote of incoming loaned books arrives in the circulation/ILL workroom; the technician empties the tote, matches routing and hold slips, receives/checks each barcoded or RFID-tagged item into the ILL system and ILS, straps a patron band/slip on it, routes it to the holds shelf or pickup locker, and triggers patron notification.

Borrowing side, mailed shipment: padded mailers and small boxes arrive from distant lenders via USPS/UPS; the technician cuts open each package, extracts the book (often wrapped, rubber-banded with the lender's loose paper paperwork), reads the lender's restrictions off the slip, matches it to the ILLiad/WorldShare request, saves the wrapper and return label, bands and shelves the book, notifies the patron.

Lending side: a request from another library arrives; the technician verifies availability in the catalog, walks the open stacks to pull the volume by call number (or reports it missing), checks its condition, checks it out to the borrowing library, prints and inserts the paperwork band with due date and restrictions, packs it in a courier tote or padded mailer with an address label, and places it in outgoing delivery.

Returns in both directions: a patron returns a borrowed ILL item at the desk or return chute; the technician checks it in, removes the band, repacks it in the original mailer or courier tote, labels and ships it back to the lender; on the lending side, the technician receives the library's own items back, checks them in, clears the ILL record, and returns them to the stacks.

Document delivery: an article or chapter request; the technician locates the bound journal volume or book in the stacks, scans the specific pages on a copier/overhead or book scanner, checks legibility, crops/OCRs and uploads the PDF to the ILL system or Article Exchange for electronic delivery, then reshelves the volume.

Exceptions and patron-facing service at the desk: rush and hard-to-fill requests, unfilled/cancelled requests, renewals and recalls, damaged or lost item assessment and correspondence with the lending library, non-circulating 'library use only' items handed to and monitored with the patron, searching the building for a requested item reported missing, copyright and invoice judgment calls.

instances.label: Set up, operate and strike projection and sound gear for a library program, class or meeting: move the projector/cart or screen into a meeting room or classroom, aim it, connect a laptop/DVD player and speakers/mic, power up, focus and keystone, set levels, run and adjust playback live while patrons are present, then shut down, coil cables and return the gear to storage. Patron-request playback at a viewing/listening/microform station: pull the requested videocassette, DVD, audio tape or microfilm reel from a media cabinet, load it into the matching deck or reader, cue and start playback, monitor and correct tracking/jams, then unload and refile the media.

Routine cleaning and functional testing of playback/recording decks in the workroom: run cleaning cartridges or cleaning discs through tape decks and drives, check heads and transport, run a test playback to verify sound and picture, log condition and flag units needing repair.

Preventive maintenance and minor repair on projectors, monitors, PA/amplifier gear and players at a workbench: open the case or lamp door, replace lamp module, air filter, belt or batteries, clean the lens and vents, check and reseat connectors, reassemble and functionally test the unit.

Duplication, dubbing or digitization runs in the media workroom: load source cassettes/discs into decks and recorders, start the record or transfer, monitor signal problems and re-run failures, then label, verify and file the output copies.

AV equipment lending and restocking: retrieve the requested projector, camera, laptop, recorder or hotspot from storage, confirm accessories and charge level, issue it to the patron, then receive it back, inspect for damage and missing parts, recharge and restock it.

roles.description: Instruct and advise individuals and families engaged in agriculture, agricultural-related processes, or home management activities. Demonstrate procedures and apply research findings to advance agricultural and home management activities. May develop educational outreach programs. May instruct on either agricultural issues such as agricultural processes and techniques, pest management, and food safety, or on home management issues such as budgeting, nutrition, and child development.

tasks.label: Advise farmers and demonstrate techniques in areas such as feeding and health maintenance of livestock, growing and harvesting practices, and financial planning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: On-farm livestock consultation: extension educator drives to a working beef, dairy, or small-ruminant operation, walks the barn/lot/pasture with the producer, evaluates feed bunk management, body condition, and health records, then demonstrates hands-on techniques (body-condition scoring on live animals, correct subcutaneous injection site, drenching, hoof/udder inspection, forage probe sampling of a bale) while explaining the reasoning and answering the producer's specific questions.

On-farm crop consultation and demonstration of growing/harvesting practices: educator meets a grower in the field or machine shed, digs stand counts and checks planting depth, scouts pests/disease, demonstrates sprayer nozzle calibration or a combine harvest-loss check on the grower's own equipment, and advises on adjustments for that farm's soils, varieties, and conditions.

Field day / twilight tour at a university research or demonstration farm: educator sets up demonstration plots or livestock stations and demonstrates practices (variety trials, cover-crop termination, grazing layout, calving assistance equipment) to a group of 20-60 producers, narrating and fielding questions from the crowd.

Indoor workshop or short course at an extension office, fairgrounds building, or community hall: educator delivers a presentation plus hands-on stations (nozzle calibration, hay probe use, vaccine handling and syringe technique, record-book and enterprise-budget spreadsheet exercises) and coaches individual participants through the steps.

Farm financial planning consultation: kitchen-table or office session with a farm family reviewing production and financial records, building cash-flow projections and enterprise budgets, running loan/expansion scenarios, and advising on decisions; the deliverable is information and a written plan, with no physical act required.

sources.developer: MIT / academic research team (published in PLOS ONE / PMC)
sources.title: TeachBot: Towards teaching robotics fundamentals for human-robot collaboration at work - PMC
sources.claim: TeachBot is a research prototype of an autonomous robotic instructor that teaches manufacturing-line workers introductory robotics through verbal, graphical and hands-on interaction in a lab/factory-training setting; it is the closest demonstrated case of a robot instructing humans, and it is limited to scripted lessons about operating the robot itself.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = a robot instructing humans in a skill. Transfer fails: TeachBot teaches a fixed curriculum about its own arm in a controlled training station; it cannot assess a specific farm's livestock, crops or finances, nor demonstrate husbandry/agronomic techniques on live animals, plants, or a producer's own machinery.

sources.title: Automatic Milking Robot | Lely Astronaut A5 Next
sources.claim: Lely Astronaut robotic milking units are commercially deployed at scale (tens of thousands of installations worldwide), performing teat cleaning, attachment and milking autonomously inside purpose-built robot boxes in dairy barns; they execute a livestock husbandry operation but provide no advising or teaching of producers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = autonomous execution of a livestock-handling technique. Transfer fails: the robot works on cows that present themselves in a fixtured stall and outputs milk, not instruction; it cannot evaluate a producer's feeding/health program or demonstrate and explain a technique to that producer.

sources.title: AI Weed Control: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder - Lidar News
sources.claim: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder performs autonomous computer-vision weeding in commercial growers' fields and is deployed across many countries, showing that field crop operations can be automated, but the machine performs production work rather than advising or instructing growers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = performing a growing-practice operation in an open field. Transfer fails: the instance requires diagnosing a particular grower's practice, demonstrating the corrected technique, and explaining it; the LaserWeeder executes a single pre-defined operation and produces no advice or demonstration for a human learner.

sources.system: Autonomous weeding robot demonstration event (multiple vendor machines)
sources.developer: Colorado State University Extension (event organized by specialist)
sources.title: Armed with lasers and blades and programmed to destroy all weeds, A.I. ag robots are coming to Colorado | Colorado State University
sources.claim: In extension practice, autonomous agricultural robots are the subject matter that a human educator demonstrates and explains to farmers; the advising and demonstration role at these events is filled by an extension specialist, not by a machine.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant context: at agricultural demonstration events the robot is the exhibit while a human extension educator performs the advising/teaching, indicating no deployed robotic system substitutes for the educator in this task.

instances.label: Crop/agronomy field day: extension educator establishes and then walks 15-40 farmers through demonstration plots on a cooperating producer's field or county research plot (new variety, cover crop termination, nutrient or tillage practice) — digging soil pits, pulling plants to show roots/nodulation, comparing treatments, taking stand counts, and fielding site-specific questions, outdoors in variable weather and terrain.

Equipment / precision-ag product demonstration: educator sets up and operates a new implement, sprayer, or drone in a farmyard or field edge for a watching group — e.g., sprayer nozzle selection and calibration with water-sensitive cards, drone spray/scouting setup, GPS guidance or variable-rate demo — troubleshooting on the spot and letting participants try the equipment.

Livestock husbandry demonstration at a producer's barn, corral, or fairground pen: showing body condition scoring, low-stress cattle handling, vaccination/injection technique, hoof or udder health checks, or a new feeding technology, with live animals present and participants gathered close.

Family and consumer sciences demonstration in an extension teaching kitchen, community center, or church hall: pressure-canning/food preservation demo or a nutrition cooking demo — assembling equipment, processing the product step-by-step in front of 10-30 participants, checking gauges and temperatures, sampling, and answering food-safety questions.

Horticulture / master gardener demonstration in a demonstration garden or homeowner landscape: pruning fruit trees or grapevines, showing IPM scouting and pest identification, planting/grafting, drip irrigation or composting setup, taught hands-on to a small group of volunteers or homeowners.

sources.title: Carbon Robotics releases new line of laser weed-zappers for more types of farms and budgets – GeekWire
sources.claim: Carbon Robotics' LaserWeeder autonomously identifies and kills weeds with lasers in commercial open-field vegetable and row-crop production; over 250,000 acres weeded across 100+ crops, with 100+ growers using it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing an agronomic operation in an open farm field. It shows machines can act on crops in E3 field conditions, but the system executes a single pre-set operation and does nothing to set up, narrate, or adapt an instructional demonstration for an audience of farmers.

sources.title: John Deere Reveals New Autonomous Machines & Technology at CES 2025
sources.claim: John Deere sells second-generation autonomy kits enabling driver-out tillage on 8R/9RX tractors in commercial fields; upgrade kits are available for specified model years.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous field machinery operation. Relevant because equipment demonstrations involve running machines in fields, but the autonomy covers only route-following field work on a mapped field with people kept clear — not operating varied new implements for a surrounding audience, calibrating them, or teaching the practice.

sources.title: Robotic kitchen in a box cooks, cleans and serves 120 meals an hour
sources.claim: Circus SE's CA-1 autonomous robotic kitchen prepares meals end-to-end inside an enclosed glass unit installed in a REWE supermarket in Germany.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously executing a food-preparation procedure in a facility. It is the closest analogue to a canning/cooking demonstration, but it runs a fixed menu inside a purpose-built sealed enclosure and provides no instruction, safety coaching, or audience interaction, so it does not deliver the educational output.

sources.title: The Interactive Museum Tour-Guide Robot – Robotics Institute, Carnegie Mellon University
sources.claim: Autonomous tour-guide robots have been deployed in museums, navigating among visitors and delivering explanatory information about exhibits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomously guiding and informing a group of people in a facility. It covers only the narration/guidance element on a fixed indoor route; it performs no manipulation of tools, crops, animals, or food, so it cannot demonstrate a product or technique.

instances.label: Row-crop or specialty-crop farm call: extension/agronomy educator schedules the appointment by phone/text, drives to the operation, meets the grower at the shop or field edge, walks fields to look at stand, pests and disease, discusses management options, and records the visit. Muddy field roads, variable field layouts, farm dogs and equipment traffic.

Livestock, dairy or poultry operation visit: educator arranges a time around chores/milking, travels to the farmstead, walks through the barn, parlor, feed bunk or pasture with the producer, observes animals and facilities, and talks through herd health, feeding and recordkeeping. Manure, loose animals, biosecurity boot-wash protocols.

Farm business/financial management visit: instructor sits at the farm office desk or kitchen table with the operator and spouse, opens their books or farm software, reviews cash flow, leases and transition plans, and leaves an action list. Private premises, papers and laptops, family members present.

Scheduling round and multi-farm windshield route: educator phones/emails a dozen producers to set visit dates around weather, planting and harvest, sequences them into a day's route across a rural county, and drives farm to farm on gravel roads and long driveways, adjusting when a producer is out in the field.

Family and consumer sciences / nutrition (e.g., EFNEP) home visit to a rural or farm family: educator schedules with the client, drives to the residence, enters the home, delivers a nutrition or budgeting lesson at the kitchen table, does a food-preparation or recordkeeping follow-up, and documents the contact. Private home, pets, children, no controlled layout.

sources.title: Solinftec boosts Solix autonomy with Discovery Mode, Starlink, and obstacle detection - Future Farming
sources.claim: Solinftec's Solix is a commercially deployed, solar-powered autonomous field robot that navigates row-crop fields on customer farms across the US Midwest to scout crops and pests and spot-spray; it automates in-field scouting but not the scheduling, travel and advisory consultation that make up an educator's farm visit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous crop scouting in open fields. It covers only the observational sub-step of a crop-farm visit; the machine stays on one farm, is hauled between sites by people, and outputs sensor data rather than a scheduled face-to-face advisory session with the grower, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.

sources.title: Robotics for poultry farming: Challenges and opportunities - ScienceDirect
sources.claim: Faromatics' Scout (formerly ChickenBoy) is a commercial autonomous ceiling-suspended barn robot that monitors birds and house conditions inside poultry sheds; it performs in-barn sensing on a single farm and does not travel to farms or conduct advisory visits with producers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous livestock-house inspection. It replaces part of the observation done during a livestock advisory visit, but it is installed on rails in one fixed barn and produces monitoring reports, not a scheduled on-farm consultation, so it does not transfer to the whole instance.

sources.title: AVA Robotics - Webex Community
sources.claim: Ava Robotics' telepresence robot navigates workplaces autonomously but exists to carry a remote human's video presence; the professional content of any 'visit' it enables is supplied live by the person on the far end, i.e. continuous remote operation of the interaction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile telepresence 'visits' inside buildings. Navigation is autonomous but the visit itself is delivered by a remote human driver/speaker, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment for making an advisory visit.

sources.title: Waymo's skyrocketing ridership in one chart | TechCrunch
sources.claim: Waymo operates the largest driverless passenger service in the US, but only within mapped metropolitan service areas; no driverless service covers rural county roads, gravel lanes and farm driveways, and it transports people rather than performing a visit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point road travel, the transport leg of a farm call. It is confined to mapped urban service areas and only moves a human passenger; it does not deliver the on-farm advisory contact that is the output of the instance.

instances.label: Grid or zone soil sampling on a cooperating farmer's row-crop field: drive/walk to GPS points across 40-500 acres, pull cores to a set depth through residue and variable moisture, composite into bagged, labeled samples, and submit them to a testing lab with the point map.

Soil sampling on pasture, hay ground, or other non-row-crop farm parcels: irregular boundaries, sod, fences, gates, livestock, wet spots and rougher terrain; composite cores by paddock or management zone, bag, label, and send for testing.

Collecting herbage/plant material for testing: clipping representative forage from a grazed pasture or hayfield, or pulling corn stalk/leaf tissue samples across a standing crop, then compositing, bagging, chilling/labeling and delivering the samples for nutrient, nitrate or forage-quality analysis.

Routine monitoring round over a farmer's fields to report on crop condition: traversing the growing crop, checking stand counts, weed escapes, disease and insect pressure against thresholds, and reporting findings and recommendations to the producer.

Supervising a farm property more broadly for an owner or landlord: walking the farmstead and fields to assess buildings, fences, drainage, stored grain, livestock and equipment, diagnosing a specific problem the farmer called about, and directing follow-up work.

Purchasing or selling products and supplies on the farmer's behalf: sourcing and comparing seed, fertilizer, feed or equipment, negotiating and placing the order or sale, and arranging pickup/delivery to the operation.

sources.claim: ROGO operates a commercial fleet of robotic soil samplers in open Midwestern row-crop fields, sampling hundreds of thousands of acres per season for dealers and farmers; part of the fleet is described as autonomous.

sources.title: Inside an Autonomous Soil Sampling Robot | Central Valley Ag
sources.claim: A cooperative describes how the ROGO robots it contracts with self-drive to each core location in the field on RTK GPS, extract cores to within 1/8 inch of target depth, and sensor-verify each core's quality.

sources.title: Soil Sampling Robot – ROGO
sources.claim: ROGO's current commercial system self-drives between sampling points on RTK GPS, repeats sample locations year to year, and records sampling metadata and barcode labeling automatically, with a stated 1-in-1,000 sample error rate.

sources.title: Autonomous robots enter fields to collect precise soil samples (Purdue Research Foundation News)
sources.claim: Purdue's release describes SmartCore as an autonomous robot that collects repeatable soil samples in farm fields and brings them to the field edge for shipment to the lab, working with farmers in IN, OH, IL and IA.

sources.developer: BioSense Institute, University of Novi Sad
sources.title: Agrobot Lala—An Autonomous Robotic System for Real-Time, In-Field Soil Sampling, and Analysis of Nitrates (Sensors)
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed unmanned ground vehicle performs fully autonomous in-field soil sampling with georeferenced samples and on-board nitrate analysis, demonstrating that the coring-and-sample-handling loop can run without a human in the field.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous In-situ Soil Sampling and Mapping in Large-Scale Agricultural Environments (arXiv)
sources.claim: A robotic soil sampling and on-site analysis system was field-validated on a large Australian pasture farm, consistently acquiring 50 g samples at 200 mm depth; the journal version describes the system as semi-autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (soil sampling) but on pasture/grazing land rather than row crop; cited to show the setting has been worked in, though autonomy level is not established.

sources.title: Solinftec Expands U.S. Footprint 243%, Deploys 100+ Autonomous Robots ... at Commodity Classic 2026
sources.claim: Solinftec reports more than 100 autonomous Solix ... deployed on US farms with sustained operations across row crops and specialty segments, after a 243% year-over-year increase in acreage under operation.

sources.title: Solinftec to Release Solix Sprayer Robot for Precise Pesticide Application – Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: The solar-powered Solix robots roam growers' fields autonomously and generate the agronomic scouting outputs a field visit produces: crop population, weed identification and density, disease and insect identification against thresholds, and nutrient deficiency maps.

sources.title: Breaking the field phenotyping bottleneck in maize with autonomous robots (Communications Biology)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed report of five seasons of autonomous under-canopy field data collection by TerraSentia robots across roughly 198,000 maize plots at US and Canadian field sites for Corteva, EarthSense and the University of Illinois.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-field crop monitoring/phenotyping. Transfers to a scouting round because the robot traverses the same standing crop and records the plant-level condition data an agent's monitoring visit produces.

sources.title: P-AgBot: In-Row & Under-Canopy Agricultural Robot for Monitoring and Physical Sampling (IEEE RA-L)
sources.claim: A research robot navigates autonomously under the corn canopy and physically collects leaf samples, but succeeds on only about 80% of sampling attempts and is a university prototype rather than a service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical plant-tissue sampling in a field, the closest analogue to herbage sampling; cited to show the state of the art is a prototype below worker reliability, not to support completion.
